name: Anjana Gutika

sections.introduction: Anjana gutika is an herbal formulation. This is used as Anjana which is applied over the eyes. This procedure is helpful in indigestion.
sections.ingredients:
Flowers of Mahua: This herb pacifies vata and pitta dosha. This herb provides nutrition to the body. Botanically it is called Bassia latifolia . 
 Apamarga Tandula powder ( Achyranthes aspera ): This herb is bitter and pungent in taste. It pacifies Vata and kapha Dosha. It acts as a laxative and appetizer. 
 Haldi ( Curcuma longa ): Haldi is useful in many diseases. It acts as an antibiotic. It pacifies pitta dosha. This is effective in skin problems, blood disorders etc. 
 Trikatu: This is obtained by mixing Shunthi ( Zingiber officinalis ), Pippali ( Piper longum ), Maricha ( Piper nigrum ). This is effective in kapha disorders. 
 Powder of roots of white variety Aprajita: Scientifically it is known as Clitoria ternatea. It pacifies all three dosha. It is effective in indigestion. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all drugs in equal quantity (1 part each) 
 Firstly filter the powder of all above said drugs except flowers of mahua. 
 Make a paste of Flowers of Mahua. 
 Then mix this powder with this paste and give proper frolement with water 
 Make 500mg tablets and dry them 
 Keep in an airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Anjana gutika is effective in eye disorders and also improves indigestion. Flower of mahua pacifies vata and pitta dosha and provides nutrition to the body. Trikatu is best for digestive problems. Apamarg acts as laxative and Haldi have the best antibacterial property and are useful in stomach infections.
sections.indications:

 Low digestive fire 

 How to Apply 
 Apply on eyes twice daily. 
 Cautions

T riphala: This is prepared by mixing equal parts of Amalaki ( Emblica officinalis ), Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula ), Bibhitaki ( Terminalia bellerica ).  Trikatu: This is obtained by mixing Shunthi ( Zingiber officinalis ), Pippali ( Piper longum ), Maricha ( Piper nigrum ). It is very effective in kapha elevated disorders as it pacifies kapha Dosha. It also stimulates the digestive juices and alleviates the toxins from the body. 
 Vacha: Scientifically it is known as Acorus calamus. This acts as an appetizer due to its deepana (increases digestive fire) and pachana (digestive properties) properties. It is also indicated in various neurological and psychological disorders.

 Datura ( Datura metel ): This stimulates digestive fire and is used as an appetizer. It pacifies kapha Dosha and used in numerous upper Respiratory tract disorders. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all the above dravya (things) in equal quantity. 
 Make a fine powder. After then apply bhavna of goat’s urine to the latter 
 Make tablets and let it dry.

 This anjana is best for anxiety and depression patients. Dhatura is useful in brain problems. It pacifies kapha dosha. Triphala and trikatu are best for digestion.  Introduction 
 Antrakutara Gutika (Vati) is an ayurvedic formulation. This is formulated from the mixture of herbs and mineral. This is known to treat various body ailments. 
 Ingredients 
 
 Hingula – Red Sulphide of Mercury (HgS) 
 Kuberaksha – Caesalpinia crista 
 Yavakshara – Hordeum vulgare 
 Nirgundi – Vitex negundo 
 Lashuna – Allium sativum 
 Tankana – Borax (Sodium borate) 
 Hingu – Ferula asafoetida 
 Vacha – Acorus Calamus 
 Abhaya – Terminalia chebula (Chebulic Myrobalan fruit rind) 
 Saindhava – Black salt 
 
 Medicinal Properties 
 It is poly herbal tablet formulation which possesses various medicinal properties. It has anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties and helps to reduce the inflammation and pain. It is useful in the management of inguinal hernia, menstrual pain and abdominal cramps. It has various medicinal properties like carminative, digestive stimulant, anti-spasmodic and also acts as an excellent detoxifier. It also improves the appetite and helps in anorexia. It acts as digestive stimulant and helps to enhance the acid secretion. 
 Indications 
 
 Udara (Stomach problems) 
 Shotha (Inflammation) 
 Udavarta (Painful menstrual discharge) 
 Antra Vruddhi (Inguinal hernia) 
 
 Dose 
 125 mg two times a day along with honey or water. 
 Contraindications 
 Take the medicine under ayurvedic doctor’s prescription. 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

 Hysteria is not a common issue as it is found in 1-4 % of the general population and more common during the 18th and 19th centuries. Hysteria is known as ungovernable emotional excess. For the management of Hysteria we have an amazing formulation named Aptantrakari vati. In this article, we are going to discuss this Aptantrakari vati in detail! Let’s have a Look!
sections.introduction: The Siddha Yoga Sangraha is a classical Ayurveda text which has many formulations being mentioned in it. One of such formulations is Aptantrakari Vati and is mentioned under Vata Vyadhi. Following content is the detailed information about it.
sections.ingredients_and_quantity:
Bhuni hing ( Ferula asafoetida – Roasted in Go Ghrit) – 12 grams 
 Camphor ( Cinnamomum camphora ) – 12 grams 
 Ganja seeds ( Cannabis sativa seeds ) – 1 gram 
 Khurasani Ajwain ( Hyoscyamus niger ) – 24 grams 
 Tagar ( Valeriana wallichii ) – 24 grams 
 Jatamansi Kwath (Decoction of Jatamansi) 



 Ingredient Description 
 1. Bhuni hing (Ferula asafoetida – Roasted) 
 It is a very good blood thinning agent and also has its impact on high blood pressure . In addition, it balances the Vata dosha in the body. 
 2. Camphor (Cinnamomum camphora) 
 It is a rare herb which is popular for its coolant property. Even after that it is an impressive kapha stabiliser. 
 3. Ganja seeds (Cannabis sativa seeds) 
 If taken as a medicine, this herb has immunomodulatory Impact. It helps in stimulating neurons. 
 4. Khurasani Ajwain (Hyoscyamus niger) 
 As it is having an impact in balancing the excess of Vata dosha, it soothes nerves and is also used in neuralgia. It also acts as an antispasmodic agent. 
 5. Tagar (Valeriana wallichii) 
 It is effective in many neurological conditions and is best for inducing sleep. It helps in psychiatric problems as well

 Take Powder of all the Ingredients in the given quantity and then put it in the mortar.

 Form Of Formulation 
 Tablets

name: Ardhnareshwar Rasa

sections.introduction: Ardhnareswar rasa is a herbo-mineral composition. This Ayurvedic formulation is best for kaphaj shiroshoola (headache due to vitiated kapha dosha).
sections.ingredients:
Cowrie Bhasma – 5 parts 
 Shuddha Tankan – 5 parts 
 Maricha Churna – 9 parts 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – 3 parts
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Cowrie Bhasma (Ash of Cypraea moneta ) – This bhasma is prepared from kapardika (yellow colored cowry shells. This bhasma mainly contains CACO3. It pacifies Kapha dosha. It has antipyretic, antiemetic, and mucolytic actions. 
 Shuddha Suhaga – This is also known as Citrus tankan. It improves digestion and relieves bloating. It pacifies vata and kapha dosha and is effective in headache, anemia and jaundice. 
 Maricha Churna ( Powder of Piper nigrum ) – It improves the function of the digestive system. It has a pungent taste and promotes digestive fire and is effective in Headache. 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha ( Aconitum ferox ) – This is used as medicine after detoxifying. It has an abundance of health benefits such as antipyretic, diaphoretic and analgesic properties. It pacifies all the tridosha such as vata, pitta and kapha dosha, especially balances vata and kapha dosha. It improves and enhances digestion, and very effective in piles also. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Properly mix these above ingredients in a kharal yantra. 
 Give bhavna with mother’s milk. 
 Make 375 mg tablets and dry them under shadow. 
 Kept these tablets in airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 This is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this formulation pacifying kapha dosha and relieves the symptoms caused by vitiated kapha dosha. The ingredients in this herbal formulation also have digestive properties.
sections.indications:
Headache due to vitiated kapha (kaphaj shirshoola). 
 How to Apply 
 Give nasya (nasal drops) after abrading the tablet with water once a day (morning). 
 Caution 
 Take under medical supervision. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Arjakadi vati is an Ayurvedic formulation. This is the best herbal drug for enhancing sperm motility. The ingredients in this formulation help in increasing testosterone level.

 Vidarikanda ( Pueraria tuberosa ) 
 Gokshura Beej (Seeds of Tribulus terrestris ) 
 Kapikachu Beej (Seeds of Mucuna pruriens ) 

 Quantity of Ingredients 
 Take every drug in equal quantity that is 50 gms each.
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Barbari Mool ( Ocimum basilicum ) – It has pungent and astringent taste. It pacifies all three doshas. It provides strength to the rasadi dhatu and hence enhances testosterone level in the body. It also acts as an appetizer. Barbari is also useful in blood disorders. 
 Shankhpushpi ( Convolvulus pluricaulis ) – Shankhpushpi is known as medhya (brain tonic), and an amazing herb for nervous coordination. This calms the mind and body by inducing sleep. It also helps in managing the nervous diseases. 
 Jaiphal ( Myristica fragrans ) – It is a nutritious herb which is hot in potency and mainly balances pitta and kapha dosha. It acts as anti-inflammatory, antipyretic and acts as aphrodisiac. It provides strength to the body and also useful in liver and spleen disorders. It is also effective in the brain and nervous system. 
   Shatavari ( Asparagus racemosus ) – It is the best drug for female reproductive health. It also has spermapoietic property, it increases sperm count also and provides strength to the body. Shatavari helps in treating all types of menstrual disorders such as dysmenorrhea, amenorrhea, oligomenorrhea etc. It is very good in relieving pelvic pain. 
 Gokshura ( Tribulus terrestris ) – It has a sweet taste and is useful in pacifying Vata dosha. It has aphrodisiac property. It increases sperm count and motility. It also acts as diuretic. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make a fine powder of above drugs. 
 Give Bhavna with the decoction of babulamoola ( Vachellia nilotica ). 
 Make 1 gm tablet and let them under sunlight. 
 Kept these tablets in airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Arjakadi vati is an effective drug for sexual problems. The ingredients such as kapikachu, gokshur, shatavari, anantmool, jaiphal, shweta mushli are helping in increasing sperm motility and also enhancing testosterone level in the body. This is the best Aphrodisiac drug.

name: Arkeshwar Rasa

sections.introduction: Arkeshwar rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this medicine are effective in various blood disorders.
sections.ingredients:
Abhrak Bhasma 
 Loha Bhasma 
 Vanga Bhasma 
 Swarna-makshik Bhasma
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Abhrak Bhasma – Abhrak bhasma is calcined mica ash. It is used in ayurveda for abdominal, respiratory problems. It has anti-inflammatory and digestive properties. 
 Loha Bhasma – It has hematogenic properties (helps in formation of RBCs). It pacifies pitta dosha. It maintains the normal level of blood in the body. 
 Vanga Bhasma – It is very good in patients with anemia, urinary tract infections, diabetes, asthma etc. It also helps in obesity by promoting weight loss. 
 Swarna-makshik Bhasma – The purified powder of swarna makshik is very effective in jaundice, anemia, joint pain and weakness, insomnia, etc. It aids in treating chronic fever also. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Properly mix all the above ingredients in a kharal yantra. 
 Give Guduchi swaras bhavna ( Tinospora cordifolia ) and after cooked this mixture over gaj put (specially designed instrument). 
 Remove this mixture from gajput and give proper frolement. 
 Kept this mixture in airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Arkeshwar rasa is a herbo-mineral composition. This formulation has hematogenic properties which is useful in the formation of RBCs. Swarna (Gold) is used for the nourishment of rasadi dhatus (bodily tissues). This Ayurvedic formulation is used for the treatment of Raktapitta (various blood disorders).
sections.indications: Raktapitta (various blood disorders like ITP, Glanzmann thrombasthenia, Epistaxis etc.).
sections.dosage:
2 tablets twice a day with the extracts of Vasa ( Adhatoda vasica ). 
 Cautions 

 Avoid in pregnancy. 
 Take under the medical supervision. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Arkmurti Rasa

sections.introduction: Arkmurti rasa is a herbo-mineral Ayurvedic formulation and is effective in jwara (Fever). It improves digestion by increasing digestive power.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parade – 2 parts 
 Shuddha Gandhak – 4 parts 
 Shuddha Vatsnabha – 16 parts 
 Loha Bhasma – 8 parts 
 Tamra Bhasma – 1 part
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) – This acts as Rasayan after detoxifying this mineral. This is used in various diseases such as indigestion, fever, diarrhea, skin diseases etc . It balances all three dosha.   
 Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulphur) – Sulphur is used as medicine after purification of this substance. This is a non-metallic solid element found in nature. In Ayurveda it is used in various types of fever, indigestion, psoriasis etc. Pure form of sulphur also used as Rasayan (Rejuvenate). 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – This is known as Aconitum ferox . This is used as medicine after detoxifying this drug. It has antipyretic and diaphoretic properties and also has an analgesic effect. 
 Loha Bhasma – It is effective in skin disorders, anemia, tuberculosis. It pacifies all three dosha. 
 Tamra Bhasma ( Copper ash ) – This has Astringent taste. This pacifies Vata and kapha dosha. This is used as medicine after detoxifying this mineral. This is effective in fever. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make a kajjali from shuddha Parada and shuddha Gandhak in a kharal yantra. 
 Then mix the fine powders of tamra and loha bhasma. 
 Give bhavna with the decoction of chitrakmool (roots of Plumbago zeylanica) under the sunlight for 7 days. 
 After that mix 16 parts of shuddha Vatsanabha powder in this kajjali and give bhavna with panch pitta (Biles of rohu fish, buffalo, pig, goat and peacock). 
 Make 125 mg tablets and let them dry. 
 Kept in airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Arkmurti rasa is an effective medicine for sannipataj jwara (fever associated with three doshas i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha). The ingredients in this formulation are effective in digestion by improving digestive power. Parada and Gandhak acts as Rasayan and detoxifies the body from various toxins. All the ingredients are helpful in digesting Aama (Endotoxins).
sections.indications:
Sannipataj jwara (fever associated with three doshas i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha) 
 Indigestion 
 Vomiting
sections.dosage:
1 tablet twice a day with the extracts of Adraka ( Zingiber officinale ) or madhu (Honey). 
 Cautions 

 Take under the medical supervision. 
 Don’t overdose this medicine. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

 Arkmurti rasa is a herbo-mineral Ayurvedic formulation and is effective in jwara (Fever). It improves digestion by increasing digestive power. 
 Ingredients 
 
 Shuddha Parade – 2 parts 
 Shuddha Gandhak – 4 parts 
 Shuddha Vatsnabha – 16 parts 
 Loha Bhasma – 8 parts 
 Tamra Bhasma – 1 part 
 
 Description of Ingredients 
 
 Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) – This acts as Rasayan after detoxifying this mineral. This is used in various diseases such as indigestion, fever, diarrhea, skin diseases etc . It balances all three dosha.   
 Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulphur) – Sulphur is used as medicine after purification of this substance. This is a non-metallic solid element found in nature. In Ayurveda it is used in various types of fever, indigestion, psoriasis etc. Pure form of sulphur also used as Rasayan (Rejuvenate). 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – This is known as Aconitum ferox . This is used as medicine after detoxifying this drug. It has antipyretic and diaphoretic properties and also has an analgesic effect. 
 Loha Bhasma – It is effective in skin disorders, anemia, tuberculosis. It pacifies all three dosha. 
 Tamra Bhasma ( Copper ash ) – This has Astringent taste. This pacifies Vata and kapha dosha. This is used as medicine after detoxifying this mineral. This is effective in fever. 
 
 Method of Preparation 
 
 Make a kajjali from shuddha Parada and shuddha Gandhak in a kharal yantra. 
 Then mix the fine powders of tamra and loha bhasma. 
 Give bhavna with the decoction of chitrakmool (roots of Plumbago zeylanica) under the sunlight for 7 days. 
 After that mix 16 parts of shuddha Vatsanabha powder in this kajjali and give bhavna with panch pitta (Biles of rohu fish, buffalo, pig, goat and peacock). 
 Make 125 mg tablets and let them dry. 
 Kept in airtight glass container. 
 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Arkmurti rasa is an effective medicine for sannipataj jwara (fever associated with three doshas i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha). The ingredients in this formulation are effective in digestion by improving digestive power. Parada and Gandhak acts as Rasayan and detoxifies the body from various toxins. All the ingredients are helpful in digesting Aama (Endotoxins). 
 Indications 
 
 Sannipataj jwara (fever associated with three doshas i.e. Vata, Pitta and Kapha) 
 Indigestion 
 Vomiting 
 
 Dosage 
 1 tablet twice a day with the extracts of Adraka ( Zingiber officinale ) or madhu (Honey). 
 Cautions 
 
 Take under the medical supervision. 
 Don’t overdose this medicine. 
 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – It is a silver coloured metal known as quicksilver. A purest form of herb is used as a medicine. It is mixed with gandhak and used. Parada is a very effective drug which balances all the doshas i.e. vata, pitta and kapha. The health benefits of mercury is balya (nourishes the body), aphrodisiac (vrishya) and has rejuvenating properties (rasayan). It is very beneficial for neurological disorders.   
 Shuddha Gandhak – It is used as medicine in various diseases.  This is a non-metallic solid element found in nature. It is useful in piles after improving digestion. As said in Charaka Samhita that Arsh (piles) are due to low digestive fire ( Mandagni ). It improves digestive power by stimulating digestive fire. 
 Cow’s Urine – As per ayurvedic context, it is very beneficial and assists in treating lots of diseases such as leprosy, kidney diseases, fever, peptic ulcers, liver diseases etc. It also possesses anti-cancerous properties thus removing all the ill-elements or toxins from the body. 
 Snuhi Ksheera (Milk latex of Euphorbia neriifolia ) – Snuhi ksheera is very effective in patients with piles. It also helps in cough and sore throat. It corrects the imbalance of dosha and sustains normal body functioning. 
 Suran Churna – It is pungent and astringent in taste thus pacifies vata and kapha dosha. It acts as purgative and digestive fire stimulating property. It sustains the healthy digestive system by eliminating the ailments.  
 Dantimool Churna – This is an amazing herb which possesses anti-cancerous, purgative, immune boosting, anti-microbial and hepato-protective properties. It corrects the imbalance of doshas and maintains normal functioning of the body.  
 Yavakshar – It is a very good remedy for kidney stones or any other obstruction in the body or throat. It also enhances digestion and corrects the urine retention; UTI’s which are very common nowadays. It also possesses hepatoprotective property and is helpful in prostate enlargement.   
 Shunthi ( Zingiber officinale ) – This is very effective in digestive problems. It pacifies Vata and kapha dosha. It is helpful in piles. 
 Maricha – Maricha is known as Piper nigrum. It improves the function of the digestive system. It has a pungent taste and promotes digestive fire and ultimately treats Arsh (piles). 
 Pippali – Pippali is known as Piper longum. It promotes digestive fire and has rejuvenating property. It pacifies Vata and Kapha. It is helpful in various digestive problems. 
 Shuddha Suhaga – This is also known as Citrus tankan. It improves digestion and relieves bloating. It pacifies vata dosha and is effective in anemia and jaundice. 
 Loha Bhasma – Iron ash is effective in skin disorders, tuberculosis and pacifies all three doshas. It pacifies pitta dosha and hence useful in amlapitta. It is also effective in anemic conditions. 
 Tamra Bhasma ( Copper Ash ) – This pacifies Vata and kapha dosha. This is used as medicine after detoxifying this mineral. This is effective in Gastric problems. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make a kajjali from Parada and Gandhak in a kharal yantra. 
 Mix all the above powders in this kajjali. 
 Then add snuhikshir (Extracts of Euphorbia nerifolia ) and cow’s urine. 
 Cooked this formulation over low flame. 
 Then filtrate this mixture and kept in airtight glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Arshkuthar ras is an Ayurvedic formulation. This helps in improving low digestive fire. The ingredients in this formulation help in enhancing digestive fire. According to Acharya Charaka Arsha (piles) is caused by mandagni (low digestive fire). So this herbal medicine is best for improving digestion of the Arsha patient.

name: Arshohar Gutika

sections.overview: Arshohar Gutika – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction:
Piles, known as Arsha in Ayurveda, are engorged and inflamed vascular swellings in the anal canal, often arising from chronic constipation, sedentary lifestyle, low-fiber diet, and aggravated Vata and Pitta dosha. Clinically, they present with pain, bleeding during defecation, itching, swelling, and discomfort that significantly affect quality of life. Ayurveda considers impaired digestive fire (Agnimandya) and accumulation of toxins (Ama) as root contributors. Arshohar Gutika, a classical Ayurvedic formulation, is traditionally used to manage piles by correcting digestion, reducing inflammation, and supporting healthy bowel movement. Its herbal-mineral components exhibit mild laxative, anti-inflammatory, and hemostatic properties, helping to shrink pile masses and reduce bleeding. By addressing both symptoms and underlying doshic imbalance, Arshohar Gutika offers a holistic and supportive approach in the management of piles. Let’s discuss this formulation in detail!

 First Method
sections.ingredients_with_description:
1. Pearl Shell (Mukta Shukti) 

Pearl shell, known as Mukta Shukti in Ayurveda, is rich in natural calcium compounds and is processed into bhasma through repeated calcination. It possesses sheeta (cooling) and pitta-pacifying properties. In piles, especially bleeding and burning types, Mukta Shukti helps reduce heat, inflammation, and irritation in the anorectal region. Its astringent and healing action supports the contraction of dilated veins and assists in controlling bleeding. Additionally, it strengthens mucosal tissues and promotes faster healing of ulcers or fissure-like lesions commonly associated with hemorrhoids.

 2. Radish Juice (Raphanus Sativus) 

Radish juice is described as deepana (appetizer) and bhedana (mild laxative) with the ability to pacify aggravated Vata in the lower abdomen. It improves digestion, relieves constipation, and reduces abdominal bloating—major contributing factors in piles. Its natural fiber and detoxifying action help soften stools and ensure smooth bowel evacuation, minimizing strain during defecation. By clearing accumulated ama (toxins) and improving liver function, radish juice supports overall gastrointestinal health, thereby indirectly reducing recurrence and severity of hemorrhoids.

 3. Aluva (Aloe Vera) 

Aluva, commonly identified with Aloe vera, is known for its mridu virechana (gentle laxative) and soothing properties. It pacifies Pitta and Vata, reduces dryness in the intestines, and promotes smooth bowel movement. In piles, Aloe vera helps reduce inflammation, burning sensation, and irritation. Its wound-healing and cooling effects soothe swollen hemorrhoidal tissues and aid tissue repair. By preventing constipation and maintaining intestinal lubrication, Aluva plays a supportive role in both managing symptoms and preventing further aggravation of piles.

 4. Rasont (Rasaut – Berberis Aristata Extract) 

Rasont, a concentrated extract of Daruharidra, has strong astringent and anti-inflammatory properties. It pacifies Pitta and Kapha and is particularly beneficial in bleeding piles. Its astringent action helps constrict dilated veins and control rectal bleeding, while its antimicrobial properties protect against secondary infections. Rasont also improves digestion and reduces intestinal inflammation, addressing the root causes such as mandagni and ama accumulation. Through its cooling and healing action, it supports faster recovery and long-term relief in hemorrhoidal conditions.

 Method Of Preparation 

 Take a pearl shell and give it 3 putas (calcination cycles) in radish juice to prepare bhasma (calx). 
 Then mix this bhasma with Aelu and Rasaut in equal parts. 
 Triturate with radish juice for 7 days and prepare pills of 1–2 ratti each.
sections.dosage:
Take 1–2 pills with fennel distillate or water, morning and evening.

 Clinical Use And Indication 

 This preparation purifies the bowels. 
 It alleviates piles and liver disorders, constipation, abdominal enlargement, colic pain, Mandagni (Low digestive fire), and Piles. 
 It stops bleeding of piles and has also been found beneficial in flatulence. 
 It relieves enlargement of the liver, splenic disorders, accumulation of toxins (ama), and disorders caused by ama. As it contains pearl shell bhasma, it also helps in conditions arising from calcium deficiency such as skin eruptions, boils, or disorders resembling cold-type eruptions. 
 If excessive purgation occurs, the medicine should be stopped temporarily or the dose should be reduced by half. This is a time-tested formulation and is considered highly effective. 

 Conclusion 

In conclusion, piles (Arsha) require a comprehensive approach that not only relieves symptoms but also corrects the underlying digestive imbalance. Arshohar Gutika serves as a supportive Ayurvedic formulation that helps regulate bowel movements, reduce inflammation, control bleeding, and soothe discomfort. By improving Agni and minimizing Ama accumulation, it assists in preventing recurrence and promoting anorectal health. When taken under proper guidance along with dietary modifications and a healthy lifestyle, this formulation can be used for good relief and long-term management of piles, offering a natural and holistic pathway toward improved comfort and well-being.

 Reference : Ras Tantra Saar and Siddha prayog Sangreha 
 Classical Indication : Arsha (Piles) 
 Introduction 
 
Piles, known as Arsha in Ayurveda, are engorged and inflamed vascular swellings in the anal canal, often arising from chronic constipation, sedentary lifestyle, low-fiber diet, and aggravated Vata and Pitta dosha. Clinically, they present with pain, bleeding during defecation, itching, swelling, and discomfort that significantly affect quality of life. Ayurveda considers impaired digestive fire (Agnimandya) and accumulation of toxins (Ama) as root contributors. Arshohar Gutika, a classical Ayurvedic formulation, is traditionally used to manage piles by correcting digestion, reducing inflammation, and supporting healthy bowel movement. Its herbal-mineral components exhibit mild laxative, anti-inflammatory, and hemostatic properties, helping to shrink pile masses and reduce bleeding. By addressing both symptoms and underlying doshic imbalance, Arshohar Gutika offers a holistic and supportive approach in the management of piles. Let’s discuss this formulation in detail!
 
 First Method 
 Ingredients With Description 
 1. Reetha (Sapindus Mukorossi) 
 
Reetha, commonly known as soapnut, is valued in Ayurveda for its cleansing and detoxifying properties. It possesses katu (pungent), tikta (bitter) rasa, and helps balance Kapha and Pitta dosha. Reetha acts as a mild laxative and supports proper bowel movement, reducing strain during defecation—one of the main causes of piles. Its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial nature helps soothe swollen hemorrhoidal tissues and prevent infection. By promoting gentle cleansing of the intestines and reducing accumulated toxins (ama), Reetha assists in relieving bleeding, itching, and discomfort associated with piles, thereby supporting healthy anorectal function.
 
 2. Rasont (Rasaut – Extract Of Berberis Aristata) 
 
Rasont, prepared from the concentrated extract of Daruharidra (Berberis aristata), is known for its tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) properties. It pacifies Pitta and Kapha dosha and acts as a powerful anti-inflammatory and wound-healing agent. In piles, Rasont helps reduce bleeding due to its astringent action, which constricts dilated veins and controls excessive discharge. Its antimicrobial and cooling properties soothe burning sensations and irritation in bleeding hemorrhoids. Additionally, it improves digestion and reduces inflammation in the lower gastrointestinal tract, thereby addressing the root cause of piles and promoting faster healing of affected tissues.
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 
 Mix equal parts of Ritha bark and Rasaut with water and grind well. Prepare pills of 1–2 ratti each by adding sufficient water. 
 
 Dosage 
 
Take 1–2 pills twice daily. After swallowing, drink 10 tolas of goat’s milk that has been boiled and then cooled.
 
 Clinical Use And Indication 
 
By taking this preparation, bleeding piles are relieved within 1–2 weeks.
 
 Second Method 
 Ingredients With Description 
 1. Purified Mainshil (Realgar – Arsenic Disulfide) 
 
Mainshil, after proper purification (shodhana), is used in classical Ayurveda in very minute doses. It is considered ushna (heating) and helps pacify aggravated Kapha and Vata. In piles, especially chronic and painful types, purified Mainshil helps reduce hard swelling, improves sluggish circulation in the anorectal region, and supports the resolution of mass-like growths. It also stimulates digestive fire (agni), preventing constipation—one of the main causative factors of hemorrhoids. Due to its potency, it is always used under strict supervision and in properly processed form.
 
 2. Purified Gandhak (Sulphur) 
 
Shuddha Gandhak is widely valued for its rasayana (rejuvenative) and anti-inflammatory properties. It balances Pitta and Vata, supports healthy digestion, and acts as a mild laxative. In piles, Gandhak helps reduce inflammation, burning sensation, itching, and pain. Its antimicrobial nature protects the affected tissues from infection and promotes wound healing. By improving bowel regularity and reducing dryness in the intestines, it prevents straining during defecation, thereby assisting in both the management and prevention of hemorrhoids.
 
 3. Bhang Juice (Cannabis Sativa) 
 
Bhang juice, derived from Cannabis sativa leaves and processed traditionally, is described in Ayurveda as deepana (digestive stimulant) and vedanasthapana (pain-relieving). In piles, it helps relieve severe pain, spasm, and discomfort associated with inflamed hemorrhoidal veins. It also supports appetite and digestion, reducing ama formation and constipation. When used in controlled, classical formulations, bhang acts as a synergistic medium (bhavana dravya), enhancing the potency and absorption of other ingredients while calming irritation in the lower gastrointestinal tract.
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 
 Take purified Mainshil (realgar) and purified Gandhak (sulphur) in equal parts. 
 Triturate them in bhang (cannabis) juice for 7 days and prepare pills of 1–2 ratti each. 
 
 Dosage 
 
Take 1–2 pills with buttermilk or goat’s milk, twice daily.
 
 Clinical Use And Indication 
 
This preparation relieves piles (internal and external), Mandagni (low digestive fire), abdominal pain, constipation, and weakness.
 
 Third Method 
 Ingredients With Description 
 1. Pearl Shell (Mukta Shukti) 
 
Pearl shell, known as Mukta Shukti in Ayurveda, is rich in natural calcium compounds and is processed into bhasma through repeated calcination. It possesses sheeta (cooling) and pitta-pacifying properties. In piles, especially bleeding and burning types, Mukta Shukti helps reduce heat, inflammation, and irritation in the anorectal region. Its astringent and healing action supports the contraction of dilated veins and assists in controlling bleeding. Additionally, it strengthens mucosal tissues and promotes faster healing of ulcers or fissure-like lesions commonly associated with hemorrhoids.
 
 2. Radish Juice (Raphanus Sativus) 
 
Radish juice is described as deepana (appetizer) and bhedana (mild laxative) with the ability to pacify aggravated Vata in the lower abdomen. It improves digestion, relieves constipation, and reduces abdominal bloating—major contributing factors in piles. Its natural fiber and detoxifying action help soften stools and ensure smooth bowel evacuation, minimizing strain during defecation. By clearing accumulated ama (toxins) and improving liver function, radish juice supports overall gastrointestinal health, thereby indirectly reducing recurrence and severity of hemorrhoids.
 
 3. Aluva (Aloe Vera) 
 
Aluva, commonly identified with Aloe vera, is known for its mridu virechana (gentle laxative) and soothing properties. It pacifies Pitta and Vata, reduces dryness in the intestines, and promotes smooth bowel movement. In piles, Aloe vera helps reduce inflammation, burning sensation, and irritation. Its wound-healing and cooling effects soothe swollen hemorrhoidal tissues and aid tissue repair. By preventing constipation and maintaining intestinal lubrication, Aluva plays a supportive role in both managing symptoms and preventing further aggravation of piles.
 
 4. Rasont (Rasaut – Berberis Aristata Extract) 
 
Rasont, a concentrated extract of Daruharidra, has strong astringent and anti-inflammatory properties. It pacifies Pitta and Kapha and is particularly beneficial in bleeding piles. Its astringent action helps constrict dilated veins and control rectal bleeding, while its antimicrobial properties protect against secondary infections. Rasont also improves digestion and reduces intestinal inflammation, addressing the root causes such as mandagni and ama accumulation. Through its cooling and healing action, it supports faster recovery and long-term relief in hemorrhoidal conditions.
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 
 Take a pearl shell and give it 3 putas (calcination cycles) in radish juice to prepare bhasma (calx). 
 Then mix this bhasma with Aelu and Rasaut in equal parts. 
 Triturate with radish juice for 7 days and prepare pills of 1–2 ratti each. 
 
 Dosage 
 
Take 1–2 pills with fennel distillate or water, morning and evening.
 
 Clinical Use And Indication 
 
 This preparation purifies the bowels. 
 It alleviates piles and liver disorders, constipation, abdominal enlargement, colic pain, Mandagni (Low digestive fire), and Piles. 
 It stops bleeding of piles and has also been found beneficial in flatulence. 
 It relieves enlargement of the liver, splenic disorders, accumulation of toxins (ama), and disorders caused by ama. As it contains pearl shell bhasma, it also helps in conditions arising from calcium deficiency such as skin eruptions, boils, or disorders resembling cold-type eruptions. 
 If excessive purgation occurs, the medicine should be stopped temporarily or the dose should be reduced by half. This is a time-tested formulation and is considered highly effective. 
 
 Conclusion 
 
In conclusion, piles (Arsha) require a comprehensive approach that not only relieves symptoms but also corrects the underlying digestive imbalance. Arshohar Gutika serves as a supportive Ayurvedic formulation that helps regulate bowel movements, reduce inflammation, control bleeding, and soothe discomfort. By improving Agni and minimizing Ama accumulation, it assists in preventing recurrence and promoting anorectal health. When taken under proper guidance along with dietary modifications and a healthy lifestyle, this formulation can be used for good relief and long-term management of piles, offering a natural and holistic pathway toward improved comfort and well-being.

Abstract 
 Ayurveda describes various types of formulation in classical texts such as oil, ghee, rasa, bhasma, gutika/ tablet forms. These days tablets are the most convenient form of medicine as it is easily accessible, taken. This gutika preparation has anti diarrheal, constipating and digestive properties. It contains herbomineral and toxic ingredients which can affect the brain, heart so always used with caution.
sections.introduction:
Ashtakshari gutika is a standardised tablet formulation prepared from various herbal medicines. It has anti diarrheal, carminative and antispasmodic action. This preparation helps in improving intestinal and gut health. These tablets should be taken under medical supervision as it contains ahiphena ( Papaver somniferum) and shudh hingul like ingredients. Thos preparation contains 16 ingredients which only acts on digestive disorders. The main indication of this formulation is malabsorption syndrome, loose stools, colic pain and digestive weakness. 
 Classical Indication 
 According to classics, Astha kshari gutika is mentioned in the text of Sahasrayogam to improve gut health or abdominal disorders. Among all dosha (vata, pitta and kapha), it helps in pacifying vata and kapha dosha. Some of the classical indications mentioned are as follows- 

 Grahani (IBS- Irritable bowel syndrome) 
 Arsha (Hemorrhoids) 
 Atisara (Loose stools) 
 Pravahika (Dysentery) 
 Shula (Colic pain) 
 Anaha (Abdominal distension)
sections.ingredients:
The list of ingredients used are listed below- 

 Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum) – 1 part 
 Shweta chandana (Santalum album)- 1 part 
 Rakta chandana (Pterocarpus santalinus) – 1 part 
 Ajaji ( Myristica fragrans) – 1 part 
 Shuddha hingula (Cinnabar- mercury compound)- 1 part 
 Pippali (Piper longum) – 1 part 
 Hingu (Asafoetida) – 1 part 
 Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum) – 1 part

 Yavani ( Trachyspermum roxburghii) – qs 
 Dhayanak ( Coriandrum sativum) – qs 
 Jambhira (Lemon juice)- qs 

 Benefits Of Ingredients 

 Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum)- It is a thick latex obtained from poppy seeds. These seeds mainly act on vata dosha and increase kapha dosha. It has a great role in loose stools, dysentery or abdominal pain like symptoms. It also calms the mind, anxiety, muscular spasms, pain. It acts as nerve sedative, relaxant, analgesics and calming in nature. 
 Shweta chandana (Santalum album)- Chandan helps in managing lower GI related issues such as decreased inflammation from intestines and urinary system. It prevents growth of bacteria and balances pitta dosha so also corrects digestive issues. It also has entero toxic properties so prevents diarrhoea like symptoms. 
 Rakta chandana (Pterocarpus santalinus)- This variety of chandan plays a protective role in abdominal issues, heals gastric ulcers and reduces production of gastric acid. It has cold potency and wound healing properties. 
 Ajaji ( Myristica fragrans)- Ajaji has a cyto-toxic effect as it protects healthy cells and reduces inflammatory changes in the body. It has antibacterial properties, improves digestion, anorexia like abdominal disorders. 
 Shuddha hingula (Cinnabar)- Hingul works on balancing kapha, pitta dosha and manages conditions like nausea, vomiting, jaundice like conditions. It helps in managing liver and spleen disorders. 
 Pippali (Piper longum)- Pippali fruits are used as it has hot potency so is very effective in respiratory and digestive disorders. It has carminative and antiflatulent properties. It is beneficial in flatulence, bloating, abdominal distension like conditions. It has analgesic, anti helminthic and carminative properties. 
 Hingu (Asafoetida)- Hingu is the most beneficial drug for abdominal disorders like constipation, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain. It restores pH level of the body, maintains metabolism and provides strength. 
 Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum)- Ativisha is helpful in managing diarrhoea as it helps in absorption of water from the body. It promotes digestion, prevents infections and corrects indigestion problems. It enhances weight loss and improves immunity. 
 Rasana ( Pluchea lesiulata)- Rasna helps in abdominal disorders like indigestion, flatulence or loose stools. It improves digestive fire due to hot potency. It helps in reducing colic pain, abdominal distension and bloating 
 Sunthi  (Zingiber officinalis)- Dry ginger has antioxidant and antibacterial properties. It prevents various infections, pain and inflammations in the body. It improves digestion and reduces acidity problems. 
 Jiraka (Cuminum cyminum)- Jeera is an aromatic compound which has digestive functioning due to presence of thymol in it. It helps in reducing diarrhoea, loose stools, pain in abdomen like symptoms. It reduces production of gas and boosts immunity. 
 Dusparsha ( Solanum xanthocarpum)- Kantakari improves digestive fire and corrects all ailments related to digestion. It is hot in potency so it manages indigestion, pain in abdomen and flatulence. 
 Musta (Cyperus rotundus)- It promotes lower abdominal comfort and GIT disorders. Without aggravating pitta it improves digestion, eliminates toxins from the body. It promotes healthy absorptions and corrects metabolism. 
 Yavani ( Trachyspermum roxburghii) – Yvani helps in managing abdominal spasms, discomfort, heartburn and indigestion-like symptoms.  It promotes appetite by removing toxins from the body, corrects gas, constipation like digestive conditions.   
 Dhayanak ( Coriandrum sativum)- Coriander aids digestion and corrects diarrhoea, abdominal pain, indigestion, irritable bowel syndrome and improves liver health. It improves bloating, abdominal distension and intestinal disorders. 
 Jambhira (Lemon juice)- Due to the presence of citric acid it helps in production of gastric juices which aids in digestion. It helps in removing undigested food and aids appetite. It helps in bleeding gums and digestive issues. 

 Method Of Preparation 
 The steps for preparation of Ashta kshari gutika are given as follows- 

 Firstly collect all the drugs mentioned above and wash them properly. 
 Keep the drugs in the shade away from direct sunlight for drying. 
 Then prepare a fine powder of all ingredients mentioned. (separately) 
 Then triturate powder of all drugs with the mardan drugs in a clean vessel. 
 Mix the solution properly by continuously stirring it. 
 At last prepare the pills of the obtained solution and let them dry in shade. 
 After drying these pills should be stored in an airtight glass container. 
 This preparation is known as Astaksari gutika.
sections.properties:
The properties of Astha kshari gutika are given as following- 

 It improves digestive disorders. 
 Maintains gut health. 
 Increases blood circulation. 
 Removes toxins from the body. 
 Reduces excessive mucus from the body. 
 Controls peristaltic movements. 
 It has carminative, analgesic properties. 
 Reduces inflammation, prevents infections. 
 Act as sedative and tranquilliser.
sections.indications:
The various indications are given as following-

 Anorexia 
 Piles

 Abdominal pain 
 Abdominal distension 
 Boosts energy
sections.contraindications:
The conditions when Ashta kshari gutika is not given are as follows- 

 Heartburn 
 Ulcers 
 pregnant females 
 lactating mothers 
 Hypertension 
 Fluid retention 
 No recorded side effects are known but must be taken under medical supervision. 
 Keep away from the reach of children.
sections.dosage:
1-2 tablets twice daily. 
 Anupana 
 Lukewarm water, Curd, Honey. 
 Taste 
 Bitter, Astringent (Tikht, Kashya) 
 Smell 
 Not particular 
 Conclusion 
 Above mentioned formulation is poly herbal prepared according to classics, mainly it has antidiarrheal effects. This preparation should be taken by proper medical supervision as it contains some minerals also with the herbs. It has deepan (Improves appetite), krimighan (worm infestation) and shulaghan (analgesics) properties. It helps in improving digestion, reduces colic pain, indigestion and if any severity you may concern to the physician.

name: Atisaravarana Rasa

sections.introduction: Atisaravarana rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation which is effective in diarrhea. It consists of a mixture of herbs. This formulation is known for their properties like digestive, anti-diarrheal etc.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Hingula ( Ferula assa-foetida ): This herb acts as an appetizer, effective in dyspnea and digest Aama (undigested food), useful in bloating, relieves abdominal pain etc. 
 Shudha Kapura ( Cinnamomum camphora ): It has an anti-inflammatory, anti-bacterial, antifungal and antioxidant properties. This is helpful in digestive problems and kills bacterial growth in the gut. 
 Nagarmotha ( Cyperus scariosus ): This is also known as nut grass. It helps improve digestion because of its deepan and paachan properties. It has anti-diarrheal, antispasmodic and carminative properties. It protects us from various bacterial infections due to its antibacterial property also. 
 Indrayava ( Holarrhena antidysenterica ): This is very effective in diarrhea due to its anti-diarrheal property. It also has anti-microbial, antipyretic properties. It is an essential remedy for gastrointestinal problems. 
 Shudha Afima ( Papaver somniferum ): It has an analgesic effect thus relieves abdominal pain. It also acts as an appetizer. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make fine powder by taking the above ingredients in equal quantity. 
 Mix Afeema with water and give it water frolement once. 
 Prepare tablets of 125mg and store in airtight glass bottles. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Atisaravarana rasa is a very effective formulation in every diarrheal condition. Hingula is very effective in digestive problems. It gives relief, bloating, abdominal pain etc. Afima is very helpful in abdominal pain due to chronic diarrhea. This formulation basically improves digestive power and improves digestion.
sections.indications:
Indigestion 
 Malabsorption 
 Diarrhea (all types of diarrhea) 
 Dyspepsia 
 Ulcerative colitis
sections.dosage:
1 tablet twice a day with plain water after meals.

 Don’t take this medicine without any medical supervision 
 Take precaution while giving to the child

 Shudha Afima ( Papaver somniferum ): It has an analgesic effect thus relieves abdominal pain. It also acts as an appetizer. 
 
 Method of Preparation 
 
 Make fine powder by taking the above ingredients in equal quantity. 
 Mix Afeema with water and give it water frolement once. 
 Prepare tablets of 125mg and store in airtight glass bottles. 
 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Atisaravarana rasa is a very effective formulation in every diarrheal condition. Hingula is very effective in digestive problems. It gives relief, bloating, abdominal pain etc. Afima is very helpful in abdominal pain due to chronic diarrhea. This formulation basically improves digestive power and improves digestion. 
 Indications 
 
 Indigestion 
 Malabsorption 
 Diarrhea (all types of diarrhea) 
 Dyspepsia 
 Ulcerative colitis 
 
 Dosage 
 1 tablet twice a day with plain water after meals. 
 Cautions 
 
 Don’t take it in overdose 
 Don’t take this medicine without any medical supervision 
 Take precaution while giving to the child 
 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Avalgujadi gutika is an Ayurvedic formulation which is made from Elephant dung and urine. This is effective medicine for Kushtha roga (skin diseases).
sections.ingredients:
Hathi ki lida (Elephant’s dung) – 100 kg 
 Hathi mutra (Elephant’s urine) – 13 litre 
 Bakuchi churna (Psoralea corylifolia) – 1200 gms
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Hathi’s Lida – Elephant’s dung is made from a variety of plants and leaves and has more medicinal properties. Inhaling the smoke of the dung will heal the headache and also relieves form toothache. Paste of this dung is helpful in treating skin issues. 
 Hathi Mutra – Elephant’s urine is salty in taste and is effective in worm infestation and various skin disorders. Also it is useful in constipation, urine retention, piles etc.  
 Bakuchi Churna – This powder has a sweet and bitter taste. So it is useful in Pitta disorders. It is effective in skin disorders. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take this dung and properly burn this dung over flames. 
 Take that burnt part for about 12 kg and properly filtrate. 
 Then mix this with urine (13 litres). 
 Then decant this mixture for approximately 24 hours. 
 Next day remove the blackish part. 
 Kept this mixture in stainless steel container. 
 Take that 12 kg elephant’s dung and mix 1/10 part of bakuchi churna and heat over low flame. 
 When urine is dried off then place this medicine in the tray. 
 Make 1-1 gm tablets and kept in glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Avalgujadi gutika is an Ayurvedic formulation and very effective in Vitiligo disease (a skin disorder). The ingredients in this formulation has Astringent property which purifies blood and also pacifies pitta Dosha. This is also used in various skin disorders.
sections.indications:
Vitiligo 
 Leucoderma 
 Psoriasis 

 How To Apply 
 Apply over affected part after abrading the tablet with water twice a day. 
 Cautions 
 Take under medical supervision.

sections.reference_ashtangahrudayam_uttarasthana_: Bilwadi Gutika (Vati) is a tablet, used in Ayurvedic treatment of insect bites, rodent bites, gastro enteritis etc.
sections.ingredients:
10 g of each of:- 

 Bilva – Bael (root) – Aegle marmelos 
 Surasa – Holy Basil – Ocimum sanctum 
 Karanja – Indian Beech (bark / seed) – Pongamia pinnata 
 Nata – Indian valerian (root) – Valeriana wallichi 
 Surahva – Himalayan cedar (bark) – Cedrus deodara 
 Triphala – (Haritaki – Terminalia chebula, Vibhitaki – Terminalia bellirica, Amalaki – Emblica officinalis) 
 Trikatu – (Shunti – Ginger Rhizome – Zingiber officinalis, Maricha – Black pepper – Piper nigrum and Pippali – Long pepper fruit – Piper longum) 
 Nisha – Turmeric (Rhizome) – Curcuma longa 
 Daru Haridra – Tree Turmeric (stem) – Berberis aristata 
 Goat urine – Quantity Sufficient. 

 How to make? 
 The fine powder of above ingredient is triturated with goat urine and tablets are prepared. 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Bilwadi Gutika is an effective Ayurvedic tablets providing healing effects from problems arising due to imbalance of Kapha and Vata Dosha. It helps to curb the acute toxic pathological conditions. 
 It is an Ayurvedic remedy that has ability to counter the toxic effects that arise due to bites from cobra, scorpion, rodents, and insects, spiders, thereby providing relief from painful and inflammatory conditions. 
 This Ayurvedic medicine is also very useful in gastrointestinal conditions, it is suitable in gastro enteritis, providing relief from abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting and reduces the frequency of watery stools. It also helps to improve digestion in case of indigestion and strengthens the digestive power, as well as helpful in dyspepsia, relieving the symptoms of flatulence and indigestion. It is even beneficial in cholera, improves the health of the patient by preventing the diarrheal condition. It is even helpful in managing the condition of Ulcerative Colitis. It is suitable medicine to manage the fever arising, reduces the fatigue. Also found to be useful in certain psychological conditions.

 Fever 
 Bite from insect, cobra, scorpion, rodents, and spiders 
 Psychological condition
sections.dosage: 1 – 2 tablets once or twice a day, before food or as directed by Ayurvedic doctor.

Should use only under medical supervision. Its higher dose may cause burning sensation in stomach.

name: Brihat Mahashankh Vati

sections.overview: Brihat Mahashankh Vati – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction: Born from the crucible of ancient alchemy, Mahashankh Vati is a potent restorative for the internal fire. This classical Ayurvedic formulation marries the mineral strength of purified mercury and conch shell ash with the sharp heat of black pepper and ginger. Each tablet acts as a catalytic key, unlocking stagnant digestion and dispelling the turbulent winds of Vata that cause abdominal distress. Whether extinguishing the burning hunger of Bhasmak or neutralizing acute colic through a precise acidic-alkaline dance, it serves as a reliable guardian of the gut—a timeless remedy for the modern belly’s many woes.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Mercury (Parada) 
 Shuddha Sulfur (Gandhaka) 
 Conch Shell Ash (Shankha Bhasma) 
 The five salts (Pancha Lavana) 
 Tamarind Bark Ash (Imli ka Kshar) 
 Dry Ginger (Sonth) 
 Black Pepper (Kali Mirch) 
 Long Pepper (Pippali) 
 Asafoetida (Hingu) 
 Purified Aconite (Shuddha Vatsanabh) 
 Apamarg Swaras 
 Chitrak kwath 
 Lemon juice
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) 
 In the Ayurvedic tradition, Purified Mercury is known as Yogavahi, a unique “carrier” that adopts and amplifies the medicinal properties of the herbs it is mixed with. It is considered a supreme Rasayana (rejuvenative) that can penetrate deep into the tissues to settle disturbed Doshas. From a modern perspective, when Mercury is processed into a sulfide (Kajjali), it becomes an organometallic catalyst. In conditions like Agnimandya (weak digestive fire), it acts as a metabolic “jumpstart,” stimulating the cellular machinery to restart the production of essential digestive juices and enzymes. 
 2. Shuddha Gandhaka (Purified Sulfur) 
 Sulfur is revered in Ayurveda for its Krimighna (antimicrobial) and blood-purifying properties. It is the “fuel” that sustains the heat of the digestive fire. Modern science recognizes sulfur as a vital component of amino acids and a natural antiseptic that maintains the health of the gut lining. In cases of Visuchika (gastroenteritis-like symptoms with piercing pain), Sulfur works to neutralize harmful pathogens in the intestinal tract, effectively “disinfecting” the gut and preventing the fermentation of undigested food that leads to bloating and toxicity. 
 3. Shankha Bhasma (Conch Shell Ash) 
 This is a potent alkaline preparation used in Ayurveda to pacify aggravated Pitta and treat Grahani (malabsorption). It is essentially a natural form of Calcium Carbonate ($CaCO_3$). In a modern sense, it acts as a rapid-acting antacid that neutralizes the “sourness” or hyperacidity often found in Ajeerna (indigestion). By balancing the pH levels in the stomach, it creates the perfect environment for digestive enzymes to work, stopping the burning sensation and “heavy” feeling that follows a poorly digested meal. 
 4. Pancha Lavana (The Five Salts) 
 The combination of Saindhava, Samudra, Vida, Sauvarchala, and Romaka salts is used to stimulate Ruchi (taste) and facilitate Vata-Anulomana (the downward movement of gas). Modern science views these as essential electrolytes—Sodium, Potassium, and Magnesium—which are critical for maintaining the osmotic balance in the intestines. In Visuchika, where the body loses fluids and salts rapidly, these minerals help prevent dehydration. In Ajeerna, they act as a “softener” for the food mass, ensuring it moves smoothly through the digestive tract. 
 5. Imli Ka Kshar (Tamarind Bark Ash) 
 This alkaline ash is a powerful Chedana agent, meaning it “scrapes away” the sticky, toxic sludge known as Ama that coats the intestinal walls. Chemically, it is rich in Potassium Carbonate ($K_2CO_3$), which helps emulsify fats and break down complex food particles that the body struggles to process. In Agnimandya, where the digestive “channels” are clogged, this ingredient acts like a biological detergent, clearing the path so that nutrients can once again be absorbed effectively by the body. 
 6. Sonth (Dry Ginger) 
 Often called Vishwabheshaja (the Universal Medicine), Dry Ginger is a warm, pungent root that kindles the appetite and digests Ama. Modern research confirms that its active compounds, gingerols and shogaols, significantly increase gastric motility and stimulate the secretion of saliva and bile. This is vital for managing Ajeerna, as it speeds up the time food spends in the stomach, preventing the fermentation and “sour belching” that occur when food sits for too long without being processed. 
 7. Kali Mirch (Black Pepper) 
 Black Pepper is valued for its Tikshna (sharp) quality, which allows it to pierce through thick mucus and stimulate the nerves of the digestive tract. It contains Piperine, a modern “bio-enhancer” that increases the absorption of all other ingredients in the formula. In Agnimandya, Kali Mirch acts as a direct irritant to the gastric mucosa in a helpful way, forcing the stomach to release hydrochloric acid and pepsin, ensuring that even heavy, fatty foods are broken down into simpler forms. 
 8. Pippali (Long Pepper) 
 Pippali is unique because it is a Deepana (appetite-kindler) that also has Rasayana (rejuvenating) properties for the liver and spleen. Modern science notes its ability to stimulate the gallbladder to release bile, which is essential for fat digestion. In the recovery phase of Visuchika, Pippali helps restore the strength of the intestinal villi. It ensures that the digestive fire doesn’t just flare up temporarily but stays consistently strong enough to prevent the return of indigestion. 
 9. Hingu (Asafoetida) 
 Hingu is the ultimate Ayurvedic remedy for Vata disorders, specifically for clearing Adhmana (bloating). It is a powerful carminative and anti-spasmodic. Modern pharmacology identifies it as an intestinal sedative that relaxes the smooth muscles of the gut. This is crucial for managing the “piercing pain” (Shool) associated with Visuchika and Ajeerna. By relaxing the gut and allowing trapped gas to pass freely, Hingu provides almost instant physical relief from the pressure and cramping of a bloated belly. 
 10. Shuddha Vatsanabh (Purified Aconite) 
 Though toxic in its raw state, when purified (Shuddha), Vatsanabh becomes a potent, fast-acting medicine that spreads through the body like “lightning.” Ayurveda uses it to treat acute pain and coldness. Modern studies show that in micro-doses, it acts on the peripheral nervous system to block pain signals. In Visuchika, where the patient may experience cold sweats and intense abdominal agony, Vatsanabh acts as a biological “reset,” calming the nervous system and stopping the acute pain in its tracks. 
 11. Apamarg Swaras (Prickly Chaff Flower Juice) 
 The juice of Apamarg is bitter and pungent, used in Ayurveda to “break” the accumulation of Kapha and Ama. It has a modern reputation as a natural diuretic and digestive stimulant. In the context of Agnimandya, it helps flush out metabolic waste through the kidneys while simultaneously alerting the stomach to prepare for food. It acts as a cleansing agent that ensures the “engine” of the stomach is clean before the next meal is added. 
 12. Chitrak Kwath (Leadwort Decoction) 
 Chitrak is considered the most powerful herb for “stoking” the digestive fire without aggravating Pitta excessively. Its active chemical, Plumbagin, is a known stimulant for the digestive enzymes like pepsin and trypsin. In managing Ajeerna, Chitrak acts like the “bellows” to a fire—it takes a dying, weak flame and turns it into a robust heat source capable of incinerating even the most stubborn, undigested food particles remaining in the stomach. 
 13. Lemon Juice (Nimbu Swaras) 
 Lemon juice is the acidic medium that brings this entire formula to life. In Ayurveda, its sour taste (Amla Rasa) is the primary stimulant for the salivary glands and the stomach’s protective lining. Modern science highlights its Citric Acid content, which helps acidify the stomach to trigger the digestion of proteins. In this formula, the acid reacts with the alkaline salts (Kshars and Lavanas) to create a “fizzing” action that mechanically breaks up gas bubbles and neutralizes toxins, providing the quick relief known as “belching peace” in Ajeerna. 
 Method Of Preparation 

 First, prepare a Kajjali (black sulfide of mercury) by processing Mercury and Sulfur together. 
 Add the Shankha Bhasma and Vatsanabh to this mixture and grind thoroughly. 
 Then, add all remaining ingredients except for the Asafoetida. 
 Grind well (mardan) and subject the mixture to Bhavana (levigation/infusion) with the juice or decoction of Apamarg, followed by the decoction of Chitrak, and finally, Lemon juice. 
 Continue the lemon juice Bhavana until the entire mixture attains an acidic taste (Amla Rasa). 
 Once the grinding is complete, mix the Asafoetida into a little lemon juice and add it to the mixture. 
 Grind quickly and thoroughly, then roll into tablets of 2 Ratti (approx. 250mg) each. 
 Dry them in the shade. 

 Note 
 Asafoetida is added at the end to prevent its volatile aroma and potency from dissipating during prolonged grinding and drying. Adding it earlier reduces the tablet’s efficacy. 
 Variations In Classical Texts 
 According to the Bhaishajya Ratnavali, if Iron Ash (Loha Bhasma) and Tin Ash (Vang Bhasma) are added to this recipe, it is called Mahashankh Vati. However, many manufacturers and physicians prepare and sell the version without these ashes under the same name. In the text Rasendra Saar Sangrah, the version without Iron and Tin ashes is referred to as Brihat Mahashankh Vati.
sections.indications:
This tablet quickly ignites the digestive fire (Jatharagni). 
 It treats Bhasmak Roga (excessive hunger/hyper-metabolism) and aids in the rapid digestion of heavy meals. 
 It is beneficial for all types of indigestion (Ajirna), fever, abdominal tumors (Gulma), anemia (Pandu), skin diseases (Kushtha), colic pain (Shool), diabetes/urinary disorders (Prameh), gout (Vatarakta), and severe inflammation (Mahashoth). 
 It destroys excess Vata, Pitta, and Kapha and treats piles, lethargy, anorexia, and dysentery. 

 Clinical Use 
 1. Abdominal Pain Gas 
 It provides immediate relief in abdominal colic and gas. When gas is trapped in the abdomen causing distress, this tablet provides instant calm. 
 2. Diarrhea With Vata 
 In cases of diarrhea where watery stools are passed with gas, 2 to 4 Ratti of this medicine mixed with an equal part of Sajjikhar or Soda Bi carb provides relief. 
 It has been observed that if abdominal pain is accompanied by a Pitta imbalance, adding Soda Bi carb creates a chemical “neutralization” when it reacts with the acidic components of the tablet, leading to immediate belching, passing of gas, and relief. 
 3. Constipation 
 If constipation is the primary symptom, it is better to use the tablet alone rather than adding alkaline salts (Kshar). For acute pain, grinding the tablet into a fine powder before administration is more effective. A whole tablet dissolves slowly in the stomach, whereas the powder acts immediately on the pain. 
 4. Intestinal Colic 
 For severe pain caused by Vata blockage in the small or large intestine, taking two tablets (4 Ratti) in powdered form with water provides quick relief. If the pain doesn’t subside in an hour, a second dose can be given. 
 5. Joint Pain Due To Indigestion 
 In elderly patients, “Am-dosha” (toxins from undigested food) can cause knee pain and stiffness. In such cases, one dose every 4 hours (3-4 times a day) is beneficial. 
 6. Appendicitis (Upantra Shoth) 
 This medicine is excellent for appendicitis. During acute pain, instead of modern painkillers, a powdered dose of Brihat Mahashankh Vati can control the pain. Continuing this for 21 to 45 days can prevent recurrence. If the patient also suffers from constipation, Kumaryasava should be taken twice a day after meals. The total treatment duration should be 30 to 40 days for a permanent recovery.
sections.dosage_2_to_4_ratti_approx_250mg_to_500m:
Anupana (Vehicle): Normal water or lukewarm water. 

 Conclusion 
 In conclusion, Mahashankh Vati stands as a sophisticated masterpiece of Ayurvedic bio-chemistry, bridging the gap between elemental minerals and potent botanicals. By integrating the catalytic power of purified Mercury and Sulfur with the alkaline stability of Conch shell and the thermal intensity of the “Three Peppers,” it provides a multi-dimensional approach to gut health. It doesn’t merely mask symptoms; it restores the biological rhythm of the digestive fire (Agni). Whether neutralizing the acidic chaos of Ajeerna or calming the spastic agony of Visuchika, this formulation remains a timeless, reliable anchor for metabolic balance and systemic vitality.

 Tamarind Bark Ash (Imli ka Kshar) 
 Dry Ginger (Sonth) 
 Black Pepper (Kali Mirch) 
 Long Pepper (Pippali) 
 Asafoetida (Hingu) 
 Purified Aconite (Shuddha Vatsanabh) 
 Apamarg Swaras 
 Chitrak kwath 
 Lemon juice 
 
 
 Description Of Ingredients 
 1. Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) 
 In the Ayurvedic tradition, Purified Mercury is known as Yogavahi, a unique “carrier” that adopts and amplifies the medicinal properties of the herbs it is mixed with. It is considered a supreme Rasayana (rejuvenative) that can penetrate deep into the tissues to settle disturbed Doshas. From a modern perspective, when Mercury is processed into a sulfide (Kajjali), it becomes an organometallic catalyst. In conditions like Agnimandya (weak digestive fire), it acts as a metabolic “jumpstart,” stimulating the cellular machinery to restart the production of essential digestive juices and enzymes. 
 2. Shuddha Gandhaka (Purified Sulfur) 
 Sulfur is revered in Ayurveda for its Krimighna (antimicrobial) and blood-purifying properties. It is the “fuel” that sustains the heat of the digestive fire. Modern science recognizes sulfur as a vital component of amino acids and a natural antiseptic that maintains the health of the gut lining. In cases of Visuchika (gastroenteritis-like symptoms with piercing pain), Sulfur works to neutralize harmful pathogens in the intestinal tract, effectively “disinfecting” the gut and preventing the fermentation of undigested food that leads to bloating and toxicity. 
 3. Shankha Bhasma (Conch Shell Ash) 
 This is a potent alkaline preparation used in Ayurveda to pacify aggravated Pitta and treat Grahani (malabsorption). It is essentially a natural form of Calcium Carbonate ($CaCO_3$). In a modern sense, it acts as a rapid-acting antacid that neutralizes the “sourness” or hyperacidity often found in Ajeerna (indigestion). By balancing the pH levels in the stomach, it creates the perfect environment for digestive enzymes to work, stopping the burning sensation and “heavy” feeling that follows a poorly digested meal. 
 4. Pancha Lavana (The Five Salts) 
 The combination of Saindhava, Samudra, Vida, Sauvarchala, and Romaka salts is used to stimulate Ruchi (taste) and facilitate Vata-Anulomana (the downward movement of gas). Modern science views these as essential electrolytes—Sodium, Potassium, and Magnesium—which are critical for maintaining the osmotic balance in the intestines. In Visuchika, where the body loses fluids and salts rapidly, these minerals help prevent dehydration. In Ajeerna, they act as a “softener” for the food mass, ensuring it moves smoothly through the digestive tract. 
 5. Imli Ka Kshar (Tamarind Bark Ash) 
 This alkaline ash is a powerful Chedana agent, meaning it “scrapes away” the sticky, toxic sludge known as Ama that coats the intestinal walls. Chemically, it is rich in Potassium Carbonate ($K_2CO_3$), which helps emulsify fats and break down complex food particles that the body struggles to process. In Agnimandya, where the digestive “channels” are clogged, this ingredient acts like a biological detergent, clearing the path so that nutrients can once again be absorbed effectively by the body. 
 6. Sonth (Dry Ginger) 
 Often called Vishwabheshaja (the Universal Medicine), Dry Ginger is a warm, pungent root that kindles the appetite and digests Ama. Modern research confirms that its active compounds, gingerols and shogaols, significantly increase gastric motility and stimulate the secretion of saliva and bile. This is vital for managing Ajeerna, as it speeds up the time food spends in the stomach, preventing the fermentation and “sour belching” that occur when food sits for too long without being processed. 
 7. Kali Mirch (Black Pepper) 
 Black Pepper is valued for its Tikshna (sharp) quality, which allows it to pierce through thick mucus and stimulate the nerves of the digestive tract. It contains Piperine, a modern “bio-enhancer” that increases the absorption of all other ingredients in the formula. In Agnimandya, Kali Mirch acts as a direct irritant to the gastric mucosa in a helpful way, forcing the stomach to release hydrochloric acid and pepsin, ensuring that even heavy, fatty foods are broken down into simpler forms. 
 8. Pippali (Long Pepper) 
 Pippali is unique because it is a Deepana (appetite-kindler) that also has Rasayana (rejuvenating) properties for the liver and spleen. Modern science notes its ability to stimulate the gallbladder to release bile, which is essential for fat digestion. In the recovery phase of Visuchika, Pippali helps restore the strength of the intestinal villi. It ensures that the digestive fire doesn’t just flare up temporarily but stays consistently strong enough to prevent the return of indigestion. 
 9. Hingu (Asafoetida) 
 Hingu is the ultimate Ayurvedic remedy for Vata disorders, specifically for clearing Adhmana (bloating). It is a powerful carminative and anti-spasmodic. Modern pharmacology identifies it as an intestinal sedative that relaxes the smooth muscles of the gut. This is crucial for managing the “piercing pain” (Shool) associated with Visuchika and Ajeerna. By relaxing the gut and allowing trapped gas to pass freely, Hingu provides almost instant physical relief from the pressure and cramping of a bloated belly. 
 10. Shuddha Vatsanabh (Purified Aconite) 
 Though toxic in its raw state, when purified (Shuddha), Vatsanabh becomes a potent, fast-acting medicine that spreads through the body like “lightning.” Ayurveda uses it to treat acute pain and coldness. Modern studies show that in micro-doses, it acts on the peripheral nervous system to block pain signals. In Visuchika, where the patient may experience cold sweats and intense abdominal agony, Vatsanabh acts as a biological “reset,” calming the nervous system and stopping the acute pain in its tracks. 
 11. Apamarg Swaras (Prickly Chaff Flower Juice) 
 The juice of Apamarg is bitter and pungent, used in Ayurveda to “break” the accumulation of Kapha and Ama. It has a modern reputation as a natural diuretic and digestive stimulant. In the context of Agnimandya, it helps flush out metabolic waste through the kidneys while simultaneously alerting the stomach to prepare for food. It acts as a cleansing agent that ensures the “engine” of the stomach is clean before the next meal is added. 
 12. Chitrak Kwath (Leadwort Decoction) 
 Chitrak is considered the most powerful herb for “stoking” the digestive fire without aggravating Pitta excessively. Its active chemical, Plumbagin, is a known stimulant for the digestive enzymes like pepsin and trypsin. In managing Ajeerna, Chitrak acts like the “bellows” to a fire—it takes a dying, weak flame and turns it into a robust heat source capable of incinerating even the most stubborn, undigested food particles remaining in the stomach. 
 13. Lemon Juice (Nimbu Swaras) 
 Lemon juice is the acidic medium that brings this entire formula to life. In Ayurveda, its sour taste (Amla Rasa) is the primary stimulant for the salivary glands and the stomach’s protective lining. Modern science highlights its Citric Acid content, which helps acidify the stomach to trigger the digestion of proteins. In this formula, the acid reacts with the alkaline salts (Kshars and Lavanas) to create a “fizzing” action that mechanically breaks up gas bubbles and neutralizes toxins, providing the quick relief known as “belching peace” in Ajeerna. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 
 First, prepare a Kajjali (black sulfide of mercury) by processing Mercury and Sulfur together. 
 Add the Shankha Bhasma and Vatsanabh to this mixture and grind thoroughly. 
 Then, add all remaining ingredients except for the Asafoetida. 
 Grind well (mardan) and subject the mixture to Bhavana (levigation/infusion) with the juice or decoction of Apamarg, followed by the decoction of Chitrak, and finally, Lemon juice. 
 Continue the lemon juice Bhavana until the entire mixture attains an acidic taste (Amla Rasa). 
 Once the grinding is complete, mix the Asafoetida into a little lemon juice and add it to the mixture. 
 Grind quickly and thoroughly, then roll into tablets of 2 Ratti (approx. 250mg) each. 
 Dry them in the shade. 
 
 Note 
 Asafoetida is added at the end to prevent its volatile aroma and potency from dissipating during prolonged grinding and drying. Adding it earlier reduces the tablet’s efficacy. 
 Variations In Classical Texts 
 According to the Bhaishajya Ratnavali, if Iron Ash (Loha Bhasma) and Tin Ash (Vang Bhasma) are added to this recipe, it is called Mahashankh Vati. However, many manufacturers and physicians prepare and sell the version without these ashes under the same name. In the text Rasendra Saar Sangrah, the version without Iron and Tin ashes is referred to as Brihat Mahashankh Vati.

 This tablet quickly ignites the digestive fire (Jatharagni). 
 It treats Bhasmak Roga (excessive hunger/hyper-metabolism) and aids in the rapid digestion of heavy meals.

 Vida lavan- It improves skin conditions like rashes, rosacea, eczema and has an anti-inflammatory, antibacterial effect. 
 Suvarchala- It acts as a cleanser for skin, unclog pores and removes dirt.

 Danti- It helps in wound healing as it has an antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effect. It reduces swelling, edema and skin allergies. 
 Twak- It is a potent herb used for repairing damaged tissues and manages various skin infections. 
 Patar- It helps in preventing dandruff, boils and different types of fungal infections. 
 Ela- It heals breakouts and purifies blood so manages skin complexion, blemishes. 
 Vanshlochan- The extract of this plant is used for strengthening the body and helpful in conditions pertaining to skin, hairs and nails (cosmetic concern). 
 Loha bhasma (24 grams) – it is very helpful in anaemia and improves general weakness. It improves skin texture, complexion. 
 Sita (Sugar) – It exfoliates skin and removes dead skin. It rejuvenates skin pores and it is rich in elastin and collagen. 
 Shilajit- It has a major anti-ageing property of skin as it repairs cell damage. It nourishes skin and prevents inflammation. 
 Guggulu- It improves itching, redness, skin discoloration. It is helpful in managing psoriasis, eczema like inflammatory conditions. 

 Clinical Significance Of Chandraprabha Vati In Skin Disorders 

 According to the various textbooks, Chandraprabha vati is mentioned for different types of skin disorders such as vicharchika (psoriasis) and kustha roga, its types (leprosy disease). 
 Chandraprabha vati works on all three dosha (vata, pitta and kapha) as when there is predominance of vata so it causes dry, rough, scaly skin (rukash, khara twacha). 
 When there is predominance of pitta dosha it causes burning sensation, hot flushes, etc. (ushma, daha, davthu) and when there is vitiation of kapha dosha it causes itching, swelling (kandu, shoath) like symptoms. 
 The cause behind kustha like skin disorders mentioned is ayurveda are as below- 

 Kaleda (Putrefaction/ suppuration) 
 Rakta Dushti (Impure blood) 
 Krimi (Worm infestation) 

 So in classics Chandraprabha vati is considered “uttam kaleda ghaan” which means best medicine to prevent from putrefaction . 
 This tablet formulation also has the property of blood purifying due to the presence of some ingredients like haridra (Curcuma longa ), daru haridra (Berberis aristata ), swaran makshika (purified copper iron sulphate), etc. 
 It also possesses krimighna property (prevent from worm infestations) due to the presence of musta ( Cyperus rotundus ), guduchi ( Tinospora cordifolia), dhanyaka (Coriander ), ativisha ( Aconitum heterophyllum), trivrit ( Operculenis terpenthum ), vidanga ( Emblica ribes ) and chitraka (Plumbago Zeylanica) in its composition. 
 This formulation has great properties against suppuration and worm infestation so it is very useful in various types of skin diseases associated with discharge, itching, redness, worms, etc. 
 As it has anti-inflammatory properties it prevents all types of rashes, boils, acne or any marks. It reduces edematous swelling or any growth in the body. 
 It has great exfoliating and cleansing properties so it helps in removing dead skin and it makes it clear, glowing. It also acts as antiseptic for dermis and prevents all infections with wound healing. 
 As there is predominance of pitta in skin diseases and this tablet is of cold potency so it acts very efficiently in skin related issues. 

 Method Of Preparation 
 The steps for the preparation of Chandraprabha vati are given as following- 

 Firstly collect all the drugs mentioned above and wash them properly. 
 All the plant origin drugs are dried and made into fine powders. 
 Now the described quantity of base drugs are taken, which are sugar and guggulu in a clean stainless steel vessel and mix them properly. 
 Then the required quantity of water is added into the vessel and heated over mild flame with continuous stirring. 
 Once the syrup-like consistency is formed of solution then add fine powder of drugs in small quantities. 
 Stir the solution well till desirable consistency is obtained. 
 Then the mass of drugs is rolled up into vati/ pills according to desired size and shape. 
 At last prepared pills are dried in shade and stored in a clean airtight glass container.
