sections.introduction: ĀgantukaJvara (exogenous fever) is described in Ayurveda as a type of fever arising from external factors rather than internal doṣic imbalance. Classical texts explain that trauma (abhighāta), poison (viṣa), infection by organisms (bhūta–krimi), seasonal influences, or sudden environmental changes can initiate Agantuj fever. These external insults first disturb the body’s normal equilibrium and subsequently vitiate Vāta, Pitta, and Kapha, leading to the manifestation of fever. Ayurveda emphasizes that although the origin is external, timely management should address both the causative factor and the secondary doṣic involvement to prevent complications and progression into sannipātika conditions. So In this article we will discuss one such formulation which works wonderfully in managing Sannipataj fevers i.eKesharadivati. Let’s discuss it in detail!
sections.ingredients:
Saffron (Keshar)-1 Tola 
 Nutmeg (Jayaphala)- 1 Tola 
 Mace (Javitri) – 1 Tola 
 Clove (Lavanga)- 1 Tola 
 PīppalaMūla (Piper longum)- 1 Tola 
 Musk (Kastūrī)- 3 masha
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Saffron (Kesar – Crocus sativus) 
 Kesar possesses UṣṇaVīrya (hot potency) and Tikta–Madhura Rasa, helping to pacify Kapha and Vāta involved in chronic or irregular fevers. It supports Āma-pācana (metabolic toxin digestion) and improves circulation, which assists in restoring normal body temperature. Kesar is also described as Hṛdya and Medhya, helping in post-febrile weakness. 
 2. Nutmeg (Jāyaphala – Myristicafragrans) 
 Jāyaphala is Uṣṇa, Laghu and Grahī, making it useful in fevers associated with digestive impairment and diarrhea. It aids in Agni dīpana and Āmaśoṣaṇa, helping reduce fever caused by indigestion. Its Vāta-Kaphaśāmaka action supports relief from body ache and chills during fever. 
 3. Mace (Jāvitri – Myristicafragrans Aril) 
 Jāvitri enhances Jatharagni and assists in the digestion of Āma, a key pathological factor in Jvara. Its UṣṇaVīrya helps counter cold-type fevers and supports sweating. Classical texts describe it as Vāta-Kapha hara, useful in recurrent or lingering fevers. 
 4. Clove (Lavaṅga – Syzygiumaromaticum) 
 Lavaṅga acts as a Dīpana–Pācana dravya, helping clear Āma from the system. Its Uṣṇa and Tikṣṇa properties assist in relieving chills, headache, and heaviness seen in febrile states. It also supports respiratory comfort in fevers associated with cough and congestion. 
 5. Pippalīmūla (Piper Longum Root) 
 Pippalīmūla is a classical Jvaraghna herb known for regulating Vāta-Kapha-dominant fevers. It strengthens Agni, reduces abdominal distension, and helps break the fever cycle caused by metabolic imbalance. Its action on Prāṇavahasrotas supports breathing comfort during fever. 
 6. Musk (Kastūrī) 
 Kastūrī is described as Uṣṇa, Tikṣṇa and Sūkṣma, enabling it to act quickly in severe or sudden fevers. Classical usage highlights its role in restoring consciousness and circulation during high-grade fevers. It helps remove Srotorodha (channel obstruction) and supports rapid systemic response. 
 7. Rasamanikya (Purified Arsenic Sulfide) 
 Rasamanikya is traditionally used in Viṣama and SannipātajaJvara after proper purification. It exhibits Kapha-Vātaśāmaka action and supports elimination of deeply lodged Āma and Doṣic toxins. Classical Rasashastra texts emphasize its potency in stubborn and recurrent fevers when administered judiciously. 
 8. Abhraka Bhasma (Purified Incinerated Mica) 
 AbhrakaBhasma acts as a Rasāyana and supports Dhātu-poshana during prolonged or chronic fevers. It enhances Agni at both digestive and tissue levels, helping recovery from fever-induced weakness. Classical texts describe its utility in JīrṇaJvara and fever with respiratory involvement. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 All the ingredients should be finely powdered and triturated with the juice of betel leaves (Nāgar Bela ke Pān) and ginger juice (Ādraka Svarasa) for 1–1 day each and Prepare pills of medium size.
sections.indications_and_clinical_use: KesharādiVati is highly effective in delirious fevers, sannipātika fever, Postpartum fevers and acute febrile conditions. When the patient becomes restless, delirious, experiences confusion, tearing of clothes, intense shivering, or tremors, this formulation acts swiftly like an antidote. Just as HingukarpūraVaṭī is beneficial in delirium, this formulation also produces rapid and effective results in such conditions.
sections.dosage:
1 to 2 pills, administered every 1–2 hours 2 or 3 times a day. 
 Conclusion 
 ĀgantukaJvara demands prompt and decisive management, as externally induced fevers can rapidly disturb all three doṣas and progress toward severe or delirious states. Ayurveda emphasizes addressing both the external causative factor and the resulting doṣic imbalance to prevent complications. Classical formulations such as KesharādiVaṭī are described for acute, agitated, and sannipātika presentations of fever, where restlessness, confusion, or delirium are prominent. By acting swiftly on the disturbed doṣas and supporting the body during critical stages, KesharādiVaṭī reflects the precision of Ayurvedic therapeutics in managing complex febrile conditions while preserving the integrity of vital systems.

sections.introduction: Krimighatini gutika is a potent Ayurvedic medicine and it is used in the treatment of Krimi roga (Worm infestation). It is a herbo-mineral composition.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha kupilu Churna  (Purified Strychnos nuxvomica ) – 60 gm 
 Palash Beej Churna ( Butea monosperma ) – 50 gm 
 Vidanga Churna ( Embelia ribes ) – 40 gm 
 Ajmoda ( Apium graveolens ) – 30 gm 
 Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulphur) – 20 gm 
 Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) – 10 gm
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Kupilu Churna – This is a purified form of Kuchila. This is a poisonous herb and used as a medicine after the detoxification process. This is a famous Ayurvedic herb. It balances vata and kapha dosha but increases pitta dosha. Action of this herb is krimi hara (worm infestation), shwashara (useful in respiratory disorders), gulmahara (useful in abdominal problems) etc. 
 Palash Beej Churna – This herb is also known as Dhak, Palas, Flame of the forest etc. It has an anthelmintic properties which is used in the treatment of intestinal worm infestation. This herb also has antimicrobial and antifungal properties. It pacifies vata dosha and somewhat pitta dosha. 
 Vidanga Churna – This is an effective herb which is used in the treatment of worm infestation. It also helps in controlling vomiting, nausea. This herb is beneficial in indigestion, bloating and flatulence due to its hot potency. It also manages constipation due to its rechana (Laxative) property. 
 Ajmoda – This is one of the popular Indian spices which is used in improving digestion strength. It is widely used for its stimulant, antispasmodic (Relieves abdominal pain) properties. This is also helpful in treating urinary diseases. It pacifies vata and kapha dosha. It detoxifies the body. 
 Shuddha Gandhak – It is sulphur which is used in a pure form. It is first detoxified and then used in Ayurvedic medicines as a main ingredient. It purifies Blood and helps in treating blood related disorders. It improves digestion power and stimulates appetite. It also helps in preventing intestinal worm infestations. 
 Shuddha Parada – It is a main ingredient used in Ayurvedic formulations because it enhances the strength of the other herbs in an Ayurvedic medicine. It also provides strength of the body. It acts as a Rasayan and hence useful in all disorders. It pacifies all three dosha. It also helps in digesting the Aama (Endotoxins). 

 Method of Preparation 

 First of all in a Kharal yantra, prepare a kajjali from Parada and Gandhak. 
 Then add rest of the ingredients in this kajjali and properly mixes it. 
 After then again properly mixes it with madhu (Honey). 
 Make 250 mg tablet and dry them under the shadow. 
 Kept these tablets in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Krimighatini gutika is a classical ayurvedic formulation. It is mainly used in the treatment of krimi roga (Worm infestation). The ingredients are also helpful in managing abdominal diseases. They are useful in improving digestion power. The herb vidanga helps in detoxifying the body as it has a laxative effect and also it is very beneficial in krimi roga.

sections.description_of_ingredients:

 Take all the ingredients in same quantity.

sections.introduction: In the landscape of Ayurvedic clinical medicine, Pandu (anemia) is viewed as a systemic metabolic failure where the Pitta dosha becomes aggravated, leading to the “fading” of the body’s natural luster and vitality. Ksharadi Mandur offers a targeted, high-potency solution for this condition, particularly when the root cause involves intestinal toxicity or “soil-eating” habits. By blending Mandur Bhasma (Iron Calx) with sharp, alkaline (Kshariya) herbs and digestive stimulants, this formulation acts as an internal cleanser that restores the intestinal environment. It ensures that iron is not just ingested, but effectively synthesized into healthy Rakta Dhatu, providing a rapid recovery from hematological depletion.Let’s discuss it in detail!
sections.ingredients:
Take equal parts of these 6 ingredients: 

 Rock Salt (Sendha Namak): Halite / Sodium Chloride (Natural Mineral) 

 Elua (Aloe Extract / Musabbar): Aloe barbadensis 

 Sunthi (Dry Ginger): Zingiber officinale 

 Maricha (Black Pepper): Piper nigrum 

 Pippali (Long Pepper): Piper longum 

 Mandur Bhasma: Ferroso-ferric Oxide (Processed/Incinerated Iron Ore)
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Sendha Namak (Rock Salt) 
 In Ayurveda, Saindhava Lavana is the only salt considered Chakshushya (beneficial for the eyes) and Hridya (beneficial for the heart). Unlike common salt, it is cooling in nature and balances all three Doshas. It acts as a potent Deepana (appetizer) and Pachana (digestive) agent, ensuring that the heavy mineral components of the formulation do not cause bloating or metabolic stagnation. It supports the secretion of hydrochloric acid in the stomach, creating an acidic environment that is essential for efficient mineral absorption and digestive function. 

 2. Elua (Aloe Extract / Musabbar) 
 Elua is the dried, concentrated juice of Aloe vera (Aloe barbadensis). It is regarded as a powerful Rechana (purgative) and Pleeha-Yakrit Uttejaka (liver and spleen stimulant). Traditionally, it is used to clear intestinal congestion, remove accumulated toxins, and support healthy liver and spleen function. By promoting intestinal cleansing and improving digestive efficiency, it helps create favorable conditions for the absorption of nutrients and supports overall metabolic health. 

 3. Sunthi (Dry Ginger) 
 Sunthi (Zingiber officinale) is celebrated as Agni-mukha (the face of digestive fire). Although pungent in taste, it possesses a sweet post-digestive effect (Madhura Vipaka), making it suitable for long-term use. It helps clear Ama (undigested metabolic waste) and supports the healthy transformation of nutrients. Modern studies highlight ginger’s ability to enhance gastrointestinal motility, stimulate bile secretion, and support digestive comfort. It helps prevent heaviness after meals and promotes efficient digestion and nutrient utilization. 

 4. Maricha (Black Pepper) 
 Maricha (Piper nigrum) is a sharp and penetrating herb known for its Srotovishodhana (channel-cleansing) properties. It helps remove accumulated Kapha and Ama from the digestive tract, supporting optimal nutrient absorption. Its active alkaloid, piperine, is widely recognized for enhancing the bioavailability of nutrients and herbal compounds. By stimulating digestive activity and thermogenesis, Maricha helps improve metabolism and ensures more efficient utilization of the formulation’s ingredients. 

 5. Pippali (Long Pepper) 
 Pippali (Piper longum) is a renowned Rasayana (rejuvenative) herb that supports digestion, metabolism, and tissue nourishment. Unlike many pungent herbs, it is considered suitable for prolonged use due to its balanced post-digestive effect. Traditionally, it is used to strengthen digestive fire, improve nutrient assimilation, and support liver function. Modern research suggests hepatoprotective properties, making it valuable for maintaining healthy metabolic processes and overall vitality. 

 6. Mandur Bhasma (Ferroso-ferric Oxide) 
 Mandur Bhasma is a classical Ayurvedic preparation of purified and incinerated iron. Traditional Ayurvedic texts describe it as Lahu (light) and Tikshna (penetrating), allowing it to reach deep tissues and support blood and liver health. The repeated purification and incineration process transforms the material into a fine, highly processed form that is intended to improve digestibility and assimilation. Mandur Bhasma has historically been used in formulations designed to support healthy blood formation, vitality, and overall metabolic strength. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Mix all ingredients and grind them (Kharal) with Aloe Vera juice for 3 days. Prepare tablets of 2-2 Ratti (approx. 250mg) 


 Benefits 

 It is traditionally described as beneficial in Mitti-bhakshaj Pandu (anemia associated with the habit of eating soil) as well as other forms of Pandu (anemia), helping to improve blood quality and restore strength. 

 It acts as an intestinal cleanser and is useful in conditions associated with the accumulation of Ama (undigested toxins), waste materials, soil, and other harmful substances within the digestive tract. 

 It supports the elimination of accumulated impurities from the intestines and helps improve digestive and absorptive functions. 

 It is traditionally administered in patients whose abdomen has become enlarged, distended, or feels hard on pressure, helping to relieve abdominal discomfort and improve digestive health. 


 Dietary Regimen 

 Curd with rice or buttermilk with rice should be given as the recommended diet during treatment. 

 If swelling (Shoth) is present, salt should be avoided in the diet. 

 If fever is present, the patient should be maintained on a light diet consisting of milk and rice. 

 Note: These are potent Ayurvedic formulations containing processed metals (Bhasma). They should only be consumed under the strict supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic physician.
sections.dosage:
1 to 3 tablets, twice a day, with cow urine or water. 

 Conclusion 
 At last we can say that Ksharadi Mandur represents a specialized clinical solution for Pandu (anemia), particularly when rooted in chronic intestinal stagnation or “Mitti-bhakshaj” (Pica-related) iron deficiency. Its unique strength lies in the synergy between nanoparticulate Mandur Bhasma and potent Kshariya (alkaline) digestive stimulants like Elua and Saindhava Lavana. This combination does not merely supplement iron; it actively “scrapes” the intestinal villi, clearing metabolic toxins (Ama) that obstruct nutrient uptake. By restoring hepatic efficiency and improving the intestinal environment, Ksharadi Mandur ensures that iron is synthesized effectively into healthy Rakta Dhatu, providing a rapid and sustainable recovery from systemic hematological depletion.

name: Kshargutika

sections.introduction: Kshargutika is an Ayurvedic formulation. This is a classical remedy used in the treatment of every throat and oral diseases.
sections.ingredients:
Pippali ( Piper nigrum ) 
 Chavya ( Piper chava ) 
 Chitrakmool ( Plumbago zeylanica ) 
 Shunthi ( Zingiber officinale ) 
 Talishpatra ( Abies webbiana ) 
 Choti Elaichi ( Elettaria cardamomum ) 
 Dalchini ( Cinnamomum verum ) 
 Palash Kshar ( Butea monosperma ) 
 Ghantapatlakshar (Alkali of Stereospermum suaveolens ) 
 Yavakshar ( Hordeum vulgare ) 
 Purana Gud (Old jaggery)
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Pippali – This is an effective herb for throat infections. It is helpful in sore throat, tonsillitis, stomatitis, mouth ulcers. This herb is also effective in indigestion, anorexia, vomiting etc. 
 Chavya – This herb is useful in anorexia, constipation, indigestion, abdominal pain, bloating etc. This is also effective in throat infections. 
 Chitrakmool – The roots of this herb are very beneficial in a variety of diseases. This is one of the good digestive and carminative herbs used in the treatment of indigestion, bloating, flatulence etc. This herb is also beneficial in mouth problems. It has an expectorant effect also. 
 Shunthi – This is one of the best ingredients in throat infections. It acts as an expectorant and helps in cough and cold. It is a good appetizer and digestant. 
 Talishpatra – It is an Ayurvedic medicinal plant. Its leaves are used in the treatment of respiratory diseases such as cough, cold, asthma, chronic bronchitis and upper respiratory infections. 
 Choti Elaichi – It is used in the treatment of throat infections, mouth ulcers, indigestion etc. It has a strong, unique taste and extensively soothing aroma. This is useful in dyspnea, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting and used to expel the phlegm out of the body. 
 Dalchini – This is an aromatic spice obtained from the bark of severe trees of the cinnamon. It helps to maintain the blood sugar level, control, vomiting, reduces breathlessness etc. It is also used in common cold, cough and tonsillitis. 
 Palash Kshar – This is an alkaline Ayurvedic medicine in powder from. It is used in the treatment of kidney, spleen and liver disorders. It is a natural diuretic. It is used in Ayurvedic treatment for chronic fever, oedema, malabsorption syndrome etc. 
 Ghantapatlakshar – It has anti-inflammatory action and is used over various inflammations. It is useful in balancing Vata dosha. It is also helpful in piles and acts as a blood purifier. 
 Yavakshar – It is an Ayurvedic medicine, used in treating urinary diseases, abdominal pain, bloating etc. This alkali is prepared from the whole plant of barley. It is beneficial in throat obstruction, coughing etc. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all these ingredients in equal quantity (1 part each). 
 Make a fine powder from all the ingredients. 
 Take gud and little water in a stainless steel container and make sugar syrup over flames. 
 When this preparation becomes very thick then adds all the above mentioned ingredients in this sugar syrup. 
 Make a tablet like a size of ber (Indian jujube) and cover it with Erandapatra (leaves of Ricinus communis) and keep this formulation under the tree (Ghantapatla tree) for 1 week. 
 After 1 week keep this in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Kshargutika is a classical Ayurvedic formulation. It is used in the treatment of Throat infections. This formulation shows great effect in chronic cough. It is useful in balancing kapha dosha. The ingredients are beneficial in sore throat, tonsillitis, mouth ulcers, bad breath, pharyngitis etc.

 Mouth ulcers 
 Stomatitis
sections.dosage:
It should be taken sublingually 2- 3 times a day (2- 3 tablets). 
 Cautions 
 It should be taken under medical advise. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Hingula – This is a preparation of Mercury. This is used in the treatment of Inflammation, digestive problems, respiratory problems etc. This is used in ayurvedic preparation to increase the strength of other ingredients. 
 Lavang Churna – This is an Ayurvedic medicine in powder form. It is used in the treatment of digestive problems such as diarrhea, bloating, abdominal pain etc. It is also helpful in subsiding inflammation in the body. It balances Vata and Kapha dosha. 
 Shuddha Afeem – It has a digestive and appetizer action. This ingredient improves digestion power and provides strength to the body. This has an analgesic effect too, so used in mild to moderate pain. 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – This is a poisonous herb and used in a variety of diseases after the purification process. This herb has anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic properties. It is also used in fever, pain. 
 Jaiphal – This is capable of digestive problems. It is also known as nutmeg. It is useful in clearing the throat, useful in relieving bloating, flatulence and abdominal pain. Jaiphal is also helpful in inflammation. 
 Shuddha Dhaturbeej – This is a strong Narcotic plant. It is extensively used for alleviating pain, treating fever, in subsiding inflammation. It is also beneficial in respiratory disorders. 

 Method of Preparation 

 First of all make a fine powder of all kashthaushadiyan. 
 Then add all the ingredients in a kharal yantra and properly mixes it with the extracts of Bhang ( Cannabis sativa ) for 3 hours. 
 Make 60 mg tablets and let them dry under the shadow. 
 Keep this in glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Ksheer vati is a classical Ayurvedic formulation. This is used in treating inflammation. The ingredients such as lavang, afeem and jaiphal are effective in treating digestive problems. This Ayurvedic formulation is also helpful in grahani (IBS and IBD), fever, indigestion etc problems. This improves digestion power of the person.

 Shuddha Dhaturabeej (Purified Dhatur metal ) – 6 gm 
 
 Description of Ingredients 
 
 Shuddha Hingula – This is a preparation of Mercury. This is used in the treatment of Inflammation, digestive problems, respiratory problems etc. This is used in ayurvedic preparation to increase the strength of other ingredients. 
 Lavang Churna – This is an Ayurvedic medicine in powder form. It is used in the treatment of digestive problems such as diarrhea, bloating, abdominal pain etc. It is also helpful in subsiding inflammation in the body. It balances Vata and Kapha dosha. 
 Shuddha Afeem – It has a digestive and appetizer action. This ingredient improves digestion power and provides strength to the body. This has an analgesic effect too, so used in mild to moderate pain. 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – This is a poisonous herb and used in a variety of diseases after the purification process. This herb has anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antipyretic properties. It is also used in fever, pain. 
 Jaiphal – This is capable of digestive problems. It is also known as nutmeg. It is useful in clearing the throat, useful in relieving bloating, flatulence and abdominal pain. Jaiphal is also helpful in inflammation. 
 Shuddha Dhaturbeej – This is a strong Narcotic plant. It is extensively used for alleviating pain, treating fever, in subsiding inflammation. It is also beneficial in respiratory disorders. 
 
 Method of Preparation 
 
 First of all make a fine powder of all kashthaushadiyan. 
 Then add all the ingredients in a kharal yantra and properly mixes it with the extracts of Bhang ( Cannabis sativa ) for 3 hours. 
 Make 60 mg tablets and let them dry under the shadow. 
 Keep this in glass container. 
 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Ksheer vati is a classical Ayurvedic formulation. This is used in treating inflammation. The ingredients such as lavang, afeem and jaiphal are effective in treating digestive problems. This Ayurvedic formulation is also helpful in grahani (IBS and IBD), fever, indigestion etc problems. This improves digestion power of the person. 
 Indications 
 
 Shotha roga (Inflammation) 
 Grahani (IBS and IBD) 
 Jeerna Jwara (Chronic fever) 
 
 Dosage 
 
 1 tablet with milk in inflammatory conditions. 
 1 tablet with the extract of Vijaya ( Cannabis sativa ). 
 
 Contraindications 
 
 Lavan (Salt) and Jala (Water) should be contraindicated during the course of this medicine. 
 If a person feels thirst then give milk or coconut water instead of plain water. 
 It should be strictly taken under the medical advice as it contains Afeem, datura and Vatsnabha. 
 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Kumarika vati is an old formulation used since centuries. It is a herbo-mineral compound used in female reproductive problems.
sections.ingredients:
Musabbar (Processed Aloe vera juice) 
 Afeem ( Papaver somniferum )

sections.description_of_ingredients:
Musabbar – This is the best herb for female’s health. It is also called Kumari. As name indicates it is beneficial in a female’s reproductive health. It is also effective in obesity, constipation, dyslipidemia etc. 
 Afeem – It is used in the treatment of infertility. It should be taken cautiously because it has sedative properties. It is also beneficial in insomnia, bone strength, improves digestion, good for thyroid function etc. 
 Shuddha Kasis – This is an Ayurvedic medicine, prepared from green vitriol which is also known as ferrous sulphate. It is used in Ayurvedic treatment after Shodhna process (purification). It is used in the treatment of leucoderma, Leucorrhea, infertility, amenorrhea, Fever, helminthiasis etc. 
 Vanga Bhasma – This is prepared from Tin metal. This ingredient is beneficial in the treatment of male and female reproductive problems. It is mainly useful in adrenal gland problems. It has analgesic, antibacterial, anti-inflammatory properties. 
 Agastya Pushp – This is helpful in pacifying Pitta dosha. It is also helpful in managing abdominal tumors. This is very effective in reproductive problems. It can help the body in detoxifying toxins. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all the ingredients in equal quantity. 
 Properly grind these ingredients together with added water. 
 Make 250 mg tablet and let them dry. 
 Keep in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Kumarika Vati is an Ayurvedic formulation. This is very effective in all reproductive problems of females. It contains Kumari, Vanga and kasis which is mainly used in female health problems. This formulation is also beneficial in Fever, lower abdominal pain, vaginal pain. It provides strength to the reproductive organs of the females.

name: Kutaj Ghan Vati

sections.overview: Kutaj Ghan Vati – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Kutaj Ghan Vati is an herbal formulation, in tablet from. It is useful in curing diarrhea, dysentery, intestinal infections and bleeding disorders etc. These tablets also provide relief in irritable bowel syndrome. Kutaj Ghan Vati has antidysenteric, antidiarrheal, anti-amoebic action and hemostatic properties.
sections.ingredients:
Kutaj (Holarrhena antidysenterica) 
 Ativisha (Aconitum heterophyllum) 

 Method of Preparation 
 Boil Kutaj in 16 times water till just 1/8th part is remaining. Remove the decoction from the flame and and let it cool down and filter it through a muslin cloth. Cook it for some more time till it thickens. Let it dry under sunlight and add Ativisha powder. Make 175 mg tablets each and put it in the dryer till all the moisture has evaporated. Store it in an airtight container. 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Kutaj ghan vati is an ayurvedic medicine available in tablet form. It is meant to manage the various digestive disorders. Natural ingredients used in the formulation of this medicine are packed with antimicrobial properties. In diarrhea and dysentery use of this medicine is quite effective as it helps to extrude the microorganism from the body. These tablets also help to manage the symptoms like abdominal pain, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhea with mucus or pus etc. It is quite a good remedy to manage the problem of loose stools in fever. Use of this medicine is quite good in malabsorption syndrome as it accelerates the absorption of nutrients in body and helps to fulfill the nutritional deficiencies in the body. Besides of all this, calmative and cooling action of this medicine helps to manage the rectal bleeding in ulcerative colitis.
sections.indications:
Diarrhea 
 Dysentery 
 Malabsorption syndrome 
 Loose stools due to fever 
 Ulcerative colitis
sections.dosage: 2 to 3 tablets thrice a day with plain water after meals.
sections.contraindications:
There are no reported side effects of this medicine. 
 Over dosage should be strictly avoided. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Lashunadi Vati

sections.introduction: Lashunadi Vati is an herbal formulation in a tablet form. It is used in treating diarrhea, dyspepsia, and intestinal disorders. Lashun means garlic and that is the prime ingredient of this formulation. It equalizes Kapha and Vata and also enhances pitta.
sections.ingredients:
Garlic (Allium sativum) 
 Cumin (Cuminum cyminum) 
 Saindhav Lavana (Rock salt) 
 Shudh Gandhaka (Purified Sulphur) 
 Saunth/ dry ginger (Zingiber officinalis) 
 Long pepper (Piper longum) 
 Black pepper (Piper nigrum) 
 Asafetida 
 Sufficient amount of lemon juice 

 Method of Preparation 
 Clean and grind all the ingredients to a fine powder and mix in sufficient amount of lemon juice and mix it till it forms the consistency of a paste and make tablets from it and let these tablets be in the dryer till they harden. Now, store them in a clean and dry place in an air tight jar.
sections.dosage: 1 to 2 tablets twice daily with water or as prescribed by your doctor.

 Diarrhea 
 Low digestive power 
 Dyspepsia 
 Intestinal ailments 
 Stomach ailments

 As it contains salt, patients with hypertension should take it under strict medical advice.

sections.introduction: Lavangadi Vati is an Ayurvedic medicine in tablet form used for treating upper respiratory infections like cough, congestion, cold and allergic respiratory conditions. It is demulcent, anti-inflammatory and expectorant in action. Clove is the main ingredient of this medicine. Clove has Kapha dosha balancing, antispasmodic, antiseptic and carminative properties. It reduces vata and kapha but increases pitta. It is hot in potency it increases blood pressure and pitta. Hence should be taken cautiously in high, pitta condition and high blood pressure.

 Black pepper (Piper nigrum) 
 Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica)

 Water concoction of Babul (Acacia Arabica) 

 Method of Preparation 
 Grind all the ingredients to a fine powder and triturate with the formed decoction, a semisolid paste will be formed and make pills from this paste and let them dry and store them in an air tight container.

Respiratory problems like cough, colds, congestion, bronchitis, and asthma.

 Chest pain 
 Bronchitis

 Cough and cold 
 Sore throat

sections.introduction: Mahadhanwantharam Gulika (Vati) is also known as Garbharakshini because it protects and shelters pregnancy and also it has anti-inflammatory properties.
sections.ingredients:
Ela (Elettaria cardamomum) 
 Ginger (Zingiber officinale) 
 Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 Celery (Achyranthes aspera) 
 Eggplant/aubergine (Solanum melongena) 
 Indian Echinacea – (Andrographis paniculata) 
 Cubeb/tailed pepper – (Piper cubeba) 
 Bhoonimba – (Andrographis paniculata) 
 Rudra’s tear drops – (Elaeocarpus ganitrus) 
 Himalayan cedar – (Cedrus deodara) 
 Shiral (Grewia nervosa) 
 Kapoor (Cinnamomum camphor) 
 Mango ginger (Curcuma amada) 
 Cumin (Cuminum cyminum) 

 Method of Preparation

name: Mandur Vatak

sections.overview: Mandur Vatak – Ingredients, Preparation, Indications Dosage
sections.introduction: Mandur Vatak is a classical Ayurvedic herbo-mineral formulation, traditionally revered as a potent "life-giving" tonic for hematological and metabolic disorders. Its complex composition bridges traditional pharmacology and clinical efficacy, combining fifteen synergistic herbs—including the Trikatu and Triphala groups—with purified Mandur Bhasma (Iron Calx) processed in cow urine. Primarily indicated for Pandu (anemia) and Kamla (jaundice), its therapeutic action extends to stabilizing the Agni (digestive fire) and resolving "bio-ecological disruptions" within the liver and spleen. When integrated with a traditional buttermilk regimen, Mandur Vatak serves as a sophisticated agent for systemic rejuvenation and iron bio-availability. Let’s discuss it in detail!
sections.ingredients:
Sunthi: Zingiber officinale 
 Maricha: Piper nigrum 
 Pippali: Piper longum (Fruit) 
 Haritaki: Terminalia chebula 
 Baheda: Terminalia bellirica 
 Amla: Phyllanthus emblica 
 Nagarmotha: Cyperus rotundus 
 Vidanga: Embelia ribes 
 Chavya: Piper chaba 
 Chitrakmool: Plumbago zeylanica 
 Daruhaldi: Berberis aristata 
 Dalchini: Cinnamomum zeylanicum 
 Swarna Makshik Bhasma: Chalcopyrite (Purified/Incinerated) 
 Pippalamool: Piper longum (Root) 
 Devdaru: Cedrus deodara- 8 Tola (approx. 96g) each of these 15 herbs 
 Mandur Bhasma: Ferroso-ferric oxide (Processed Iron Ore)– 240 Tola (approx. 2.88 kg) 
 Gomutra: Bos taurus (Urine)- 1920 Tola (approx. 23 kg or 25 Ser )
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Sunthi (Zingiber officinale) 
 In Ayurveda, Sunthi is Vishwa-bheshaja (the universal medicine). It possesses Deepana (appetite-stimulating) and Pachana (digestive) properties that ignite the Jatharagni. By clearing Amadosha (metabolic toxins), it ensures that the iron in Mandur Bhasma is properly assimilated rather than excreted. Gingerol and shogaols enhance gastrointestinal motility and stimulate the secretion of digestive enzymes. Sunthi acts as a bioavailability enhancer, improving the absorption of micro-nutrients in the small intestine, which is critical for treating malabsorption-linked anemia. 

 2. Maricha (Piper nigrum) 
 Maricha is a potent Pramathi herb, meaning it forcefully clears obstructions in the micro-channels (Srotas). It helps in reducing Kapha and Vata, which often stagnate in the liver and spleen during chronic anemia. Its primary alkaloid, piperine, is a documented bio-enhancer. It inhibits metabolic enzymes that might otherwise break down the herbal compounds prematurely. In anemia management, it increases the thermogenic response of the gut, significantly boosting the systemic uptake of iron and other fat-soluble vitamins required for erythropoiesis. 

 3. Pippali (Piper longum) 
 Pippali is a premier Rasayana (rejuvenative) for the respiratory and digestive systems. It specifically enhances Rakta Dhatu Agni (the metabolic fire responsible for blood formation), ensuring that the nutrients are converted into healthy red blood cells. Pippali contains piperine and piperlongumine, which exhibit hepatoprotective and splenoprotective properties. Since the liver and spleen are the primary sites for iron storage and RBC recycling, Pippali ensures these organs function optimally to maintain healthy hemoglobin levels and prevent the cellular hypoxia associated with anemic states. 

 4. Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 Known as the "King of Medicines," Haritaki is Anulomana, ensuring the smooth downward movement of waste. In Pandu (anemia), it prevents the constipation often associated with iron-heavy formulations and cleanses the Rasavaha Srotas. It is rich in chebulinic acid and polyphenols. Haritaki acts as a mild laxative and a potent antioxidant. By reducing oxidative stress in the gut and improving bowel regularity, it creates a healthy mucosal environment for iron transporters (like ferroportin) to function without interference from accumulated fecal toxins. 

 5. Baheda (Terminalia bellirica) 
 Baheda is primarily Vibhitaki, meaning "that which keeps away disease. It focuses on balancing Kapha and Pitta. In the context of Mandur Vatak, it helps reduce the inflammatory markers that often lead to anemia of chronic disease. It contains gallic and ellagic acids, which provide significant cytoprotective effects to the liver. By enhancing liver function, Baheda assists in the synthesis of transferrin, the protein responsible for transporting iron through the blood, thereby ensuring that the iron from the Bhasma reaches the bone marrow efficiently. 

 6. Amla (Emblica officinalis) 
 Amla is a premier Chakshushya and Vayasthapana herb. In Ayurveda, its high Pitta-pacifying energy cools the blood and supports the liver (Yakrit). It is considered the best support for Rakta Dhatu. Amla is one of the richest sources of stable Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid). Scientifically, Vitamin C is essential for iron absorption; it reduces ferric iron ($Fe^{3+}$) to ferrous iron ($Fe^{2+}$), the only form the human body can absorb. Without Amla, the high dose of Mandur Bhasma would be significantly less effective. 

 7. Nagarmotha (Cyperus rotundus) 
 This herb is Grahi (absorbent) and Deepana. It is specifically used in Ayurveda to treat Amapachana and fever associated with anemia. It targets the "dampness" or excess Kapha that clogs the metabolic pathways of the liver. It possesses essential oils and flavonoids that exhibit anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective activities. In anemic patients, chronic low-grade inflammation often traps iron in macrophages (locking it away from use). Nagarmotha helps modulate this inflammatory response, potentially releasing "locked" iron stores back into the plasma for hemoglobin synthesis. 

 8. Vidanga (Embelia ribes) 
 Vidanga is the foremost Krimighna (anti-parasitic) herb. Ayurveda recognizes that many cases of Pandu (anemia) are caused by Krimis (intestinal worms) that consume the host’s nutrients and cause blood loss. Its active constituent, embelin, has proven anthelmintic properties. By eliminating hookworms and other parasites that cause occult GI bleeding, Vidanga treats the root cause of iron-deficiency anemia. Additionally, its antioxidant properties protect the RBC membranes from premature hemolysis (destruction), extending the lifespan of circulating red cells. 

 9. Chavya (Piper chaba) 
 Chavya is a pungent herb that specifically targets the Grahani (small intestine). It increases the "bio-fire" and clears the coating of Ama from the intestinal walls, which often blocks the absorption of minerals like iron. Chavya stimulates the secretion of bile and gastric juices. This acidic environment is crucial for dissolving mineral Bhasmas. By improving the overall "dissolution rate" of the formulation in the stomach, Chavya ensures that the Mandur (Iron) is in a soluble state when it reaches the duodenum for absorption. 

 10. Chitrakmool (Plumbago zeylanica) 
 Chitrak is considered the most powerful Agni-vardhaka (fire-enhancer). It specifically stimulates the liver and spleen. In Ayurveda, it "scrapes" away the excess Kapha that causes the paleness and heaviness seen in anemic patients. It contains plumbagin, a compound that stimulates the liver to produce more bile and enhances the metabolic rate. By increasing the metabolic activity of the liver and spleen, Chitrakmool supports the hematopoietic system in the production of new erythrocytes, directly counteracting the lethargy and metabolic stagnation of anemia.

Cinnamon improves peripheral circulation and has insulin-mimetic effects. Improved blood flow ensures that the newly formed hemoglobin and oxygen are delivered efficiently to the tissues. Its antimicrobial properties also help maintain a healthy gut microbiome, which is increasingly recognized as a factor in the efficient absorption of dietary and supplemental iron. 

 13. Swarna Makshik Bhasma (Chalcopyrite Calx)

It is considered less "heating" than pure iron and is highly compatible with the human body. It provides a synergistic blend of Iron ($Fe$) and Copper ($Cu$).  Gomutra is used as the processing medium ( Bhavana ). It is Tikshna (penetrating) and Kshariya (alkaline). It "scrubs" the channels and acts as a powerful catalyst for the mineral ingredients.  First, mix the Mandur Bhasma in cow urine and cook it. 
 Then, mix the finely powdered remains of the other herbs into it and prepare tablets of 2 Ratti (approx. 250mg) each.

sections.introduction: Marichadi Gutika (Vati) is known as one of the great ayurvedic formulation that is prepared from various mixture of herbs. This is known to treat the problem of respiratory system.
sections.ingredients:
Guda – Jaggery 
 Maricha – Piper nigrum 
 Pippali – Piper longum 
 Yava Kshara – Hordeum vulgare 
 Dadima – Punica granatum 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take the ingredients in its appropriate quantity, guda up to 96 grams, yava kshara up to 6 grams, maricha and pippali up to 12 grams and dadima up to 24 grams. 
 Powder all the ingredients and pounded with jiggery/guda. 
 Make pills from them. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Marichadi Gutika (Vati) is an efficient Ayurvedic formulation that is able to maintain the balance of Vata and Kapha dosha in the body. 
 It is very useful to get rid of respiratory conditions. It is an effective Ayurvedic medicine which is helpful in bronchitis, where it improves the immunity and reduces fever and along reduces inflammation in the airways. It is also able to control the cough and relaxing the sufferer as well as provides soothing feeling in cold. It is beneficial in rhinitis too, boosts the immunity, and helps to reduce inflammation of the nose and relieves congestion and promotes easy elimination of mucus from the nose and, impart relief from sneezing and lessens the irritation in the throat.

 Method of Preparation 

 Take ingredients number 1 to 23 up to 192 grams. 
 Powder all these herbs.

It imparts relief from painful micturition, supports easy passing of urine. 
 Provides beneficial results in nervous disorders, effective in syncope and helpful in giddiness as well as faintness. It reduces headache effectively.

sections.introduction: Step into the realm of Panchanan Vati, a formidable masterpiece of Ayurvedic alchemy designed to combat the most stubborn forms of Pandu (Anemia). This isn’t just a supplement; it is a high-potency “warrior” formula that blends purified heavy metals like Mercury and Copper with the intense purgative power of Jamalgota (Croton seeds). Crafted to tackle complex conditions like Pernicious Anaemia and Lymphatic Leukaemia, it works through a systematic “Search and Destroy” mission—first purging deep-seated toxins from the gut, then “burning” impurities within the blood, and finally revitalizing the liver and heart. It represents the pinnacle of ancient cellular detoxification. Let’s study about this in detail!
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) 
 Shuddha Gandhaka (Purified Sulphur) 
 Tamra Bhasma (Incinerated Copper) 
 Abhraka Bhasma (Incinerated Mica) 
 Shuddha Guggulu (Purified Commiphora mukul resin) 
 Shuddha Jamalgota (Purified Croton tiglium seeds)
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) 
 In Ayurveda, Parada is considered Yogavahi—a catalyst that carries the properties of other herbs deep into the tissues (Dhatus). When purified, it balances all three Doshas and acts as a powerful rejuvenator (Rasayana). It enhances the bioavailability of the entire formula. Modern science views processed mercury (in the form of sulfide) as a potential immuno-modulator in minute, non-toxic doses, though it remains controversial. In this context, it acts as a carrier to ensure cellular uptake of iron-boosting minerals. 
 2. Shuddha Gandhaka (Purified Sulphur) 
 Gandhaka is known as the “soul” of mercury. It purifies the blood (Rakta Shodhaka) and addresses skin diseases often associated with blood impurities. In Ayurveda, it “scrapes” away toxins (Amavisha) that block nutrient absorption. Scientifically, sulfur is essential for the synthesis of glutathione, a major antioxidant that protects red blood cells from oxidative stress and premature breakdown (hemolysis). 
 3. Tamra Bhasma (Incinerated Copper) 
 Tamra Bhasma is a specialized copper preparation used for liver and spleen disorders. It is particularly effective for Udar-rog (abdominal diseases) and Pandu. Ayurveda uses it to stimulate the liver, the seat of Ranjan Pitta (the fire that colors blood). Modern science confirms that copper is an essential cofactor for ceruloplasmin, the enzyme required to transport iron and incorporate it into hemoglobin. 
 4. Abhraka Bhasma (Incinerated Mica) 
 This is a powerhouse of trace minerals, traditionally used to treat chronic exhaustion, respiratory issues, and severe anemia. It acts as a Rakta Vardhak (blood builder) and strengthens the heart muscle. Biologically, mica contains magnesium, potassium, and iron. It helps in increasing the red blood cell count by providing a mineral-rich environment for hematopoiesis (blood cell formation) in the bone marrow. 
 5. Shuddha Guggulu (Purified Commiphora Mukul) 
 Guggulu is a potent oleo-gum resin used to clear “clogged” channels (Srotas) and reduce excess fat (Meda). It improves circulation and ensures that the blood-forming nutrients reach the peripheral tissues. Modern research highlights its anti-inflammatory properties and its ability to improve lipid profiles, which prevents the sluggish circulation often found in chronic anemic states. 
 6. Shuddha Jamalgota (Purified Croton Tiglium) 
 This is the “engine” of Panchanan Vati. It is a powerful Virechana (purgative) agent that must be strictly purified to be safe. Ayurveda believes anemia is often caused by “stagnant waste” in the gut preventing absorption. Jamalgota forcibly flushes this waste. Scientifically, by inducing controlled purgation, it resets the gut microbiome and removes intestinal parasites or “biofilms” that may be competing for iron and B12 absorption. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 1. First, create a Kajjali (black sulphide of mercury) by grinding the Parada and Gandhaka together. 
 2. Then, gradually mix in the Bhasmas and remaining medicines. 
 3. Grind the mixture with 1 Tola (approx. 12g) of Ghee for 3 hours (1 Prahar). 
 4. Form into pills weighing 1 Ratti (approx. 125mg) each.
sections.therapeutic_uses_and_indications:
General Use: This medicine cures Pandu (Anemia) accompanied by Shotha (edema/swelling). It is specifically indicated when swelling arises due to dietary errors, lifestyle mistakes, or liver dysfunction. 
 Specific Conditions 
 1. Progressive Pernicious Anaemia (Tridoshaj Pandu) 
 Symptoms include bleeding from the eyes, skin, and mucous membranes; blood spots on the skin; swelling spreading from feet to knees0-; increased body fat; loss of strength; rapid heartbeat; heart enlargement; frequent fainting; and persistent night fever (102°F–104°F). It is used to eliminate toxins from the blood. 
 2. Lymphatic Leukaemia 
 Indicated when the face becomes pale/lifeless, lymph nodes are enlarged, indigestion occurs, and the spleen is enlarged. Take this in the morning only. During the afternoon and night, use medicines predominant in Iron (Loha) or Mandura. 
 How It Works (The Three Functions)? 
 1. Elimination 
 Jamalgota (Croton) acts as a powerful purgative to forcibly expel accumulated toxins and waste from the digestive tract and colon. 
 2. Purification 
 Once the waste is cleared, the Tamra (Copper) and Kajjali (Mercury/Sulphur) work to “burn” or neutralize toxins that have entered the deeper tissues (Dhatus) and blood. 
 3. Strengthening 
 Abhraka (Mica) and Guggulu strengthen the nervous system, liver, and spleen. 
 Abhraka treats blood deficiency, heart palpitations, and breathlessness. 
 Guggulu strengthens the veins/nerves, eliminates internal foul odors, reduces excess fat, and nourishes the heart.
sections.contraindications:
Do not use it if there is intestinal inflammation (pain when pressing on the abdomen). 
 Do not use it if there are kidney lesions or if pus is present in the urine. 
 It should not be used if the patient has diarrhea or active hemorrhaging
sections.dose_1_to_2_pills_in_the_morning:
Anupana (Vehicle): Take with water or a decoction of Punarnava. 
 Dietary Note: Avoid cold water and sour foods during the treatment period. If there is swelling (edema), salt should also be avoided. 


 Conclusion 
 In conclusion, Panchanan Vati stands as a sophisticated testament to the “aggressive healing” philosophy of ancient Rasa Shastra. Far from a simple iron supplement, it is a comprehensive metabolic reboot designed for cases where standard treatments fail due to deep-seated systemic toxicity. By combining the “scorched earth” purgative action of Jamalgota with the restorative alchemy of incinerated metals, it doesn’t just add blood to the body—it clears the path for the body to manufacture its own. However, its potency is its greatest risk. The inclusion of purified mercury and croton seeds makes it a “double-edged sword” that requires the steady hand of a master practitioner. When used correctly, it is a life-restoring elixir for chronic anemia; when misused, it can be hazardous. Ultimately, Panchanan Vati reminds us that in the Ayurvedic tradition, true healing begins not with what we add to the body, but with what we have the courage to remove.

Its main effects appear on uterus and ovaries. These tablets stimulate the ovulation and corrects the ovarian functions. It also promotes the menstrual discharge due to its emmenagogue action. Raja Pravartini Vati is helpful in the treatment of amenorrhea, oligomenorrhea, dysmenorrhea associated with light menstruation or scanty periods and backache during menstruation. It is beneficial when patient feels outflow obstruction during menstruation. This medicine should only be taken under medical supervision.
sections.ingredients:
10 g fine powder of each of:- 

 Ghritkumari – Aloe vera

 Tankana – Borax 
 Hing – Asa foetida

name: Rasamanikya

sections.reference_siddha_bheshaja_manimala_jwara: Rasamanikya is an Ayurvedic medicine available in tablet and powder form. This herbal powder is used in the treatment of fever, bronchitis, Asthma etc. This medicine contains heavy metal as an ingredient, hence take it strictly under medical supervision. It balances the Vata and Kapha doshas in the body.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha haratala (arsenic trioxide) and mica sheets. 
 Method of preparation 
 Small pieces of Purified Haratala (Arsenic trioxide) are taken and made into fine powder. It is squeezed in between sheets of mica. It is burnt in open air, till the internal mass turns to coppery red color. 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Rasamanikya is an efficient Ayurvedic formulation with properties to manage the disease occurring due to vitiation of Vata and kapha doshas. 
 It is a very useful Ayurvedic remedy to bring effective results in respiratory problems. It is helpful in bronchitis, helps to reduce inflammation in bronchi, ease in expectoration of phlegm, and improves the breathing, giving relief in chest pain. It also provides relief in Asthma, dilate the bronchial passage, helps in easy breathing, preventing its recurrence. It can control the cough. Useful medicine to regulate the body temperature in the body. 
 It is even beneficial to manage various chronic skin problems like, leprosy, have properties to heal wounds rapidly and relieves the pus filled boils, disease with excessive dryness of skin, lessen the rashes, helps to get rid of eczema, reduces the inflammations of eczema., leukoderma etc. 
 It is suitable for certain nervous disorders too.
sections.indications:
Fever 
 Bronchitis 
 Asthma 
 Gout 
 Chronic wounds 
 Syphilis 
 Rashes 
 Dryness of skin 
 Leucoderma
sections.dosage:
125 mg once or twice a day, before or after food or as directed by an Ayurvedic doctor. 
 It is traditionally administered along with ghee and honey.
sections.side_effects:
Self-medication with this medicine may prove to be dangerous, as it contains Arsenic as an ingredient. 
 Take this medicine for a limited period of time, in precise doses or as advised by the doctor. 
 Over-dosage is dangerous with medicine. 
 This medicine should be avoided in pregnancy, lactation and in children. 
 Keep out of reach and sight of children. 
 Store in a dry cool place. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Rason Karpura Vati

sections.overview: Rason Karpura Vati – Ingredients, Preparation, Uses Dosage
sections.introduction: Digestive disturbances such as sudden indigestion, abdominal discomfort, and acute gastrointestinal upset often arise when the digestive fire becomes weak and toxins begin to accumulate in the gut. In traditional Ayurvedic practice, Rason Karpura Vati is a powerful formulation designed to restore digestive balance and support the body during such acute conditions. Prepared with potent ingredients like garlic, camphor, and asafoetida, this classical remedy works to kindle the digestive fire, ease abdominal spasms, and support normal gut function. Its stimulating and carminative nature helps clear stagnation, reduce discomfort, and promote digestive harmony, making it a valuable traditional support for maintaining gastrointestinal stability.
sections.ingredients:
Camphor 

 One Clove of Purified Garlic 

 Asafoetida (Hing) 

 Onion Juice 

 All taken in equal proportions.
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Camphor (Karpura) 
 In a clinical context, only Bhimseni (Natural) Camphor is used internally. It is a powerful stimulant and antispasmodic. In cases of Visuchika, where there is often a sudden collapse of digestive strength and coldness in the extremities, Camphor acts as a diffusive stimulant. It instantly warms the stomach and stimulates the heart and circulation. Its aromatic properties help suppress nausea and vomiting associated with indigestion, while its antimicrobial nature helps maintain digestive hygiene. Because it is highly volatile, it penetrates quickly and is traditionally valued for helping clear accumulated Ama and supporting digestive fire (Agni). 

 Purified Garlic (Shuddha Lasun) 
 Single-clove garlic, when purified, loses much of its harshness while retaining its concentrated organosulfur compounds. For Agnimandya, garlic acts as a Bhedana (piercing) agent, helping to break through heavy mucus and digestive stagnation that may interfere with nutrient absorption. In Visuchika, it is traditionally regarded as a natural antimicrobial that helps address fermentation and putrefaction within the digestive tract. Its heating (Ushna) potency supports the revival of appetite and encourages the proper secretion of digestive juices, thereby assisting in the management of indigestion. 

 Asafoetida (Hing) 
 Asafoetida is one of Ayurveda’s foremost herbs for Vata-Anulomana, promoting the downward movement of gas and relieving digestive discomfort. In cases of indigestion, it acts as a potent carminative, helping to prevent Udavarta (upward movement of Vata) that may contribute to abdominal pressure, chest discomfort, and headaches. In Visuchika, it is traditionally used to calm spasmodic contractions of the stomach and intestines. It supports digestion by aiding the breakdown of starches and proteins and helps clear the bodily channels (Srotas), facilitating the elimination of accumulated toxins. 

 Onion Juice (Palandu Swarasa) 
 Onion juice serves both as a medicinal vehicle (Anupana) and as an active therapeutic ingredient. Rich in sulfur compounds and prebiotic fibers, it stimulates the gastric mucosa and supports digestive activity. In Visuchika, onion juice has traditionally been used to help maintain fluid balance and soothe the intestinal lining. It exerts a mild calming effect on the nerves of the digestive tract, reducing the churning sensation often associated with indigestion. For Agnimandya, its pungent yet slightly sweet nature provides balanced stimulation that rekindles digestive fire without causing excessive irritation. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Mix all the ingredients together and triturate them in onion juice for about 3 hours. 
 After proper grinding, prepare pills of about 1 ratti each.
sections.indications_and_clinical_use:
This pill is highly beneficial in Visuchika (severe gastrointestinal disorder resembling cholera). It helps relieve indigestion, abdominal colic, coldness, and diarrhea while stimulating the digestive fire (Agni). After the severity of the condition decreases, this formulation does not cause excessive weakness. It can also be administered safely and repeatedly to individuals with a weak heart. 

 In severe attacks of Visuchika, one pill should be given every half hour. Along with this, administer 2 teaspoons of very cold water (such as ice-cold water) at intervals. As the intensity of the disease reduces, the frequency of administration should be gradually decreased.
sections.dosage:
Give one pill every half hour along with onion juice, or it may be swallowed with 1 masha of sugar. 

 Conclusion 
 At last we can say that Rason Karpura Vati stands as a potent classical preparation valued for its ability to quickly restore digestive stability during acute gastrointestinal disturbances. Its carefully selected ingredients work together to stimulate metabolism, relieve abdominal discomfort, and support proper movement within the digestive tract. By enhancing digestive strength and reducing internal stagnation, this formulation helps the body regain balance and resilience. Unlike many remedies that merely suppress symptoms, it supports the natural functioning of the gut and promotes recovery from within. When used appropriately according to traditional guidance, Rason Karpura Vati serves as a reliable Ayurvedic aid for maintaining digestive vitality and overall gastrointestinal wellbeing.

sections.ingredients:
Guduchi (Giloy) – Indian Tinospora (stem) – Tinospora cordifolia 
 Coarse powder of herb Guduchi ( Tinospora cordifolia) is made. 
 It is boiled in the water until it is reduced to a quarter part. Then it is filtered. 
 It is further boiled to form a semi solid mass. 
 It is then rolled into pill form. 


 Method of preparation 

 Coarse powder of herb Guduchi ( Tinospora cordifolia) is made. 
 It is boiled in the water until it reduced to a quarter parts. Then it is filtered. 
 It is further boiled to form a semi solid mass. 
 It is then rolled into pills form.

 Samshamani Vati is an Ayurvedic medicine formulated to manage fever. Major ingredient of this medicine is Giloya (Indian Tinospora). This herb has great medicinal importance in Ayurveda to lower down the elevated body temperature in chronic fever. This medicine helps to strengthen the body’s immune system and enhances the body’s ability to fight against the various bacterial, viral and fungal infections. It is effective for weakness as it helps to boost up strength and energy in the body.

 Chronic fever 
 Anemia 
 Weakness

There are no known side effects with this medicine.

sections.reference_siddha_yoga_sangraha_bhrama_an: Sarpagandha Ghan Vati is a classical polyherbal medicine. It is used in the treatment of high blood pressure, lack of sleep, increased pulse, insomnia etc. It should only be used under strict medical supervision. It balances Vata and Pitta.
sections.ingredients:

 Khurasani ajwain – Trachyspermum ammi – 2 g

 Sarpagandha ghan vati is an Ayurvedic medicine available in the tablet form. Herbs used in the formulation of this medicine comprise the calmative, diuretic, hypertensive etc. properties. In the problem of hypertension it regulates the blood pressure by maintaining the balance of myocardial oxygen. Sarpagandha ghan vati helps to flush out the toxins from body. It also helps in blood purification and maintains the proper blood supply throughout the body. Besides of this, it is good medicine for various neurological problems like anxiety, stress etc. Use of this medicine is quite effective in psychological disorders like uncontrollable emotion or excitement in hysteria.

name: Sukha Virechana Vati

sections.reference_ayurved_sar_sangrah_17th_editi: Sukha Virechana Vati is an Ayurvedic medicine in herbal tablet form. It is used in the treatment of constipation. This medicine is also used in Virechana (Purgation) therapy, which is done to balance the pitta dosha.
sections.ingredients:
Jamalgota – Croton tiglium – 13g 
 Shunti – Ginger Rhizome – Zingiber officinalis – powder – 24 g 
 Water – Quantity sufficient for grinding. 

 Method of Preparation 
 Jamalgota (Croton tiglium) seeds are broken into two parts. These seeds are dipped in the boiling water by covering it completely for whole night. In the morning proper washing and grinding is done. After the complete grinding, add the 24 gram powder of Shunti (Zingiber officinalis). This mixture is minced with water for 8 hours to make the tablets. Tablets are dried and stored. 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Sukha virechana vati is an efficient Ayurvedic formulation that helps to keep the Pitta and Vata doshas in balanced condition. It has laxative property. As per Ayurveda, Ama or undigested food is considered as a root cause for all the diseases including digestive and other such as rheumatoid arthritis. If body metabolism is proper, one can avoid plenty of diseases to happen. This herbal remedy can be taken on regular basis to have proper motion without efforts in all such conditions including anal fistula, piles and fissures. Well indicated in chronic constipation as well.
sections.indications: It helps to relieve constipation.
sections.dosage: 1 tablet of 250 mg at bed time as directed by Ayurvedic doctor.
sections.side_effects:
Over dosage may cause heart burn and diarrhea. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Swasanandam Gulika (Vati)

sections.introduction: Swasanandam gulika is an ayurvedic formulation that is known to have mixture of effective herbs. This is known to treat the problems related to respiratory system.
sections.ingredients:
Triphala – Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), Amalaki (Emblica officinalis), Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 Karpoora – Cinnamomum camphora 
 Shuddha Hingula – Purified and processed Cinnabar (An ore of Mercury and Sulphur) 
 Vatsanabha – Purified and processed Aconitum ferox 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all the herbs and powder them. 
 At last mix all the powdered herbs and make pills from them by taking the quantity of mixture up to 125 mg. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Swasanandam gulika is an Ayurvedic medicine available in tablet form. This medicine is meant to manage the respiratory complications. Herbs used in the formulation of this are packed with antimicrobial properties that protect the body from various infections. Use of this medicine is quite effective to manage health issues like asthma, bronchitis, cough etc. Expectorant and decongestant action of this medicine helps to clear the phlegm, cough, mucous from air ways and air channels. It manages the symptoms with bronchitis like wheezing, persistent cough, low fever and chills, chest tightening, sore throat, body aches, breathlessness, blocked nose, headache and sinuses etc.
sections.indications:
Cold and cough 
 Bronchitis 
 Asthma
sections.dose: One to two tablets, two times a day, after meals.
sections.contraindications:
Avoid in pregnancy and lactation. 
 Gastritis problem may arise in over dose. 
 Take under medical prescription. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Talisapatradi Vatakam

sections.introduction: Talisapatradi Vatakam is known as one of the effective ayurvedic formulation that has mixture of good herbs. This formulation is known to treat the problems related to respiratory and digestive systems.
sections.ingredients:
Talisapatra – Abies webbiana 
 Maricha – Piper nigrum 
 Chavika – Piper chaba 
 Anantamoola – Hemidesmus indicus 
 Pippali – Piper longum 
 Dry Ginger – Zingiber officinalis 
 Usheera – Vetiveria zizanioides 
 Chaturjata – Known to have combination of following herbs: 


 Cinnamon (Cinnamomum zeylanicum) 
 Patra (Cinnamomum tamala) 
 Cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum) 
 Nagakeshara (Mesua ferrea) 

 Method of Preparation 

 Took the herbs in its given quantity. 
 Took 1 to 3 herbs up to 48 grams, 4 and 5 up to 96 grams, shunthi up to 144 grams, 7 and 8 ingredients up to 12 grams. 
 Powder all the ingredients and mix with three times of jaggery. 
 Make pills from this paste. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Talisapatradi Vatakam aids in pacifying diseases related to Vata and Kapha. It acts as an extremely useful Ayurvedic formulation in managing digestive disorders as it is helpful to control vomiting, sprue, provides relief in abdominal pain, effective in controlling gastritis and bloating. It efficaciously manages all types of cough and controls occurrence of asthma and promotes easy breathing and is beneficial in controlling other respiratory ailments like bronchitis, it reduces the inflammation in the bronchial tract and improves the process of breathing. It helps in regulating the body temperature as a result controlling fever, and has potent anti-inflammatory property that reduces inflammation. It possesses the property to improve the hemoglobin level which helps to overcome anemia. In Bloating, It reduces the abdominal distention. In case of ascites, reduces inflammation in fistula. Along with this, it also helps in igniting the digestive fire which controls the digestive problems. It manages the Malabsorption syndrome which as a result improves the nutrient absorption.

name: Udaymartand Rasa

sections.introduction: Udaymartand rasa is a herbo-mineral composition. This is an effective medicine for Udavarta, anaha (flatulence, constipation).
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Hingula – 40 gms 
 Shuddha Jaiphal – 20 gms 
 Shuddha Suhaga – 10 gms 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – 5 gms
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Hingula – Botanically it is known as Red sulphide of mercury. It stimulates digestion and aids in relieving the pain and inflammation. This pacifies vata and kapha dosha.  
 Shuddha Jaiphal – Jaiphal is also known as Myristica fragrans. It promotes digestive fire. It corrects the balance of vata and kapha dosha mainly. This shows effectual results in relieving pain, inflammation and acts as liver tonic due to its hepatoprotective property.   
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – This is known as Aconitum ferox . This is used as medicine. But firstly detoxify this drug. It has antipyretic and diaphoretic properties. It pacifies vata, pitta and kapha dosha, especially balances the vata and kapha dosha. It is a very good analgesic and anti-inflammatory. 
 Shuddha Suhaga – This is also known as Citrus tankan. It improves digestion and relieves bloating. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Give proper frolement to all the above mentioned ingredients in a kharal yantra. 
 Now give water bhavna and make 250 mg tablets. 
 Let them dry and kept in glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Udaymartand rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this formulation have digestive properties. They digest the Aama (Endotoxins) in the gut and maintain the digestive power.
sections.indications:
Indigestion 
 Flatulence 
 Constipation 
 Oedema 
 Skin disorders 
 Fistula 
 Piles
sections.dosage:
2 tablets twice a day with plain water, extracts of Adraka (Zingiber officinale) or decoction of trikatu. 
 Cautions 

 Take under medical supervision. 
 Avoid this formulation in pregnancy. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Udrari Rasa

sections.introduction: Udrari rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this are effective in digestive problems. They have digestive properties.
sections.ingredients:
Pippali Churna – 1 Part 
 Shuddha Jaiphal – 1 Part 
 Ras Sindoor – 1 Part 
 Shuddha Tutha – 1 Part 
 Amaltas ( Cassia fistula ) – 1 Part
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Pippali Churna – Pippali is known as Piper longum. This herb is very effective in diarrhea, indigestion and other gastric ailments. It pacifies Vata and Kapha. Thus promoting the digestive fire by enhancing the gastric secretions. 
 Shuddha Jaiphal ( Myristica fragrans ) – It promotes digestive fire. It pacifies kapha and vata dosha. This is effective in relieving pain, reduces inflammation and is useful in abdominal problems. 
 Ras Sindoor – Ras sindoor is an Ayurvedic medicine. It is used in Ayurveda to improve immunity, useful in digestion and promotes body’s immunity and strength. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all the above drugs in equal quantity (1 part each). 
 Properly mixed all the ingredients in a kharal yantra and give snuhi ksheera (extracts of Euphorbia nerifolia ) bhavna. 
 Make ½ rati tablets (62 mg) and let them dry. 
 Kept these tablets in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Udrari rasa is a herbo-mineral composition. The ingredients in this formulation have digestive properties. They digest the Aama which is an endotoxin in our gut. Amaltas have purgative properties also. These all are helpful in ascitic problems.
sections.indications:
Ascitis (Specially in females) 
 Indigestion 
 Abdominal pain 
 Constipation
sections.dosage:
1 tablet twice a day with extracts of Imli ( Tamarindus indica ). 
 Cautions 

 Take under medical supervision. 
 Avoid in pregnancy. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Shunthi – The latin name of shunthi is Zingiber officinale. It is very beneficial in gastric and digestive issues. This is effective in bloating, diarrhea and abdominal pain. Shunthi provides strength to the nervous system and sustains normal functioning of the body. 
 Maricha – Maricha also known as Piper nigrum. This increases the gastric secretions and enhances the peristaltic movements of the gut, thus improving the function of the digestive system. It has a pungent taste. It stimulates the appetite and possesses antibacterial properties. 
 Pippali – Pippali is known as Piper longum. This possesses rejuvenating, antacid, analgesic, and appetite stimulant properties thus very effective in diarrhea, pain in stomach, indigestion etc. 
 Haritaki Churna – Haritaki is known as Terminalia chebula. It promotes digestion and improves strength. It is effective in indigestion, liver and spleen problems, cough, asthma etc. 
 Chitrak – This is called Plumbago zeylanica. Due to pungent and hot properties, it acts as an appetizer and digestant. It is useful in indigestion, anorexia, abdominal pain. 
 Amalaki Churna ( Powder of Emblica officinalis ): It improves digestion. It is effective in indigestion, constipation etc. It pacifies all three dosha (Vata, Pitta and Kapha). It improves brain function by providing nourishment to the brain. 
 Bibhitaki Churna ( Powder of Terminalia bellerica ) – It has an astringent taste. It pacifies pitta and kapha dosha. It acts as a laxative and antitussive. 

 Quantity of Ingredients 
 All drugs in equal quantity (20 gms) except loha bhasma (440 gm). 
 Method of Preparation 

 Give proper frolement to above drugs in a kharal yantra. 
 Then give water bhavna for 1 day and mix properly this mixture. 
 Make 500 mg tablet and let them dry. 
 Kept these tablets in glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 This is a herbo-mineral composition. It is effective for the treatment of seizures and other psychological conditions. The ingredients in this formulation are useful in improving digestion and provide strength to the nervous system.

sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Trikatu – Trikatu includes Shunthi ( Zingiber officinale ), Maricha ( Piper nigrum ), Pippali ( Piper longum ). Trikatu is well known for its numerous health benefits. It is very beneficial in respiratory disorders such as asthma, rhinitis, sinusitis, cough, cold etc. It balances the tridosha and maintains the normal functioning of the body. 
 Shuddha Manahshila ( Realgar ) – It is very useful in upper respiratory tract infections. It pacifies all the three dosha and does detoxification of the body. It alleviates all the harmful toxins and makes it free from all the ailments. 
 Katuki ( Picrorhiza kurroa ) – Katuki is mainly known for its hepatoprotective property. It strengthens the functioning of the liver and spleen. It mainly pacifies Pitta dosha and improves digestive fire. It also enhances the function of nerves.   
 Vacha ( Acorus calamus ) – It is very good for memory loss, Alzheimer disease, anxiety, depression and other psychosomatic disorders. It improves the function of nerves and strengthens the CNS. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make a fine powder of above drugs. 
 Give proper frolement with cow’s urine. 
 Make suppositories of this mixture and let them dry. 
 Kept these suppositories in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Unmada bhanjani vatika is a herbo-mineral composition. This Ayurvedic formulation is good for psychological disorders. It improves brain function by providing strength to the nervous system.

name: Unmada Gajankush Ras

sections.introduction: Unmada gajankush rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this are effective in digestive and mental problems.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – 75 gms 
 Shuddha Tamra Churna – 25 gms 
 Shuddha Dhatura Beej – 25 gms 
 Abhrak Bhasma – 25 gms 
 Shuddha Gandhak – 325 gms 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – 25 gms
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – It is a pure form of mercury (Hg). Parada is a silver coloured liquid metal also called as Quicksilver which is very effective. It balances all the three doshas (Vata, Pitta and Kapha). This improves the brain function and assists in relieving various psychological disorders. 
 Shuddha Gandha – Sulphur is also used as medicine in various diseases.  This is a non-metallic solid element found in nature. In Ayurveda it is first detoxified to get shuddha Gandhak. It acts as laxative and alterative. Pure form of sulphur is used as Rasayan (Rejuvenate). It improves digestion by stimulating digestive fire and is helpful in psychological condition also. 
 Abhrak Bhasma (Calcined mica) – It is useful in digestive problems. It provides nutrition to the Rasadi dhatus (bodily tissues) and improves brain function by providing nourishment to the brain tissues. 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha ( Aconitum ferox ) – This is used as medicine after detoxification. It has antipyretic and diaphoretic properties. It pacifies vata, pitta and kapha dosha. It improves the brain function by strengthening the neuron’s activity. 

 Bhavna Dravya (Ingredients) 

 Dhatura Patra Swaras (Extracts of Datura metel ) 
 Pippali Swaras (Extracts of Piper longum ) 
 Kupilu Kwath (Decoction of Strychnos nuxvomica ) 

 Method of Preparation 

 Keep the Parada in kharal yantra and properly mix this parada with the Extracts of Dhatura patra for 3 days. 
 Again give proper frolement to this mixture with the extracts of Pippali swaras and the extracts of Kupilu kwath for 3 days. 
 Make a pishti of this parada by adding shudha Tamra churna. 
 Then take shuddha Gandhak in a pot and place this pishti over this gandhak and give cooked this in a gajput yantra. 
 Do this procedure 2- 3 times. 
 Make 325 mg tablets and let them dry. 
 Kept these tablets in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Unmada gajankush rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this are very effective in mental illness. They provide strength to the nerves of the nervous system. The ingredients also act as digestive means they improve digestive power by stimulating digestive fire.
sections.indications:
Unmada (obsessive compulsive disorders) 
 Epilepsy 
 Fever
sections.dosage:
1 tablet twice a day with warm ghee. 
 Cautions 

 Avoid in pregnancy and lactating women. 
 Take under the medical supervision. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Unmada Gajkesari rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. The ingredients in this are effective in digestion and mental conditions.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – 50 gms 
 Shuddha Gandhak – 50 gms 
 Shuddha Manahshila (Realgar) – 50 gms 
 Shuddha Dhatura Beej (Seeds of Datura metel ) – 50 gms
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – Parada is known as mercury. Its purified form is used as medicine. It holds numerous health benefits which are already mentioned in our ancient texts. It mainly balances the tridosha and is effective in all types of nervous and psychological disorders. It has antioxidant, antipyretic, immune modulating and anti- cancerous properties thus, improves the coordination between the neurons. 
 Shuddha Gandhak – It is also known as purified Sulphur. It is a wonderful digestive stimulant which corrects the balance of agni (fire) and increases the secretion of gastric juices in the stomach. It also pacifies the vitiated dosha and is very useful in vata related disorders. This helps in sustaining the nervous system healthy and also acts as laxative and purgative . 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take all the above ingredients in equal quantity (50 gms). 
 Firstly make a kajjali from Parada and gandhak. 
 Give proper frolement by adding Manahshila in this kajjali. 
 Then again add shudha powder of datura seeds and give 7 bhavna with decoction of Vacha ( Adhatoda vasica ). 
 After that again give 7 bhavna with the extracts of Brahmi ( Bacopa monnieri ) and let them dry under the sunlight. 
 Keep this mixture in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 This is an Ayurvedic formulation and this medicine is a herbo-mineral composition. This is effective in psychological conditions. They nourish the nerves of the nervous system. These herbs are useful in opening up the blocked channels in the blood vessels and nerves. Brahmi is also known as brain tonic. It enhances brain function too.
