 Hemagarbha-Pottali Rasa works best with: Guduchi Ghana, Sudarshan Churna, Mahasudarshan, Warm water. 
 3. Lung Injury Chronic Cough (Kshata-Ksheena) 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali Rasa works best with: Vasavaleha, Kantakari Ghrita, Sitopaladi + Ghee, Pippali Rasayana. 
 4. Severe Debility Wasting (Dhatu-Kshaya) 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Ashwagandha Lehyam, Drakshasava, Amritarishta, Ghee + Honey. 
 5. Loss of Appetite Indigestion 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Pippali, Shunthi, Jeerakarishta, Warm water/Honey. 
 6. Anemia With Weakness (Pandu) 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Punarnava Mandur, Drakshavaleha, Lohasava, Cow ghee. 
 7. Recurrent Infections 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Guduchi + Tulsi, Amalaki Rasayana, Sitopaladi, Chitrak Haritaki. 
 8. Post-TB Weakness 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Chyawanprash, Ashwagandha + Milk, Pippali Rasayana, Drakshasava. 
 9. Low Immunity (Ojas Kshaya) 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with: Brahma Rasayana, Amrit Ghrita, Guduchi Satva, Warm milk + Ghee. 
 10. Chronic Cardiac Diseases (Low LVEF) 
 Hemagarbha-Pottali works best with honey and Dashmoolarisht + Arjunarisht.

 Vata — (Strongly pacifies Vata — main action) 
 Kapha — (Moderately reduces Kapha) 
 Pitta — (Neutral to mildly balancing; does not aggravate Pitta) 
 Indications 
 
 Rajayakshma (Pulmonary Tuberculosis) 
 Dhatukshaya (Tissue depletion) 
 Chronic fever (Dirgha-kala jvara) 
 Kshata-ksheena (Lung injury with chronic debility) 
 Chronic breathlessness (Shvasa-kashtata) 
 Weight loss and cachexia (Karshya) 
 Immunodeficiency (Ojo-ksaya)

 Malaise and low vitality (Daurbalya)

 125 mg to 500 mg (1-4 ratti) To be taken with Pippali churna – 500 mg and Honey or ghee – 500 mg 
 Contraindications 
 
 Unsupervised Long-Term Use 
 
 Conclusion 
 Hemagarbha Pottali Rasa stands as a highly potent Rasoushadh (herbo-mineral formulation) crafted to address the deep-seated pathology of Rajayakshma (chronic wasting disorder). By combining the rejuvenative power of Svarna Bhasma (gold calx), the catalytic potency of Suta Bhasma (mercury–sulphur complex), the healing strength of Shuddha Gandhak (purified sulphur), and the metabolic activation of Chitraka root juice, this formulation nourishes depleted Dhatus (body tissues), strengthens Pranavaha and Rasavaha Srotas (respiratory and circulatory microchannels), restores Agni (digestive fire), and enhances immunity and vitality. It offers comprehensive support in chronic cough, fever, tissue depletion, weakness, and post-infectious debility, making it a superior Rasayana (rejuvenative) therapy for restoring strength, resilience, and long-term wellness in individuals suffering from Rajayakshma (chronic wasting disorder).

 Hinguleshwar ras is an effective Ayurvedic medicine to manage the various problems like chronic fever, headache, body ache, rheumatoid, joint pain etc. This medicine is quite good to manage the vata disorders. Moreover, anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic action of this medicine is known to be quite effective to alleviate the various symptoms like joint pain, inflammation, morning stiffness, etc. For the joint stiffness, this medicine works well to improve the blood circulation in the affected areas. It is greater pain reliever in the body pains. It is a good immunity booster and thus helps the body to fight against various infections. It helps to lower the high body temperature in various types of fever.

name: Hridayarnava Rasa

sections.overview: Hridayarnava Rasa – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Hridayarnava Rasa is an ayurvedic formulation that is known to have mixture of herbs and minerals. This formulation is known to treat the problems related with heart.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – Purified Mercury 
 Shuddha Gandhaka – Purified Sulphur 
 Tamra Bhasma – Bhasma prepared from Copper 

 To prepare water decoction from following: 

 Kakamachi – Solanum nigrum 
 Haritaki – Terminalia chebula 
 Vibhitaki – Terminalia bellirica 
 Amalaki – Emblica officinalis 

 Method of preparation 

 Take mercury and Sulphur up to 10 gram and copper up to 20 grams. Powder all the ingredients and keep aside. 
 Take herbs vibhitaki, amalaki, kakamachi and haritaki. Make the water decoction of these herbs by boiling these herbs in water. Boil the water till the water volume is reduced up to one fourth level. After boiling process, filter the mixture and collect the filtrate. The decoction is prepared. 
 Now take the powdered ingredients and ground with water decoction. 
 After this process, take the paste up to 125 to 250 mg according to need, make pills from this and dry the pills in last.
sections.dose: One tablet one to two times a day, before or after meals, with kakamachi water decoction.
sections.indications:
Cardiac disorder with breathing difficulty 
 Heaviness in chest 
 Kapha related heart problems
sections.contraindications:
Avoid in pregnancy and lactation. 
 Take the medicine under doctor’s prescription. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.overview: Jawsamhar Ras – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction: Fever (Jwara) is regarded in Ayurveda as a profound disturbance of the body–mind equilibrium, arising from the imbalance of Doshas along with impairment of Agni and accumulation of Ama. Classical texts describe Jwara as the foremost of diseases, as it affects both physical vitality and mental clarity. Ayurvedic management of fever emphasizes restoring digestive fire, clearing metabolic toxins, and supporting innate resilience rather than merely suppressing temperature. The formulation named JwarsaamharRas described here integrates purified mineral preparations with time-honored medicinal herbs, selected for their Jwaraghna, Deepana, Pachana, and Rasayana attributes.
sections.ingredients:
Purified Rasindoor – Mercuric sulphide (HgS) – 13 tola 
 Black Pepper – Piper nigrum – 2 tola 
 Long Pepper – Piper longum – 2 tola 
 Shunthi – Zingiber officinale – 2 tola 
 Kutki – Picrorhiza kurroa – 2 tola 
 Neem bark (Inner bark) – Azadirachta indica – 2 tola 
 Kutaja bark – Holarrhena antidysenterica – 2 tola 
 Nagarmotha – Cyperus rotundus – 2 tola 
 Sarson – Brassica juncea – 2 tola 
 Seeds of Indrajau (Kutaja) – Holarrhena antidysenterica (seeds) – 2 tola 
 Suhaga – Borax (Sodium borate) – 2 tola 
 Raktachandan – Pterocarpus santalinus – 2 tola 
 Atees (Ativisha) – Aconitum heterophyllum – 2 tola 
 Mameera – Coptis teeta – 2 tola
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Purified Rasindoor (Mercuric Sulphide, HgS) 

In Ayurveda, Rasindoor is Ushna, Tikshna, and Yogavahi, helping penetrate deep tissues and balance aggravated Vata–Kapha in Sannipatajwara. It is traditionally processed to enhance safety and bioavailability. Classical texts emphasize its role in restoring Agni. Modern mineral pharmacology recognizes HgS as chemically stable when properly processed.

 2. Black Pepper (Piper Nigrum) 

Black pepper is Ushna, Tikshna, and Deepana, aiding digestion and Amapachana in fever. Piperine enhances bioavailability of other compounds. Modern studies show antipyretic and immunomodulatory activity through cytokine regulation.

 3. Long Pepper (Piper Longum) 

Pippali balances Vata–Kapha and rejuvenates weakened Agni during chronic or recurrent fever. It acts as Rasayana in post-fever debility. Research suggests piperlongumine exhibits anti-inflammatory and immune-supportive effects.

 4. Pippali (Fruit) (Piper Longum) 

The fruit form is milder yet potent in Jwara associated with respiratory involvement. Ayurveda values it for Pranavaha srotas support. Scientific studies show antioxidant and antipyretic properties.

 5. Kutki (Picrorhiza Kurroa) 

Kutki is Tikta, Sheeta, and Pitta-shamaka, useful in fevers with liver involvement. It supports detoxification and bile regulation. Modern research highlights hepatoprotective and anti-inflammatory effects.

sections.introduction: Jwalanal ras is an Ayurvedic herbal formulation. It is based on herbal and mineral composition. It is used in the treatment of indigestion.
sections.ingredients:
Bhang Churna (Powder of Cannabis sativa ) – 9 parts

 Sarjikakshara (Sodium carbonate) – 1 part 
 Shuddha Parada (Purified Mercury) – 1 part

sections.description_of_ingredients:
Bhang Churna – This is used in ayurveda for its health benefits. It has a sedative effect. In Ayurveda, it is used in treating low digestion, IBS, insomnia and pains. It comes under the Upavisha group which means sub-toxic herbs. It balances vata and kapha dosha. 
   Shigru Twak Churna – This Ayurvedic herb has been used as a part of diet in India since ages. It is used in the treatment of the digestive, heart and circulatory system. It shows good results in indigestion. 
 Yavakshar – This is an alkali preparation which is prepared from Barley. It promotes digestion and is helpful in digesting Aama dosha (Endotoxins). It is beneficial in indigestion, bloating, diarrhea etc. 
 Sarjikakshara – It is an Ayurvedic medicine mainly indicated in abdominal pain and abdominal lump. It helps in kindling the digestive fire and improves digestion. It balances vata and kapha dosha. 
 Shuddha Parada – This detoxified mercury showed very good results in the treatment of digestive ailments. It has a digestant and appetizer action. It provides strength to the body. 
 Shuddha Gandhak – This is used in the Ayurvedic treatment after purification. It is light yellow in colour. It promotes good gut health and is also beneficial in skin diseases. 
 Pippali Churna – This herb is very best for digestive problems. It helps in proper digestion, stimulates digestive fire etc. It is also beneficial in throat infections. 
 Chavya Churna – This herb helps in treating coughs, asthma, abdominal pain, bloating etc. It also relieves constipation, improves digestion and also shows good effects in worm infestation. 
 Chitrakmool Churna – This Ayurvedic herb is good in treating digestive symptoms such as indigestion, constipation, bloating, abdominal distension etc. It helps in digestive ailment due to its deepan (Appetizer) and pachana (digestion) properties. 
 Shunthi Churna – This is also known as Ginger. It is quite a recognized Ayurvedic herb. It is very effective in poor digestion. It has an appetizer effect. It stimulates the appetite of the person. It helps in digestion of undigested food. It also helps in abdominal pain. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 In a kharal make a kajjali with a mixture of parad and gandhak. 
 Add rest of the powders in this kajjali and give 3 alternative bhavna with Bhanga swaras (Extracts of c annabis sativa ), shigru kwak swaras (Powder of Moringa oleifera ), chitrakmool kwath (Decoction of Plumbago zeylanica ) and Bhringraj swaras (Extracts of Eclipta alba ). 
 After drying, give light heat to this preparation. 
 After cooling take out this medicine and again give 7 bhavna with Adraka swaras (Extracts of Z i ngiber officinale ). 
 Make 250 mg tablet and dry them under the shadow. 
 Keep this formulation in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Jwalanal ras is a classical medicine. This formulation is used in digestive ailments. The ingredients help in increasing or enhancing the power of the digestive fire. The ingredients such as Shunthi, Pippali are very much effective in treating digestive disorders. They just promote good digestive health.
sections.indications:
Indigestion 
 Bloating 
 Abdominal distension 
 Constipation 
 Cardiac diseases
sections.dosage:
1 tablet twice a day with warm water 
 Caution 
 It should be taken under the medical advice. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Shuddha Parad (Purified Mercury) 
 Shuddha Parad acts as a Yogavahi, enhancing the potency and rapid action of other ingredients. It helps regulate Agni, supports systemic balance, and assists in breaking stubborn, chronic, or deep-seated fevers. 
 2. Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulfur) 
 Gandhak possesses UshnaVirya and Deepana–Pachana properties, helping digest Ama , a key causative factor in fever. It supports detoxification and stabilizes metabolic disturbances during febrile states. 
 3. Tamra Bhasma (Copper Calx) 
 Tamra Bhasma helps clear Srotorodha (channel obstruction) and supports liver and metabolic functions. By improving internal circulation and digestion, it aids in resolving fever associated with toxicity and congestion. 
 4. Shuddha Vatsanabha (Purified Aconite) 
 Vatsanabha exhibits strong Ushna and Tikshna properties, making it useful in severe fevers with chills, coldness, and collapse. It stimulates circulation and revives weakened physiological functions. 
 5. Shuddha Hingula (Purified Cinnabar) 
 Hingula supports Pranavaha and Rasavaha Srotas, helping stabilize vitality during intense fever. Its Sukshma nature allows deeper tissue penetration, assisting in rapid systemic correction. 
 6. Dhatura Seeds ( Datura spp. ) 
 Dhatura seeds help pacify Vata–Kapha–dominant fevers associated with spasms, restlessness, or respiratory distress. They support nervous system stability during high-grade or delirious fever states. 
 7. Godanti Bhasma (Gypsum Calx) 
 Godanti Bhasma has a Sheetala (cooling) effect , helping reduce excessive body heat and burning sensation. It is especially useful in Pitta-dominant fevers with headache and thirst. 
 8. Shuddha Manashila (Purified Realgar) 
 Manashila helps counter toxic and infectious factors in fever by supporting internal cleansing. Its Tikshna quality assists in resolving stubborn or irregular fevers. 
 9. Tankan (Purified Borax) 
 Tankan acts as a Kapha-shamaka and channel-clearing agent, aiding expectoration and reducing heaviness. It supports fever management when congestion and mucus accumulation are present. 
 10. Yashad Bhasma (Zinc Calx) 
 Yashad Bhasma supports tissue strength and metabolic balance during prolonged fevers. It helps stabilize Rasa and Rakta Dhatu , reducing debility associated with chronic febrile conditions. 
 11. Shuddha Jamalghota (Purified Croton Seeds) 
 Jamalghota promotes strong Pachana and Shodhana, helping expel deep-seated toxins contributing to fever. It supports elimination of accumulated Ama in stubborn conditions. 
 12. Black Snake Venom (Traditional Use) 
 In classical formulations, minute processed quantities act as a powerful stimulant , reviving vital functions in life-threatening fevers. It supports circulation and nervous system responsiveness in collapse-like states. 
 13. Swarnamakshik Bhasma (Chalcopyrite Calx) 
 Swarnamakshik Bhasma strengthens Agni and supports blood and metabolic functions. It helps manage fever associated with weakness, anemia, or chronic tissue depletion. 
 14. Loha Bhasma (Iron Calx) 
 Loha Bhasma nourishes Rakta Dhatu and improves strength during long-standing fevers. It supports recovery and prevents post-fever debility. 
 15. Vang Bhasma (Tin Calx) 
 Vang Bhasma stabilizes metabolism and supports nervous and reproductive tissues. In fever, it assists in restoring balance after prolonged systemic stress. 
 Method Of Preparation 

 Firstly make kajjali of Purified mercury and Purified sulphur by titurating in a decoction of Gokshura ( Tribulusterrestris) for 12 hours. Then dry it and prepare a fine powder. 
 Then sequentially add Sarpa-visha (Snake Venom) and Vatsanabha, triturating properly. After this, add Bhasma, Hingula, Manashila, Jamalgota, Sohaga, Datura etc, one by one and triturate thoroughly. 
 Then titurate this mixture in Aak (Calotropis) milk, Dashmoola decoction, and LaghuPanchamoola decoction for 12–12 hours, and prepare pills of ½ ratti each.
sections.indications_and_clinical_use:
This formulation is highly effective in acute and life-threatening fevers. It is especially beneficial in severe febrile conditions where common treatments fail. In Kapha-dominant fever, its effect appears immediately. When symptoms such as Fever reaching 104°F or above, Slow pulse, Severe heaviness, Distress from cold air or water, ltered consciousness, Difficulty in breathing, Chest congestion, Loss of physical strength are present, this medicine provides remarkable benefit. If excess stool accumulation is present in the abdomen, it should first be expelled using Eranda oil (castor oil) or similar purgatives. 
 In Vata-dominant fever, symptoms include Sudden onset, Tremors, Burning sensation, Pain, Numbness in legs, Abdominal movement, Delirium at high temperature, Dryness and accumulation of hard stool in intestines . After correcting constipation, administration of KalagnibhairavRas with ArkadiKwath gives relief . 
 Vata-Kapha-Dominant Fever- When fever presents with Shivering, Muscle pain, Fever exceeding 102°F, Digestive disturbance, Headache, Restlessness, Insomnia and Delirium this medicine becomes effective when given with Guduchi decoction along with Pippali, Tulsi, Trikatu, Lavanga, Kalimirch, Peepal, and Saunth, prepared as a decoction according to need. 
 When fever does not subside even after several days due to improper treatment or dietary negligence, the patient develops Severe weakness, Loss of strength, Pallor, Digestive failure, Persistent high fever (100–102°F). In this stage, administration of this Ras along with PravalPishti and BaladiVati acts as life-saving therapy. 
 Rat-Bite Fever – In fever caused by rat bite, bluish-red patches appear at various locations on the body, accompanied by muscle pain and Vata aggravation. To control intense pain and high fever, this Ras should be administered three times daily with Manjistha decoction or other Raktashodhak (Blood purifying) decoctions. 
 Plague Fever – Plague is an extremely fatal disease. If proper treatment is not administered immediately, the patient’s life comes under serious threat. In this condition, fever rises from 103°F to 107°F. If KalagniBhairavRas is administered in the initial stage, it yields beneficial results. 
 Pneumonia (PranavahaSrotas Disorder) – In pneumonia, one or both lungs are affected. When both lungs are involved, it is termed double pneumonia. As the disease progresses, lungs become filled with thick Kapha. When placed in water, it sinks, and air passages become blocked with Kapha, causing severe respiratory distress. Fever fluctuates between 102–104°F. Until Kapha and respiratory difficulty remain moderate, recovery is possible. If Kapha becomes excessive, the condition turns critical. In such advanced stages also, appropriate use of KalagniBhairavRas along with external therapy often yields success.
sections.dosage_and_adjuvant: ½ to 1 pill, administered 3 times daily at intervals of 2–3 hours. Give it with Arka juice, Tandulodaka (rice water), or Devadaru decoction.
sections.precautions:
Dosage should be adjusted after considering strength of disease, strength of patient, age, and digestive power. Excess dose in weak patients or in Pitta-dominant conditions can cause harm, while insufficient dose may fail in severe conditions. 
 Jamalgota is included in very small quantities. It may assist in stool elimination, but initially mild purgation should be induced separately if required. 
 In patients with a history of abdominal disorders, if abdominal discomfort is present, this medicine should be administered along with Roasted Jeera, BelgiriChurna or other appropriate digestive support. 
 This Ras should not be given to pregnant women or individuals with predominant Pitta constitution. 

 Conclusion 
 This classical formulation reflects the advanced clinical understanding of Ayurveda in managing severe and life-threatening fevers. By combining potent herbal, mineral, and animal-derived substances, it acts swiftly to correct Agni , clear Ama , and stabilize vital functions. The text emphasizes careful preparation, precise dosing, and patient-specific judgment, highlighting the responsibility of the physician in its use. When administered appropriately, the formulation demonstrates effectiveness in complex conditions such as high-grade fever, pneumonia, rat-bite fever, and plague-like states. This conclusion reinforces Ayurveda’s systematic, experience-based approach to acute care while stressing caution, skill, and classical wisdom.

When symptoms such as Fever reaching 104°F or above, Slow pulse, Severe heaviness, Distress from cold air or water, ltered consciousness, Difficulty in breathing, Chest congestion, Loss of physical strength are present, this medicine provides remarkable benefit. If excess stool accumulation is present in the abdomen, it should first be expelled using Eranda oil (castor oil) or similar purgatives. 
 In Vata-dominant fever, symptoms include Sudden onset, Tremors, Burning sensation, Pain, Numbness in legs, Abdominal movement, Delirium at high temperature, Dryness and accumulation of hard stool in intestines . After correcting constipation, administration of KalagnibhairavRas with ArkadiKwath gives relief . 
 Vata-Kapha-Dominant Fever- When fever presents with Shivering, Muscle pain, Fever exceeding 102°F, Digestive disturbance, Headache, Restlessness, Insomnia and Delirium this medicine becomes effective when given with Guduchi decoction along with Pippali, Tulsi, Trikatu, Lavanga, Kalimirch, Peepal, and Saunth, prepared as a decoction according to need. 
 When fever does not subside even after several days due to improper treatment or dietary negligence, the patient develops Severe weakness, Loss of strength, Pallor, Digestive failure, Persistent high fever (100–102°F). In this stage, administration of this Ras along with PravalPishti and BaladiVati acts as life-saving therapy. 
 Rat-Bite Fever – In fever caused by rat bite, bluish-red patches appear at various locations on the body, accompanied by muscle pain and Vata aggravation. To control intense pain and high fever, this Ras should be administered three times daily with Manjistha decoction or other Raktashodhak (Blood purifying) decoctions. 
 Plague Fever – Plague is an extremely fatal disease. If proper treatment is not administered immediately, the patient’s life comes under serious threat. In this condition, fever rises from 103°F to 107°F. If KalagniBhairavRas is administered in the initial stage, it yields beneficial results. 
 Pneumonia (PranavahaSrotas Disorder) – In pneumonia, one or both lungs are affected. When both lungs are involved, it is termed double pneumonia. As the disease progresses, lungs become filled with thick Kapha. When placed in water, it sinks, and air passages become blocked with Kapha, causing severe respiratory distress. Fever fluctuates between 102–104°F. Until Kapha and respiratory difficulty remain moderate, recovery is possible. If Kapha becomes excessive, the condition turns critical. In such advanced stages also, appropriate use of KalagniBhairavRas along with external therapy often yields success. 
 
 Dosage and Adjuvant 
 ½ to 1 pill, administered 3 times daily at intervals of 2–3 hours. Give it with Arka juice, Tandulodaka (rice water), or Devadaru decoction. 
 Precautions 
 
 Dosage should be adjusted after considering strength of disease, strength of patient, age, and digestive power. Excess dose in weak patients or in Pitta-dominant conditions can cause harm, while insufficient dose may fail in severe conditions. 
 Jamalgota is included in very small quantities. It may assist in stool elimination, but initially mild purgation should be induced separately if required. 
 In patients with a history of abdominal disorders, if abdominal discomfort is present, this medicine should be administered along with Roasted Jeera, BelgiriChurna or other appropriate digestive support. 
 This Ras should not be given to pregnant women or individuals with predominant Pitta constitution. 
 
 Conclusion 
 This classical formulation reflects the advanced clinical understanding of Ayurveda in managing severe and life-threatening fevers. By combining potent herbal, mineral, and animal-derived substances, it acts swiftly to correct Agni , clear Ama , and stabilize vital functions. sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Shuddha Parad (Purified Mercury) 

In Ayurveda, it acts as a Yogavahi, improving drug delivery and cellular penetration. Scientifically, properly processed mercury sulfide forms (used in Rasashastra) show enhanced bioavailability and catalytic action, helping regulate metabolic and immune responses when used in classical formulations.

 2. Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulfur) 

Known for Jwaraghna and Krimighna actions. Sulfur exhibits antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties, supporting detoxification and immune modulation during infectious and inflammatory fevers.

 3. Shuddha Vatsanabha (Purified Aconitum ferox) 

After classical detoxification, its alkaloids (e.g., aconitine derivatives in reduced toxicity form) stimulate digestion, circulation, and thermoregulation, helping resolve severe, Vata-Kapha dominant fevers.

 4. Shuddha Manshila (Purified Arsenic Disulfide) 

Traditionally used in chronic and relapsing fevers. Scientifically, arsenic compounds in controlled, processed forms exhibit immunomodulatory and antimicrobial activity, aiding fever reduction under strict Ayurvedic purification principles.

 5. Swarn Makshik (Calcined Copper-Iron Sulfide) 

Acts on Rasavaha and Raktavaha srotas. Copper and iron compounds support enzymatic activity, hematinic function, and immune defense, helping correct metabolic toxins (Ama) linked to fever.

 6. Suhaga (Borax) 

It facilitates drug penetration and digestion. Boron compounds exhibit mild antimicrobial and metabolic regulatory effects, supporting antipyretic action indirectly by improving digestion and Ama clearance.

 7. Marica (Black Pepper – Piper nigrum) 

It contains piperine, proven to enhance bioavailability, stimulate digestive enzymes, and show anti-inflammatory and antipyretic effects, making it valuable in fever management.

 8. Pippali (Long Pepper – Piper longum) 

It is rich in piperlongumine and piperine, which demonstrate immunomodulatory, anti-inflammatory, and respiratory-supportive effects, beneficial in fevers with Kapha involvement.

 9. Sonth (Dry Ginger – Zingiber officinale) 

It contains gingerols and shogaols, known for antipyretic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant actions; promotes sweating, relieves myalgia, and supports digestion during fever.

Abstract 
 Ayurveda is an ancient medicine science which has a solution for each and every ailment. In ayurveda the prime importance has been given to jatharagni (digestive fire) and acharyas mentioned that every disease is due to low digestive fire. In today’s world almost every person is suffering from indigestion. Digestion is a process in which there is breakdown of food items into small pieces so that the essential nutrients get absorbed by the blood. What if our digestion gets disturbed? As per ayurveda , the primary cause of this is imbalance pitta. So for managing pitta, we are going to put a limelight on a classical herbo-mineral formulation named kamdudha ras and its tremendous health benefits.
sections.introduction:
Kamdudha ras is an ancient herbomineral classical ayurvedic formulation in tablet form. It is widely used in ayurvedic practice for the management of gastritis and bleeding disorders. It also promotes digestion, relieves burning sensation, vertigo, nausea, vomiting etc. 
 Classical Indication 
 Raktaja vikara
sections.ingredients:
Mukta pishti 
 Praval pishti 
 Shukti pishti 
 Kapardak bhasma 
 Shankh bhasma 
 Shuddha sonageru 
 Giloy satva
sections.description_of_the_ingredients:
Mukta pishti (calx of pearl) – It normalises kapha and pitta dosha and is very good for burning sensation in feet and hands. Mukta is a rejuvenator which nourishes the body very well. 
 Praval pishti (Calx of coral) – Praval is a wonderful gemstone which assists in managing raktapitta (bleeding disorders), kasa (cough), eye disorders and weak digestion. 
 Shukti pishti (Pearl oyster shell) – Shukti pshti mainly pacifies pitta dosha and aids in relieving symptoms of indigestion, diarrhea, bloating, acid reflux , gastritis etc. 
 Kapardak bhasma (Calx of marine shell) – Kapardak bhasma normalizes vata and kapha dosha due to its katu (pungent) rasa and ushna (hot) properties. It helps in relieving pain, IBS, Tuberculosis and many other disorders. 
 Shankh bhasma (Conch shell) – It possess Antacid, Stool binding agent, Anti-diarrheal, Appetite stimulant and Digestive stimulant, Antispasmodic, Anti-inflammatory (effects appear on liver, spleen and intestines), Calcium Supplement (not used alone), Antioxidant and Anti-emetic properties. Thus, detoxifies the body and sustains its normal functioning. 
 Shuddha sonageru (Purified ochre) – It is very beneficial in bleeding disorders, vomiting, hiccups due to its cold in potency, sweet and soft in nature. 
 Giloy satva (Extract of Tinospora cordifolia ) – Giloy is a wonderful herb which assists  in managing all types of disorders by boosting immunity of the body. It possesses antioxidants, anticancer, anti-inflammatory and various other properties. So it detoxifies the cells and increases the ability of the body to fight the infections. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Take all the ingredients in equal proportion 
 And now do mardan (ticturation) in the kharal yantra 
 When all the ingredients are properly mixed then prepare a tablet of 1-3 ratti accordingly. 
 Store it in a airtight glass container 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Followings are the properties:- 

 Kamdudha ras sheet veerya (cold potency), kshobhanasahak () and shakti dayak (strengthens the body). It also pacifies pachan kriya (Increased metabolism), rudhirabhisaran (bleeding), vata vahana (regulation of vata dosha in the body), mutramarga (urinary tract). This is a wonderful rasayan which can be used in all types of pitta disorders. 
 In bleeding disorders kamdudha ras is very beneficial but it should be given with durva swaras (juice of Cynodon dactylon ) and pomegranate juice. We can also use amla murabba with kamdudha ras in blood disorders.  
 Headache due to pitta elevation – In this type of  condition, it should be given with makkan (butter) and dharoshan dudh (Fresh milk of cow). This combination will alleviate excessive pitta from the body and maintain the normal state of tridosha. 
 Amlapitta (Acid reflux) – In acid reflux, it is advised to take kamdudha ras with sutshekhar ras, amla swaras, cow’s ghee. 
 In diarrhea , kamdudha ras is very good medicine which helps in sustaining the electrolyte imbalance and normalise them with their pitta pacifying action. 
 In pitta predominant unmada (Psychological disorders) – Kamdudha ras is also useful in managing pitta predominant Unmada if given with 2 masha (1944 mg) brahmi ( bacopa monnieri ) churna or shankhpushpi ( Convolvulus pluricaulis ) churna. 
 In gynecological issues , it should be given with rice water and cow’s milk 
 In diabetes it is advised to take with Pippali churna ( Piper longum ) 
 In vertigo, Kamdudha ras should be taken with arjuna bark powder (if Vertigo is due to poor circulation), Jatamansi churna (If vertigo is due to anxiety), Drakshavaleha (if vertigo is due to Anemia), Chandi bhasma and sarivadi vati (if vertigo is due to inner ear problem) etc.

sections.ingredients:

 Shuddha gandhaka – Calcinated and purified sulphur 
 Saunth – Zingiber officinale 
 Maricha – Piper nigrum 
 Pippali – Piper longum 
 Tamra bhasma – Calcinated and purified copper 
 Loha bhsama – Calcinated and purified iron 
 Kateli – Solanum surattense 
 Kutki – Picrorhiza kurroa 
 Dhattura – Datura stramonium 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take the ingredients in equal quantity. 
 Take mercury and Sulphur, mix till the minerals lose its shine and form like kajali. 
 Now mix this kajali with loha and tamra bhsama mixture. 
 Take the ingredients saunth, pippali and maricha. Powder the ingredients and mix with kateli flower’s juice in mortar pestle for 6 hours. 
 After then tincture with kutki’s kwath and dhattura’s leaves. 
 Now take the paste up to 125 mg and make its pills.

name: Karpura Rasa

sections.overview:
Karpura Rasa – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Reference : Reference– Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Atisaaradhikara, Verse 125-126. A.F.I.- Part 1 – 20:7

 Abstract 

Targeting diarrhoeal disease at multiple levels—from infected lumen to febrile systemic response-this classical herbo-mineral formulation Karpura rasa unites Shuddha Hingula (purified Cinnabar), Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum), Musta (Cyperus rotundus), Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica), Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans) and Karpurra (Cinnamomum camphora) into a single synergistic therapy. Quick stool-binding and flow-checking action, paired with strong anti-amoebic, antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory support, means this formulation does far more than just “stop motions” for a while. It gently calms an overstimulated gut, tackles the infection smouldering behind repeated loose stools and helps the intestines find their normal rhythm again, so the person feels lighter, safer and more in control of everyday life.
sections.introduction:
Karpura Rasa is a classical herbo-mineral formulation, meaning a carefully balanced preparation made from processed minerals and medicinal herbs as a single therapeutic compound. The name “Karpura Rasa – literally means “camphor-based essence,” highlighting a formulation in which camphor is one of the key active principles. It is indicated in acute and chronic diarrhoea, diarrhoea with fever and bloody loose stools, helping to arrest excessive bowel movements, calm abdominal cramps and correct impaired digestive fire while supporting deeper restoration of intestinal balance.

 Classical Indication 
 Atisaar (Diarrhea)
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Hingula – Purified and processed Cinnabar. 
 Ahiphena – Papaver somniferum 
 Musta – Cyperus rotundus 
 Indrayava – Holarrhena antidysenterica 
 Jatiphala – Myristica fragrans 
 Karpura – Cinnamomum camphora
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Shuddha Hingula (Purified Cinnabar) 

Shuddha Hingula (Purified Cinnabar), is described with tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light), snigdha (unctuous) and sara (mobile) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). In Karpura Ras this acts as a yogavahi (catalytic carrier), enhancing penetration of the other drugs, stimulating agni and helping to burn ama (endotoxins), which supports control of fever and systemic toxicity in diarrhoeal conditions.

 2. Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum) 

Ahiphena (opium)- latex of Papaver somniferum, has tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa with slight madhura (sweet) note, ruksha (dry), laghu (light), sukshma (subtle) and vyavayi (rapidly spreading) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Its alkaloids such as morphine and codeine reduce intestinal motility, give strong stambhana (checking of excessive flow) and relieve shoola (colicky pain), so stool frequency and cramps fall quickly in acute and chronic diarrhoea.

 3. Musta (Cyperus rotundus) 

Musta (Cyperus rotundus), shows tikta (bitter), katu (pungent) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light) and ruksha (dry) guna, predominantly sheeta (anushna-sheeta – mildly cooling) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Its essential oils like cyperene with flavonoids are antispasmodic, antipyretic and antimicrobial, thus improving digestive fire, drying intestinal kleda (excess fluid) and helping to bind stools while lowering associated jvara (fever).

 4. Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica) 

Indrayava- seeds of Kutaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica), has tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light) and ruksha (dry) guna, sheeta virya (cold potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). The alkaloids such as conessine give powerful anti-amoebic, antibacterial and antidiarrhoeal action, directly attacking dysentery organisms, reducing mucosal inflammation and effectively stopping mucus and blood loss in rakta pravahika (bloody diarrhoea).

 5. Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans) 

Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans), carries tikta (bitter), katu (pungent), kashaya (astringent) with slight madhura rasa (sweet taste), laghu (light), snigdha (unctuous) and tikshna (sharp) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Nutmeg has volatile oils such as myristicin, elemicin and eugenol act as antispasmodic, carminative, antimicrobial and mild sedatives, reducing intestinal spasm and gas and reinforcing grahi (stool-binding) effect, especially in chronic low-grade diarrhoea.

 6. Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora) 

Karpura Cinnamomum camphora, exhibits katu (pungent) and tikta (bitter) rasa, laghu (light), ruksha (dry) and tikshna (sharp) guna, systemically sheeta virya (cold potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Natural camphor and related terpenoids provide antimicrobial, antispasmodic, mildly analgesic and carminative actions, quickly calming excessive peristalsis, reducing gut spasms and inhibiting pathogens so that, in combination with the other ingredients, Karpura Ras efficiently manages acute and chronic diarrhoea, diarrhoea with fever and bloody loose stools.

 Method Of Preparation 

 All six ingredients of Karpura Rasa are taken in equal parts in their purified form (Shuddha Hingula – purified Cinnabar, Ahiphena – Papaver somniferum, Mukta, Indrayava – Holarrhena antidysenterica, Jatiphala – Myristica fragrans and Karpura – Cinnamomum camphora). 
 Each drug is powdered very finely, then all powders are mixed thoroughly to achieve a uniform blend. 
 A sufficient quantity of clean water is added gradually to this mixture and soft dough-like paste is made. 
 From this paste, small tablets (around 125–250 mg each) are rolled or shaped. 
 The tablets are dried completely in shade and then stored in an airtight glass container to protect their volatile and delicate components. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Jvara-Atisara (Diarrhoea With Fever) 

Karpura Rasa as a short-term antidiarrhoeal to quickly reduce the frequency of stools and colicky pain. The combination of Karpura Rasa with Guduchi-based medicines such as Guduchi Ghana Vati or Amritarishta to lower fever, support immunity and prevent recurrence. Honey or lukewarm water works well as anupana (adjuvant).

 Pakva-Atisara And Malabsorption / Chronic Loose Stools 

Karpura Rasa with Kutaja preparations such as Kutajghan Vati or Kutajarishta, with anupana of takra (buttermilk) or thin rice-gruel after meals, according to the degree of weakness and digestive fire.

 Rakta Pravahika And Dysentery Associated With Blood 

Karpura Rasa with Praval-, Mukta- or Kamdudha-based Pitta-pacifying medicines, with anupana of cold water, goat’s milk or isabgol husk slurry after food, selected as per intensity of burning and bleeding.

 Acute Diarrhoea, Gastro-Enteritis And Infective Gastrointestinal Conditions 

Karpura Rasa with Kutajavaleha, Musta Churna or Bilvadi Churna, with anupana of jeera-water, musta-kashaya or light rice-gruel, used during the acute phase until stool frequency, cramps and nausea settle.

 Impact On Dosha 

Karpura Rasa primarily balances Vata and Kapha while needing some caution in strong Pitta prakriti or Pitta-dominant states. Karpura Rasa pacifies Vata by its warm, channel-clearing, antispasmodic action and pain-relieving effect, which calms excessive peristalsis and colic in diarrhoea. At the same time it reduces Kapha by drying excess mucus and kleda in the gut and improving digestive fire, so Kapha-related heaviness, mucus-laden stools and ama formation decrease.


Karpura Rasa has a mixed impact on Pitta. The cooling effect of camphor and the stool-binding nature of absorbent drugs can ease bleeding, burning and fever, so mild to moderate Pitta aggravation in diarrhoea usually settles. However, the whole formulation is relatively heated and strongly binding, so people with very high Pitta, very hot constituents, or those already suffering from active gastritis, intense burning or heavy bleeding should take it only in lower doses, for a short period, and strictly under medical supervision.
sections.indications:
Diarrhoea – acute and chronic 
 Diarrhoea associated with fever 
 Bloody diarrhoea / Dysentery 
 Malabsorption and irritable bowel-type conditions 
 Gastro-enteritis and other inflammatory gastrointestinal conditions 
 General gastrointestinal complaints with cramps, mucus and weakness
sections.dosage_and_adjuvants:
For Karpura Rasa, adult doses are usually very small and always need medical supervision.


 Dose (adult) : 125 mg tablet once or twice daily, before or after food, as directed by an Ayurvedic physician.

 Common Anupana (Adjuvant) 

 Honey or honey with a little ghee (not in equal quantity) in Vata-Kapha-dominant diarrhoea. 
 Musta (Cyperus rotundus) decoction, cumin water or thin rice-gruel in diarrhoea, dysentery and gastro-enteritis to support digestion and absorbency.
sections.contraindications_and_precautions: Karpura Rasa needs careful, short-term, supervised use because it is a potent herbo-mineral and opium-containing formulation.
sections.contraindications:
Pregnancy and lactation. 
 Infants and children (unless strictly supervised by an Ayurvedic physician). 
 Known allergy or intolerance to camphor, opium, mercury compounds or other ingredients. 
 Severe liver or kidney disease, uncontrolled hypertension, serious heart or neurological disorders. 
 Marked Pitta aggravation with strong burning, active gastritis or peptic ulcer unless adjusted and closely monitored.
sections.precautions:
Always use the minimum effective dose, for a limited duration, under professional guidance. 
 Avoid self-medication, especially using higher or more frequent doses, due to risk of opium- and metal-related toxicity. 
 Monitor for warning signs such as burning in stomach or throat, nausea, dizziness, confusion, unusual bleeding, rash or breathing difficulty; stop and seek urgent care if these occur. 
 Use cautiously with other strong modern medicines (especially sedatives, pain-killers, anticoagulants and hepatotoxic drugs); keep at least a 30 minute gap and coordinate with both treating doctors. 
 Store securely away from children and vulnerable individuals; never exceed the prescribed course or share leftover tablets with others. 

 Conclusion 

Karpura Rasa is a focused, short-term medication for acute and chronic diarrhoeal disorders, especially when loose stools are accompanied by fever, colic or blood. Karpura Rasa – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Reference : Reference– Bhaishajya Ratnavali, Atisaaradhikara, Verse 125-126. A.F.I.- Part 1 – 20:7
 
 Abstract 
 
Targeting diarrhoeal disease at multiple levels—from infected lumen to febrile systemic response-this classical herbo-mineral formulation Karpura rasa unites Shuddha Hingula (purified Cinnabar), Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum), Musta (Cyperus rotundus), Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica), Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans) and Karpurra (Cinnamomum camphora) into a single synergistic therapy. Quick stool-binding and flow-checking action, paired with strong anti-amoebic, antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory support, means this formulation does far more than just “stop motions” for a while. It gently calms an overstimulated gut, tackles the infection smouldering behind repeated loose stools and helps the intestines find their normal rhythm again, so the person feels lighter, safer and more in control of everyday life.
 
 Introduction 
 
Karpura Rasa is a classical herbo-mineral formulation, meaning a carefully balanced preparation made from processed minerals and medicinal herbs as a single therapeutic compound. The name “Karpura Rasa – literally means “camphor-based essence,” highlighting a formulation in which camphor is one of the key active principles. It is indicated in acute and chronic diarrhoea, diarrhoea with fever and bloody loose stools, helping to arrest excessive bowel movements, calm abdominal cramps and correct impaired digestive fire while supporting deeper restoration of intestinal balance.
 
 Classical Indication 
 Atisaar (Diarrhea) 
 Ingredients 
 
 Shuddha Hingula – Purified and processed Cinnabar. 
 Ahiphena – Papaver somniferum 
 Musta – Cyperus rotundus 
 Indrayava – Holarrhena antidysenterica 
 Jatiphala – Myristica fragrans 
 Karpura – Cinnamomum camphora 
 
 Description Of Ingredients 
 1. Shuddha Hingula (Purified Cinnabar) 
 
Shuddha Hingula (Purified Cinnabar), is described with tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light), snigdha (unctuous) and sara (mobile) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). In Karpura Ras this acts as a yogavahi (catalytic carrier), enhancing penetration of the other drugs, stimulating agni and helping to burn ama (endotoxins), which supports control of fever and systemic toxicity in diarrhoeal conditions.
 
 2. Ahiphena (Papaver somniferum) 
 
Ahiphena (opium)- latex of Papaver somniferum, has tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa with slight madhura (sweet) note, ruksha (dry), laghu (light), sukshma (subtle) and vyavayi (rapidly spreading) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Its alkaloids such as morphine and codeine reduce intestinal motility, give strong stambhana (checking of excessive flow) and relieve shoola (colicky pain), so stool frequency and cramps fall quickly in acute and chronic diarrhoea.
 
 3. Musta (Cyperus rotundus) 
 
Musta (Cyperus rotundus), shows tikta (bitter), katu (pungent) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light) and ruksha (dry) guna, predominantly sheeta (anushna-sheeta – mildly cooling) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Its essential oils like cyperene with flavonoids are antispasmodic, antipyretic and antimicrobial, thus improving digestive fire, drying intestinal kleda (excess fluid) and helping to bind stools while lowering associated jvara (fever).
 
 4. Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica) 
 
Indrayava- seeds of Kutaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica), has tikta (bitter) and kashaya (astringent) rasa, laghu (light) and ruksha (dry) guna, sheeta virya (cold potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). The alkaloids such as conessine give powerful anti-amoebic, antibacterial and antidiarrhoeal action, directly attacking dysentery organisms, reducing mucosal inflammation and effectively stopping mucus and blood loss in rakta pravahika (bloody diarrhoea).
 
 5. Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans) 
 
Jatiphala (Myristica fragrans), carries tikta (bitter), katu (pungent), kashaya (astringent) with slight madhura rasa (sweet taste), laghu (light), snigdha (unctuous) and tikshna (sharp) guna, ushna virya (hot potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Nutmeg has volatile oils such as myristicin, elemicin and eugenol act as antispasmodic, carminative, antimicrobial and mild sedatives, reducing intestinal spasm and gas and reinforcing grahi (stool-binding) effect, especially in chronic low-grade diarrhoea.
 
 6. Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora) 
 
Karpura Cinnamomum camphora, exhibits katu (pungent) and tikta (bitter) rasa, laghu (light), ruksha (dry) and tikshna (sharp) guna, systemically sheeta virya (cold potency) and katu vipaka (pungent post-digestive effect). Natural camphor and related terpenoids provide antimicrobial, antispasmodic, mildly analgesic and carminative actions, quickly calming excessive peristalsis, reducing gut spasms and inhibiting pathogens so that, in combination with the other ingredients, Karpura Ras efficiently manages acute and chronic diarrhoea, diarrhoea with fever and bloody loose stools.
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 
 All six ingredients of Karpura Rasa are taken in equal parts in their purified form (Shuddha Hingula – purified Cinnabar, Ahiphena – Papaver somniferum, Mukta, Indrayava – Holarrhena antidysenterica, Jatiphala – Myristica fragrans and Karpura – Cinnamomum camphora). 
 Each drug is powdered very finely, then all powders are mixed thoroughly to achieve a uniform blend. 
 A sufficient quantity of clean water is added gradually to this mixture and soft dough-like paste is made. 
 From this paste, small tablets (around 125–250 mg each) are rolled or shaped. 
 The tablets are dried completely in shade and then stored in an airtight glass container to protect their volatile and delicate components. 
 
 Medicinal Properties 
 Jvara-Atisara (Diarrhoea With Fever) 
 
Karpura Rasa as a short-term antidiarrhoeal to quickly reduce the frequency of stools and colicky pain. The combination of Karpura Rasa with Guduchi-based medicines such as Guduchi Ghana Vati or Amritarishta to lower fever, support immunity and prevent recurrence. Honey or lukewarm water works well as anupana (adjuvant).
 
 Pakva-Atisara And Malabsorption / Chronic Loose Stools 
 
Karpura Rasa with Kutaja preparations such as Kutajghan Vati or Kutajarishta, with anupana of takra (buttermilk) or thin rice-gruel after meals, according to the degree of weakness and digestive fire.
 
 Rakta Pravahika And Dysentery Associated With Blood 
 
Karpura Rasa with Praval-, Mukta- or Kamdudha-based Pitta-pacifying medicines, with anupana of cold water, goat’s milk or isabgol husk slurry after food, selected as per intensity of burning and bleeding.
 
 Acute Diarrhoea, Gastro-Enteritis And Infective Gastrointestinal Conditions 
 
Karpura Rasa with Kutajavaleha, Musta Churna or Bilvadi Churna, with anupana of jeera-water, musta-kashaya or light rice-gruel, used during the acute phase until stool frequency, cramps and nausea settle.
 
 Impact On Dosha 
 
Karpura Rasa primarily balances Vata and Kapha while needing some caution in strong Pitta prakriti or Pitta-dominant states. Karpura Rasa pacifies Vata by its warm, channel-clearing, antispasmodic action and pain-relieving effect, which calms excessive peristalsis and colic in diarrhoea. At the same time it reduces Kapha by drying excess mucus and kleda in the gut and improving digestive fire, so Kapha-related heaviness, mucus-laden stools and ama formation decrease.
 
 
Karpura Rasa has a mixed impact on Pitta. The cooling effect of camphor and the stool-binding nature of absorbent drugs can ease bleeding, burning and fever, so mild to moderate Pitta aggravation in diarrhoea usually settles. However, the whole formulation is relatively heated and strongly binding, so people with very high Pitta, very hot constituents, or those already suffering from active gastritis, intense burning or heavy bleeding should take it only in lower doses, for a short period, and strictly under medical supervision.
 
 Indications 
 
 Diarrhoea – acute and chronic 
 Diarrhoea associated with fever 
 Bloody diarrhoea / Dysentery 
 Malabsorption and irritable bowel-type conditions 
 Gastro-enteritis and other inflammatory gastrointestinal conditions 
 General gastrointestinal complaints with cramps, mucus and weakness 
 
 Dosage And Adjuvants 
 
For Karpura Rasa, adult doses are usually very small and always need medical supervision.
 
 
 Dose (adult) : 125 mg tablet once or twice daily, before or after food, as directed by an Ayurvedic physician.
 
 Common Anupana (Adjuvant) 
 
 Honey or honey with a little ghee (not in equal quantity) in Vata-Kapha-dominant diarrhoea. 
 Musta (Cyperus rotundus) decoction, cumin water or thin rice-gruel in diarrhoea, dysentery and gastro-enteritis to support digestion and absorbency. 
 
 Contraindications And Precautions 
 
Karpura Rasa needs careful, short-term, supervised use because it is a potent herbo-mineral and opium-containing formulation.
 
 Contraindications 
 
 Pregnancy and lactation. 
 Infants and children (unless strictly supervised by an Ayurvedic physician). 
 Known allergy or intolerance to camphor, opium, mercury compounds or other ingredients. 
 Severe liver or kidney disease, uncontrolled hypertension, serious heart or neurological disorders. 
 Marked Pitta aggravation with strong burning, active gastritis or peptic ulcer unless adjusted and closely monitored. 
 
 Precautions 
 
 Always use the minimum effective dose, for a limited duration, under professional guidance. 
 Avoid self-medication, especially using higher or more frequent doses, due to risk of opium- and metal-related toxicity.

 Shuddha para (purified and processed mercury) – 48 grams 
 Tamra bhsama (copper bhsama) -12 grams 
 Loha bhsama (iron bhsama) – 12 grams 
 Baer ki lkdi – Ziziphus mauritiana’s wood 
 Arandi ke patte  – Ricinus communis’s leaves 
 Jambhiri lemon (Citrus jambhiri) 
 Pippali (Piper longum) 
 Pipplamool (Piper longum’s root) 
 Chavya (Piper retrofractum) 
 Chitrakmool (Plumbato zeylanica’s root) 
 Saunth (Zingiber officinalis) 
 Amla (Phyllanthus emblica) 
 Maricha (Piper nigrum) 
 Kala namak (black salt) 
 Suhage ke phool (borax yakshawar’s flowers) 

 Method of Preparation 

 Took the shuddha para and made its kajjali. After this mixed this kajjali into mixture of loha and tamra bhsama. 
 Then do the process of parpati parkaran, in this boiled the ingredients (in this case the above kajjali mixture) up to heating point and made its liquid. Boiled under the mild flames of baer’s wood and pour on arandi’ leaves to made parpati of the mixture. 
 Cooled it down and do the grind in mortar pestle. 
 After this process put the mixture in iron’s pot and warm it on mild fire. In the intervals during process, added little jambhiri lemon juice. 
 Know took up to 4800 grams and dry it up. 
 Then triturated up to 50 times above mixture with the kwath of herbs (pippali, pipplamool, chivya, chitrakmool, saunth and amla). 
 After then took up to similar quantity of above mixture and suhage’s flower. Added half volume of black salt and maricha in the mixture. 
 Now keep the mixture besides chanak kshara for seven days and mixed the mixture properly in mortar pestle to make fine paste. 
 Took 125 mg of the paste and made its pills.

sections.introduction: Krimi Kantak Ras is a classical Ayurvedic formulation traditionally used for managing intestinal worms (krimi) and associated digestive disturbances. It contains potent herbal-mineral ingredients that exhibit anthelmintic, deepana (digestive stimulant), and pachana (digestive) properties. This formulation helps eliminate parasites, reduce abdominal discomfort, bloating, itching, and irregular bowel habits. It also supports gut cleansing and improves nutrient absorption by restoring digestive fire (agni). Additionally, Krimi Kantak Ras aids in preventing recurrence of infestations and enhances overall gastrointestinal health. Let’s discuss it in detail!

sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Dry Ginger (Zingiber officinale) 
 Known for its “Deepana” (appetite-stimulating) properties, dry ginger helps digest “Ama” (metabolic toxins) which often serve as a breeding ground for larvae. Its thermogenic nature creates a harsh environment for worms, while its gingerols provide mild anti-parasitic activity and reduce the abdominal cramping often associated with infestations. 
 2. Black Pepper (Piper nigrum) 
 This potent fruit contains piperine, which enhances the bioavailability of other herbs in the formula. Its sharp, piercing quality helps break down the protective mucosal biofilms that parasites use to adhere to the intestinal wall, facilitating their detachment and eventual expulsion from the gastrointestinal tract. 
 3. Long Pepper (Piper longum) 
 Long pepper is a powerful “Rasayana” that specifically targets the digestive and respiratory systems. In cases of worm infestation, it acts as a vermifuge, particularly effective against roundworms. It also strengthens the intestinal lining to prevent re-infection by improving local immunity and tissue integrity. 
 4. Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) 
 Primarily used as a carminative, fennel relaxes the smooth muscles of the intestine. This is crucial during worm infestations to alleviate spasms and bloating. Its mild antimicrobial properties support the overall cleansing process without irritating the sensitive mucosal lining of the gut. 
 5. Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 Acting as a “basti” (colon) cleanser, Haritaki has a natural laxative effect that helps in the physical expulsion of worms. Its astringent properties also help heal any micro-lesions in the intestinal mucosa caused by the attachment of parasitic hooks or suckers. 
 6. Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) 
 This fruit is particularly effective at breaking down excess mucus in the gut. Since many intestinal parasites thrive in a high-mucoid environment, Bibhitaki’s ability to “scrape” and dry out excess secretions helps starve the parasites of their preferred habitat. 
 7. Amla (Phyllanthus emblica) 
 While not a direct anthelmintic, Amla provides vital antioxidant support. Parasitic infections often cause oxidative stress and inflammation; Amla’s high Vitamin C content and cooling nature balance the heat generated by the pungent peppers, protecting the gut during the detoxification process. 
 8. Roasted Hing (Asafoetida) 
 Hing is one of the most powerful anti-flatulent tools. When roasted, it becomes easier to digest. It possesses strong antimicrobial and anthelmintic properties, specifically targeting pinworms and roundworms by paralyzing their nervous systems, making it easier for the body to eliminate them. 
 9. White Cumin (Cuminum cyminum) 
 White cumin, commonly known as jeera, is a widely used culinary and medicinal spice in Ayurveda. It stimulates digestion, enhances appetite, and helps relieve bloating and indigestion. Rich in antioxidants and essential oils, it supports liver function and nutrient absorption. Its mild carminative and antimicrobial properties make it beneficial for maintaining overall digestive balance and metabolic health. 
 10. Black Cumin (Nigella sativa) 
 Black cumin, also called kalonji, is a potent medicinal seed valued for its broad therapeutic benefits. It contains thymoquinone, known for strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Traditionally, it supports immunity, respiratory health, and metabolic balance. It also aids digestion, regulates blood sugar, and promotes skin and hair health, making it a versatile herb in both Ayurveda and Unani systems. 
 11. Ajwain (Trachyspermum ammi) 
 Ajwain, commonly known as carom seeds, is a potent digestive herb widely used in Ayurveda. It is rich in thymol, which enhances gastric secretions, relieves indigestion, bloating, and flatulence. Its carminative and antimicrobial properties make it effective in managing gut disorders. Ajwain also helps in respiratory conditions by clearing congestion and supporting overall metabolic health. 
 12. Khorasani Ajwain (Hyoscyamus niger) 
 Khorasani Ajwain, derived from Hyoscyamus niger, is a powerful herb known for its sedative, antispasmodic, and analgesic properties. It is traditionally used in small, controlled doses to relieve severe pain, nervous irritability, and spasmodic conditions like asthma or colic. Due to its potent alkaloids, it must be used cautiously under expert supervision in Ayurvedic and Unani practices. 
 13. Kirmani Ajwain (Carum copticum / Ptychotis ajowan variant) 
 Kirmani Ajwain is a variety of ajwain known for its strong aroma and enhanced therapeutic potency. It is particularly valued for its digestive and carminative actions, helping to relieve abdominal discomfort, gas, and weak digestion. It also exhibits mild antimicrobial properties and is often used in traditional formulations to support gut health and improve appetite. 
 14. Ajmoda (Apium graveolens) 
 Often used for its diuretic and carminative actions, Ajmoda helps in cleansing the gut and reducing the “heaviness” associated with parasitic loads. Its volatile oils contribute to the overall pungent profile of the formula, which serves to irritate and dislodge intestinal guests. 
 15. Hingupatri (Ferula jaeschkeana) 
 A botanical relative of Asafoetida, these leaves share similar sulfurous compounds. They reinforce the action of Hing, providing a sustained release of compounds that discourage the colonization of the small intestine by parasites and larvae. 
 16. Bayvidang (Embelia ribes) 
 Widely regarded as the premier herb for “Krimi” (worms). Its active constituent, embelin, has been shown to paralyze and kill various intestinal worms. It is effective across a broad spectrum, including tapeworms, pinworms, and roundworms, making it the functional anchor of this formulation. 
 17. Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica seeds) 
 Traditionally used for amoebic dysentery, these seeds are highly effective against protozoal infections and larger parasites. They possess a bitter taste that tones the intestines and prevents the loose stools often triggered by parasitic irritation. 
 18. Nagarmotha (Cyperus rotundus) 
 This rhizome is a powerful digestive stimulant that also absorbs excess moisture in the gut. By reducing “Kleda” (excessive dampness/fluid), it removes the environmental conditions required for parasitic eggs to hatch and thrive. 
 19. Atis (Aconitum heterophyllum) 
 A potent but non-toxic (in processed form) bitter tonic. It is highly valued for pediatric worm infestations and diarrhea. Its bitter alkaloids act as a potent deterrent for parasites while simultaneously strengthening the digestive system’s ability to resist future infestations. 
 20. Neem Bark (Azadirachta indica) 
 Neem is perhaps the most famous bitter antimicrobial. The bark contains nimbin and nimbidin, which have systemic anti-parasitic effects. It cleanses the blood and the gut, ensuring that any systemic toxins released by dying parasites are neutralized. 
 21. Chirayata (Swertia chirayita) 
 An extremely bitter herb that serves as an excellent internal cleanser. Its bitterness stimulates the liver and gallbladder; increased bile flow is a natural defense mechanism against parasites, as bile itself is inhibitory to many types of worms. 
 22. Kalamba (Jateorhiza palmata) 
 Also known as Calumba, this bitter root is used to tone the stomach and intestines. It is particularly helpful in the recovery phase of a worm infestation, as it helps restore the appetite and ensures the digestive juices are secreted in the correct concentrations. 
 23. Rock Salt Black Salt 
 These salts serve two purposes: they act as “Srotoshodhana” (channel cleansers) to help the herbal active ingredients penetrate deeper, and they provide an osmotic effect that can dehydrate soft-bodied parasites, aiding in their destruction. 
 24. Tamra Bhasma (Incinerated Copper) 
 Copper is traditionally used in minute, processed doses for its intense “Krimighna” (anthelmintic) and “Lekhana” (scraping) properties. It is considered highly effective for stubborn or chronic infestations that have resisted herbal-only treatments. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 All ingredients should be powdered finely after pounding and sieving through cloth.

 Conclusion 
 In conclusion, Krimi Kantak Ras offers a focused Ayurvedic approach to restoring internal balance by targeting parasitic disturbances and supporting digestive integrity. It works beyond symptomatic relief, helping to create an unfavorable environment for unwanted organisms while nurturing overall gut resilience. Regular and guided use can contribute to improved assimilation, better energy levels, and enhanced comfort. By aligning with classical principles of cleansing and strengthening, this formulation supports long-term wellness. However, mindful administration under qualified supervision ensures optimal outcomes, making it a valuable addition to traditional protocols for maintaining a healthy and balanced gastrointestinal system.

 This potent fruit contains piperine, which enhances the bioavailability of other herbs in the formula.  3. Long Pepper (Piper longum) 
 Long pepper is a powerful “Rasayana” that specifically targets the digestive and respiratory systems. In cases of worm infestation, it acts as a vermifuge, particularly effective against roundworms. It also strengthens the intestinal lining to prevent re-infection by improving local immunity and tissue integrity. 
 4. Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) 
 Primarily used as a carminative, fennel relaxes the smooth muscles of the intestine. This is crucial during worm infestations to alleviate spasms and bloating. Its mild antimicrobial properties support the overall cleansing process without irritating the sensitive mucosal lining of the gut. 
 5. Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 Acting as a “basti” (colon) cleanser, Haritaki has a natural laxative effect that helps in the physical expulsion of worms. Its astringent properties also help heal any micro-lesions in the intestinal mucosa caused by the attachment of parasitic hooks or suckers. 
 6. Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) 
 This fruit is particularly effective at breaking down excess mucus in the gut. Since many intestinal parasites thrive in a high-mucoid environment, Bibhitaki’s ability to “scrape” and dry out excess secretions helps starve the parasites of their preferred habitat. 
 7. Amla (Phyllanthus emblica) 
 While not a direct anthelmintic, Amla provides vital antioxidant support. Parasitic infections often cause oxidative stress and inflammation; Amla’s high Vitamin C content and cooling nature balance the heat generated by the pungent peppers, protecting the gut during the detoxification process. 
 8. Roasted Hing (Asafoetida) 
 Hing is one of the most powerful anti-flatulent tools. When roasted, it becomes easier to digest. It possesses strong antimicrobial and anthelmintic properties, specifically targeting pinworms and roundworms by paralyzing their nervous systems, making it easier for the body to eliminate them. 
 9. White Cumin (Cuminum cyminum) 
 White cumin, commonly known as jeera, is a widely used culinary and medicinal spice in Ayurveda. It stimulates digestion, enhances appetite, and helps relieve bloating and indigestion. Rich in antioxidants and essential oils, it supports liver function and nutrient absorption. Its mild carminative and antimicrobial properties make it beneficial for maintaining overall digestive balance and metabolic health. 
 10. Black Cumin (Nigella sativa) 
 Black cumin, also called kalonji, is a potent medicinal seed valued for its broad therapeutic benefits. It contains thymoquinone, known for strong antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Traditionally, it supports immunity, respiratory health, and metabolic balance. It also aids digestion, regulates blood sugar, and promotes skin and hair health, making it a versatile herb in both Ayurveda and Unani systems. 
 11. Ajwain (Trachyspermum ammi) 
 Ajwain, commonly known as carom seeds, is a potent digestive herb widely used in Ayurveda. It is rich in thymol, which enhances gastric secretions, relieves indigestion, bloating, and flatulence. Its carminative and antimicrobial properties make it effective in managing gut disorders. Ajwain also helps in respiratory conditions by clearing congestion and supporting overall metabolic health. 
 12. Khorasani Ajwain (Hyoscyamus niger) 
 Khorasani Ajwain, derived from Hyoscyamus niger, is a powerful herb known for its sedative, antispasmodic, and analgesic properties. It is traditionally used in small, controlled doses to relieve severe pain, nervous irritability, and spasmodic conditions like asthma or colic. Due to its potent alkaloids, it must be used cautiously under expert supervision in Ayurvedic and Unani practices. 
 13. Kirmani Ajwain (Carum copticum / Ptychotis ajowan variant) 
 Kirmani Ajwain is a variety of ajwain known for its strong aroma and enhanced therapeutic potency. It is particularly valued for its digestive and carminative actions, helping to relieve abdominal discomfort, gas, and weak digestion. It also exhibits mild antimicrobial properties and is often used in traditional formulations to support gut health and improve appetite. 
 14. Ajmoda (Apium graveolens) 
 Often used for its diuretic and carminative actions, Ajmoda helps in cleansing the gut and reducing the “heaviness” associated with parasitic loads. Its volatile oils contribute to the overall pungent profile of the formula, which serves to irritate and dislodge intestinal guests. 
 15. Hingupatri (Ferula jaeschkeana) 
 A botanical relative of Asafoetida, these leaves share similar sulfurous compounds. They reinforce the action of Hing, providing a sustained release of compounds that discourage the colonization of the small intestine by parasites and larvae. 
 16. Bayvidang (Embelia ribes) 
 Widely regarded as the premier herb for “Krimi” (worms). Its active constituent, embelin, has been shown to paralyze and kill various intestinal worms. It is effective across a broad spectrum, including tapeworms, pinworms, and roundworms, making it the functional anchor of this formulation. 
 17. Indrayava (Holarrhena antidysenterica seeds) 
 Traditionally used for amoebic dysentery, these seeds are highly effective against protozoal infections and larger parasites. They possess a bitter taste that tones the intestines and prevents the loose stools often triggered by parasitic irritation. 
 18. Nagarmotha (Cyperus rotundus) 
 This rhizome is a powerful digestive stimulant that also absorbs excess moisture in the gut. By reducing “Kleda” (excessive dampness/fluid), it removes the environmental conditions required for parasitic eggs to hatch and thrive. 
 19. Atis (Aconitum heterophyllum) 
 A potent but non-toxic (in processed form) bitter tonic. It is highly valued for pediatric worm infestations and diarrhea. Its bitter alkaloids act as a potent deterrent for parasites while simultaneously strengthening the digestive system’s ability to resist future infestations. 
 20. Neem Bark (Azadirachta indica) 
 Neem is perhaps the most famous bitter antimicrobial. The bark contains nimbin and nimbidin, which have systemic anti-parasitic effects. It cleanses the blood and the gut, ensuring that any systemic toxins released by dying parasites are neutralized. 
 21. Chirayata (Swertia chirayita) 
 An extremely bitter herb that serves as an excellent internal cleanser. Its bitterness stimulates the liver and gallbladder; increased bile flow is a natural defense mechanism against parasites, as bile itself is inhibitory to many types of worms. 
 22. Kalamba (Jateorhiza palmata)

name: Krimi Kuthar Ras

sections.introduction: Krimi Kuthar Ras is an ayurvedic formulation that is prepared from the mixture of minerals and herbs. This is known to treat problems related with stomach worms.
sections.ingredients:
Karpura – Cinnamomum camphora – 80 g 

 10 g fine powder of each of:- 

 Ajamoda – Trachyspermum roxburghianum 
 Indrayava – Holarrhena antidysenterica 
 Trayamana – Gentiana kurroo 
 Vidanga – Embelia ribes 
 Shuddha Hingula – Purified and processed Cinnabar (Mercury) 
 Shuddha Vatsanabha – Purified Aconitum ferox 
 Nagakeshara – Mesua ferrea 
 Juice extract of Vijaya – Cannabis sativa – quantity sufficient for grinding for one day 
 Seed powder of Palasha – Butea monosperma – 150 g 
 Mushakarni – quantity sufficient for grinding. 
 Brahmi – Bacopa monnieri – juice extract quantity sufficient for grinding. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take the ingredients from number 1 to 8. Mix them all and put in mortar pestle with extract of Vijaya for six hours. 
 Then take palasha, mushakarni and brahmi and tincture with first mixture. 
 Now take the paste up to 250 mg and make their pills. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 As the name suggests, Krimi Kuthar is an ayurvedic preparation which is beneficial for stomach worms like helminthiasis. The herbs included in this formulations are kapura, ajmoda, vidanga, indrayava etc. These herbs have antioxidant, analgesic, carminative, anthelmintic, astringent, anti-toxic properties in it. These have constituents like cineol, pinene, terpineol, menthol, thymol, terpenoids, conessine, isoconessimine, conessimin, conimin,amarogentin, gentiopicrin, embelin, christembine, homoembelin, vilangine,pseudo-aconitine, mensuol, silosterol, fatty acids, mesuanic acid, cannabidiol, vit A, B1, B2, B6, C, D, F, omega acids, herpestine, apigenin etc. in it. Due to its anthelmintic property it expels out parasitic worms from the body. It has de-worming action due to which it acts against intestinal worms like helminthiasis etc. Due to its anti-oxidant property it detoxifies the body. It is beneficial in anorexia and many other related problems.
sections.indications:

 Anorexia
sections.dose: One pill, One to two times a day, before or after meals, with black salt.
sections.contraindications:
Avoid in pregnancy and lactation. 
 Take medicine under doctor’s prescription. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Krimighan rasa is a classical Ayurvedic formulation which is used in the treatment of krimi roga (worm infestation) and other digestive problems.
sections.ingredients:

sections.description_of_ingredients:
Vidanga Churna – This herb is best in treating intestinal worm infestation that includes roundworms, threadworms etc. It stimulates digestion. It is also helpful in constipation due to its laxative property.

 Ras-Sindoor – It is a purified and processed formulation of mercury. It is very useful in enhancing immunity and provides strength to the body. It also helps in improving digestion power.. 

 Method of Preparation 

 At first properly mixes the Ras-Sindoor in a kharal yantra. 
 After then add all the other ingredients in this Ras-Sindoor mixture. 
 Keep this formulation in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Krimighan rasa is an Ayurvedic formulation. It is very effective in fighting against Krimi roga (worm infestation). The ingredients help in improving digestion power and also stimulate appetite. This formulation has laxative property. It helps in detoxification of the body.

sections.introduction: Krishna Chaturmukh Rasa is an Ayurvedic medicine. It is used in the treatment of all vataj disorders. It is a herbo-mineral composition.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Parada (Purifies Mercury) – 12 gm 
 Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulphur) – 12 gm 
 Loha Bhasma (Iron Calx) – 12 gm 
 Abhrak Bhasma (Mica Calx) – 12 gm 
 Swarna Bhasma (Gold Calx) – 3 gm
sections.description_of_ingredients:
Shuddha Parada – This is a good appetizer. It stimulates the digestive fire. It is used in maximum Ayurvedic formulation as a main ingredient. It provides strength to the body. It is used in the preparation of Ayurvedic medicine to enhance the strength of other herbs. It pacifies all three dosha. Thus also helpful in pacifying vata disorders. 
 Shuddha Gandhak – This is an ayurvedic mineral based formulation and used after purification of Sulphur. It helps in purifying blood and provides nutrition to the bodily tissues. It is used in all skin disorders. It provides strength to the digestive system. 
 Loha Bhasma – This is used in pacifying Vata and pitta dosha. It is helpful in balancing the vata disorders. It is also helpful in anemic conditions. It provides strength to the body. 
 Abhrak Bhasma – This is an Ayurvedic formulation prepared by Mica after the shodhan process (purification). It improves digestion power. It provides nourishment to the dhatus (bodily tissue) of the body. It is used in cough, diabetes etc. 
 Swarna Bhasma – This is a gold formulation. Gold has a variety of health benefits. It strengthens the immunity of the person. It stimulates digestion power. Swarna is used in general debility conditions. It also manages cancer diseases. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Make a kajjali from Gandhak and Parada. 
 Mix all the ingredients in this kajjali preparation. 
 Give Ghritkumari (Aloe vera) swaras bhavana and give properly frolement for one day. 
 Make a ball shaped out of it and cover it with Eranda leaves and secretly kept in a rice container for 3 days. 
 Take out this mixture after 4rth day and again mixes it properly in a kharal yantra. 
 Again give bhavana with kumariswaras (Aloe vera). 
 Make 125 mg tablet and let them dry. 
 Kept in a glass container. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Krishna Chaturmukh Rasa is a classical Ayurvedic medicine and used in the treatment of various vata disorders. This formulation balances the agni of the person. As said by our acharya that mandagni is the root cause of every disease. So the ingredients in this formulation are helping in digesting the Aama (endotoxins) and helpful in balancing the vitiated vatadi dosha. It is helpful in managing digestive as well as respiratory symptoms.
