sections.ingredients:
The various ingredients for preparation of Marichadi thailam are given as follows- 

 Marich ( Piper nigrum ) 
 Hartal ( Purifies orpiment ) 
 Trivrit ( Operculena terpenthum ) 
 Raktachandana ( Pterocarpus santalinus ) 
 Musta ( Cyperus rotundus ) 
 Mansheela ( Purified realgar ) 
 Jatamansi (Nardostachys jatamansi ) 
 Haridra (Curcuma longa ) 
 Daruharidra ( Berberis aristata ) 
 Vishala ( Citrullus colocynthis ) 
 Karveera (Nerium indicum ) 
 Kushta ( Saussrea lappa ) 
 Araka ( Calotropis procera ) 
 Goomayrasa ( Cow dung water) 
 Gomutra (Cow’s urine) 
 Mustard oil (Brassica junica ) 
 Water

 Marich – It is useful for skin related issues such as dark spots, dryness, aging, etc. It is extremely effective in respiratory disorders like cold, cough, congestion, and sinusitis and even in managing asthma. 
 Hartal – It is pungent, astringent and hot in nature. It is useful in skin diseases with itching, cough, cold, bronchitis, syphilis, etc. It helps in purification of blood and balances pitta dosha. 
 Trivrit – It helps to remove toxins from the body, act as antipyretic and anti-inflammatory. It is good for healing infected wounds and removes worm infestations. 
 Raktachandana – It helps to remove inflammation and pain like symptoms. It has a cooling effect so it is good for skin health and very effective in blemishes and aches. 
 Musta – It corrects the overall body’s metabolism, promotes healthy skin and inflammatory response. It helps in managing kapha and pitta related diseases. It reduces burning sensation and excessive thirst. 
 Mansheela – It helps in managing eye and skin related disorders. It removes toxins from the body and corrects bronchitis, insomnia, and psychological conditions. 
 Jatamansi – It prevents bacterial, fungal infections and removes toxins from the body. It helps in healing wounds and relief from stress, anxiety and depression. 
 Haridra – It removes toxins from the body and promotes healthy skin. Prevents itching, allergy, infections and skin disorders. It promotes wound healing, reduces pain, swelling and inflammation. 
 Daruharidra – It is a bitter tonic used as antiseptic and antipyretic. It is used to manage infections, ulcers, boils, wounds and ear problems. Also effective in psoriasis and edema. 
 Vishala – It acts as an immunity booster and antioxidant. It is natural antiseptic and kills viruses and bacteria. It manages skin diseases and intestinal worm infestations. 
 Karaveera – It reduces pain, swelling and acts as an antiseptic agent. It is useful in asthma, epilepsy, ringworm, leprosy and ulcer. It stimulates muscles and relieves pain. 
 Kushta – It prevents growth of bacteria, reduces pain, inflammation and leprosy. It increases blood supply to the skin surface. 
 Araka – It acts as an antioxidant and is rich in various vitamins, minerals. Useful in skin disorders, worm infestations, cough and bleeding disorders. It has a hot potency, light in nature. 
 Goo Mayrasa – It decreases inflammation and boosts the immune system. It mainly acts on vata and kapha and increases pitta dosha. It is rich in many beneficial microbes and nutrients. 
 Gomutra – It is cleansing and detoxifying in nature, it helps to nourish hair and skin. It has antimicrobial and anthelmintic properties. It has antioxidant effects and reduces stress level. 
 Mustard oil – It strengthens red blood cells, prevents bacteria, fungus and it boosts the immune system. It contains vitamin E so helps in hydrating skin.

 The steps for the preparation of Marichadi Thailam are given as following- 

 Firstly collect all the drugs and wash them properly. 
 Then make kalka (paste) of all the drugs mentioned above and add water in it. 
 Then add gomutra and gomay rasa (cow’s urine and dung). 
 Boil the solution till it remains one fourth in quantity. 
 At last mix it with mustard oil which is used as a base. 
 Mix the solution properly and filter it in a clean vessel. 
 Then store the oil obtained in an airtight glass container and keep away from direct sunlight.

It is prepared as mustard oil and its base with various natural herbs. With skin related issues, it also helps in respiratory system related disorders. So, this oil can be used for skin issues under any physician’s guidance.

name: Naadivranhar Taila

sections.overview: Naadivranhar Taila – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction:
Naadivranhar Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil formulated with penetrating, cleansing, and tissue-purifying substances processed in a sesame oil base. The preparation is traditionally indicated for external application in chronic sinus wounds and non-healing ulcerative tracts characterized by discharge, tissue degeneration, and persistent inflammation. The formulation integrates Tikshna (penetrative), Shodhana (cleansing), and Ropana (healing) supportive dravyas to assist in purification of affected tissue and promotion of structural repair. 
 The formulation describes preparation of medicated oil by sequential processing of selected ingredients in heated sesame oil followed by trituration of mineral substances and filtration. The oil is used externally through local application or medicated dressing as a supportive measure in chronic discharging wounds.
sections.composition:
I. Taila Dravya (Base Oil) 

 Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Sesame Oil) 

 II. Kalka Dravyas (Processed Ingredients) 

 Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium – Marking Nut) 
 Kapikacchu Beeja (Mucuna pruriens – Cowhage Seed) 
 Khorasani Yavani (Hyoscyamus niger – Henbane Seed) 
 Murdasanga (Lead Oxide – traditionally used mineral preparation) 
 Nila Tuttha (Copper Sulphate – purified mineral preparation) 

 Method Of Preparation 
 Measured Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) is heated in a suitable vessel over mild fire. When the oil begins to boil, Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) is introduced and properly processed. Finely powdered Kapikacchu Beeja (Mucuna pruriens) and Khorasani Yavani (Hyoscyamus niger) are then added and stirred uniformly. The vessel is removed from heat and triturated with Murdasanga and Nila Tuttha until uniform dispersion is achieved. The preparation is filtered when required and stored in a clean airtight glass container. 
 Method Of Use 

 External application only. 
 The medicated oil is applied locally over the affected area or used to soak sterile dressing material for placement over sinus wounds as directed by a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Vrana-shodhana (wound cleansing supportive action) 
 Vrana-ropana (wound healing supportive action) 
 Lekhana supportive effect on unhealthy tissue 
 Krimighna supportive action 
 Shothahara supportive action 

 Clinical Indications 

 Chronic sinus wounds (Naadi Vrana) 
 Non-healing ulcers with discharge 
 Suppurative lesions requiring purification 
 Long-standing external wound tracts 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) exhibits Tikshna, Ushna, and Kaphahara properties supporting purification of unhealthy tissue and local stimulation. Kapikacchu Beeja (Mucuna pruriens) provides Brimhana-supportive and tissue restorative effects that assist structural recovery. Khorasani Yavani (Hyoscyamus niger) contributes Shothahara and Vedanasthapana-supportive actions beneficial in chronic inflammatory states. Nila Tuttha (Copper Sulphate) demonstrates classical Shodhana-supportive action assisting removal of unhealthy tissue components. Murdasanga provides traditional Ropana-supportive effects when properly processed. Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) acts as a Sukshma, Snigdha, and penetrating medium facilitating delivery of active constituents into deeper tissue planes.
sections.precautions:
For external use only. 
 Avoid inhalation of fumes during preparation, especially from Bhallataka processing. 
 Use only under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. 
 Do not apply over highly sensitive or acutely inflamed tissue without guidance. 

 Conclusion 
 Naadivranhar Taila represents a traditionally structured Ayurvedic medicated oil designed for management of chronic sinus wounds through purification, protection, and healing-supportive mechanisms. The integration of Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium), Kapikacchu Beeja (Mucuna pruriens), Khorasani Yavani (Hyoscyamus niger), and classical mineral preparations in Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) produces a preparation intended to support tissue cleansing and structural restoration. By assisting removal of unhealthy tissue components and promoting localized repair, this classical formulation serves as a supportive therapeutic measure in persistent discharging wounds. When applied appropriately under professional supervision, the oil contributes to stabilization of tissue integrity and enhancement of natural healing processes in chronic sinus conditions.

sections.introduction: Neelibhringadi Taila (Oil) is an Ayurvedic and herbal hair oil, which is a useful product to improve the quality of hair, to treat split hairs, premature graying and baldness.
sections.ingredients:
Neeli swarasa ( Indigofera tinctoria ) – Juice extract or decoction of – 768 ml 
 Bhringraj swarasa ( Eclipta alba ) – Juice extract or decoction of – 768 ml 
 Shatakratulata (Karnasphota) ( Cardiospermum halicacabum) – decoction – 768 ml 
 Dhatri (Amla) ( Emblica officinalis ) – 768 ml 
 Aja ksheera (Goat milk) – 768 ml 
 Nalikera Ksheera (coconut) – 768 ml 
 Mahishiksheera – Buffalo milk – 768 ml 
 Dhenudbhava (Cow milk) – 768 ml 
 Taila (Coconut oil) – 768 ml 
 Yashti (Licorice) ( Glycyrrhiza glabra ) – 32 g

 Anjana ( Berberis aristata ) – Aqueous extract of – 32 g 

 Method of Preparation 
 Take juices, animal milks and base oil (coconut or sesame oil). Prepare herbal paste using water or milk. Then, mix all ingredients and heat the mixture till only oil is left behind. The Leftover oil is Neelibhringadi Taila (Oil). 
 Leave the Neelibhringadi Taila (Oil) with herbal residues for its natural cooling for 24 to 48 hours. After all this filter Neelibhringadi Oil and remove the residues. Finally Neelibhringadi Taila (Oil) is ready to use.

This oil is for external application only. 
 Its application over the scalp followed by its gentle massage for five minutes.

sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Nimb ( Azadirachta indica ) – This herb is well known for its antimicrobial properties. It gets rid of unwanted toxins and is a stimulant of liver functions. This herb also possesses healing, analgesic and detoxifying properties. 
 Amrita ( Tinosporia cordifolia ) – This potent herb works as an appetizer, digestive and antiemetic in nature. Its anti-inflammatory and anti-secretory action makes it effective against toxin accumulations.It is a tridosha balancing herb that is used as an adaptogen in ayurveda and works effectively against stress and illness. 
 Erand ( Ricinus communis ) – This herb alleviates Vata and hence subsides the associated pain. It is “deepen” being ushna veerya and also possesses “bhedan” guna by its tikshna properties. This is very effective against severe constipation. 
 Vrisha ( Adhatoda vasica ) – This herb balances pitta dosha and helps improve digestion. 
 Nisa (Curcumin longa) – This herb is a very potent anti-inflammatory herb that acts as an appetizer, laxative and a cholagogue. It also possess analgesic actions 
 Marich ( Piper nigrum ) – This herb consists of piperine, piperidine, chavicin, starch etc. Due to its tikshna and ushna gunas it stimulates salivation, and digestive juices. The herb is a potent liver stimulant and increases appetite. It helps beneficially against indigestion. 
 Rohini ( Picrorhiza kurroa )- This herb is an effective appetizer, purgative, liver stimulant and vermifuge. It relieves constipation, flatulence and ascites. This makes it an effective detoxifier. 
 Yavani ( Trachyspermum Amani ) – This herb is a very effective analgesic. It treats anorexia, indigestion, flatulence and abdominal pain. 
 Manjistha ( Rubia cordifolia ) – This herb works against the “aama dosa” (toxins) being formed and also provides the body with strength and energy.
sections.direction_for_use:
Apply externally over the affected area 
 For internal consumption – 5 ml 

 Precaution 

 Seek medical advice before the consumption of this product. 
 Do not consume if contraindicated to castor oil. 
 Do not use if suffering from conditions like  Dysentery or Diarrhoea. 
 Avoid during pregnancy. 
 Keep out of the reach of children. 
 Store in cool and dry place. 
 Avoid spillage over floor.
sections.pharmacological_actions: Ayurveda considers the site of formation of most of the diseases is gut. Intake of improper food at the improper times is difficult to digest (causing indigestion) and expel out of the body (causing constipation). This incomplete digestion leads to the formation of aama or toxins in the body which vitiates Rasa, Rakta, Mamsa and Lasika. Thereby it becomes the cause of many chronic inflammatory and skin disorders. Nimbamritadi errand tail works on this aama (toxins) and gives relief from so many ailments.
sections.indications:
Skin disorders 
 Rheumatoid arthritis 
 Constipation
sections.side_effects: The oil has no known side effects, but to be taken under physician’s recommendation.
sections.shelf_life:
This oil is best before 3 years from the date of its manufacturing. Once opened should be consumed within 4 months. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.overview: Nonganadi Taila – Ingredients, Preparation, Medicinal Properties, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction: Nonganadi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil formulation primarily indicated in Shlipada (elephantiasis / lymphatic filariasis). The oil is processed in the fresh juice of Nongana (identified in regional practice as Trinavisesha group herb) along with Patha (Cissampelos pareira) and Karkata Shringi (Pistacia integerrima) as paste ingredients. The formulation is administered internally and is described to alleviate swelling, inflammation, and lymphatic obstruction associated with chronic lymphedema. Owing to its Shothahara (anti-inflammatory), Lekhana (scraping), Krimighna (anti-parasitic), and Kapha-Vata shamaka properties, it is considered beneficial in managing glandular enlargement and progressive edema of the lower limbs.
sections.classical_reference:
नोङ्गणस्य रसे सिद्धं पाठाकर्कटकल्कवत्। 
तैलं पानात्प्रशमयेच्छ्लीपदं शीघ्रमेव हि।। 
 The verse explains that sesame oil processed in the fresh juice of Nongana and combined with the paste (kalka) of Patha (Cissampelos pareira) and Karkata Shringi becomes effective in alleviating Shlipada (elephantiasis). It further emphasizes that when this medicated oil is taken internally (pana), it quickly reduces the symptoms of Shlipada. The Malayalam commentary reiterates that regular intake of this oil helps in relieving severe swelling of the legs (perumpadam – elephantiasis). 
 Commentary (Sanskrit–Malayalam Version) 
 नोंगणस्यरसे सिद्धं पाठाकर्कट कल्कमाय्। 
 एण्णवेंतु कुडिप्पिच्चालिल्लतेपों पेरुंपदं ।।
sections.ingredients:
I. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredient) 
 Nongana (Trinavisesha) Svarasa 
 Fresh juice of Nongana herb (640 ml). 
 (Botanical identification varies regionally; traditionally grouped under Trina (grass) varieties used in edema and inflammatory disorders.) 
 II. Taila Dravya 
 Murchita Tila Taila ( Sesamum indicum ) – Processed sesame oil (160 ml) 
 III. Kalka Dravyas (Paste Ingredients) 

 Patha (Cissampelos pareira) – 20 gm 
 Common name: Velvetleaf / False pareira 
 Karkata Shringi (Pistacia integerrima) – 20 gm 
 Common name: Crab’s claw gall 

 Method of Preparation 
 Fine paste (kalka) of Patha (Cissampelos pareira) and Karkata Shringi (Pistacia integerrima) is prepared separately. This paste is added to murchita tila taila along with the fresh juice of Nongana in a stainless-steel vessel. The mixture is heated over mild fire following classical Taila Paka Vidhi (medicated oil preparation) until the aqueous portion evaporates completely and only the medicated oil remains in the quantity of taila dravya. After proper paka lakshanas (signs of completion), the oil is filtered and stored in clean, airtight glass containers. 
 Pharmacological Properties 
 Nonganadi Taila possesses Shothahara (anti-inflammatory), Lekhana (reducing excessive tissue growth), Krimighna (anti-parasitic), Kandughna (anti-itching), and Kapha-Vata hara properties. 

 Patha (Cissampelos pareira) exhibits anti-inflammatory, lymphatic decongestant, and antimicrobial effects, useful in chronic swelling and glandular disorders. 
 Karkata Shringi (Pistacia integerrima) is known for its Kapha-reducing, anti-inflammatory, and astringent actions. 
 Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) acts as a yogavahi (carrier), facilitating deep tissue penetration and systemic action when administered internally. 

 Collectively, the formulation works on lymphatic stagnation, chronic edema, and tissue hypertrophy seen in Ślīpada. 
 Indication 

 Shlipada (Elephantiasis / Lymphatic filariasis) 
 Chronic lymphedema with Kapha-Vata predominance 

 Method Of Use 

 Internal administration (Paana)
sections.dose: 10 ml twice daily (b.i.d.), or as directed by an Ayurvedic physician.
sections.precautions:
Should be taken under medical supervision. 
 Not advised during pregnancy without consultation. 
 Monitor digestion and appetite, as oil preparations require proper Agni (digestive fire). 

 Conclusion 
 Nonganadi Taila is a specialized classical formulation indicated in Shlipada, a condition characterized by chronic lymphatic obstruction and progressive swelling. Processed in Nongana juice and fortified with Patha (Cissampelos pareira) and Karkata Shringi (Pistacia integerrima), the oil exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and Kapha-Vata pacifying actions. Its internal administration helps reduce edema, tissue hypertrophy, and inflammatory manifestations associated with elephantiasis. When used judiciously under expert supervision, this formulation serves as a valuable therapeutic option in traditional Ayurvedic management of lymphatic disorders.

name: Panchamla Thailam

sections.introduction: Panchamla thailam is an Ayurvedic formulation known for its amazing benefits in the treatment of Rheumatoid arthritis and ascites. Its action is known to be anti-edematous and works effectively when given an external application over dropsy.
sections.ingredients:
Panchamla thailam has following contents: 

 Amlavetasa – Tikul ( Garcinia pedunculata ) 
 Vrikshamla ( Garcinia morella ) 
 Chincha – Tamarind 
 Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula ) 
 Cow Urine 
 Supernatant Parts of Curd (Mastu) 
 Badara Patra – (Leaves of   Ziziphus jujuba ) 
 Dadim – Pomegranate ( Punica granatum ) 
 Amla parni ( Rheum emodi ) 
 Tila Taila – Gingelly Oil
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Amla Parni ( Rheum emodi ) – This herb consists of acids, resin,mucin,tannic acid, starch, pectin etc and is very effective against skin diseases and inflammation. 
 Vrikshamla ( Garcinia morella ) – This herb has Protocatechuic acid (27), caffeic acid (28), ferulic acid (29), and vanillic acid (30) active ingredients which makes this herb possess a pacifying action over pain, tumour and inflammation. 
 Amlavetasa ( Garcinia pedunculata ) – This herb is amla (sour) in its rasa and vipaka and possess antihistaminic, antiulcerogenic, antimicrobial, antiviral properties. 
 Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula ) – This herb is made up of gallic acid, ellagic acid, tannic acid, which gives it anti-inflammatory properties over the swellings. Its ruksh (dry) properties makes its excellent medicinal use. 
 Dadim ( Punica granatum ) – Its madhur, amla and kshaya rasa makes it very much potent against pain, edema and swellings.The chemical constituents such as flavonoids, ellagitannin, punicalagin, ellagic acid, makes for its use against arthritis, viral and bacterial infections etc. 
 Badra Patra ( Ziziphus jujuba ) – This herb acts as refrigerant and cleans, heals the wounds.This herb when directly applied over skin is also thought to  treat dry skin, ease sunburn, and reduce wrinkles along with other signs of aging. 
 Chincha ( Tamarindus indica ) – Tamarind helps to reduce the chances of joint pain, swelling and inflammation associated with arthritis due to its Vata balancing property. 
 Mastu (Curd’s whey), cow’s urine  are used for their sour properties. 
 Tila Taila – The base of sesame oil is given. 

 Application 

 This oil is for external application only. 
 Apply the oil over the affected area and leave it for 10 – 15 min. 
 Then wash away the oil with lukewarm water. 
 Application of oil prior bathing is advised. 

 Precaution 

 The oil must not be consumed. 
 When applied over feet, should thoroughly be washed off or else could make walking very slippery. 
 Do not spill over the floor. 
 Generally safe during pregnancy and lactation (avoid if had witnessed any prior allergic reactions on its applications).
sections.pharmacological_actions: The amla varga herbs used in this oil are known for their Shodhan, Maaran and Dravaan action. They work effectively against edema and arthritis.

 Edema
sections.side_effects:
There are no known side effects of this oil.

name: Panchasneha Taila

sections.overview: Panchasneha Taila – Ingredients, Preparation, Medicinal Properties, Indications More
sections.introduction: Panchasneha Taila is a classical Ayurvedic polyherbal oil formulation prepared using five different Sneha dravyas (lipid substances), which enhances its nourishing and Vata-pacifying properties. The presence of multiple fats increases tissue penetration and provides deep unctuousness, making it highly effective in chronic Vata Vyadhi (neuromuscular and musculoskeletal disorders). This formulation is especially indicated in conditions involving stiffness, wasting, restricted shoulder movement, chronic fracture pain, and degenerative disorders. The combination of nourishing decoction drugs, fermented liquid (Dhanyamla), milk, and five fats makes it both strengthening and rejuvenating.
sections.classical_reference:
दशमूलबलामाषाकार्पासास्थिकुल्थकम् । 
 प्रस्थं प्रस्थं पृथक् क्षुष्णं जलद्रोणद्वये पचेत् ।। 
 धान्याम्लं शूर्पसंयुक्तं पादशेषेन तेन तु। 
 बाराहीतिलजैरन्डनालिकेरजतक्रजैः ।। 
 पृथक् पृथक् त्रिकुडवं स्नेहस्य द्विगुणं पयः। 
 कल्कैरेतेर्विपक्तव्यं रास्नासैन्धवदारुकम् ।। 
 कार्पासास्थिकुलत्यानि गण्डीरं सुपेषितैः। 
 जयेद्वातरुजास्तम्भदीर्घभग्नरुजास्तथा ।। 
 वाहुशोषापबाहुश्च बाहुस्तम्भमथापि वा। 
 करोति बाहुवृद्धिं च वातरोगं निहन्ति च।। 
 पञ्चस्नेहमिदं प्रोक्तं ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पुरा।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 The verse explains that decoction should be prepared from Dashamula (roots of 10 herbs), Bala (Sida cordifolia), Masha (Vigna mungo), Karpasasthi (Gossypium herbaceum), and Kuluttha (Macrotyloma uniflorum) in a large quantity of water. To this, Dhanyamla (fermented sour gruel) and milk are added along with five types of fats (Sneha) – Varahi taila, Tila taila ((Sesamum indicum), Eranda taila (Ricinus communis – Castor oil), Nalikera taila (Cocos nucifera – Coconut oil), and Goghrita (Cow’s ghee). The formulation is further processed with specific Kalka dravyas. This oil alleviates Vata disorders, stiffness, chronic fracture pain, muscle wasting, Apabahuka (frozen shoulder), and Bahu Stambha (arm rigidity). It is described as a formulation originally created by Lord Brahma.
sections.composition:
I. Kvatha Dravyas (Decoction Ingredients) 

 Dashamula (Group of ten roots – Vata pacifying) – 640 gm 
 Balamula (Sida cordifolia – Country mallow root) – 640 gm 
 Masha (Vigna mungo – Black gram) – 640 gm 
 Karpasasthi (Gossypium herbaceum – Cotton seed/inner part) – 640 gm 
 Kuluttha (Macrotyloma uniflorum – Horse gram) – 640 gm 
 Water – 20.48 litres (reduced to one-fourth) 

 II. Sneha Dravyas (Five Fats) 

 Varahi Taila – 480 ml 
 Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Sesame oil) – 480 ml 
 Eranda Taila (Ricinus communis – Castor oil) – 480 ml 
 Nalikera Taila (Cocos nucifera – Coconut oil) – 480 ml 
 Goghrita (Cow’s ghee) – 480 ml 

 III. Other Drava Dravyas 

 Dhanyamla (Fermented sour gruel) – 20.48 litres 
 Goksira (Cow’s milk) – 4.8 litres 

 IV. Kalka Dravyas 

 Rasna (Pluchea lanceolata) – 90 gm

sections.overview:

sections.introduction: Panchavalkaladi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic external oil formulation designed primarily for inflammatory and exudative skin disorders. The formulation is based on Panchavalkala, a well-known group of five astringent barks combined with blood-purifying and cooling herbs. Skin diseases associated with Rakta (blood) and Pitta Dosha vitiation often present with redness, burning sensation, discharge (kleda), itching, and inflammation. This Taila works through its Rakta-shodhaka (blood-purifying), Pitta-shamaka (Pitta pacifying), and Kledahara (moisture-reducing) actions. It is particularly useful in conditions where inflammation and oozing predominate.
sections.classical_reference:
पंचवल्कलनिशागोपीकषाये तिलजं पचेत्। 
 रम्भोदकन्दमधुकत्वकुशीरामयचन्दनैः।। 
 रक्तपित्तोत्तरे कुष्ठे विसर्पे क्लेदवत्यपि।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 The verse explains that sesame oil should be processed in the decoction (kashaya) of Panchavalkala along with herbs such as Haridra (Nisha) (Curcuma longa) and Sariba (Gopi)(Hemidesmus indicus). It is further cooked with paste (kalka) of cooling and wound-healing drugs like Kadalikanda (banana rhizome), Yastimadhu (Glycyrhiza glabra), Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides), Kustha (Saussurea lappa), and Chandana (Santalum album). This medicated oil is indicated in Raktapittottara Kuṣṭha (skin disorders associated with vitiated blood and Pitta) and in Kledayukta Visarpa (moist, inflammatory spreading skin conditions resembling erysipelas).
sections.ingredients:
I. Kvatha Dravyas (Decoction Ingredients) 

 Nyagrodha Tvak (Ficus benghalensis – Banyan bark) – 40 gm 
 Udumbara Tvak (Ficus racemosa – Cluster fig bark) – 40 gm 
 Ashvattha Tvak (Ficus religiosa – Peepal bark) – 40 gm 
 Plaksha Tvak (Ficus lacor – Wavy-leaf fig bark) – 40 gm 
 Parisha Tvak (Thespesia populnea – Portia tree bark) – 40 gm 
 Haridra Tvak (Curcuma longa – Turmeric bark/rhizome) – 40 gm 
 Sariba Tvak (Hemidesmus indicus – Indian sarsaparilla) – 40 gm 
 Water – 4.8 litres (reduced to one-fourth) 

 II. Taila Dravya 

 Murchita Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Processed sesame oil) – 300 ml 

 III. Kalka Dravyas (Paste Ingredients) 

 Kadalikanda (Musa paradisiaca – Banana rhizome) – 12.5 gm 
 Tvak (Cinnamomum verum – Cinnamon bark) – 12.5 gm 
 Yastimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra – Licorice) – 12.5 gm 
 Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides – Vetiver) – 12.5 gm 
 Kustha (Saussurea lappa – Costus root) – 12.5 gm 
 Candana (Santalum album – Sandalwood) – 12.5 gm 

 Method Of Preparation 
 First, a decoction is prepared from the Kvatha dravyas by boiling them in water and reducing it to one-fourth of the original quantity. The Kalka dravyas are finely ground into a smooth paste. This paste is mixed with Murchita Tila Taila, and the prepared decoction is added. The mixture is heated over mild fire following classical Sneha Paka Vidhi (medicated oil preparation method) until only the oil remains and proper Taila Siddhi Lakshanas (signs of prepared oil) appear. After cooling, the oil is filtered and stored in airtight glass containers.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Rakta-shodhaka (blood purifier) 
 Pitta-shamaka (pacifies Pitta Dosha) 
 Kledahara (reduces excessive moisture and discharge) 
 Vrana-ropaka (wound healing) 
 Dahahara (relieves burning sensation) 

 Panchavalkala group provides strong astringent (Kashaya rasa) and wound-healing properties. Haridra (Curcuma longa) and Sariva (Hemidesmus indicus) act as anti-inflammatory and blood-purifying agents. Chandana (Santalum album) and Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides) impart cooling action, reducing burning and redness.
sections.indications:
Raktapittottara Kushtha ( skin disorders with blood and Pitta involvement) 
 Kledayukta Visarpa (moist inflammatory spreading skin lesions) 
 Oozing dermatitis 
 Inflammatory skin conditions with discharge 

 Method Of Use 

 Abhyanga (External application over affected area)
sections.precautions:
For external use only unless advised by a physician. 
 Avoid application over deep open wounds without medical guidance. 
 Perform a patch test in sensitive skin. 

 Conclusion 
 Panchavalkaladi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic formulation primarily indicated in inflammatory and exudative skin disorders associated with Rakta (blood) and Pitta dosha vitiation. The synergistic action of the Panchavalkala group, Haridra (Curcuma longa), Sariba (Hemidesmus indicus), and cooling herbs like Chandana (Santalum album) and Ushira (Vetiveria zizanioides) helps reduce inflammation, discharge, redness, and burning. Its strong astringent and wound-healing properties make it particularly beneficial in Raktapittottara Kushtha (skin disorders with blood and Pitta involvement) and Kledayukta Visarpa (moist inflammatory spreading skin lesions). When used appropriately under Ayurvedic guidance, this Taila serves as an effective topical remedy for managing moist and inflammatory dermatological conditions.

name: Panchgun Tailam (Oil)

sections.introduction: Panchgun Tailam is herbal Ayurvedic medicated oil that has property to keep the Vata and Pitta balanced. This is Ayurvedic medicine that is useful in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, ear ache, non-healing wounds, etc.
sections.ingredients:
Haritaki ( Chebulic Myrobalan ) fruit rind ( Terminalia chebula ) – 60 g 
 Vibhitaki ( Belliric Myrobalan ) fruit rind ( Terminalia bellirica ) – 60 g 
 Amalaki (Indian gooseberry) ( Emblica officinalis ) fruit – 60 g 
 Nimba (Neem) ( Azadirachta indica ) – Leaves of – 180 g 
 Sambhalu (Nirgundi) ( Vitex negundo ) – Leaves – 180 g 
 Water 
 Til taila (Sesame oil) – 960 ml 
 Madhuchishta (Honey bee wax) 
 Gandhaphiroja (Sarala) ( Pinus longifolia ) – Long leaved pine (wood, resin) 
 Shilarasa (Turushka) ( Amber orientalis ) – Liquid 
 Rala (Shala) ( Shorea robusta ) 
 Guggulu (Indian bedelium) (gum resin) ( Commiphora mukul ) 
 Karpoora (Camphor) ( Cinnamomum camphora ) – 60 g 
 Tarapina taila (Turpentine oil) – 30 ml 
 Tailaparna (Eucalyptus oil) – 30 ml 
 Kejoputi taila – 30 ml 

 Method of Preparation 

 Prepare decoction using Haritaki, Vibhitaki, Amalak, Nimba and Sambhalu with about 4.320 liters which is boiled till it get reduced to 1.080 liters. 
 Now form a paste using 48 g of each of Madhuchishta, Gandhaphiroja, Shilarasa, Rala and Guggulu. 
 Mix all the ingredients and boil till its whole moisture is lost from the oil and then filter it. 
 Add Eucalyptus, and Turpentine oil at the end and stir it well. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Panchgun Tailam is efficient Ayurvedic oil that is much helpful to keep the vata and pitta balance and provides relief from disease. It has only external use. 
 It possesses antiseptic property that helps in good healing in case of wounds, cuts and burn injuries. This oil is very beneficial in arthritis, massaging with this oil provides relief from pain and swelling, improving the movements in joints. It is effective to get rid of pain in sprain and reduces joint pain, helps in easy movements. It is very suitable in rheumatoid arthritis. Reliving pain, swelling and redness in joints. It is also good to use in ear ache, dropping little drops of this oil in ear helps to lessen the pain in ear.
sections.how_to_use: Panchgun Tailam is only for external application. Use appropriate amount of oil and smoothly rub it over the affected area and it can be used for 3-6 months as recommended by doctor.
sections.therapeutic_uses:
This Ayurvedic remedy is for treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis. 
 Also a good relief in case of ear ache, and non-healing wounds. 
 This is even useful remedy for internal muscular Pain, sprain. 
 It can give relief from Burn injury.
sections.contraindications_side_effects:
No side effects has been known with external application of this oil. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Coconut oil – It is an edible oil produced from the kernel of mature coconuts. This oil is popular for its pleasant aroma, taste, and powerful antioxidants. By consuming internally, it enhances strength and vitality, wound healing and relieves skin diseases like eczema, psoriasis. Coconut oil is valuable in pacifying Vata and Pitta Dosha while it increases Kapha dosha. 
 Udumbara ( Ficus racemosa ) – Also known as cluster fig is used since ancient times. It is cold in potency and treats bleeding disorders instantly. It cures intestinal worms, alleviates Pitta and rakta, fatigue, burning sensation and thirst. 
 Aswattha ( Ficus religiosa ) – This tree is also from vata kula. Its bark contains tannin,rubber,wax. This herb helps in to enhance complexion, wound healing, reducing pain and swelling and acts as haemostatic. It is also prescribed as an aphrodisiac. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Crush the roots of Paranthi, Saptachakra – 48g each and add water in it. 
 Boil the mixture and reduced to 1/4th (decoction). 
 Add coconut oil 768ml + swarasa of Nimbu, Durva kalka of drugs  in decoction and boil it. 
 When whole water is evaporated and oil is left behind.Kept aside to cool. 
 Filter the oil and add Ahiphena, vibhitaka etc. should be added.

name: Parinathakeryadiksheeradi Thailam

sections.introduction: Parinathakereeksheeradi thailam is an ayurvedic formulation that is mainly used for the treatment of Paralysis. It is often caused by interrupted blood supply. Ayurveda refers to paralysis as Pakshaghat and attributes its occurrence to Vata vikruti.
sections.ingredients:
Drava Dravya 

 Parinatakeriksheera (Coconut oil) – 640ml 
 Jambira Swarasa – 640ml 
 Murchita Tila Taila – 320ml 

 Kalka Dravyas 

 Haridra ( Curcuma longa) 
 Guggulu ( Commiphora mukul )
sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Parinatakeriksheera (Coconut oil) – It is an edible oil produced from the kernel of mature coconuts. This oil is popular for its pleasant aroma, taste, and powerful antioxidants. By consuming internally enhances strength and vitality, wound healing and reat skin woes like eczema, psoriasis. Coconut oil is valuable in pacifying vata and pitta dosha while it increases Kapha dosha. 
 Haridra ( Curcuma longa ) – This shrub belongs to Kushthaghna, Kandughna, Vishaghna group. It is mainly Kapha Vata shamak. Commonly used for disorders caused by tridoshas.Local application of turmeric is anti-inflammatory, analgesic and complexion enhancer. It stimulates blood formation and treating various bleeding disorders. Bhasma of tintruturated with turmeric is an effective remedy for prameha. It reduces and helps in treating weakness. 
 Guggulu ( Commiphora mukul ) – Pure guggul is snigdha, soft, sticky with a sweet smell, bitter taste and soluble in water. It is anti-inflammatory, analgesic, vata shamak, pitta shodhak in nature. Guggul works on all tissues of body and is effective in rejuvenating body tissues and increasing strength.it is also a good Rasayan in obesity and diseases of vata kapha. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Prepare the Kalka of kalka dravyas and mix it with taila dravya, drava dravyas taken in stainless steel vessel 
 Then it should be subjected to a heating process till it remains the quantity of Murchita tila taila. On completion of the process, it should be filtered and stored in glass bottles.
sections.indications:
Vataroga 
 Paralysis 
 Osteoarthritis 
 Osteoporosis 
 Rheumatic pain 
 Neurological disorders 
 Cervical spondylosis
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Anti-inflammatory 
 Analgesic 
 Nervine tonic 
 Anti-paralytic 
 Neuroprotective 

 Usage 

 It can be used as both Abhyanga and Nasya 
 Use a small amount of oil and massage all over the body. 
 It can be used before taking a bath.
sections.side_effects:
Mainly there are no side effects noted till now as if you are consuming internally or externally. In high doses more than 5ml it can cause abdominal discomfort, nausea, indigestion etc. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Peedashamak Taila

sections.overview: Peedashamak Taila – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction:
Peedashamak Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil formulated with potent Vata-shamaka (vata dosha pacifying), vedanasthapana (analgesic), and srotoshodhaka (channel cleansing) substances processed in sesame oil. The preparation is traditionally indicated for external application in painful conditions associated with aggravated Vata dosha, traumatic injury, stiffness, and impaired local circulation. The formulation combines penetrating herbal leaves, aromatic stimulants, and mineral salts processed through classical oil preparation techniques to produce a preparation that supports reduction of pain, restoration of mobility, and improvement of tissue function. 
 The formulation describes preparation of medicated oil by triturating specified ingredients into a paste and processing them in heated sesame oil followed by incorporation of aromatic camphor. The oil is used externally through massage and mild fomentation as a supportive measure in localized pain and stiffness.
sections.composition:
I. Taila Dravya (Base Oil) 

 Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Sesame Oil) 

 II. Patra Dravyas (Leaf Ingredients) 

 Siris Patra (Botanical: Albizia lebbeck – Siris Leaf) 
 Dhattura Patra (Botanical: Datura metel – Thorn Apple Leaf) 
 Nirgundi Patra (Botanical: Vitex negundo – Five-Leaved Chaste Tree Leaf) 
 Sarpadamshtra / Sitaba Patra (Botanical: Tribulus terrestris – Caltrop Leaf) 

 III. Kalka Dravyas (Paste Ingredients) 

 Medalakadi (traditional aromatic wood ingredient as per classical reference) 
 Sunthi (Zingiber officinale – Dry Ginger Rhizome) 
 Ajamoda / Ajavayana (Trachyspermum ammi – Ajwain Fruit) 
 Vacha (Acorus calamus – Sweet Flag Rhizome) 
 Saindhava Lavana (Rock Salt – natural mineral salt) 
 Vatsanabha Shuddha (Aconitum ferox – Purified Aconite) 
 Kuchila Shuddha (Strychnos nux-vomica – Purified Nux Vomica Seed) 
 Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora – Camphor) 

 Method Of Preparation 
 Except Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora), all ingredients are cleaned and coarsely powdered. The powdered substances are triturated with water to obtain a uniform kalka (paste). Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) is heated in a suitable vessel. The prepared paste is introduced gradually and processed in heated oil by frying portions of the paste until proper infusion of active principles is achieved. The oil is filtered immediately while warm. Finely powdered Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora) is added to the warm oil, mixed thoroughly, and stored in airtight glass containers after cooling. 
 Method Of Use 
 External application only. 
The oil is applied over the affected region and gently massaged. Mild local fomentation may be administered after application as directed by a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Vedanasthapana (analgesic) supportive action 
 Vata-shamaka effect (vata dosha pacification) 
 Shothahara supportive action (antiinflammatory) 
 Srotoshodhaka supportive action (channel cleansing) 
 Stambhana-supportive stabilization of tissues 
 Circulatory enhancing local action 

 Clinical Indications 

 Localized pain due to aggravated Vata dosha 
 Post-traumatic residual pain and stiffness 
 Joint rigidity and restricted mobility 
 Musculoskeletal discomfort with impaired circulation 
 Chronic pain following injury 
 Vataja sandhishula and asthishula (joint pain) 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Siris Patra (Albizia lebbeck) exhibits Vata-Kapha shamaka and shothahara supportive effects beneficial in inflammatory states. Dhattura Patra (Datura metel) demonstrates Vedanasthapana and Ushna properties that support pain reduction. Nirgundi Patra (Vitex negundo) provides Vata-shamaka and shothahara supportive actions assisting mobility. Sarpadamshtra (Tribulus terrestris) contributes Shothahara (antiinflammatory) and srotoshodhaka (channel cleansing) supportive properties. Sunthi (Zingiber officinale) and Ajamoda (Trachyspermum ammi) exhibit Deepana and Vatahara (vata pacifying) actions supporting improved circulation. Vacha (Acorus calamus) provides penetrating and channel-clearing properties. Saindhava Lavana supports Sukshma (mild) and srotoshodhaka (channel cleansing) action facilitating absorption. Vatsanabha (Aconitum ferox, purified) and Kuchila (Strychnos nux-vomica, purified) are traditionally described as potent stimulatory agents when properly processed. Karpura (Cinnamomum camphora) enhances penetration and provides a soothing aromatic effect. Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) acts as a Snigdha (unctuous), Sukshma (mild), and deeply penetrating base facilitating delivery of active constituents.
sections.precautions:
For external use only. 
 Wash hands thoroughly after application due to the presence of potent ingredients. 
 Use only under supervision of a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner. 
 Avoid contact with eyes and mucous membranes. 
 Do not apply over open wounds or hypersensitive skin. 

 Conclusion 
 Peedashamak Taila is a traditionally formulated Ayurvedic medicated oil designed to provide localized relief in painful Vata-dominant conditions through external application. The integration of Siris Patra (Albizia lebbeck), Dhattura Patra (Datura metel), Nirgundi Patra (Vitex negundo), and classical stimulatory substances processed in Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum) produces a preparation intended to support reduction of pain, improvement of circulation, and restoration of functional mobility. When used appropriately under professional supervision, this classical formulation serves as a supportive therapeutic measure for stabilization of musculoskeletal function and enhancement of tissue resilience following injury or chronic Vata dosha aggravation.

name: Pinda Thailam (Oil)

sections.overview:
Pinda Thailam (Oil) – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage 
 Reference: Charaka Samhita Chikitsa Sthana 29/123, Ashtanga Hridayam Chikitsa Sthana 22/22
sections.introduction: Pinda Thailam is an Ayurvedic medicated oil having anti-inflammatory properties. This herbal oil is useful to relieve pain especially caused due to gouty arthritis. It is for external application only.
sections.ingredients:
Madhuchhista (Honey bee wax) – 280 g 
 Manjishta ( Rubia cordifolia ) – 455 g 
 Sarjarasa ( Vateria indica ) –  – 186 g 
 Sariva ( Hemidesmus indicus ) – 455 g 
 Taila ( Sesamum indicum ) Oil – 6 liters 
 Water – 24 liters 

 Method of Preparation 
 Heat all the above given ingredients till all the moisture content gets evaporated and Taila is formed. Then the oil is filtered and preserved. Keep it in cool and dry place. 
 Medicinal Properties

sections.description_of_main_ingredients:
Bala – The plant Sida cordifolia is a medicinal plant. The various portions of plant such as the root, stem and leaves can be used. It is analgesic, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory. The chemical composition of this herb comprises alkaloids, flavonoids, sterols, fatty acids. Its leaves contain small quantities of both ephedrine and pseudoephedrine which stimulate the CNS. 
 Shatavari ( Asparagus racemosus ) – Shatavari is antispasmodic, nervine, anti-inflammatory, and antibacterial in nature.  It helps in balances pitta and kapha doshas. It contains Diosenin, rutin, flavonoids, Sarsapogenin etc

 Add 25.6gms each of herbs in 24.576L water and boil it until reduced to 6.144L (Decoction).

 When all moisture evaporates and oil is left behind, off the gas.

These phytochemicals are known to provide therapeutic properties such as – antioxidant, analgesic, anti-inflammatory, stimulatory etc. One more, anti-nociceptive properties control problems related to painful or injurious stimulus by sensory neurons. The Immunologic adjuvant properties known to enhance the immune system. The analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties provide relief from pain and stiffness in the muscles and joints. 
 Therapeutic Uses 
 Prasarini Thailam (Oil) is a useful to treat rheumatoid arthritis, sciatica, neck pain, stiffness etc. It is used for external application. 
 How to Use? 
 It is used as external application for massage and externally it can be used for a long period of time. 
 Contraindications / Side Effects 
 No side effects have been reported with its external application. 
 
 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.overview:
Puvankurundaladi Taila – Ingredients, Preparation, Uses, Indications, Benefits More 
 (पूवन्कुरुन्दलादि तैलम्) 
 Also known as Uttamakanyakādi Eranda Taila / Pūvankurundalādi Āvanakkenna
sections.introduction: Pūvankurundalādi Taila is a classical internal Ayurvedic formulation prepared primarily in Eranda Taila (Castor oil – Ricinus communis ) base. It is widely referenced in Kerala Ayurvedic practice and is especially known for managing chronic fevers, pediatric Vata disorders (Phakka/Kana), respiratory distress, and gastrointestinal dysfunction. The formulation is highly complex, combining numerous Swarasa dravyas (fresh herbal juices) with a potent blend of Kalka dravyas having Deepana (digestive stimulant), Pachana (metabolic correction), Jvaraghna (anti-pyretic), and Vata-Kapha pacifying properties. Due to the castor oil base, it also exerts mild purgative and detoxifying actions.
sections.classical_reference:
सहदेवी पलंवशि ताम्बूलं क्षीरिणो तथा। 
 पर्णाजमोदो भृङ्गश्च जम्बूपत्रं तथैव च।। 
 यासापत्रं शक्रलता विष्णुक्रान्ता च तिन्दुकम्। 
 ब्रह्मी मण्डूकपर्णी च पत्रं च कटुतुम्बिजम्।। 
 पल्लवाः आम्रवृक्षस्य काकमाची च सर्वतः। 
 बिल्वार्धमानसंयुक्तालयरसं ग्राहयेद्भिषक्।। 
 तुलस्याश्च रसोनस्य रसो ग्राह्यश्च तत्समः। 
 दद्याद्विकुडवं तत्र तैलमेरण्डसंभवम्।। 
 कल्कार्थं सारिवा मुस्ता पाठा कुटजमूलकम्। 
 बालं दाडिमकं चैव पर्पटं चाष्टमाषकम्।। 
 देवदारु यवानी च रास्नामधुकजीरकम्। 
 निम्बाश्वगन्धातिविषा भारङ्गी कटुरोहिणी।। 
 हिङ्गु निर्वेषी जातिपत्रिका जातीफलं लवङ्गकम्।। 
 तैलं संसाध्य विधिवद्भक्षयेच्च विधानवित्। 
 ज्वरं श्वासं बालरोगं विवन्धं मलमूत्रयोः। 
 जिह्वापाकं कोष्ठपाकं मोहालस्यं च नाशयेत्।। 
 पानाज्ज्वरं तथा तीव्रं चतुःषष्टिविधं जयेत्।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 Meaning Of The Shloka 
 The verse describes a medicated castor oil preparation processed with numerous herbal juices such as Sahadevi, Tambula, Vishnukranta, Brahmi, Tulasi, and Lasuna. It is fortified with digestive, carminative, anti-pyretic, and Vata–Kapha pacifying herbs. The oil, when prepared properly and administered internally in appropriate dosage, alleviates Jvara (fever), Śvāsa (dyspnea), Balaroga (childhood Vata disorders), constipation, urinary obstruction, oral inflammation, digestive disorders, Moha (delirium), Alasya (lethargy) and is said to manage even 64 types of fever.

The oil is filtered and stored in airtight glass containers.

sections.dose_5_10_ml_twice_daily: Time: Morning and evening, as directed by an Ayurvedic physician
sections.indications:
Jvara (acute and chronic fevers) 
 Chatushashti Jvara (64 types of fevers) 
 Shvasa (breathlessness, respiratory distress) 
 Balaroga (especially Kerala-described ‘Kana’ – pediatric Vata disorder) 
 Malavibandha (constipation) 
 Mutravibandha (urinary obstruction) 
 Jihvapaka (oral inflammation) 
 Kosthapaka (intestinal inflammation) 
 Moha (delirium) 
 Alasya (lethargy)
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Jvaraghna (anti-pyretic) 
 Vata-Kapha shamaka 
 Deepana and Pachana (digestive stimulant and metabolic corrector) 
 Mild virechana (purgative action due to castor oil) 
 Shvasa hara (relieves respiratory distress) 

 Conclusion 
 Pūvankurundalādi Taila is a highly potent internal classical formulation centered on castor oil, enriched with numerous Swarasa dravyas and powerful digestive–anti-pyretic herbs. Its broad therapeutic spectrum, especially in fevers, respiratory disorders, pediatric Vata conditions, and gastrointestinal dysfunction, demonstrates the depth of Ayurvedic pharmaceutics in designing multi-target formulations. The synergy of Tulasi (( Ocimum sanctum )), Lasuna ( Allium sativum ), Deepana-Pachana herbs, and Eranda Taila (castor oil) enables detoxification, digestive correction, and systemic Vata-Kapha regulation. Classical texts attribute to it the capacity to manage even complex and severe febrile conditions. When administered in proper dosage under medical supervision, Pūvankurundalādi Taila serves as a comprehensive Ayurvedic internal remedy for chronic metabolic and febrile disorders.

 तैलं संसाध्य विधिवद्भक्षयेच्च विधानवित्। 
 ज्वरं श्वासं बालरोगं विवन्धं मलमूत्रयोः। 
 जिह्वापाकं कोष्ठपाकं मोहालस्यं च नाशयेत्।। 
 पानाज्ज्वरं तथा तीव्रं चतुःषष्टिविधं जयेत्।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 Meaning Of The Shloka 
 The verse describes a medicated castor oil preparation processed with numerous herbal juices such as Sahadevi, Tambula, Vishnukranta, Brahmi, Tulasi, and Lasuna. It is fortified with digestive, carminative, anti-pyretic, and Vata–Kapha pacifying herbs. The oil, when prepared properly and administered internally in appropriate dosage, alleviates Jvara (fever), Śvāsa (dyspnea), Balaroga (childhood Vata disorders), constipation, urinary obstruction, oral inflammation, digestive disorders, Moha (delirium), Alasya (lethargy) and is said to manage even 64 types of fever. 
 Composition 
 I. Drava Dravyas (Fresh Juices – Swarasa) 
 
 Sahadevi ( Vernonia cinerea ) – 20 ml 
 Palamvamsi (regional herb) – 20 ml 
 Tambula ( Piper betle – Betel leaf) – 20 ml 
 Ksirini (milky latex plant, regional reference) – 20 ml 
 Parnajamoda ( Trachyspermum roxburghianum ) – 20 ml 
 Bhringaraja ( Eclipta alba ) – 20 ml 
 Jambu Patra ( Syzygium cumini leaf) – 20 ml 
 Vasa Patra ( Adhatoda vasica ) – 20 ml 
 Shakralata (regional creeper) – 20 ml 
 Vishnukranta ( Evolvulus alsinoides ) – 20 ml 
 Tinduka ( Diospyros peregrina ) – 20 ml 
 Brahmi ( Bacopa monnieri ) – 20 ml 
 Mandukaparni ( Centella asiatica ) – 20 ml 
 Katutumbi ( Lagenaria siceraria ) – 20 ml 
 Amra Patra ( Mangifera indica tender leaf) – 20 ml 
 Kakamachi ( Solanum nigrum ) – 20 ml 
 Tulasi ( Ocimum sanctum ) – 320 ml 
 Lasuna ( Allium sativum – Garlic) – 320 ml 
 
 II. Taila Dravya 
 
 Murchita Eranda Taila ( Ricinus communis – Processed castor oil) – 320 ml 
 
 III. Kalka Dravyas 
 
 Sariva ( Hemidesmus indicus ) – 8 gm 
 Musta ( Cyperus rotundus ) – 8 gm 
 Patha ( Cissampelos pareira ) – 8 gm 
 Kutaja Mula ( Holarrhena antidysenterica ) – 8 gm 
 Bala ( Sida cordifolia ) – 8 gm 
 Dadima ( Punica granatum ) – 8 gm 
 Parpataka ( Fumaria indica ) – 8 gm 
 Devadaru ( Cedrus deodara ) – 2 gm 
 Yavani ( Trachyspermum ammi – Ajwain) – 2 gm 
 Rasna ( Pluchea lanceolata ) – 2 gm 
 Yastimadhu ( Glycyrrhiza glabra ) – 2 gm 
 Jiraka ( Cuminum cyminum ) – 2 gm 
 Nimba ( Azadirachta indica ) – 2 gm 
 Ashwagandha ( Withania somnifera ) – 2 gm 
 Ativisha ( Aconitum heterophyllum ) – 2 gm 
 Bharangi ( Clerodendrum serratum ) – 2 gm 
 Katuki ( Picrorhiza kurroa ) – 2 gm 
 Haritaki ( Terminalia chebula ) – 2 gm 
 Hingu ( Ferula asafoetida ) – 2 gm 
 Jatipatrika ( Myristica fragrans – Mace) – 2 gm 
 Jatiphala ( Myristica fragrans – Nutmeg) – 2 gm 
 Lavanga ( Syzygium aromaticum – Clove) – 2 gm 
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 The Kalka dravyas are finely ground into a paste. These are added to the Murchita Eranda Taila along with all Drava dravyas in a stainless steel vessel. The mixture is cooked over mild heat with continuous stirring until the liquid content evaporates and only the prescribed quantity of castor oil remains, indicating proper Sneha Siddhi. The oil is filtered and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 Internal Administration 
 
 Dose: 5–10 ml twice daily 
 Time: Morning and evening, as directed by an Ayurvedic physician 
 
 Indications 
 
 Jvara (acute and chronic fevers) 
 Chatushashti Jvara (64 types of fevers) 
 Shvasa (breathlessness, respiratory distress) 
 Balaroga (especially Kerala-described ‘Kana’ – pediatric Vata disorder) 
 Malavibandha (constipation) 
 Mutravibandha (urinary obstruction) 
 Jihvapaka (oral inflammation) 
 Kosthapaka (intestinal inflammation) 
 Moha (delirium) 
 Alasya (lethargy) 
 
 Pharmacological Actions 
 
 Jvaraghna (anti-pyretic) 
 Vata-Kapha shamaka 
 Deepana and Pachana (digestive stimulant and metabolic corrector) 
 Mild virechana (purgative action due to castor oil) 
 Shvasa hara (relieves respiratory distress) 
 
 Conclusion 
 Pūvankurundalādi Taila is a highly potent internal classical formulation centered on castor oil, enriched with numerous Swarasa dravyas and powerful digestive–anti-pyretic herbs. Its broad therapeutic spectrum, especially in fevers, respiratory disorders, pediatric Vata conditions, and gastrointestinal dysfunction, demonstrates the depth of Ayurvedic pharmaceutics in designing multi-target formulations. The synergy of Tulasi (( Ocimum sanctum )), Lasuna ( Allium sativum ), Deepana-Pachana herbs, and Eranda Taila (castor oil) enables detoxification, digestive correction, and systemic Vata-Kapha regulation. Classical texts attribute to it the capacity to manage even complex and severe febrile conditions. When administered in proper dosage under medical supervision, Pūvankurundalādi Taila serves as a comprehensive Ayurvedic internal remedy for chronic metabolic and febrile disorders.

Abstract 
 Rasnadi Thailam is a herbal oil formulation mentioned in classical texts. It is usually used in painful conditions and inflammation. It is also beneficial in cold and cough-like symptoms. This oil is prepared by using coconut oil or sesame oil as base. It is basically used in managing diseases affecting the head. In this article we will discuss Rasnadi oil ingredients, method of preparation, benefits and dosage.
sections.introduction:
Rasnadi thailam is a medicated oil prepared from natural herbs. It mainly acts on vata dosha. So, the important feature of aggravated vata is pain in different parts of the body. As the name suggests Rasnadi thailam, Rasna ( Pluchea lanceolata ) is its primary ingredient. It applied locally over painful regions. It contains oil and water soluble photo chemicals of herbal drugs used. It corrects all nervous and muscular disorders. 
 Classical Indication 
 According to classical texts, it helps in pacification of vitiated vata dosha among other dosha (vata, pitta and kapha) but some Acharya’s believe it in rakat (blood) and pitta dosha. There is dushti (affecting) of various dhatus (body ailments) like rasa (body fluid), rakat (blood), asthi (bone). The various classical indications of Rasnadi oil is as following- 

 Ardit (Facial palsy) 
 Ardhavbhedak (Migraine) 
 Vaatrakt (Gout) 
 Amavata (Rheumatoid arthritis)
sections.ingredients:
The drugs required for preparation of Rasnadi thailam are given as following- 

 Rasna (Pluchea lanceolata) 
 Madhuk ( Glycyrrhiza glabra) 
 Bala (Sida cordifolia) 
 Atibala ( Abutilon indicum) 
 Bilwa ( Aegle marmelos) 
 Agnimanth ( Premna mucronata) 
 Shayonak (Oroxylum indicum ) 
 Gambhari (Gmelina arborea) 
 Patla ( Stereospermum suaveolens) 
 Shalparni ( Desmodium gangeticum) 
 Prishniparni ( Uraria picta) 
 Brihati ( Solanum indicum) 
 Kantakari ( Solanum xanthocarpum) 
 Gokshura ( Tribulus terrestris) 
 Til tail ( Sesame oil) 
 Cow’s milk 

 Benefits Of Ingredients 

 Rasna- It is very helpful in rheumatic pain and pacifies muscle spasms due to its analgesic activity. It is also beneficial for osteoarthritis patients. It also manages cold and cough-like symptoms. 
 Madhuk- It helps in improving blood circulation, prevents viruses, bacteria and other infections. It reduces pain, swelling and inflammation. It is very effective in cough and cold. 
 Bala- It is beneficial in skin numbness, nerve pain and in massage oil for joint diseases. It is helpful in pacifying vata dosha and improves blood circulation. 
 Atibala- It is useful in gout and other inflammatory conditions. It has an astringent, anti-inflammatory and analgesic effect so reduces pain, swelling. 
 Bilwa- It cures diseases which are caused due to vitiated vata and kapha dosha. It is bitter in taste, corrects metabolism and reduces edema. It is also beneficial for asthmatic patients. 
 Agnimantha- Very beneficial for all types of vata related disorders like nervous and musculoskeletal pain. It is useful in conditions such as neuralgia, arthritis and common cold. 
 Shayonag- It has antioxidant properties, prevents microbes and reduces inflammation. It is used as antipyretic, anti arthritic and analgesic. 
 Gambhari- It relieves pain, vertigo, inflammation and vata related disorders. Beneficial if any weakness in the nervous system. It acts as a hepato and cardio protective drug. 
 Patla- It is a neuro protective drug which removes toxins from the body and reduces pain, swelling. It strengthens full body muscles and increases metabolism of the body. 
 Shalparni- It is very effective in enteric fever, respiratory problems and strengthens the immune system. It provides power to muscles and maintains good blood flow. 
 Prishniparni- It is very effective in healing fractured bones and provides strength to bones. Also beneficial for types of fever, cough, bronchitis, gout, burning sensation. 
 Brihati- It is beneficial for digestion and edematous swelling. It prevents bacterial, viral infections and has anti-inflammatory properties. 
 Kantakari- It decoction is useful in respiratory disorders like cough, cold and fever. It has anthelmintic properties. It relieves various types of skin infections, swelling. 
 Gokshura- It is used to manage asthma, cough, edema, rheumatic pain like conditions. It provides strength to the nervous system and boosts ophthalmic nerves. 
 Til tail- It reduces pain, inflammation and acts as an antioxidant. It is very beneficial in arthritis and gingivitis. It is good for stress and depression. 
 Cow’s milk- It contains nutrients which are important for bone health such as calcium, vit.D, protein and phosphorus. It helps in healing of fractured bones. 

 Method Of Preparation 
 The steps for the preparation of Rasnadi thailam are given as following- 

 Firstly, collect all drugs mentioned above and wash them properly. 
 Then make kalka (paste) of the drugs. 
 Then add milk to the paste formed and mix them properly, keep stirring. 
 At last add sesame oil to the solution obtained and mix it properly. 
 Then filter the oil obtained in a clean vessel. 
 Store the oil in a clean airtight glass container and keep it away from direct sunlight.
sections.properties:
The properties of Rasnadi thailam are given as following- 

 It has an analgesic property. 
 Has an anti arthritic effect. 
 It has an anti-inflammatory and antioxidant property. 
 Have an anti-helminthic, anti-factorial, antifungal effect.
sections.indications:
The various indications of Rasnadi Thailam are given as following- 

 Arthritis 
 Facial palsy 
 LBA (low backache) 
 Migraine 
 Chronic fever 
 Cold and cough 
 Diseases of ear, eyes, nose, throat 
 Joint pain 
 Muscular pain
sections.contraindications:
The conditions when Rasnadi thailam not given are as following- 

 Administered as per directed by the physician. 
 Avoided in women during puerperium. 
 Difficulty in breathing.
sections.dosage_usage:
Applied locally to the painful region twice daily or given as nasya (nasal installation) 2-3 drops in each nostril. 
 Taste 
 Tikhat (Bitter) 
 Smell 
 Like Oil 
 Conclusion 
 Above mentioned oil is mentioned in our classics which manages all types of pain related disorders. It is prepared by using sesame or coconut oil as a base in this herbal formulation. It is indicated in all nervous and musculoskeletal conditions. Overall it is beneficial for ENT related or inflammatory disorders. So you can use Rasnadi oil for painful conditions under the supervision of a physician.

sections.how_to_use_sahacharadi_thailam_oil:
It is used for massage. 
 Orally – 3-5 ml, 1-2 times a day, before having meals along with warm water or warm milk, or as suggested by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 It is also used for vaginal douche, rectal enema, Greeva Basti, Janu Basti etc. 
 How long to use Sahacharadi Thailam (Oil)? 
 Externally, it can be used for a very long period of time. 
 Orally and for other Ayurvedic treatments- not more than 2-3 months.

Efficient Ayurvedic treatment for tremors, convulsions, psychosis, and stiffness of thigh, muscle cramps, and muscle wasting. 
 Also a helpful to provide relief from rhinitis and sinusitis. 
 Another use in gynecological disorders. 
 Reduces the joint pain caused due to Osteoarthritis.
sections.contraindications_side_effects:
No side effects till now is being reported with this medicine. 
 Its oral intake must be under the direction of Ayurvedic doctor. 
 Keep it away from the reach and sight of children. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Sahadevyadi Taila

sections.overview: Sahadevyadi Taila – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction: Sahadevyadi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil prepared using the fresh juice of Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea), processed sesame oil, cow’s milk, and a group of six herbs formulated as kalka (paste). The preparation is traditionally indicated for external application in various types of fever. The formulation combines cooling, soothing, and dosha-balancing properties that help reduce heat, discomfort, and systemic imbalance associated with febrile conditions.
sections.reference_shloka:
सहदेवीरसे तैलं साधयेन्मतिमान् भिषक् । 
षडङ्गकल्कं सक्षीरं सर्वज्वरहरं परम्।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 The verse explains that medicated oil prepared with Sahadevi juice, milk, and a group of six herbal pastes is highly effective in alleviating all types of fever when prepared properly by a knowledgeable physician.
sections.composition:
I. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredients) 

 Sahadevi Svarasa (Vernonia cinerea – Purple Fleabane Whole Plant Juice) – 480 ml 
 Goksira (Cow’s Milk) – 480 ml 

 II. Taila Dravya (Base Oil) 

 Murchita Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Processed Sesame Oil) – 240 ml 

 III. Kalka Dravyas (Herbal Paste Ingredients) 

 Musta (Cyperus rotundus – Nut Grass Rhizome) – 10 gm 
 Parpataka (Fumaria parviflora – Fumitory Whole Plant) – 10 gm 
 Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides – Vetiver Root) – 10 gm 
 Candana (Santalum album – Sandalwood Heartwood) – 10 gm 
 Udicya (Pavonia odorata – Fragrant Swamp Mallow Root) – 10 gm 
 Nagara (Zingiber officinale – Dry Ginger Rhizome) – 10 gm 

 Method Of Preparation 
 All kalka dravyas (pasted herbs) are cleaned, dried if necessary, and finely powdered. These powders are triturated with a small quantity of liquid to form a smooth herbal paste. The processed sesame oil is taken in a clean stainless steel vessel and combined with Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea) fresh juice and cow’s milk. The prepared herbal paste is then added to this mixture. The contents are heated over mild fire following classical Sneha Paka (oil preparation) principles. Continuous stirring is maintained to ensure proper integration of ingredients and to avoid scorching. Heating is continued until the liquid components evaporate completely and only medicated oil remains in the original oil quantity. Proper completion is identified by absence of moisture, characteristic aroma, and formation of soft, non-sticky kalka (paste) residue. After natural cooling, the oil is filtered through a clean cloth and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 The medicated oil is applied externally through Abhyanga (therapeutic oil massage). Application may be performed over the entire body or localized regions as advised by an Ayurvedic practitioner.
sections.pharmacological_actions:
Reduces febrile heat and burning sensation

 Fever associated with burning sensation and restlessness 
 Supportive external therapy during systemic heat conditions 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea) is traditionally described as a cooling and fever-alleviating herb that helps regulate systemic heat. Cow’s milk contributes nourishing, soothing, and stabilizing qualities that mitigate heat and dryness. Sesame oil acts as a penetrating base that carries the active principles of the herbs into peripheral tissues. Musta (Cyperus rotundus) and Parpataka (Fumaria parviflora) are classically recognized for their role in fever management and digestive balance. Udicya (Pavonia odorata) enhances fragrance and soothing action, while dry ginger supports circulation and proper processing of the formulation. The integration of these ingredients through Sneha Paka (oil processing) results in a balanced external therapeutic oil.

 External application through Abhyanga (massage). 
 Frequency and duration of use should be determined according to clinical condition and practitioner guidance.

Sahadevyadi Taila – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Introduction 
 Sahadevyadi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil prepared using the fresh juice of Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea), processed sesame oil, cow’s milk, and a group of six herbs formulated as kalka (paste). The preparation is traditionally indicated for external application in various types of fever. The formulation combines cooling, soothing, and dosha-balancing properties that help reduce heat, discomfort, and systemic imbalance associated with febrile conditions. 
 Reference Shloka 
 सहदेवीरसे तैलं साधयेन्मतिमान् भिषक् । 
षडङ्गकल्कं सक्षीरं सर्वज्वरहरं परम्।। (Sahasrayogam) 
 The verse explains that medicated oil prepared with Sahadevi juice, milk, and a group of six herbal pastes is highly effective in alleviating all types of fever when prepared properly by a knowledgeable physician. 
 Composition 
 I. Drava Dravyas (Liquid Ingredients) 
 
 Sahadevi Svarasa (Vernonia cinerea – Purple Fleabane Whole Plant Juice) – 480 ml 
 Goksira (Cow’s Milk) – 480 ml 
 
 II. Taila Dravya (Base Oil) 
 
 Murchita Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Processed Sesame Oil) – 240 ml 
 
 III. Kalka Dravyas (Herbal Paste Ingredients) 
 
 Musta (Cyperus rotundus – Nut Grass Rhizome) – 10 gm 
 Parpataka (Fumaria parviflora – Fumitory Whole Plant) – 10 gm 
 Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides – Vetiver Root) – 10 gm 
 Candana (Santalum album – Sandalwood Heartwood) – 10 gm 
 Udicya (Pavonia odorata – Fragrant Swamp Mallow Root) – 10 gm 
 Nagara (Zingiber officinale – Dry Ginger Rhizome) – 10 gm 
 
 Method Of Preparation 
 All kalka dravyas (pasted herbs) are cleaned, dried if necessary, and finely powdered. These powders are triturated with a small quantity of liquid to form a smooth herbal paste. The processed sesame oil is taken in a clean stainless steel vessel and combined with Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea) fresh juice and cow’s milk. The prepared herbal paste is then added to this mixture. The contents are heated over mild fire following classical Sneha Paka (oil preparation) principles. Continuous stirring is maintained to ensure proper integration of ingredients and to avoid scorching. Heating is continued until the liquid components evaporate completely and only medicated oil remains in the original oil quantity. Proper completion is identified by absence of moisture, characteristic aroma, and formation of soft, non-sticky kalka (paste) residue. After natural cooling, the oil is filtered through a clean cloth and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 The medicated oil is applied externally through Abhyanga (therapeutic oil massage). Application may be performed over the entire body or localized regions as advised by an Ayurvedic practitioner. 
 Pharmacological Actions 
 
 Reduces febrile heat and burning sensation 
 Provides cooling and soothing effect on skin and peripheral tissues 
 Supports systemic balance during fever 
 Helps pacify aggravated Pitta and Vata dosha 
 Promotes comfort, relaxation, and restoration of physiological stability 
 
 Clinical Indications 
 
 All types of Jvara (fever) 
 Fever associated with burning sensation and restlessness 
 Supportive external therapy during systemic heat conditions 
 
 Therapeutic Properties 
 Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea) is traditionally described as a cooling and fever-alleviating herb that helps regulate systemic heat. Cow’s milk contributes nourishing, soothing, and stabilizing qualities that mitigate heat and dryness. Sesame oil acts as a penetrating base that carries the active principles of the herbs into peripheral tissues. Musta (Cyperus rotundus) and Parpataka (Fumaria parviflora) are classically recognized for their role in fever management and digestive balance. Usira (Vetiveria zizanioides) and Candana (Santalum album) provide cooling and aromatic properties that reduce burning sensation. Udicya (Pavonia odorata) enhances fragrance and soothing action, while dry ginger supports circulation and proper processing of the formulation. The integration of these ingredients through Sneha Paka (oil processing) results in a balanced external therapeutic oil. 
 Method Of Administration 
 
 External application through Abhyanga (massage). 
 Frequency and duration of use should be determined according to clinical condition and practitioner guidance. 
 
 Precautions 
 
 For external use only. 
 Application should be performed under professional supervision, especially in severe febrile states. 
 Avoid application on damaged skin unless advised. 
 
 Conclusion 
 Sahadevyadi Taila is a classical medicated oil prepared using Sahadevi (Vernonia cinerea) juice, cow’s milk, sesame oil, and a group of six herbal pastes through the Sneha Paka (oil preparation method). The formulation is primarily indicated for external application in all types of fever. Its cooling, soothing, and dosha-balancing properties make it a valuable supportive therapy for reducing heat and discomfort when prepared and used according to classical Ayurvedic principles.

sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Saindhava Lavana 
 Rock salt is primarily sodium chloride with trace minerals like magnesium, potassium, and calcium. Its hygroscopic and antimicrobial nature helps cleanse the pilonidal sinus by reducing pus and infection. The mineral salts also improve circulation, reduce swelling, and relieve stiffness. It acts as a Srotoshodhaka (channel purifier) that aids healing and tissue regeneration in inflamed areas. 
 2. Arka 
 Calotropis procera contains cardenolides, triterpenoids, flavonoids, and alkaloids. These compounds show strong antimicrobial and wound-healing effects, useful in pilonidal sinus, where bacterial infections are common. Its anti-inflammatory action helps reduce swelling around the sinus tract. In musculoskeletal conditions, it enhances local blood flow and reduces stiffness and pain. 
 3. Maricha 
 Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is rich in piperine, chavicine, and volatile oils. Piperine has antimicrobial properties that help prevent secondary infections in the pilonidal sinus. Its potent anti-inflammatory action reduces local swelling and pain. Piperine also enhances the bioavailability of other herbal compounds, strengthening their effect on musculoskeletal pain and stiffness. 
 4. Chitrak (Root) 
 Plumbago zeylanica root contains plumbagin, a naphthoquinone compound with powerful antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties. Plumbagin supports the breakdown of unhealthy tissue and aids in wound healing, making it beneficial for the pilonidal sinus. It also reduces swelling and improves circulation, thus supporting musculoskeletal recovery and reducing stiffness. 
 5. Bhringraj 
 Eclipta alba contains wedelolactone, ecliptine, and flavonoids. Wedelolactone has antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory actions that assist in healing the pilonidal sinus and reducing infection risk. It also supports the regeneration of healthy tissues. In musculoskeletal disorders, Bhringraj reduces pain, nourishes muscles, and supports recovery from weakness or stiffness. 
 6. Haridra 
 Turmeric rhizome (Curcuma longa) is rich in curcumin, demethoxycurcumin, and volatile oils. Curcumin’s strong anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects help control infection and inflammation in the pilonidal sinus. It promotes wound healing by reducing oxidative stress and encouraging tissue repair. In musculoskeletal disorders, curcumin relieves pain, reduces stiffness, and protects cartilage and joints. 
 7. Daru Haridra 
 Tree Turmeric (Berberis aristata) contains berberine, oxyacanthine, and berbamine. Berberine exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, making it useful in managing pilonidal sinus with bacterial infection. It also has wound-healing and anti-inflammatory properties that promote faster recovery. In musculoskeletal disorders, berberine reduces oxidative stress, joint inflammation, and stiffness. 
 8. Taila 
 Sesame oil (Sesamum indicum) contains sesamol, sesamolin, sesamin, and vitamin E. These compounds provide antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial benefits. In pilonidal sinus, sesame oil serves as a base that enhances penetration of herbal actives and helps in reducing local inflammation. For musculoskeletal disorders, it nourishes joints, improves flexibility, and reduces stiffness by strengthening muscles and connective tissues. 
 Method Of Preparation 

 Take Saindhava Lavana, Arka Mool Twak (Calotropis procera), Maricha (Piper nigrum), Chitraka Moola (Plumbago zeylanica), Bhringraj (Eclipta alba), Haridra (Curcuma longa), Daruharidra (Berberis aristata) (each 35 g) and Sesame oil 1 litre. 
 First, prepare the Murchchhana (purification and processing) of sesame oil to enhance its quality and remove impurities. 
 Make a fine powder of the seven herbal ingredients (excluding sesame oil). 
 Add water to this fine powder and grind on a stone slab to prepare a paste (Kalka). 
 Mix this herbal paste with the processed sesame oil and add 4 litres of water. 
 Cook the mixture on a mild fire (mandagni) until the water content evaporates, leaving only the medicated oil. 
 Once the aqueous portion is completely dried, remove the oil pot from the stove and filter the oil through a clean cloth. 
 Allow the oil to cool, then store it in a clean glass container. 


 Medicinal Properties 

 Vedanasthapana (Analgesic) 
 Shothahara (Anti-inflammatory) 
 Vatahara (Pacifies aggravated Vata) 
 Srotoshodhaka (Channel-cleansing) 
 Kaphahara (Relieves Kapha accumulation) 
 Stambhaghna (Relieves stiffness) 
 Balya (Strengthening)

To be applied locally to the affected area 


 Contraindication 

 There are no known side effects of this oil. 
 Keep out of sight and reach of children. 


 Conclusion 
 Saindhavadi Oil is a classical Ayurvedic formulation valued for its effectiveness in managing pain, stiffness, and inflammation related to Vata-Kapha disorders. It is enriched with Saindhava Lavana and other herbs in a sesame oil base, and it works as a natural analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and muscle-strengthening agent. Its application improves circulation, reduces swelling, and restores mobility in joints and muscles. It is widely used in Panchakarma therapies like Abhyanga, Kati Basti, and Janu Basti. It provides deep relief in arthritis, spondylosis, and neuralgia. By balancing doshas and clearing blocked channels, it supports overall musculoskeletal health. Regular external use helps maintain flexibility, strength, and pain-free movement naturally. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.introduction: Sarjadi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil prepared by processing Sarjarasa with sesame oil and fermented sour gruel. The formulation is traditionally used as an external application for conditions associated with burning sensation, especially in febrile states and Vatarakta. The cooling and soothing nature of the preparation is enhanced by dilution with cold water prior to application, making it suitable for localized thermal discomfort of the skin and peripheral tissues.
sections.reference_shloka:
सर्जकांजिकसंसिद्धं तैलं शीताम्बुमर्दितम्। 
ज्वरदाहापहं लेपात्सद्यो वातास्रदाहनुत्।। (Sahasrayogam) 

 The verse explains that oil processed with Sarjarasa and Kanji alleviates burning sensation in fever and provides relief in Vatarakta when applied externally after mixing with cold water.
sections.composition:
I. Main Ingredients 

 Sarjarasa (Shorea robusta – Sal Tree Resin) – 1 part 
 Murchita Tila Taila (Sesamum indicum – Processed Sesame Oil) – 4 parts 
 Kanji (Fermented Sour Rice Gruel) – 16 parts 

 Method Of Preparation 
 A clean stainless steel vessel is taken and processed sesame oil is poured into it. Sarjarasa, purified and powdered, is added to the oil and mixed thoroughly. The prescribed quantity of Kanji is then incorporated into the mixture. The contents are heated over mild fire following the classical Sneha Paka procedure. Continuous stirring is maintained to ensure uniform processing and to prevent sticking of the resin to the vessel base. The mixture is heated until the aqueous component of Kanji evaporates completely and only medicated sesame oil remains in its original oil quantity. Proper completion is identified by the absence of moisture, characteristic aroma of processed resin, and formation of soft, non-adherent residue. After self-cooling, the oil is filtered through a clean cloth and stored in airtight glass containers. 
 Method Of Use 
 The medicated oil is mixed with cold water and applied locally over the affected area. Application is generally performed as a thin topical layer or gentle external massage as advised by an Ayurvedic practitioner.
