sections.description_of_the_ingredient:
1. Inner Bark Of Neem (Azadirachta Indica) 
 It is Tikta-Kashaya (bitter-astringent) in taste and has Rakta Shodhak (blood-purifying) and Krimighna (antimicrobial) properties. It pacifies Pitta and Kapha dosha, making it valuable in treating Rakta Dosha, Charm Vikaar, and Vicharchika. Its active compounds like nimbidin, azadirachtin, and nimbin exhibit strong antibacterial, antifungal, and anti-inflammatory effects. These help in reducing skin inflammation, controlling Dadru (fungal infections), relieving Khujli (itching), and purifying vitiated blood responsible for Visarpa (erysipelas) and Vatarakta (gout-related eruptions). 
 2. Bark Of Bakayan (Melia Azedarach) 
 This herb is also known for its Tikta-Katu rasa (bitter-pungent taste), is a potent Krumighna and Raktashodhak herb. It acts on Pitta-Kapha dosha, relieving eczema (Vicharchika), itching (Khujli), and Visarpa due to its strong detoxifying and antifungal properties. The alkaloids like meliatoxin, azedarachin, and tetranortriterpenoids exhibit antimicrobial and anthelmintic effects, making it highly effective in Dadru and Rakta Dushti conditions. It helps cleanse the skin and purify the blood, thereby controlling recurrent skin eruptions and lesions. 
 3. Bark Of Kachnar (Bauhinia Variegata) 
 This herb possesses Kashaya rasa (astringent) and exhibits Lekhana (scraping), Shothahara (anti-inflammatory), and Raktaprasadak (blood-cleansing) properties. It balances all three doshas, especially Kapha-Pitta, making it ideal for treating Vicharchika, Dadru, and Visarpa. Active constituents like bauhiniastatins, flavonoids, and tannins help in tissue regeneration, reducing glandular swellings, and healing chronic skin ulcers. It is especially beneficial in Vatarakta, as it detoxifies Rakta Dhatu and reduces inflammation and pain. 
 4. Pittpapada (Fumaria officinalis) 
 It is a classical herb for Rakta Pitta vikaras due to its Tikta-Kashaya rasa, Pitta-Kapha shamak effect, and excellent Rakta-Pitta shodhana (blood and pitta purification). The key alkaloid fumarine along with fumaric acid provides hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory, and anti-pruritic properties. It soothes inflamed skin in Vicharchika, clears toxins from Rakta in Visarpa, and reduces itching in Khujli and Dadru. It also supports the management of Vatarakta by eliminating Pitta-induced vitiation in blood channels. 
 5. Jawasa (Alhagi maurorum) 
 This herb has Katu-Tikta rasa and is known for its Raktashodhak, Mutrala (diuretic), and Shothahara actions. It balances Pitta and helps expel morbid doshas from the blood. It is used in chronic skin disorders such as Vicharchika, Dadru, and Charm Vikaar due to its blood-purifying action. The active compounds including flavonoids, tannins, and alkaloids provide anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. In Vatarakta, it reduces swelling and uric acid accumulation by improving metabolic waste excretion and Rakta detoxification. 
 6. Gorakhmundi (Sphaeranthus indicus) 
 It is Tikta-Katu in rasa, Laghu-Ruksha in guna, and pacifies Kapha-Pitta dosha. It is a renowned Raktashodhak and Kusthaghna (anti-dermatosis) herb. Its active compounds such as eudesmanoids, sesquiterpene lactones, and flavonoids exert anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antipruritic effects. These make it highly effective in managing Vicharchika, Dadru, and Khujli by reducing inflammation and microbial growth. It cleanses the blood and corrects vitiated Rakta Dhatu, making it beneficial in Rakta Dosha, Visarpa, and inflammatory conditions like Vatarakta. 
 7. Anantmool (Hemidesmus indicus) 
 It has Madhura-Tikta rasa and Snigdha-Guru guna, making it Tridosha shamak, especially beneficial for Pitta-Rakta shodhana. It is known for Twachya (skin-nourishing), Dahaprashamana (burning sensation relieving), and Rasayana (rejuvenative) properties. The active constituents like hemidine, saponins, and essential oils provide detoxifying and cooling action, especially in Vicharchika, Visarpa, and Khujli. It soothes the skin, purifies blood, and helps relieve chronic eczema and gout-related skin lesions (Vatarakta). 
 8. Powder of Red Sandalwood (Pterocarpus santalinus) 
 This herb is Tikta-Kashaya rasa, Sheetala veerya, and Pitta-Kapha shamaka in nature. It is extensively used in Rakta Pitta, Twak Vikara, and Visarpa. Its bioactives, like santalin A B, pterostilbene, and flavonoids, contribute to its anti-inflammatory, cooling, and antiseptic effects. It is effective in soothing itching (Khujli), managing ringworm (Dadru), and eczema (Vicharchika). It helps reduce the burning sensation and inflammation in Vatarakta and purifies blood vitiated with Pitta-Rakta dushti. 
 9. Powder of Shisham Wood (Dalbergia sissoo) 
 This herb, known for its Katu-Tikta-Kashaya rasa, has Raktaprasadak, Kandughna (anti-itch), and Shothahara actions. Its active principles, like biochanin A, dalbergin, and isoflavonoids, exert potent anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antimicrobial effects. It is useful in Rakta Vikriti, especially in Visarpa, Khujli, Dadru, and eczema, due to its scraping and blood-purifying qualities. In Vatarakta, it helps reduce swelling and local hyperemia by acting on inflamed joints and tissues. 
 10. Manjishtha (Rubia cordifolia) 
 It is considered the most potent Raktashodhak herb in Ayurveda. It has Tikta-Kashaya rasa, Ushna veerya, and pacifies Kapha-Pitta dosha. Its alkaloids, such as rubiadin, purpurin, and manjistin, exhibit strong anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antibacterial actions. It cleanses Rakta Dhatu, reduces skin discolorations, and improves lymphatic drainage. It is beneficial in all Charm Vikaar, especially Visarpa, Vicharchika, Dadru, and Khujli, and plays a vital role in Vatarakta by detoxifying blood and reducing joint inflammation and pain. 
 11. Powder of Khadir Stem (Acacia catechu) 
 It is a prime Rakta Shodhak and Kusthaghna drug, possessing Kashaya rasa, Ruksha guna, and Sheeta virya, which help pacify Pitta and Kapha doshas. It is extensively indicated in Charm Vikaar, Vicharchika, and Dadru due to its Lekhana, Shothahara, and Krimighna properties. Active compounds like catechin, epicatechin, and tannins provide powerful antiseptic, astringent, and anti-inflammatory action. These help in controlling Rakta Dushti, soothing itching (Khujli), and clearing pus-filled skin lesions in Visarpa and Vatarakta. 
 12. Chopchini (Smilax china) 
 This herb is renowned for its Rasayana, Kandughna, and Raktashodhak effects. It has Tikta-Kashaya rasa, Laghu-Ruksha guna, and pacifies Kapha-Vata doshas, making it highly effective in Vatarakta (gout), where it removes Aam and improves circulation. Rich in saponins, flavonoids, and resins, it has anti-inflammatory, detoxifying, and antirheumatic effects. It purifies Rakta, reduces joint pain and skin eruptions, and provides relief in chronic skin diseases such as Vicharchika, Dadru, and Visarpa. 
 13. Chirayata (Swertia chirata) 
 This herb has Tikta-Kashaya rasa and Laghu-Ruksha guna, and it is an excellent Pitta-Kapha shamak, especially helpful in Rakta Dosha, Vicharchika, and Charm Vikaar. The active constituents such as swertiamarin, amarogentin, and mangiferin are known for their antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and hepatoprotective effects. Chirayata supports liver detoxification and blood purification, making it useful in chronic skin allergies, eczema, Khujli, and infections like Dadru and Visarpa. It also helps regulate metabolism in Vatarakta. 
 14. Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) 
 It is Tridosha shamak, with emphasis on Vata-Pitta pacification. It has Rasa pradhan property (all tastes except salt), Laghu-Ruksha guna, and Ushna virya. It is Raktaprasadak, Kusthaghna, and Shodhana in nature. The key compounds like chebulagic acid, chebulinic acid, and gallic acid provide antioxidant, antibacterial, and detoxifying actions. Haritaki cleanses the digestive tract and Rakta dhatu, alleviates Vicharchika, Khujli, Dadru, and controls inflammatory flare-ups in Visarpa and Vatarakta. 
 15. Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) 
 This herb has Kashaya rasa, Ruksha guna, and balances Kapha-Pitta dosha. It is known for its Lekhana, Shothahara, and Raktashodhak properties. The presence of beta-sitosterol, gallic acid, and ellagic acid contributes to its antifungal, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects. It is used in Charm Vikaar, Vicharchika, and Dadru for reducing thickened lesions and itching. In Vatarakta, it helps reduce swelling and toxic accumulation, supporting healthy blood and joint function. 
 16. Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) 
 It is Madhura-Amla rasa, Sheeta virya, and pacifies Pitta and Vata. It is a superior Rasayana, Raktashodhak, and Twachya herb. It is rich in vitamin C, tannins, and emblicanin A B, which show antioxidant, anti-aging, and anti-inflammatory properties. It rejuvenates the skin, clears Rakta Dushti, and aids in healing chronic skin conditions like Vicharchika, Khujli, and Dadru. It reduces burning and redness in Visarpa and prevents tissue damage in Vatarakta by strengthening blood vessels and cooling the system. 
 Method Of Preparation 

 Take 1 part of each herb, coarsely crush it, and soak it in warm water in the evening. Cover it and let it sit overnight. 
 In the morning, place it in a Nadika Yantra (traditional distillation apparatus) and distill the mixture properly to collect approximately 20 bottles of Ark (distilled extract). 

 Medicinal Properties 

 Helps purify the blood and balance excess Pitta, addressing the root cause of skin and blood disorders. 
 Reduces itching, swelling, and fungal infections like ringworm, eczema, and dermatitis. 
 Supports healing of damaged skin, clears chronic eruptions, and aids in systemic detox from deep-seated infections.

sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Garlic (Rason) 
 In Ayurveda, Garlic is “Rasona” (lacking only the sour taste) and is prized for its Ushna (hot) and Tikshna (piercing) attributes. It specifically pacifies Vata and Kapha, making it a prime choice for Agnimandya (weak digestive fire). Scientifically, garlic is rich in allicin, which acts as a natural broad-spectrum antimicrobial. This helps address Visuchika (gastroenteritis/cholera-like symptoms) by inhibiting pathogenic bacteria while stimulating the secretion of gastric juices. Its sulfur compounds promote peristalsis, ensuring that undigested food (Ajirna) does not stagnate and ferment in the gut. 

 2. Fresh Tulsi (Holy Basil) 
 Tulsi is regarded as Surasa in classical texts, possessing Katu (pungent) and Tikta (bitter) tastes. It is a powerful Kaphata-hara herb that clears “Amavisha” (undigested toxins). Modern pharmacology identifies Tulsi as an adaptogen with significant anti-spasmodic and anti-inflammatory properties. In cases of Visuchika, it helps soothe the intestinal lining and reduce abdominal cramps. Its essential oils, such as eugenol, enhance the bioavailability of other herbs and support the metabolic “Agni,” effectively reversing the sluggishness of Agnimandya and promoting the breakdown of complex food particles. 

 3. Unripe Black Pepper (Maricha) 
 Black pepper is a premier Deepana (appetizer) and Pachana (digestive) herb. Ayurveda utilizes its “piercing” quality to cut through the heavy, sticky mucus of Ama associated with Ajirna. The primary active alkaloid, piperine, is scientifically proven to increase the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and stimulate the thermogenic response in the digestive tract. This heat is essential for correcting Agnimandya. Furthermore, its antibacterial nature provides a defense against the pathogens responsible for the acute vomiting and diarrhea seen in Visuchika, effectively drying up excess moisture in the intestines. 

 4. Purified Alcohol (Surasar) 
 In this formulation, Surasar acts as a potent Anupana (vehicle) and preservative. Ayurveda recognizes that certain herbal principles are only soluble in alcohol, allowing the medicine to reach the cellular level (Sukshma) rapidly. Scientifically, alcohol functions as a solvent that extracts the volatile oils and alkaloids from the garlic, tulsi, and pepper. When ingested in medicinal doses, it acts as a mild vasodilator, increasing blood flow to the GI tract. This rapid absorption is crucial during Visuchika to prevent dehydration and ensure the active compounds begin neutralizing toxins immediately. 

 Method of Preparation 
 Mix all the ingredients together and fill them in a bottle. Seal the bottle with a cork. Keep it closed for 48 hours. After that, filter the liquid through filter paper.
sections.indications:
Rasonadi Ark is warming in potency, an excellent digestive stimulant (Deepana), digestive aid (Pachana), and carminative (Vata-relieving) medicine. It is useful in: 

 Udarshool (abdominal pain) 
 Aphara (bloating/gas) 
 Agnimandya (low digestive fire) 
 Ajirna (indigestion) 
 Visuchika 
 Atisara (diarrhea) 
 Vomiting 
 Cough 
 Chronic cough 
 Asthma 
 Pulmonary tuberculosis 
 Lung inflammation 
 Influenza 
 Bronchial fever (inflammation of respiratory passages) 
 Nadivrana 
 Ear ulcers (Karnavrana) 

 In present times it is also used as a supportive remedy in: 

 Motijhara 
 Raktapitta (bleeding disorders) 
 High blood pressure (Hypertension) 
 Sangrahani 
 Mumps 
 Diphtheria 
 Epilepsy 

 Remarkable benefits have also been observed when garlic injections are used in paralysis. 

 Clinical Use 

 In Visuchika (severe diarrhea or vomiting), giving 5–5 drops every half hour improves the patient’s condition within 4–6 hours. 

 In indigestion, taking 10–10 drops three times daily along with dietary control gives relief within 2 days. 

 Patients suffering from diarrhea, chronic dysentery, and malabsorption (Sangrahani) often have very weak digestion. To correct this, giving 10–10 drops three times daily for 2–3 months helps remove the disease. 

 In Motijhara, the stool becomes foul-smelling and the patient’s life force becomes weak. When Rasonadi Ark is given as a supportive medicine: Digestion improves, bowels clear properly, digestive power increases and fever subsides. 

 In coughs with foul sputum, asthma, muscle wasting, and tuberculosis, this medicine helps expel vitiated phlegm, reduces disease progression, and gradually alleviates the disorder. 

 It is also effective in pain occurring in any part of the body or head due to Vata disorders, including Udarshool (abdominal colic), Gridhrasi (sciatica), Katishool (lower back pain), and joint pain. 

 Garlic has the property of reducing excess blood pressure. Therefore, Rasonadi Ark is given to patients with hypertension. It reduces dizziness, improves sleep, and also provides benefits in obesity. 

 In mumps and paralysis, giving 5–5 drops three to four times daily prevents the disease from progressing. 

 When pus formation begins and starts damaging internal organs, diphtheria may develop. In both such conditions, soaking cotton in Rasonadi Ark and cleaning the ear regularly helps dry the pus and relieves pain quickly.
sections.dosage:
5–20 drops, mixed with 1–2 ounces of water, 3–4 times a day. 

 Conclusion 
 Rasonadi Ark is a potent Ayurvedic distillate known for its strong digestive, carminative, and rejuvenating properties. By stimulating Agni (digestive fire) and balancing aggravated Vata and Kapha, it helps in managing various disorders such as indigestion, abdominal discomfort, cough, respiratory ailments, and chronic digestive disturbances. Its warming nature promotes proper metabolism, enhances appetite, and supports the elimination of accumulated toxins from the body. Additionally, it acts as a supportive remedy in conditions like hypertension, weakness, and certain infectious disorders. With its wide therapeutic applications and simple dosage, Rasonadi Ark serves as a valuable traditional preparation for maintaining digestive strength and overall health.

sections.introduction: Sanjeevan Arka is a potent classical Ayurvedic formulation known for its fast-acting and revitalizing properties, traditionally prepared through the infusion of aromatic and therapeutic substances in purified spirit. As its name suggests, it functions like a “life-restoring elixir,” especially in acute digestive and systemic disturbances. Rich in carminative, stimulant, and antispasmodic qualities, it helps regulate digestion, control excessive bowel movements, and relieve abdominal discomfort. Its penetrating and quick-acting nature makes it particularly valuable in conditions like diarrhea, vomiting, and weakness. When used judiciously in small doses, Sanjeevan Arka supports rapid recovery and restores physiological balance effectively. Let;s discuss it in detail!
sections.ingredients:
Opium – 4 grams 
 Small cardamom seeds – 2 ounces 
 Nutmeg – 2 ounces 
 Camphor – 4 ounces 
 Purified spirit (alcohol) – 20 ounces
sections.description_of_ingredients:
1. Opium (Papaver somniferum) 
 Known as Ahiphena, it is Grahi (anti-diarrheal) and Vyavayi (fast-acting). It instantly pacifies aggravated Vata, alleviating the “piercing” colic pain characteristic of Visuchika. It stabilizes the downward movement of Apana Vayu. Opium contains alkaloids like morphine and codeine that act on mu-opioid receptors in the GI tract. This decreases intestinal motility and increases sphincter tone, effectively stopping fluid loss in acute diarrhea and providing powerful analgesia for abdominal cramps. 

 2. Small Cardamom Seeds (Elettaria cardamomum) 
 Ela is Deepana (appetizer) and Ruchivardhaka (taste enhancer). It neutralizes Amavisha (toxins from undigested food) and re-establishes the kindling of Agni to treat Agnimandya. Cardamom contains volatile oils like cineole and limonene. These are carminative, helping to expel gas and reduce bloating. It stimulates the secretion of bile and gastric juices, which mechanically aids in the breakdown of heavy food (treating Ajeerna). 

 3. Nutmeg (Myristica fragrans) 
 Jatiphala is Ushna (hot) and Katu (pungent). It is specifically indicated for Atisara (diarrhea) and Visuchika because it absorbs excess moisture in the intestines while stimulating the digestive fire. It possesses antimicrobial and antispasmodic properties. The compound myristicin helps relax the smooth muscles of the gut, reducing the waves of pain in indigestion while inhibiting the growth of pathogens that cause gastrointestinal infections. 

 4. Camphor (Cinnamomum camphora) 
 Karpoora is Chedana (clearing) and Sheetala-veerya but with a unique ability to stimulate Agni. In Visuchika, it acts as a de-obstruent, clearing the channels blocked by Ama (undigested waste). Camphor acts as a mild local anesthetic and counter-irritant to the gastric mucosa. When ingested in controlled, diluted amounts, it produces a sensation of warmth that stimulates blood flow to the gut, aiding in the absorption of other herbs and rapidly cooling internal inflammation. 

 5. Purified Spirit (Alcohol) 
 Acts as a Madya base, serving as an Anupana (vehicle) that is Teekshna (penetrating). It helps the medicinal properties of the herbs reach the cellular level (Srotas) almost instantly. Ethanol acts as a solvent, extracting the essential oils and alkaloids from the solids to create a highly bioavailable tincture. It also serves as a preservative and provides a mild vasodilatory effect, which can be helpful in the initial stages of shock often seen in severe Visuchika. 

 Method of Preparation 

 Place all the ingredients in a bottle and keep it tightly closed for 2 weeks. 
 Shake the bottle 2–3 times daily. 
 After one week, filter through filter paper and add more purified spirit equal to the amount reduced.
sections.indications:
Sanjivan Ark is useful in: 

 Indigestion 
 Diarrhea due to indigestion 
 Vomiting 
 Dysentery 
 Infective diarrhea (including cholera-like conditions) 
 Black diarrhea (severe form) 
 Fear-induced diarrhea 
 Mountain diarrhea 
 Chronic diarrhea 
 Bloody dysentery 
 Mucous diarrhea 
 Abdominal pain 
 Uterine cramps 
 Menstrual pain 
 Chest congestion 
 In ear pain, a few drops are instilled into the ear. 
 In toothache, a cotton swab soaked in it is placed over the tooth. 
 It is also beneficial in burning sensation of gonorrhea and certain female disorders. 


 Clinical Use 

 In Dysenteric Conditions – There is frequent loose stool, thirst, burning in chest, and restlessness. Administering this ark 3 times daily helps relieve the condition. 

 In Acute Indigestion – When inflammation occurs in the stomach and intestines, leading to frequent vomiting and diarrhea (5–7 times daily), this ark provides rapid relief. 

 In Cholera-like Conditions – Vomiting and diarrhea occur rapidly, along with excessive thirst and weakness. In early stages, this ark provides quick benefits. After about 12 hours, when the body becomes cold, strength diminishes, blood thickens, and speech becomes weak, the chances of benefit from medicines reduce. In such cases give 4–5 drops every half hour and then every 1–2 hours, with 1–2 teaspoons of water or sugar. 

 Severe Diarrhea (Motijhara) – Sometimes diarrhea becomes extremely distressing, causing Mental instability, Insomnia, Delirium. This ark relieves these symptoms effectively. However, the dose should be very small, otherwise intoxication may occur. 

 In Kapha Disorders (Respiratory Conditions) – Due to improper diet or cold exposure, phlegm accumulates in the chest and does not expel easily, causing restlessness. Giving 5–5 drops, three times daily, helps expel phlegm within 2–4 days and clears the chest. 

 In Uterine Disorders (Postpartum) – After delivery, due to entry of air or infection in the uterus, cold exposure, or retention of lochia, uterine pain occurs. This ark provides remarkable relief. Full dose should be given for pain relief, but care must be taken to avoid harm to the infant (through breastfeeding). 

 In Painful Menstruation – Due to obstruction or disturbance in reproductive channels, menstrual pain occurs. This ark Relieves pain, Provides strength, If constipation is present, it should be corrected and light diet followed and Dosage should be about 15 drops. 

 In Rheumatism – After exposure to cold or improper diet, symptoms appear Heart discomfort, Headache, Pain in various body parts. Give 20–25 drops with water 3 times daily. Also perform massages with suitable oils if required. 

 In Summer Diarrhea – Caused by heat exposure, overeating fruits, or drinking cold water. This ark provides relief. 

 In Hill Diarrhea – Occurs due to Traveling in mountains, Drinking contaminated water, Drinking hot beverages without rest. Also seen after pilgrimages (e.g., Badrinath, Amarnath). This ark acts as a life-saving remedy. Diet should include Curd, Whey and Light rice preparations. 

 In Gonorrhea – In the acute stage, there is burning during urination, sometimes severe enough to cause tears. This ark relieves burning within 2–3 days. 

 In Female Disorders (Leucorrhea) – Frequent urination, weakness, dryness of body occur. Its Regular use provides benefits. 

 In Excessive Purgation – When purgatives cause excessive diarrhea and weakness: Give 4–5 drops, 2–3 times daily, to restore health. 

 In Fear-induced Diarrhea – Occurs in children and women due to fear or shock. Also fever is seen. This ark acts immediately and restores normalcy.
sections.dosage:
5–15 drops, three times a day, mixed with 1–2 ounces of water or sugar. 

 Conclusion 
 At last we can say that Sanjeevan Arka emerges as a swift whisper of restoration, a formulation that bridges urgency with precision. In moments when the body falters—losing rhythm through distress, depletion, or imbalance—it acts like a spark that rekindles vitality from within. Its subtle intensity works not by force, but by awakening the body’s innate intelligence to recover and recalibrate. Each drop carries a legacy of thoughtful formulation, where potency meets restraint. When administered with care, it transforms chaos into control, weakness into resilience—truly embodying its name as a reviver of life, guiding the system gently yet decisively back to harmony.

name: Strigadantak Ark

sections.introduction: Strigadantak Ark is a specialized Ayurvedic liquid formulation traditionally used for disorders affecting the female reproductive system, especially uterine dysfunctions and abnormal vaginal discharge. The name itself suggests a medicine intended to destroy or alleviate stri-gada—diseases of women. This formulation combines classical Ayurvedic preparations with selected therapeutic oils and tinctures to create a potent uterine cleanser, anti-inflammatory support, and urinary tract restorative. Traditionally, it has been prescribed in conditions such as Rakta Pradar (menorrhagia / excessive uterine bleeding), Shweta Pradar (leucorrhoea / white discharge), Neela Pradar (bluish discharge) , uterine irritation, menstrual irregularities, painful menstruation, uterine-origin constipation, burning sensations, headache, restlessness, and associated weakness. It is also considered beneficial in urinary complaints such as dysuria, urinary retention, and yellow discoloration of urine. This formulation was initially designed for women suffering from complications associated with infectious reproductive disorders, and later gained recognition for broader gynecological use.
sections.ingredients:
Ashokarishta (Saraca asoca based classical fermented preparation) – 6 oz (~177 ml) 
 Oil Copaiba (Copaifera officinalis resin oil) – 1½ dram (~5.5 ml) 
 Sandalwood Oil (Santalum album) – 10 drops 
 Tincture Cantharides (prepared from Lytta vesicatoria) – 15 drops 
 Liquor Ferri (Iron preparation) – 4 dram (~14.8 ml) 
 Arabic Gum / Gum Acacia (Acacia senegal) – 15 grains (~1 g) 
 Aqua Camphor Concentrated (Cinnamomum camphora based camphor water) – 1½ dram (~5.5 ml) 
 Distilled Water / Steam Water – 2 oz (~59 ml) 

 Additional Ashokarishta may be added to make the total volume 12 oz (~355 ml). 

 Method of Preparation 
 First, Arabic gum is dissolved thoroughly in distilled or steam water. This mixture is then filtered to obtain a smooth mucilage. The therapeutic oils—Copaiba oil and Sandalwood oil—are blended into this mucilage gradually to ensure proper emulsification. 
 Separately, Ashokarishta is taken as the primary liquid base, and the remaining ingredients such as Tincture Cantharides, Liquor Ferri, and concentrated camphor water are added carefully. Finally, both mixtures are combined and adjusted with additional Ashokarishta until the total volume reaches approximately 12 oz (355 ml). 
 The final preparation is stored in a clean amber bottle and shaken well before use. 

 Therapeutic Properties 
 Strigadantak Ark is considered: 

 Garbhashaya Shodhak (uterine purifier) 
 Pradar Nashak (helps reduce abnormal discharge) 
 Vedana Shamak (pain-relieving) 
 Rakta Stambhak (supports control of excessive bleeding) 
 Mutrala (urinary corrective) 
 Balya (strength promoting) 
 Pitta-Kapha balancing in reproductive channels 

 Its multi-dimensional action makes it useful in chronic inflammatory uterine conditions. 

 Role of Key Ingredients 
 Ashokarishta is one of the most renowned Ayurvedic formulations for female reproductive health. Ashoka (Saraca asoca) is known for strengthening uterine tissues and regulating menstrual flow. 
 Copaiba Oil provides anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial action, especially useful in chronic irritation and infections. 
 Sandalwood Oil soothes burning sensations and supports cooling in inflammatory gynecological conditions. 
 Liquor Ferri supports blood health and addresses weakness associated with chronic discharge or prolonged bleeding. 
 Arabic Gum helps stabilize the mixture while also providing a soothing effect. 
 Camphor Water offers antimicrobial and cooling benefits.
sections.indications:
Strigadantak Ark is traditionally indicated in: 

 Uterine disorders 
 Excessive menstrual bleeding 
 Leucorrhoea 
 Chronic vaginal discharge 
 Burning sensation in uterus 
 Irregular menstruation 
 Dysmenorrhea 
 Constipation due to uterine dysfunction 
 Restlessness and weakness 
 Eye burning and headache 
 Urinary burning 
 Dribbling of urine 
 Yellow urine 
 Urinary obstruction 


 Duration of Use 
 In chronic conditions, it may be administered for 2–3 months with proper dietary discipline (Pathya Palan). 

 Special Clinical Note 
 Historically, this formulation was first prepared for women suffering from complications of infectious reproductive disorders. It was later tested in non-infectious gynecological conditions and reportedly used in over 50,000 female patients, establishing its reputation as a dependable uterine restorative. 

 Additional Advice 
 If the discharge is purulent or foul-smelling, uterine cleansing with antiseptic washes is advised. Thereafter, local applications such as Dhatakyadi Taila or Nataadi Taila may be considered for enhanced healing. 

 Conclusion 
 Strigadantak Ark is a thoughtfully designed Ayurvedic formulation addressing both uterine and urinary disorders in women. Its blend of classical Ayurvedic wisdom and functional medicinal ingredients makes it highly effective in chronic gynecological disturbances. With its cleansing, strengthening, and balancing properties, it remains a valuable preparation in traditional women’s healthcare.

name: Triphala Ark

sections.introduction: Triphala Ark is a classical Ayurvedic distillate preparation made from Triphala, one of the most respected herbal combinations in Ayurveda. The word Triphala means “three fruits,” referring to the combination of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis). This herbal formulation has been widely used for maintaining digestive strength, purifying the blood, improving metabolism, and supporting healthy elimination. Ark preparations in Ayurveda are prepared through a distillation process known as Arka Kalpana, in which the volatile and water-soluble active principles of herbs are extracted in a subtle and easily absorbable liquid form. Triphala Ark is considered lighter, faster acting, and easier to digest than heavy decoctions or powders. It is especially beneficial in chronic metabolic disorders, skin diseases, digestive disturbances, and conditions caused by accumulation of toxins (Ama). This preparation is traditionally valued for balancing all the three doshas especially Kapha dosha and Pitta dosha while gently regulating Vata dosha through proper bowel cleansing and digestive correction.
sections.ingredients:
The following ingredients are used in the preparation of Triphala Ark: 

 Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) – Chebulic Myrobalan 
 Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) – Belleric Myrobalan 
 Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) – Indian Gooseberry 


 Quantity 

 Triphala – 2½ seer (approximately 2.3–2.5 kg) 
 Water – 20 seer (approximately 18–19 liters) 

 The prepared distillate is collected in approximately 20 bottles according to the classical method. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Equal parts of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) are taken and coarsely powdered (Jaukut Churna). 
 Around 2 1⁄2 seer (approximately 2.4 kg) of the coarse Triphala mixture is soaked overnight in 20 seer (approximately 18–19 liters) of water. 
 On the following morning, the soaked material is transferred into a traditional distillation apparatus known as Bhabka Yantra. 
 The mixture is heated gently, and the vapors are condensed carefully to obtain the distilled extract known as Triphala Ark. 
 The collected Ark is filtered and stored in clean glass bottles for medicinal use. 

 The preparation should always be stored in airtight containers away from direct sunlight to maintain potency.
sections.dose_2_to_8_tola_approximately_24_96_ml:
Frequency: 3–4 times daily according to the condition 
 It may be administered alone or mixed with an equal quantity of water.

 Triphala Ark is traditionally used in Prameha and Madhumeha (Diabetes Mellitus) because it helps regulate metabolism and supports proper tissue nourishment. It may assist in reducing excessive urination, sluggish metabolism, and accumulation of unhealthy fat tissues. 
 The antioxidant-rich nature of Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) and cleansing action of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) help maintain healthier metabolic activity. 

 2. Blood Purification and Skin Health 
 This Ark is considered an excellent Rakta Shodhak (blood purifier). It is beneficial in: 

 Acne 
 Itching 
 Eczema 
 Chronic skin disorders 
 Fungal infections 
 Pama (scabies-like conditions) 
 Kushtha (chronic skin diseases) 

 By improving digestion and eliminating toxins from the bloodstream, it helps improve skin complexion and natural glow. 

 3. Supports Digestion and Relieves Constipation 
 Triphala Ark improves digestive fire (Agni) without causing excessive heat. It is useful in: 

 Indigestion 
 Loss of appetite 
 Flatulence 
 Abdominal heaviness 
 Constipation 

 Its mild bowel-cleansing action helps remove accumulated waste material while supporting healthy intestinal function. 

 4. Useful in Obesity and Excess Sweating 
 The formulation is traditionally recommended in: 

 Medovriddhi (obesity) 
 Excessive perspiration 
 Foul body odor 

 By correcting metabolism and removing toxins, it helps maintain internal cleanliness and healthier body function. 

 5. Beneficial in Liver Disorders and Jaundice 
 Triphala Ark supports liver function and is traditionally used in: 

 Pandu (anemia-like disorders) 
 Kamala (jaundice) 
 Sluggish liver function 

 The detoxifying nature of Triphala helps improve bile regulation and supports healthier digestion and nutrient assimilation. 

 6. Useful in Chronic Inflammatory Conditions 
 Ayurveda describes Triphala Ark as beneficial in: 

 Amavata (rheumatic disorders)

 Chronic inflammatory disorders 

 Its detoxifying and anti-inflammatory actions help reduce toxin accumulation responsible for joint discomfort and stiffness. 

 Modern studies on Triphala indicate the presence of important phytochemicals such as: 

 Tannins

 Vitamin C

Triphala is widely studied for its role in supporting gut health, metabolism, immunity, and skin wellness. Because Ark preparations are lighter and rapidly absorbable, Triphala Ark may provide quicker systemic action compared to heavier formulations.

 Conclusion 
 Triphala Ark is a classical Ayurvedic distillate known for its detoxifying, digestive, and rejuvenating properties. Prepared from the three powerful fruits—Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis)—this formulation supports healthy digestion, purifies the blood, improves metabolism, and promotes skin health.  Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) – Chebulic Myrobalan 
 Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) – Belleric Myrobalan

 Quantity

 Method Of Preparation 
 
 Equal parts of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) are taken and coarsely powdered (Jaukut Churna). 
 Around 2 1⁄2 seer (approximately 2.4 kg) of the coarse Triphala mixture is soaked overnight in 20 seer (approximately 18–19 liters) of water. 
 On the following morning, the soaked material is transferred into a traditional distillation apparatus known as Bhabka Yantra. 
 The mixture is heated gently, and the vapors are condensed carefully to obtain the distilled extract known as Triphala Ark. 
 The collected Ark is filtered and stored in clean glass bottles for medicinal use. 
 
 The preparation should always be stored in airtight containers away from direct sunlight to maintain potency. 

 Dosage and Administration 
 
 Dose: 2 to 8 tola (approximately 24–96 ml)

 Mildly heating and balancing

 Balances Kapha Dosha

 Acne

 Chronic skin disorders

 Indigestion

 Constipation 
 
 Its mild bowel-cleansing action helps remove accumulated waste material while supporting healthy intestinal function.

 Medovriddhi (obesity) 
 Excessive perspiration 
 Foul body odor 
 
 By correcting metabolism and removing toxins, it helps maintain internal cleanliness and healthier body function.

 Pandu (anemia-like disorders)

 Sluggish liver function

 Amavata (rheumatic disorders) 
 Vatarakta (gout-like conditions) 
 Chronic inflammatory disorders 
 
 Its detoxifying and anti-inflammatory actions help reduce toxin accumulation responsible for joint discomfort and stiffness. 

 Modern studies on Triphala indicate the presence of important phytochemicals such as:

 Vitamin C

 Take 1 part of Vayavidanga. 
 Soak it overnight in 10 parts of clean water. 
 On the next morning, transfer the soaked mixture into an Arka Yantra (traditional distillation apparatus). 
 Perform distillation and collect 20 bottles of Ark from the process. 
 Store in a clean, dry, and airtight glass container.

 It effectively eliminates intestinal parasites (Krimiroga) and improves digestion by stimulating Agni (digestive fire) and aiding in toxin removal (Ama pachana). 
 Helps reduce excess body fat (Medovriddhi), supports healthy metabolism, and balances doshas. 
 The Arka form allows for the extraction of volatile and water-soluble active principles, making it fast-acting and easily absorbable by the body.

 Acidity commonly results to heartburn. Hydrochloric acid is present in the stomach which helps in the efficient digestion of food and protect the growth of unwanted bacteria. So when there is an excessive production of this acid leads to the disturbance in the gastric glands of stomach. 
 CAUSES OF ACIDITY 

 Eating heavy meals close to bedtime 
 Highly spicy food 
 Life style 
 Consumption of beverages such as alcohol, coffee, tea, and carbonated drinks 
 Smoking 
 Anti-inflammatory medicine and some of the antibiotics 
 Being Pregnant 
 Stress and tension 

 COMPLICATIONS OF ACIDITY 
 1. Ulcers 
 Due to over secretion of gastric juices, there is the disruption in the lining of the upper part of small intestine. In some cases, ulcers can be the cause of cancer.

 Dyspepsia is the narrowing of the esophagus which creates the sensation of food being stuck in the throat. It occurs after taking meals and is brought by excess abdominal pressure. In acidity one has to face burning sensation in the chest, burping and sometimes leads to chest pain.

 Bad breath

sections.introduction:
Herbal Remedies 



 About Arthritis 
 Arthritis is a common joint problem that can affect one as well as multiple joints. Generally there are more than 100 different types of arthritis. But the most common among them are osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis. The problem of arthritis is more common in women as compared to men. In general, it occurs frequently in older people. 
 Different Types of Arthritis 
 Three most common types of arthritis are well explained below: 
 Osteoarthritis: 
 Osteoarthritis is one of the most common type of arthritis. This problem occurs mainly due to the breakdown of the cartilage in the joints. 
 In general, this type of arthritis can occur in any joint of our body. But the weight bearing joints of the hips, spine and knees are commonly affected due to this type of arthritis. 
 Osteoarthritis may sometimes, affect fingers, neck, large toe and thumb as well. 
 Ankylosing spondylitis: 
 Ankylosing spondylitis is another form of arthritis, in which, there occurs painful inflammation that mainly affects the spine. It causes the ankylosis of vertebral as well as sacroiliac joints and is more common in younger males. 
 The word ankylosing spondylitis consist of two words “ankylo” which means stiffening of a joint and the other word “spondylo” which means vertebrae. In this type of arthritis, the bones of the spine may grow or fuse together which results in a rigid spine. 
 In general, commonly affected joints by ankylosing spondylitis are the Joints between the vertebrae of the spine and joints between the spine and pelvis. It may occur in other joints as well such as the joints of the shoulders, knees and hips etc. 
 Rheumatoid arthritis: 
 Rheumatoid arthritis is also a common form of arthritis that usually starts at the middle age, but can occur in young children and elder people also. Rheumatoid arthritis affects joints on both sides of the body. 
 The hands, wrists and knees are commonly affected parts by this type of arthritis. It may affect the skin, lungs, heart, blood, eyes and nerves as well. 
 What are the Symptoms of Arthritis? 
 The common symptoms of arthritis are listed below: 

 Pain in the joints. 
 Inflammation in the joints. 
 Stiffness, swelling, redness and warmth in the joints. 
 Tenderness in the inflamed joints. 
 Sometimes, fever, weight loss and fatigue. 

 What are the Causes of Arthritis? 
 There are several causes of arthritis, but the more common ones are listed below: 

 An infection or injury to the joint. 
 Reduction in the normal amount of cartilage. 
 Weak immune system. 
 Family history. 
 Age factor. 

 How can Arthritis be Diagnosed? 
 A doctor can diagnose arthritis by physical exam. During this diagnosis, he will check for fluid around the red, swollen joints as well as the limited motion in the joints. 
 By extracting and analyzing the joint fluids, he can diagnose from what type of arthritis, a person is suffering. There are some tests that can be used to confirm the arthritis. These include X-ray, MRI and CT scans. These tests helps to see the detailed images of the bones as well as cartilage.

 Reduction in the normal amount of cartilage. 
 Weak immune system. 
 Family history. 
 Age factor.

 Types of Anxiety

 Phobia: Phobia arises out of anxiety and is different from other anxiety disorders. In this the fear may be unnecessary but the person is unable to control anxiety. 
 Social anxiety disorder: In this a person fears from opening up in from of other people or society due to the fact that he will be negatively judged by the people. As a result people avoid public situations and human contact to the point that everyday living is rendered extremely difficult. 
 Obsessive compulsive disorder: In this type of disorder, people are obsessed with cleanliness; keep on checking the locks or light switches. 
 Post-traumatic stress disorder: This type of anxiety is due to flashbacks of any trauma, sexual assault or a serious accident. In this people may often change their behavior to avoid the triggers. 
 Separation anxiety disorder: This is due to feeling of separation from a person or place that leads to anxiety.

Herbal Remedies 



 About Bacterial Vaginosis 
 Bacterial vaginosis is one of the vaginal disease, which is caused by the overgrowth of certain kind of bacteria or imbalance of the naturally occurring bacteria in the vagina. It is also known as vaginal bacteriosis or Gardneralla vaginitis. It is the most common vaginal infection in women of reproductive age. It is the vaginal condition, in which there is a fish odor like discharge. Earlier it was known as a Gardnerellas vaginosis, because it was thought that the bacterial vaginosis is caused by this bacteria only. But now, it is known as bacterial vaginosis, it reflects that there are so many types of bacteria which are present in the vagina and may grow to excess. The bacteria’s which are involved in bacterial vaginosis are Gardenerella, Lactobacillus, bacterosides, Peptostreptococcus, Eubacterium and so many other types of bacteria. It’s not dangerous, but it can cause severe complications along with pregnancy. Bacterial vaginosis double the risk of infection by a number of other sexual transmitted infection like HIV/AIDS. 
 Normally, female vagina contains lactic acid bacteria called lactobacilli. These bacteria produce lactic acid, making the vagina acidic which helps to prevent the growth of other bacteria’s. But, when due to certain conditions, the lactobacilli quantity decrease, it leads to bacteria vaginosis. 
 What can be the symptoms of the bacterial vaginosis? 

 Vaginal discharge: The discharge is usually thin or grayish white. The discharge tends to be heaviest just after a periods or sex. 
 Vaginal odor: Unpleasant fishy odor 
 Itching around the vagina 
 Burning sensation while urination 

 On a severe condition, there is an addition of the more symptoms: 

 Fever 
 Pelvic Pain 

 What can be the risk factors for bacterial vaginosis? 

 Multiple sex partner 
 New sex partner 
 Intra uterine device 
 Bubble bath and use of some scented soap 
 Recent, Antibiotic use 
 Vaginal douching 
 Cigarette smoking 

 How to diagnose the bacterial vaginosis? 

 Whiff test: This test is done with Potassium hydroxide (KOH). A drop of KOH is in contact with the drop of discharge from the woman having bacterial vaginosis; a certain fishy smell is there. 
 Pelvic Examination 

 What can be the complications of the Bacterial vaginosis? 
 If someone has bacterial Vaginosis during pregnancy, then following will be the complications: 

 Early labor 
 Miscarriage 
 Low weight baby

To treat the disorder vitiated by the kapha dosha, the treatment is generally done with the hot and dry herbs. 
 In general, doshas has very much impact on the infections. People with aggravated vata and pitta dosha are more prone to vaginal irritation and infection, while people with pitta and kapha doshas are more prone to yeast infections. The chronic infection is caused due to higher levels of kapha doshas and lower level of Agni in the body. This can be cured by modifying the diet and taking herbal remedies.

sections.introduction:
Herbal Remedies 

 Diet and Lifestyle 



 About Bell’s palsy 
 Bell’s palsy is a disorder, which mostly happens due to temporary weakness of the facial muscles. This disorder develops suddenly and affects one side of the face. In this disease complete paralysis or numbness is experienced in the facial region. The cranial nerve that controls the functioning of facial muscles on the face shows incapability to send to brain and receive signals from it. Patients suffering from this disorder show helplessness towards controlling movement of their facial muscles. This has been a very common type of facial paralysis and neurologic disorder involving the cranial nerve all throughout the globe. 
 What are the Causes of Bell’s palsy? 
 The cranial nerve is responsible for monitoring movements of the muscles in the facial region and ear region. This nerve extends from the brain to the face. 
 The primary cause of this disorder is the herpes virus, which causes inflammation of this nerve. This is the same virus that is responsible for sore throat, flu, cold and genital herpes. 
 Apart from herpes, there can be a few other viruses such as chickenpox and shingles viruses for causing this painful disease. 
 People, who are suffering from migraine headache, are more susceptible to getting affected by this disorder. Migraine headache increases the chances of this nervous system disorder by two times. 
 What are the Symptoms you can see in Bell’s palsy? 

 Facial paralysis and no control over facial muscles 
 Unable to taste or loses sense of taste 
 Feeling weakness of the muscles and nerves in the facial region 
 Difficulty in closing eyes 
 Pain in and outside ears 
 Numbness of the jaws, forehead, cheek, mouth region 
 Blurred view 
 In attempt to raise eyebrows, the forehead region affected by Bell’s palsy remains flat 
 Smiling distorts the face of the patient 

 What are the Complications of Bell’s palsy? 
 The damage that happens to the facial nerve can lead to various complications. 
 Some of them have been described below: 

 One can experience unusual contractions of facial muscles. Some of the effect of this contraction can be involuntarily closing of one of the eyes or lifting of one side of the mouth when trying to smile. 
 A patient can permanently lose the sense of taste. 
 A person can shed tears while eating. Though this complication can be fully healed but sometimes it can also be long lasting. 
 Patient’s eyelids cannot be properly shut due to the inefficiency of the lubricating tear film. The result of such complication is the dryness of cornea and lowering the production of tears. In some cases, it can get very severe and can lead to permanent loss of eye sight. 

 How to Diagnosis Bell’s palsy? 
 The sooner the diagnosis starts, better it will be for the patient to recover from its detrimental impact. The doctor will carefully see all the symptoms and causes that are leading to such facial paralysis. A comprehensive checkup will be performed of the areas including head, neck and ears of the patient. Some of the visible evidences can be presence of tumor, stroke or Lyme disease. Facial muscles are also evaluated precisely to figure out if any other nerve other than cranial nerve is impacted due to this disorder. 
 On the basis of thorough examination, if the doctor detects any change in facial structure then it can be a sign of a tumor. A visible rash can be a sign of Lyme disease. To confirm the presence of Bell’s palsy, a patient can be advised to consult a specialized ENT (ear, nose and throat) specialist i.e., an otolaryngologist. An otolaryngologist will examine the patient’s condition and would prescribe following tests for accurate identification of problem. 
 These tests are: 

 Electromyography (EMG) 
 MRI, CT scans and X-ray 
 Oral examination 
 Neurologic examination

 About Bell’s palsy 
 Bell’s palsy is a disorder, which mostly happens due to temporary weakness of the facial muscles. This disorder develops suddenly and affects one side of the face. In this disease complete paralysis or numbness is experienced in the facial region. The cranial nerve that controls the functioning of facial muscles on the face shows incapability to send to brain and receive signals from it. Patients suffering from this disorder show helplessness towards controlling movement of their facial muscles. This has been a very common type of facial paralysis and neurologic disorder involving the cranial nerve all throughout the globe. 
 What are the Causes of Bell’s palsy? 
 The cranial nerve is responsible for monitoring movements of the muscles in the facial region and ear region. This nerve extends from the brain to the face. 
 The primary cause of this disorder is the herpes virus, which causes inflammation of this nerve. This is the same virus that is responsible for sore throat, flu, cold and genital herpes. 
 Apart from herpes, there can be a few other viruses such as chickenpox and shingles viruses for causing this painful disease. 
 People, who are suffering from migraine headache, are more susceptible to getting affected by this disorder. Migraine headache increases the chances of this nervous system disorder by two times. 
 What are the Symptoms you can see in Bell’s palsy? 
 
 Facial paralysis and no control over facial muscles 
 Unable to taste or loses sense of taste 
 Feeling weakness of the muscles and nerves in the facial region 
 Difficulty in closing eyes 
 Pain in and outside ears 
 Numbness of the jaws, forehead, cheek, mouth region 
 Blurred view 
 In attempt to raise eyebrows, the forehead region affected by Bell’s palsy remains flat 
 Smiling distorts the face of the patient 
 
 What are the Complications of Bell’s palsy? 
 The damage that happens to the facial nerve can lead to various complications. 
 Some of them have been described below: 
 
 One can experience unusual contractions of facial muscles. Some of the effect of this contraction can be involuntarily closing of one of the eyes or lifting of one side of the mouth when trying to smile. 
 A patient can permanently lose the sense of taste. 
 A person can shed tears while eating. Though this complication can be fully healed but sometimes it can also be long lasting. 
 Patient’s eyelids cannot be properly shut due to the inefficiency of the lubricating tear film. The result of such complication is the dryness of cornea and lowering the production of tears. In some cases, it can get very severe and can lead to permanent loss of eye sight. 
 
 How to Diagnosis Bell’s palsy? 
 The sooner the diagnosis starts, better it will be for the patient to recover from its detrimental impact. The doctor will carefully see all the symptoms and causes that are leading to such facial paralysis. A comprehensive checkup will be performed of the areas including head, neck and ears of the patient. Some of the visible evidences can be presence of tumor, stroke or Lyme disease. Facial muscles are also evaluated precisely to figure out if any other nerve other than cranial nerve is impacted due to this disorder. 
 On the basis of thorough examination, if the doctor detects any change in facial structure then it can be a sign of a tumor. A visible rash can be a sign of Lyme disease. To confirm the presence of Bell’s palsy, a patient can be advised to consult a specialized ENT (ear, nose and throat) specialist i.e., an otolaryngologist. An otolaryngologist will examine the patient’s condition and would prescribe following tests for accurate identification of problem. 
 These tests are: 
 
 Electromyography (EMG) 
 MRI, CT scans and X-ray 
 Oral examination 
 Neurologic examination

Herbal Remedies 

 FAQs 



 What is Anemia 
 An individual suffering from Anemia means his/her blood is not able to carry the enough oxygen to the rest of body. The oxygen is carried by the hemoglobin, which is an iron-rich protein present in blood and gives red color to the blood. Furthermore, iron is required for the production of hemoglobin. Anemia has three main causes: blood loss, lack of red blood cell production, and high rates of red blood cell destruction. 
 What are the Symptoms of Anemia? 

 Pale skin 
 Weakness 
 Fatigue 
 Tiredness 
 Chest pain 
 Chest pain 
 Headache 
 Cold extremities 
 Irregular heart beat 

 What is the Main Cause of Anemia? 
 Anemia takes place when your blood doesn’t have enough red blood cells, this may happen due to:- 


 When your own body destroys red blood cells 
 When body is not able to produce red blood cells or 
 Bleeding takes place and there is huge loss of red blood cells 

 What are the Different Types of Anemia? 
 The most common types of anemia are:- 


 Iron-deficiency Anemia: As discussed earlier, it happens due to deficiency of iron. The iron deficiency occurs due to blood loss or due to poor absorption of iron and poor diet. Gastric bypass surgery has also shown the anemia in many cases. 

 Vitamin deficiency Anemia: Poor dietary intake, in which low levels of vitamin B12 (folate) is found causes anemia. There is another condition, known as Pernicious anemia, in which B12 is not observed in gastrointestinal tract, causes anemia. 

 Hemolytic Anemia: In this condition red blood cells are broken in the bloodstream or in spleen, due to leaky heart valves, infections, autoimmune disorder, and congenital abnormalities. 
 Sickle cell anemia: It is an inherited hemolytic anemia, in which red blood cells become sickle in shape leading to rigidity, clogging in circulation. 

 Aplastic Anemia: It is a rare type of anemia, in which low level of blood cells are produced. Common causes are viral infections, autoimmune disease or exposure to toxic chemicals etc. 
 Pregnancy related anemia: During pregnancy, blood is produced at larger level to support the growth of baby and body of mother. The anemic conditions arises due to the lack of iron or related nutrients in diet. 
 There are other factors, which can induce the anemia, for example dysfunction in kidney, in which hormone ‘erythropoietin’ is not produced enough. The hormone erythropoietin initiates signal to bone marrow to produce new red blood cells. The chemotherapy is used for the treatment of cancer, but continued exposer of the body to this therapy has led impairment in the production new red blood cells, which causes anemia. 

 Who is on the Risk? 
 Persons, who may lead to anemia are having poor diet, intestinal disorder, chronic diseases and infections. The chronic medical conditions and pregnant or menstrual woman are mostly at the risk of anemia. The risk of anemia has been also observed in athletes such as jogging/basketball due to red blood cells breakdown. 
 Other conditions which could lead into anemia are:- 

 Heavy periods 
 Ulcers 
 Colon polyps or colon ulcers 
 Inherited diseases 
 A diet deficient in iron, folic acids and vitamin B12 
 Blood diseases such as sickle cell anemia, thalassemia or cancer 
 Metabolic disorder 


 What are Tests and Diagnosis for Anemia? 
 Physical examination 

 Doctor can check your eyes, eyelid, nails and skin color 
 He can do abdominal examination to feel size of liver and spleen 
 He can also check your heart beat 

 Complete blood count 
 Blood sample can be taken to study hb level in red blood cells, normal hb is 14 to 16 gms for men and 12 to 16 gms in females. 
 Tests can be performed to determine size and shape of red blood cell.

 FAQ’s on Anemia 

 1. Does diet make a difference for people with Anemia? 
 Yes, bad dietary habits can be one of the reasons for Anemia. People on a limited diet and those who are taking overcooked foods and fewer amounts of green leafy vegetables can become folic acid deficient which is the main reason for Anemia. 


 2. Is Anemia curable? 
 Yes, Anemia is curable. It mainly depends upon the type of Anemia you have. Iron and folic acid deficiency are one of the main reasons for Anemia. These types of Anemia are treatable with iron-rich diet and you can also try some herbal products such as Chanderprabha Vati, Punarnava Mandoor, and Arogyavardhini Vati tablets.

 Symptoms may vary from person to person and it mainly depends upon the level of hemoglobin. Weakness, fatigue, headache, a tingling sensation in legs, irregular heartbeats, pale skin, and dizziness these are some common symptoms of iron deficiency in your body.

Herbal Remedies 

 Diet and Lifestyle 




 About Hypertension 
 Hypertension is also commonly known as high blood pressure. It is the medical condition in which the blood pressure in the arteries is persistently elevated. Blood pressure is determined by the amount of blood the heart pumps and the amount of resistance to blood flow in the arteries. Uncontrolled high blood pressure increases the serious health problems, including heart attack and stroke. 
 What are the different types of the hypertension? 

 Primary hypertension: It is also called essential hypertension. It tends to develop gradually over many years. 
 Secondary hypertension: Some people have hypertension due to sleep apnea, obesity, thyroid problem, and certain drugs like non contraceptive pills. This type of blood pressure is known as secondary hypertension. It tends to appear suddenly. 
 Gestational hypertension: High blood pressure may occur in 8-10% females during pregnancy. If two readings of the blood pressure in six hours, are more than 140/90 mm/Hg then the pregnant woman is diagnosed with the gestational hypertension. Gestational hypertension can be classified as pre-existing hypertension, gestational hypertension and pre-eclampsia. 

 Pre-eclampsia is a serious condition, which is characterized by increase in blood pressure and the presence of protein in urine. It mainly occurs in the second half of the pregnancy. The symptoms of the pre-eclampsia are headache, vomiting and swelling. It can be progressed into the life threatening condition called eclampsia. 
 What are the symptoms of the hypertension? 

 Headache (at the back of head in the morning) 
 Vertigo 
 Tinnitus 
 Fainting episodes 

 What can be the risk factors for the hypertension? 

 Age: The risk of blood pressure increases with age. In males, around 45 years age is more common and in females it is around 65 years. 
 Sex: Males are more sufferer than females. 
 Hereditary: High blood pressure tends to run in families. 
 Obesity: When a person is obese, the requirement of the blood and oxygen supply increases. As the volume of the blood circulated through the blood vessels, it will automatically increase the pressure on the artery walls. 
 Excessive use of tobacco: chewing of tobacco or smoking, will cause narrowing of the blood vessels and hence increase the blood pressure. 
 Excessive use of alcohol: Excess use of alcohol, may damage the heart. 
 Excess of salt in the diet: Excess of salt increase the fluid retain in the body, which leads to increase in blood pressure. 
 Deficiency of vitamin D: Vitamin D may affect an enzyme produced by the kidney that affects the blood pressure. 
 Stress: High stress level may increase the blood pressure temporarily. 
 Certain chronic conditions: Kidney disease, diabetes and apnea these are the certain conditions which causes hypertension. 
 Stress and anxiety: One of the major causes of the high blood pressure now a days. 

 What can be the complications of the hypertension? 

 Heart stroke: High blood pressure can cause hardening and thickening of the arteries, which can lead to heart stroke and other complications. 
 Aneurysm: High blood pressure level can cause blood vessels to weaken and bulge, forming an aneurysm. 
 Heart failure: Heart muscles may become thickened, when these muscles pump blood against the higher pressure in the arteries. The thickened muscles may have a hard time to meet body’s need, which can lead to heart failure. 
 Metabolic syndrome: The metabolic syndrome is the group of disorders, including high triglycerides, low high density lipo-protein, high blood pressure and high insulin level. 

 How to diagnose the hypertension? 


 By Examining the blood pressure 
 A blood pressure reading normally in millimeters of mercury (mm hg). 
 Normal blood pressure: systolic 90-110 mm/Hg, diastolic 60-79 mm/Hg 
 High blood pressure: systolic 120-139 mm/Hg, diastolic 80-89 mm/Hg 
 During pregnancy, one examination if two blood pressure readings within six hours are more than normal blood pressure and presence of proteins in the urine.

sections.overview: Ayurvedic Approach to Alleviating Back Pain: A Holistic Healing Tradition
sections.introduction:
Back pain is a prevalent and often debilitating condition that affects millions of people worldwide. While conventional medicine offers various treatments, an increasing number of individuals are turning to alternative and holistic approaches, including Ayurveda, an ancient system of medicine with roots in India. Ayurveda, meaning “ Knowledge Of Life ” emphasizes balance and harmony within the body to promote overall well-being. In the context of back pain, Ayurvedic treatments focus on addressing the root causes rather than just alleviating symptoms. 



 Understanding the Ayurvedic Perspective 
 According to Ayurveda, back pain is often linked to imbalances in the doshas— Vata , Pitta, and Kapha—representing the elemental forces that govern bodily functions. An imbalance in these doshas can lead to a variety of health issues, including back pain. The Ayurvedic approach to treating back pain involves restoring balance to the doshas through a combination of lifestyle modifications, dietary changes, herbal remedies, and therapeutic practices. 
 Lifestyle Modifications 

 Dinacharya (Daily Routine) : Ayurveda emphasizes the importance of Dinacharya, a balanced daily routine, as a key element in maintaining overall health and well-being. Following a regular schedule that includes consistent sleep and wake times, timely meals, and gentle daily exercise helps to regulate the body’s natural rhythms. These practices enhance digestion, mental clarity, and energy levels while also supporting the health of the spine. A well-maintained routine reduces physical strain and helps prevent imbalances that can lead to back pain or stiffness. 
 Yoga and Exercise (Vyayama): Incorporating yoga and exercise (Vyayama) is another vital component in Ayurvedic wellness, especially for maintaining back health. Specific yoga postures (asanas) are recommended to strengthen the muscles supporting the spine, increase flexibility, and encourage proper posture and alignment. Ayurvedic practitioners often personalize yoga routines based on an individual’s dosha (body constitution) to address underlying imbalances. Regular, mindful movement not only relieves existing discomfort but also serves as a preventive measure against chronic back issues. 

 Dietary Changes 

 Anti-inflammatory Foods: Ayurveda encourages a diet rich in anti-inflammatory foods to reduce pain and inflammation associated with back issues. This includes incorporating spices like turmeric and ginger, which have potent anti-inflammatory properties. 
 Balancing Doshas Through Diet: Dietary choices are tailored to balance the specific doshas contributing to back pain. For instance, individuals with excessive Vata imbalances may benefit from warm, nourishing foods and oils. 



 Herbal Remedies & Supplements for Alleviating Back Pain 

 Ayurvedic Herbs: Herbal formulations play a crucial role in Ayurvedic back pain treatment. Some commonly used herbs include Ashwagandha for its anti-inflammatory properties , Boswellia for pain relief, and Guggul for its anti-arthritic effects. These herbs are often combined in formulations to address multiple aspects of back pain. Hakam Churna is another effective anti-inflammatory preparation for pain relief in back due to sprains, strains and muscle spasms as well as sciatica. 
 Ayurvedic Oils and Balms: External application of medicated oils or balms, such as Mahanarayan Oil mixed with Orthovita Oil  is a traditional Ayurvedic practice. Massaging these formulations into the affected area can enhance blood circulation, reduce muscle stiffness, and alleviate pain. 



 Therapeutic Practices 

 Panchakarma: This is a detoxification process in Ayurveda that involves five cleansing procedures to eliminate toxins and restore balance. Panchakarma therapies like Basti (enema) and Abhyanga (oil massage) can be beneficial for individuals experiencing chronic back pain. 
 Swedana (Sweating Therapy): Application of heat, whether through steam or warm compresses, helps relax muscles and promotes the release of toxins. This therapy is often used in conjunction with other Ayurvedic treatments. 
 Kati Basti for Back Pain: Kati Basti is a therapeutic Ayurvedic treatment specifically designed to address back pain, especially in the lumbar (lower back) region. This treatment involves creating a dam-like structure on the back using a dough made from black gram or wheat flour. This structure is then filled with warm medicated oil, allowing the oil to be held in place over the affected area. Kati Basti aims to reduce pain, inflammation, and stiffness while nourishing and strengthening the muscles and tissues of the lower back. 

 Here’s a Step-By-Step guide to understanding and undergoing Kati Basti: 
 Procedures 

 Preparation of the Dough: Create a dough by mixing black gram flour or wheat flour with water. The consistency should be such that it can be molded into a small dam-like structure that can be placed over the affected area of the back.

 Diet containing low fibers.

 What is Cervical Spondylosis

sections.overview:
Ayurvedic Treatment of High Cholesterol Levels 
 Main focus of treating cholesterol is to prevent heart attacks. High cholesterol is now a universally accepted warning sign for millions of people. So what is Cholesterol actually? 

 Cholesterol is a fatty substance (lipid) produced 80% naturally by the liver and the rest comes from diet, found in the blood and which is essential for body to rebuild its cells and to make certain hormones and good health but it can become a problem when this is too much in the blood. 
 Dietary cholesterol is the cholesterol found in foods obtained from animal products like meat, cheese, poultry, or fish. High cholesterol levels in your blood are mainly caused by eating foods high in saturated fats and trans-fats. 
 Types of Cholesterol 
 Cholesterol is carried via bloodstream by attaching to certain proteins. The combination is called a lipoprotein. 
 The two main types of blood cholesterol are: 

 Low-density lipoprotein (LDL) – Known as ‘bad’ cholesterol as it promotes the build-up of fatty deposits in the walls of arteries and increases risk of getting coronary heart disease 
 High-density lipoprotein (HDL) – Known as ‘good’ cholesterol as it is helps to protect against coronary heart disease. 

 In healthy people, it is normal to have more of the ‘bad’ LDL cholesterol when compared to ‘good’ HDL cholesterol, but one should target to always maintain LDL cholesterol down and HDL cholesterol up. 
 Causes of Cholesterol Problems 
 Many factors define whether LDL cholesterol is high or low, including: 

 Age (cholesterol levels increase with age) 
 Alcohol consumption 
 Diet high in saturated fats and cholesterol 
 Inactive lifestyle 
 Gender (men have higher cholesterol) 
 Heredity 
 Level of physical activity 
 Weight- overweight 
 Inherited genetic condition (familial hypercholesterolemia) in some cases. 
 Certain medical conditions, like diabetes, hypothyroidism, liver disease, and kidney disease can raise cholesterol levels. 

 Risk Factors for Cholesterol Problems 

 Smoking and Excess alcohol. 
 A sedentary Lifestyle 
 Obesity. 
 An unhealthy diet – including eating too much salt. 

 Ayurvedic View for Cholesterol Problems 
 As per Ayurveda perspective cholesterol isn’t bad in and of itself, however, it may cause harmful effect when Ama is present in the body. Ama, are metabolic left-overs that get accumulated, like toxins in the fat tissue. 
 When excessive, accumulated Ama start spreading throughout the body, it gets mixed up with the dhatus (body tissues) and the malas (waste products). Once amavisha (dangerous type of ama) gets mixed in with the fat tissue, it damages the srotas, and this in turn leads to problems such as high cholesterol, heart disease, stroke and high blood pressure. 
 Symptoms of Cholesterol Problems 
 Mostly persons with high cholesterol don’t have any symptoms, but chronic (long-term; several decades’ worth) elevated levels can lead to serious problems affecting your heart and circulation etc. such as heart attack and stroke. 
 The first sign that of high cholesterol could be: 

 Angina 
 Heart attack 
 Stroke 
 Pain on walking 

 Other symptoms may be like bumps in the skin, hands or feet, which are caused by deposits of extra cholesterol and other types of fat.

sections.introduction:
Herbal Remedies 

 Diet and Lifestyle 



 About Depression 
 Depression is a mood disorder which causes loss of interest and a feeling of sadness in a person. The disorder is also known as clinical depression or major depressive disorder. It affects mood, thinking, feeling as well as the behavior of an affected person. A person may have trouble in doing his daily activities. 
 Causes of Depression 
 The exact cause of this disorder is not known, but there are some factors that may cause this disorder. 
 The factors are listed below: 

 A person with depression may have a different physical appearance. 
 Stress is the major reason for the same disorder. 
 Change in the functioning of neurotransmitters is also responsible for the same. Neurotransmitters are associated with the functioning of the brain. 
 Hormonal changes in the body may also cause depression. 
 A person having a family history of this disorder is also at high risk of getting this disorder. 
 Certain medications can be the reason for the same. 
 Serious health problem may cause depression. 
 Alcohol abuse is another reason for the same disorder. 

 What are the Complications of Depression? 
 This mood disorder is often gets serious and may cause some serious health complications if not treated well. 
 The complications that can be resulted due to this disorder are listed below: 

 It may lead to weight gain and in turn may cause heart disease as well. 
 Physical illness can be caused due to this disorder. 
 Conflicts within a family or family relationship may get disturbed. 
 Anxiety or any other panic disorder. 
 Pain in the body. 
 The disorder may cause suicidal feeling in the affected person. 
 The disorder may cause social isolation. 

 How can Depression be Diagnosed? 
 A doctor may diagnose the disorder by doing a physical examination of an affected person. He may ask for some test, such as blood test such as complete blood count test or he may check the functioning of the thyroid gland in order to confirm the diagnosis. A doctor may even ask about your feeling, thoughts or behavior pattern.

Herbal Remedies 



 What is Eosinophilia? 
 Eosinophilia is a chronic disorder that occurs due to increased eosinophils number in complete blood count. Normally, the eosinophil count is less than 350 cells per microliter. Eosinophils are the white blood cells which helps to fight against the disease and regulate the inflammation. The protein present in eosinophil’s damage the body. These cells become active when a person have a certain allergic diseases, infections and other medications or when the bone marrow secrete more number of cells. When eosinophils count more than 500 per microliter is generally considered as eosinophilia in the adults. A count of eosinophil’s more than 1500 for constant several months, the condition is known as hypereosinophilic syndrome. 
 What are the Different Type of Eosinophilia? 

 Extrinsic: Extrinsic eosinophilia, in which etiological factors lies outside the eosinophil cell lineage such as worm’s infestations, fungi, medications. 
 Intrinsic: Intrinsic eosinophilia, in which etiological factors lies inside the eosinophil cell lineage such as asthmatic pulmonary eosinophilia. 

 What can be the Causes of the Eosinophilia? 
 There are several disease or abnormal conditions, in which there is increase in eosinophil’s count. 

 Allergic disorders (Asthma, Hay fever, drug allergy etc.) 
 Parasitic and fungal disease (Lymphatic filariasis, Ascariasis, Trichinosis etc.) 
 Autoimmune disorders (Arthritis, Psoriasis, Pernicious anemia, Lupus etc.) 
 Skin disorders (Abscess, scabies, Impetigo etc.) 
 Tumors (Ovarian cancer, lung cancer etc.) 

 What can be the Risk Factors for the Eosinophilia? 

 Cirrhosis of liver 
 Hodgkin’s lymphoma 
 Non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma 
 Allergic food 
 Drug side effects 

 What can be the Common Symptoms of the Eosinophilia? 

 Frequent wheezing 
 Breathlessness 
 Abdominal pain 
 Diarrhea 
 Fever 
 Cough 
 Skin Rashes 

 What can be the Common Indicator of the Eosinophilia? 

 Frequent infections 
 Abscesses 
 Mouth sores

 Family history.

Ayurvedic Treatment of Fatty Liver 

 About Fatty Liver 
 Normally a liver contains a certain amount of fat, if the fat counts excides over 5-10% of the weight of the liver, then an individual must be suffering from “fatty liver” or steatosis. Fatty liver has accumulation of triglycerides and other fats in the liver cells characterized by enlarged and swollen liver with fat. In some of the patients, fatty liver may be accompanied by hepatic inflammation and liver cell death (steatohepatitis). 
 Fatty liver is a reversible condition which can be resolved with changed behavior, diet and lifestyle. 
 Fatty liver can be categorized as alcoholic and non-alcoholicliver disorder. 
 Fatty liver can exist without causing symptoms or getting worse in some people. In others, fatty liver can lead to additional health problems. 
 In fatty liver the Normal, healthy liver tissue becomes partly replaced with fatty tissue and the fat starts to capture the liver. This fatty infiltration decelerates down the metabolism of body fat stores, which means that the liver burns fat less efficiently, resulting in weight gain and inability to lose weight. However some people can have a fatty liver without being overweight. 


 Causes of Fatty Liver 

 Excessive consumption of alcohol 
 Metabolic abnormalities like glycogen storage disease. 
 Increased body weight (Obesity) 
 Insulin resistance (as occurs in diabetes) 
 High levels of triglycerides (fat) in the blood 
 Rapid loss in weight 
 Genetically Inherited 
 Some drugs like Corticosteroids, Tamoxifen 
 Pregnancy 
 Certain cancer chemotherapy drugs 



 Ayurvedic View for Cause of Fatty Liver 
 In accordance to Ayurveda, Fatty Liver disease happens due to imbalances of three types of physical energy, or doshas ( Vata, Pitta and Kapha ). The liver is regarded a fire or pitta organ, as it is essential for digestion and elimination. So the good health of liver needs to balance the pitta dosha. This will strengthen the ability of liver to flush toxins from the body. As when there is overloading of liver with toxins like alcohol or fats, it will work too hard and burn too hot. This leads to inflammation and problems throughout the body. 


 Signs and Symptoms of Fatty Liver 
 Fatty liver disease rarely causes symptoms until the liver disease is far advanced. 
 Excess fat can cause liver inflammation which is diagnosed only by physical examination and with inflamed liver one may have: 

 Pain in the center or right upper part of the belly 
 Feeling of tiredness 
 Loss of weight or poor appetite 
 Weakness 
 Enlarged spleen 
 Abdominal swelling (ascites) 
 Yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice) 
 Nausea 
 Skin on neck or under your arms may have dark, colored patches. 
 Confusion, poor judgment, or trouble in concentration may also happen. 

 In case of alcoholic liver disease, one may notice that the symptoms get worse after a period of heavy drinking.
