fullContent:
Kansya Bhasma – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More 
 Reference : Rasratna Samuchya 5
 
 Introduction 
 Kansya Bhasma is a classical Ayurvedic herbo-mineral formulation prepared from Kansya (bronze), an alloy traditionally composed of eight parts copper (Tamra) and two parts tin (Vanga). Historically, Indians have been familiar with bronze since ancient times. Its use in the form of vessels, statues, and bells is mentioned in ancient texts. Only after the development of alchemical purification and calcination processes (in the 8th century) did the preparation of its ash and its internal medicinal use become prevalent. When subjected to proper Shodhana (purification) and Marana (incineration) processes, Kansya is converted into a fine, bio-assimilable ash known as Kansya Bhasma. 
 Process Of Making Kansya Bhasm 
 Acceptable Bronze 
 Soft and smooth, slightly blackish-white, clean and shiny and red when heated is considered to be the best. 
 The Purification Of Bronze 
 It is achieved by first purifying the raw bronze by heating and quenching it seven times each in oil, takra (buttermilk), cow urine, kanji and decoction of kulatha. 
 After that, the bronze is purified by: 
 
 Heating the bronze sheets, purified with oil and buttermilk (buttermilk), to redness in a fire and then quenching them seven times in cow urine. 
 Placing cow urine and rock salt in a pot and adding fine bronze powder or filings to it. Then, heating this mixture on a stove for one prahar (3 hours) purifies the bronze. 
 
 Kansya Maran (Calcination Of Bronze) 
 
 Grind equal parts of gandhak (pure sulfur) and hartal (arsenic trisulfide) in lemon juice and apply the paste to the bronze. Let it dry. Now, seal it in a crucible, lute the joints, dry it in the sun, and then heat it in a half-sized earthen crucible furnace. After five such firings, the bronze will be reduced to ash. 
 Grind equal parts of kansya (bronze) and hingul (cinnabar) with lemon juice and subject it to three successive firings in an earthen crucible furnace. This will produce bronze ash. 
 Grind equal parts of kansya (bronze) and gandhak (pure sulfur) together with the milky sap of Calotropis procera (Arka) and subject it to three firings in an earthen crucible furnace (gajput). This will also produce bronze ash. 
 Equal parts of kansya (bronze), manashila (purified realgar), and gandhak (pure sulfur) are triturated with aloe vera juice, and then subjected to three cycles of heating in a closed crucible (gajput) to produce bronze ash. 
 
 The color of bronze ashes is black (kajjal colour). 
 Medicines Containing Kansya Bhasma 
 Kshayakesari Rasa, Chintamani Rasa, Nityananda Rasa, Makardhvaja Vati, Muktadya Churna, Lakshmivilas Rasa, Vatavidhvasana Rasa, Shadanan Rasa etc. 
 Properties Of Bronze Ashes 
 It is bitter in taste; It is light and hot in potency. 
 Actions 
 
कांस्य लघु च तिक्तीष्णं लेखनं दुप्रसादनम् । 
कृमिकुष्ठहरं वातपित्तघ्नं दीपनं हितम् ।। 
घृतमेकं विना चान्यत्सर्वे कांस्यगतं तृणाम् । 
मुक्तमारोग्यसुखदं हितं सात्म्यकरं तथा ।। (Rasratna Samuchya 5/208-209) 
 
 
 Vatapittaghna (Paicified vata and pitta) 
 Lekhana (Scraping) 
 Drishtiprasadana (cleansing the sight) 
 Dipana (Appetiser) 
 Krimmihar (Antihelminthic) 
 Kushthahara (Antileprotic) 
 
 Note 
 It is good to eat all kinds of food except ghee in a bronze vessel. 
 Clinical Usages 
 
 Improves digestive fire (Agni) and intestinal motility; useful in indigestion and constipation 
 Effective anthelmintic in intestinal worm infestations, especially when combined with Vaividang Churna 
 Beneficial in skin disorders associated with Kapha–Pitta vitiation 
 Used in eye diseases, including prevention of progression in optic neuropathy 
 Helps prevent age-related macular degeneration and oxidative damage to ocular tissues 
 Supports red blood cell formation and improves overall metabolism 
 Enhances bile secretion and liver–gut function 
 Useful in internal abscesses due to antimicrobial and pus-drying action 
 Aids in wound healing and limits spread of infection 
 Helpful in leucorrhea and Kapha-dominant gynecological conditions 
 Supports immune modulation and resistance to infections 
 Assists in relieving fatigue and depressive tendencies (tin component support) 
 
 Precautions 
 
 Kansya Bhasma is contraindicated in infants and pregnant women. 
 The medicine should strictly be consumed in prescribed doses only; higher-than-recommended doses are not advised. 
 Improper or excessive intake may lead to adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, and aggravation of anal fissures. 
 It should be avoided in patients suffering from renal impairment, renal failure, or existing anal fissures. 
 
 Dosage 
 
 Half to One ratti (60 mg to 120mg) 
 Anupan (drug delivery) with honey and various herbal substances according to disease. 
 
 Conclusion 
 Kansya Bhasma is a classical Ayurvedic formulation that exemplifies the therapeutic application of metals through refined Rasashastra techniques. When properly purified and calcined, it acts primarily as a Deepana, Lekhana, and Krimighna agent, making it useful in digestive disorders, worm infestations, and Kapha–Pitta dominant conditions. Its traditional relevance, supported by classical references such as Rasratna Samuchya, highlights its importance in Ayurvedic pharmaceutics. However, due to its potent nature, Kansya Bhasma should always be used in precise doses and under expert supervision to ensure safe and effective outcomes.

sections.reference_ras_ratna_samuchaya:
Abstract 
 In present times, fast food is the food of choice for everyone. But we all know that it is the least nutrient giving food. Still we all like it the most? Aren’t you? Yes, right! But It causes lots of abdominal diseases, so to manage these disorders what should we do? Don’t worry! Ayurveda is here to help you. Today we are going to discuss one of the wonderful formulations indicated in abdominal issues i.e. Kapardak bhasma and its numerous health benefits which are mentioned in classical texts.
sections.introduction:
Kapardak bhasma is also known as kapardika bhasma, cowrie bhasma, Kaudi bhasma, varatika bhasma. It is an ayurvedic calcined preparation mainly used in managing disorders of the digestive tract. Kapardak bhasma has hot potency but it has an alkaline effect in the stomach. Thus it stops the excess secretion of HCL. 
 Classical Indication 
 Grahani (Malabsorption syndrome)
sections.ingredients: Kapardak (Yellow coloured)
sections.description_of_the_ingredients:
Kaparda (Calcium carbonate) – It is mainly a calcium carbonate compound which helps in relieving pain, IBS, tuberculosis due to its katu (pungent), ushna (hot), digestive stimulant and aphrodisiac properties. It balances vata and kapha dosha and also aids in managing acid reflux and heartburn. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Dig a hole on the ground of 1 hand length and thickness and put a pan of iron inside the hole. 
 Then put all the kaudi (varatika) on that iron pan and cover this with a tin sheet. 
 Now spread forest thorns all over the tin sheets and light the fire. 
 After 8 hours of burning just make it lukewarm. 
 Keep the ash aside and collect the varatika (white coloured) 
 Now do mardan (frolement) of varatika with nimbu swaras and prepare muffins. 
 Dry these muffins and burn it in gajputta by closing it in sharava samputta. 
 After 1 putt, bhasma will be ready. 

 Medicinal Properties 
 Kapardak bhasma has Katu (pungent) and tikta (bitter) rasa, Laghu (light), rooksha (dry) and theekshana guna (Sharp), ushna veerya (hot potency), Katu vipaka (Result after digestion) and mainly pacifies vata and kapha dosha but it has alkaline property due to which it prevents the excessive secretion of gastric acid and pacifies the amla guna of pitta thus helpful in reducing elevated pitta. It also alleviates ama from the body and supports healthy digestion. Let’s see some of its tremendous health benefits:- 

 Kapardak bhasma possess carminative and antiflatulent and vata shamak properties therefore useful in abdominal pain, bloating, intestinal gas, and excessive flatulence. It gives better results when given with cow’s ghee and mishri. Kapardika bhasma with arogyavardhini vati is very helpful in these cases. 
 It is very good in preventing belching as it reduces the production and accumulation of ama (endotoxins) dosha in the body. It also prevents the sour taste of the mouth by correcting digestion. 
 Kapardak bhasma with swarna makshik aids in inducing vomiting and expels the Sour vomitus and mucus content. 
 If Kapardak bhasma is given with Madhu then it shows wonders in ajeerna (indigestion). But in rasa ajeerna it is advised to be given with Hingwashtak churna. 
 In parinamshoola (Duodenal ulcer), it should be given with dadim swarasa and dadimavaleha and in Annadrav shoola (Gastric ulcers) it should be given with Shankh bhasma. 
 In grahani (Malabsorption syndrome), it is advised to take jeera churna. 
 In Agnimandya (low digestive fire) it is given with trikatu churna. 
 In Shwas roga (Dyspnoea), it is given with pippali churna and madhu.  
 In karna strava (CSOM (Chronic suppurative otitis media)), it should be poured in the ear and afterwards add nimbu swaras. 
 In dry cough, it is advised to take it with malai or pan swaras. 
 In Kshaya roga it should be given with makhan.
sections.dosage:
3gm -6 mg once or twice a day or as directed by the physician. 
 Anupana (adjuvant) 
 Cow’s ghee, Mishri or as according to the disease.
sections.contraindications:
Store it in a cool and dry place 
 Keep it away from the children 
 Avoid giving in pregnancy or lactation 
 Always take after consulting an Ayurvedic physician 

 Conclusion 
 Therefore, coming to an end, we can say kapardak bhasma is beneficial in managing Various health disorders if given with proper adjuvant and in proper doses. This medicine works well if we follow the diet properly and adapt to a healthy lifestyle. For more queries you can consult online on herbalremedies123@yahoo.com. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Kasis Bhasma

sections.overview: Kasis Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Iron Sulphate is referred to as Kasis in Ayurveda. It is green in color and it is categorized under two types which are 1. Baluka Kasis and 2. Pushp Kasis. Kasis is first purified according to the apt method of purification mentioned in Ayurveda and is made into a Bhasma following the various steps involved in the process. 
 This Bhasma is used to ward off generalized weakness, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, skin and eye ailments. It has a hot potency and tastes sour. Also, it helps to balance kapha and vata.
sections.ingredients:
Pure Kasis (Crystalline ferrous sulphate) – 100 grams 

 Method of Preparation 
 Triturate purified crystalline ferrous sulphate with kanji water and make fine attenuated cakes. Now heat them in a container which is shut and sealed from all sides at a temperature of 300 – 500 degree Celsius till you obtain a fine powdered substance.
sections.dosage:
125 mg – 250 mg two times a day. 
 Stomach disorders – take it with a herbal blend of long pepper, black pepper and ginger and honey. 
 Spleen and liver enlargement – honey and cow’s urine 
 White spots – it can be taken with Triphala (Powdered Myrobalans)
sections.indications:
Anemia 
 Swelling 
 Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly 
 Weakness 
 Digestive disorders 
 Menstrual irregularities 
 Eye ailments 
 Pruritus 
 Dysuria 
 Skin diseases 
 Immunity booster 
 Anorexia
sections.contraindications:
It should not be used if you’re allergic to Green vitriol. 
 Ulcerative colitis 
 Hemolytic anemia 
 Ulcers 
 Over dosage should be strictly avoided as it may cause severe gastritis. 
 It should not be taken during pregnancy, lactation and by kids. 
 It should be taken under stern medical supervision, in a precise dose and for a given duration of time. 
 Though it doesn’t cause any side effects if taken in the prescribed dosage but it might cause nausea and vomiting. In that case the dosage can be reduced to half for a few days and increased gradually. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

It can also be called Kukkutanda Twak Bhasma, Eggshell calcium, Eggshell calx, eggshell Bhasma. It provides anti- inflammatory benefits. It is highly enriched with calcium, copper, zinc, magnesium. It also helps in pacifying Vata and Kapha.

name: Loha Bhasma

sections.overview: Loha Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Loha Bhasma is widely used in Ayurveda and it is a product of calcined iron. It strengthens the body and improves the production of RBCs. The person who suffers from loss of blood suffers from the consequences like pale skin, hair fall, loss of memory, panic attacks, fatigue etc. Lack of blood also affects the menstrual cycle in females. In such cases, iron formulation helps in improving the condition and enhances the production of RBCs. It also promotes longevity. This product helps in balancing Pitta and Kapha. 
 The basic preparation of Bhasma involves a few steps:- 

 Purification 
 Powdering 
 Stirring 
 Washing 
 Filtering 
 Heating 
 Triturating 
 Coating with herbal
sections.ingredients:
Iron 
 Triphala (Powdered Myrobalans) 
 Cow’s urine 

 Method of Preparation 
 Mix the powdered Myrobalans in 700 ml of cow’s urine and put it over the flame and boil it till It’s reduced to 200 ml. Strain this concoction to crush the refined Iron and prepare round flat cakes and put them in a closed container and heat them at a temperature of 8800 degree Celsius for 4- 5 hours. Take it out and grind it with the formed decoction for a day and heat it again in a sealed container. Repeat this process for 21 times to attain the final product.
sections.properties: Loha Bhasma is formed when Iron is calcined through inorganic preparation. This formulation is extremely useful in managing anemia, phthisis, cardiac disorders, sexual debility, worm infestations, liver and spleen disorders, obesity, dyspepsia, piles, skin disorders. Primarily, this formulation helps in increasing the hemoglobin. Iron is known to provide vigor. It has anti-aging, anti-spasmodic properties. It is known to strengthen the body. Loha bhasma helps in curing diseases which occur due to vitiated Kapha and Pitta. It is an overall rejuvenator and has immunomodulatory properties. Calcined Iron is the main ingredient of this formulation. This formulation aids in blood coagulation and promotes increase in the hemoglobin level. It helps in igniting the digestive fire and enhances lost appetite. It is extremely nourishing. Loha Bhasma tastes sour and bitter. It is beneficial in eye and skin disorders also.
sections.indications:
Anemia 
 As an anti-spasmodic 
 Dyspepsia 
 Hyperlipidemia 
 Tuberculosis 
 Worm infestations 
 Skin ailments 
 Obesity 
 Splenic disorders 
 Bowel disorders 
 Diabetes 
 Inflammation 
 Urinary disorders 
 Jaundice 
 Eye disorders 
 Respiratory diseases 
 Bloating
sections.dosage:
125mg – 250 mg two times daily after meals.

Loha Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage 
 Reference: Rasamrit 
 Introduction 
 Loha Bhasma is widely used in Ayurveda and it is a product of calcined iron. It strengthens the body and improves the production of RBCs. The person who suffers from loss of blood suffers from the consequences like pale skin, hair fall, loss of memory, panic attacks, fatigue etc. Lack of blood also affects the menstrual cycle in females. In such cases, iron formulation helps in improving the condition and enhances the production of RBCs. It also promotes longevity. This product helps in balancing Pitta and Kapha. 
 The basic preparation of Bhasma involves a few steps:- 
 
 Purification 
 Powdering 
 Stirring 
 Washing 
 Filtering 
 Heating 
 Triturating 
 Coating with herbal 
 
 Ingredients 
 
 Iron 
 Triphala (Powdered Myrobalans) 
 Cow’s urine 
 
 Method of Preparation 
 Mix the powdered Myrobalans in 700 ml of cow’s urine and put it over the flame and boil it till It’s reduced to 200 ml. Strain this concoction to crush the refined Iron and prepare round flat cakes and put them in a closed container and heat them at a temperature of 8800 degree Celsius for 4- 5 hours. Take it out and grind it with the formed decoction for a day and heat it again in a sealed container. Repeat this process for 21 times to attain the final product. 
 Properties 
 Loha Bhasma is formed when Iron is calcined through inorganic preparation. This formulation is extremely useful in managing anemia, phthisis, cardiac disorders, sexual debility, worm infestations, liver and spleen disorders, obesity, dyspepsia, piles, skin disorders. Primarily, this formulation helps in increasing the hemoglobin. Iron is known to provide vigor. It has anti-aging, anti-spasmodic properties. It is known to strengthen the body. Loha bhasma helps in curing diseases which occur due to vitiated Kapha and Pitta. It is an overall rejuvenator and has immunomodulatory properties. Calcined Iron is the main ingredient of this formulation. This formulation aids in blood coagulation and promotes increase in the hemoglobin level. It helps in igniting the digestive fire and enhances lost appetite. It is extremely nourishing. Loha Bhasma tastes sour and bitter. It is beneficial in eye and skin disorders also. 
 Indications 
 
 Anemia 
 As an anti-spasmodic 
 Dyspepsia 
 Hyperlipidemia 
 Tuberculosis 
 Worm infestations 
 Skin ailments 
 Obesity 
 Splenic disorders 
 Bowel disorders 
 Diabetes 
 Inflammation 
 Urinary disorders 
 Jaundice 
 Eye disorders 
 Respiratory diseases 
 Bloating 
 
 Dosage 
 
 125mg – 250 mg two times daily after meals. 
 It can be taken with Trikatu (Long pepper, Black pepper and ginger), honey, clarified butter. 
 
 Contraindications 
 
 Over dosage is strictly unadvisable as it may cause severe gastritis. 
 This medicine should be taken under medical supervision.

 Ingredient Description 

 Rasasindura – Rasasindura is a premier Ayurvedic Kupipakwa Rasayana prepared by the controlled sublimation of purified Mercury and Sulfur. It acts as a potent Yogavahi (catalyst), meaning it carries the medicinal properties of the other ingredients deep into the tissues (Dhatus) while significantly boosting their efficacy. It specifically stimulates the liver and spleen—the primary sites of blood formation—to correct the root cause of Pandu (anemia). Rasasindura acts as a cellular stimulant and immunomodulator. In its processed sulfide form, it is thought to enhance metabolic activity and energy production within cells, ensuring that the body’s hematopoietic system is “awakened” to produce more red blood cells while strengthening the overall immune response. 
 Loha Bhasma (Incinerated Iron) – Loha Bhasma is the cornerstone of Ayurvedic hematology, consisting of iron that has undergone hundreds of cycles of purification and incineration with herbal juices. It is the ultimate Rakta-vardhaka (blood-builder) that directly replenishes the Rakta Dhatu (blood tissue) and treats the “pallor” associated with anemia. Its cooling potency (Sheeta Virya) ensures it builds blood without causing excessive internal heat. Loha Bhasma provides iron in a nano-crystalline form (typically 10–60 nm), which offers significantly higher bioavailability and absorption rates compared to synthetic iron salts. Because these particles are absorbed through different pathways in the gut, they effectively raise hemoglobin and ferritin levels while minimizing common gastrointestinal side effects like nausea or metallic aftertaste. 
 Shuddha Gandhak (Purified Sulfur) – Shuddha Gandhak is sulfur that has been detoxified through repeated processing in cow’s ghee and milk. In Ayurveda it is a powerful Rakta-shodhak (blood purifier) and Krimighna (anthelmintic). By removing “Aama” (toxic metabolic waste) and clearing the blood-carrying channels (Srotas), it ensures that the newly formed blood is of high quality and free from impurities. Sulfur is a vital component for the synthesis of glutathione, the body’s master antioxidant. It supports Phase II liver detoxification, creating a clean internal environment that prevents the premature breakdown of red blood cells. Furthermore, its antimicrobial properties help manage anemia caused by chronic low-grade infections or intestinal parasites. 
 Semal Decoction (Bombax ceiba) – Semal Decoction, derived from the Silk Cotton tree, is prized in Ayurveda for its Brimhana (nutritive) and Stambhana (strengthening) qualities. It pacifies Pitta and provides a cooling, soothing effect on the blood vessels, which prevents the “burning” or depletion of blood cells often seen in inflammatory types of anemia. It acts as a tonic for the reproductive and circulatory systems. The bark and roots are rich in gallic acid and tannins, which provide potent antioxidant protection. These compounds stabilize the membranes of red blood cells, protecting them from oxidative stress and extending their lifespan, which is crucial for maintaining a healthy red blood cell count over time. 
 Triphala Decoction – Triphala, the legendary blend of Amalaki, Bibhitaki, and Haritaki, serves as the “cleaner” in this formulation. It balances all three Doshas and ensures the Anulomana (proper downward movement) of waste, preventing the constipation often associated with iron intake. It clears the micro-channels so that nutrients can reach the bone marrow. Triphala is an incredible source of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and chebulinic acid. Vitamin C is the most critical factor in enhancing non-heme iron absorption in the small intestine. By lowering the pH in the gut, Triphala helps convert iron into a more soluble form, ensuring that the Loha Bhasma is utilized to its maximum potential. 
 Giloy Juice ( Tinospora cordifolia ) – Giloy, known as Amrita (the root of immortality), is a powerful rejuvenative herb. It is a Sarva-dosha-hara (balancer of all humors) that specifically revitalizes the liver and enhances the quality of Rasa Dhatu (plasma), which is the precursor to blood. It builds Ojas (vitality), helping the patient recover from the extreme fatigue of anemia. Giloy is a documented hematopoietic stimulant; it triggers the proliferation of bone marrow cells and increases the count of all blood elements, including erythrocytes and leucocytes. Its anti-inflammatory properties also help manage “Anemia of Chronic Disease” by reducing the systemic inflammation that often traps iron away from the blood. 
 Trikatu Decoction – Trikatu is the “three-pungent” combination of Black Pepper, Long Pepper, and Ginger. It acts as a Deepana-Pachana (digestive stimulant) that burns away the “Aama” (toxins) blocking the absorption of minerals. It increases the “warmth” of the formulation to ensure the heavy metals don’t cause sluggish digestion. Trikatu is famous for containing Piperine, a natural bio-enhancer. Piperine increases the thermogenesis of the gut and modifies the lipid dynamics of the intestinal membrane, which significantly increases the bioavailability of the iron and sulfur in the formula, making the medicine effective even at lower dosages. 
 Ginger Juice ( Zingiber officinale ) – Ginger Juice is used as a medium to grind and stabilize the final pills. It is Agnivardhaka (appetizer) and Hridya (heart-pleasing). It ensures that the medicine is light to digest (Laghu) and does not cause bloating or heaviness in the stomach. Ginger contains gingerols and shogaols that stimulate gastric motility and the secretion of digestive enzymes. By improving the transit time and health of the stomach lining, it ensures that the potent mineral ingredients are processed smoothly by the digestive tract, preventing the common “heavy” feeling or gastric irritation that often accompanies traditional iron supplementation. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Mix all the ingredients in a mortar (Kharal) and fill them into a fire-resistant glass bottle (Aatshi Shishi). 
 Fill the bottle halfway with 24 Tole of Semal decoction (Kwath). 
 Place it in a sand bath (Baluka Yantra) and apply mild heat. 
 When the Semal decoction has nearly evaporated, add 24 Tole of warm Triphala decoction. Once that dries, add 24 Tole of warm Giloy juice. 
 When the liquid dries and the sulfur has nearly burnt off (forming a sedimented medicine at the bottom), stop the heat. 
 Heating usually needs to be maintained for about 1 day. Once it cools naturally (Swang Sheetal), remove it and grind it in a mortar with Trikatu decoction and ginger juice for 12 hours each. 
 Form into 1-Ratti (approx. 125mg) pills. 

 Note: Preparing the Sindura by grinding the three types of juices with the dry medicine in a mortar and drying it before heating in the bottle results in a medicine with superior qualities.
sections.uses_upayog:
This Lohasindura treats Pandu (Anemia) associated with dryness or tissue depletion (Dhatu-kshaya). Pandu can be caused by various fevers, intestinal worms, Rheumatoid arthritis (Amavata), Diabetes (Madhumeha), Syphilis, chronic fever, or weakness in mothers after childbirth. It also addresses anemia caused by excessive sexual activity, masturbation, fasting, mental anxiety, lack of nutritious food, tobacco addiction, or lead poisoning. 
 Clinical Use 

 For muscle wasting: Mix with Abhrak Bhasma and take with Chyawanprash or Amla Murabba to relieve dryness, Pitta aggravation, and constipation. 
 For weakness from excessive childbirth/breastfeeding: Take with Praval Pishti and Amrita Satva. 
 For weakness from early-life celibacy breakage or excess sexual activity: Use with Chyawanprash, Amritapash, or Shatavaryadi Churna.
sections.dosage: Take 1 pill, twice a day, with Chyawanprash or an appropriate carrier (Anupana) suited to the specific disease.
sections.contraindications:
It may not be effective if the anemia is caused by severe toxic conditions (Visha-prakopa), such as Tuberculosis (Rajyakshma), Albuminuria (Lasikameh), Syphilis, or Lead poisoning. 
 It does not cure anemia during high acute fever, though it may provide some strength. 
 It is not effective for Tridoshaj Pandu (Progressive Pernicious Anemia) involving hemorrhaging or heart-fatty changes. 
 It is not used for anemia arising from the lymphatic system or in cases of “Halimak” (a severe form of jaundice/anemia) where the patient appears stout rather than dry. 

 Conclusion 
 At last we can say that managing anemia is not merely about replenishing a mineral; it is about restoring the “Agnimantha” , the internal friction that sparks life. By uniting the ancient wisdom of Rasa Shastra with modern biological principles, Lohasindura offers a sophisticated solution to blood depletion. Through the synergy of nano-iron, catalytic sulfur, and bio-enhancing herbs like Triphala and Giloy, this formulation ensures that the body does not just receive iron, but actively transforms it into vitality. When the “crimson river” flows with strength once more, the ghost of fatigue vanishes, returning the vibrant, warm pulse of health to the human spirit.

name: Mukta Shukti Bhasma

sections.introduction: Mukta Shukti Bhasma is an ayurvedic herbal formulation. This is formulated from the pearl oyster shell. These are found in Indian Ocean. This is enriched with properties like being antacid and anti-pyretic etc. This is used to treat problems of digestive, respiratory system and heart. This bhasma is rich with mineral elements such as aluminum oxide, magnesium oxide, calcium carbonate and organic matter.
sections.ingredients:
Purified pearl oyster shell 
 Purification method of pearl oyster shell 

 Take oyster shell and dipped in to butter milk for three days. 
 Change the butter milk every day. 
 Place the vessel in the sunlight without its lid means uncovered vessel. 
 After 3 days, take out shell and wash with warm water. 
 Remove the black part of the oyster shell with the help of knife. 
 Now used the white part of the oyster shell. 

 Method of preparation 

 Take purified pearl oyster shell and make its powder by grinding. 
 Now powder is heated in absence of air in 900 degree Celsius for 3 hours. 
 Repeated the process three times. 
 You will get the white coloured Mukta Shukti Bhasma.

Take 120 to 250 mg one or two times in a day, before or after food. 
 Consume this bhasma with honey, butter, ghee or milk.

sections.overview: Naga Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Naga bhsama is an ayurvedic formulation which is prepared from lead. This consists of nano particle sized lead particles. Its size is up to 60 nm. This is very useful in the treatment of problems related to urinary, skin, respiratory system and liver.
sections.ingredients:
Purified lead 
 Purified manashila 
 Lemon juice 
 Purified Sulphur 

 Method of preparation 

 Take up to 960 gram purified lead and pore it in a pot. 
 Now burn the fire under this pot. 
 When it loses its hardness and changed into the liquid form, add purified manashila, in a drop wise manner while stirring. When you add same amount of manashila in the liquid, a powder is formed. 
 Now put this into iron pot and place on hot fire for three hours. 
 Then cool it down and strain this. You got the raw bhasma. 
 Now add pure Sulphur in raw bhasma and crush this with lemon juice in mortar for six hours. 
 After this dry this mixture in the sunlight. 
 Then place in a container and put that container on fire. Cow dung is used to ignite the fire. 
 After this process you got the naga bhasma.
sections.properties_of_naga_bhasma: Naga bhasma is fine powdered formulation which is used for the management of the frequent urination, urinary incontinence, diabetes mellitus, spleen enlargement, leucorrhoea, hiatus hernia, impotency, rheumatoid arthritis, etc. It is likely to act on the organs such as stomach, intestine, pancreas, urinary bladder, testes, bones, muscles, joints and ligaments. It is useful for the skin diseases and other many health related problems like cough, piles, urinary incontinence, impotency, diabetes etc. The ingredients used in the preparation of naga bhasma are able to balance the all three doshas i.e. vata, pitta and kapha and their related disorders. It is used to manage the blood sugar level naturally, useful in management of diabetes. Use of this bhasma is very effective in non-healing wounds, piles, malabsorption syndrome, helminthiasis, diarrhea, jaundice, skin diseases, itches, cough, asthma, whooping cough, bronchitis, emaciation, thirst, abdominal colic, obesity, anemia, rheumatoid arthritis, gonorrhea, leucorrhoea, bleeding, spitting and vomiting blood, epilepsy etc. Apart from this it is used in Impotency and increases the sexual desire, also improves the quality of sperm.

 Diabetes

name: Neelam Bhasma

sections.overview: Neelam Bhasma – Medicinal Properties, Ingredients, Indications, Dosage More
sections.introduction: Neelam Bhasma is a classical gem-based Ayurvedic formulation prepared from Neelam (Blue Sapphire), traditionally known as Indraneela in Rasashastra texts. While blue sapphire is widely known as a precious gemstone, Ayurvedic alchemical literature recognizes its medicinal potential when processed through systematic Shodhana (purification) and Marana (incineration). In its raw crystalline form, Neelam is extremely hard and unsuitable for internal use; however, after proper pharmaceutical processing, it is converted into a fine, bioassimilable Bhasma. Classical descriptions attribute strengthening, stabilizing, and protective properties to Neelam Bhasma, particularly in chronic disorders and conditions associated with neurological and metabolic imbalance.
sections.ingredients_of_neelam_bhasma:
Neelam (Blue Sapphire / Indraneela) 
 Shodhana Dravyas: Neeli swaras (juice of Indigofera tinctoria) 
 Marana Media: Shuddha Gandhak (sulphur), Shuddha Hartal (orpiment), Shuddha Manashila (realgar)
sections.description:
Neelam is a variety of corundum mineral primarily composed of aluminum oxide, with trace elements such as iron and titanium responsible for its deep blue coloration. Owing to its dense crystalline structure, raw sapphire is biologically inert and potentially unsafe for medicinal use. Rasashastra emphasizes that gemstones possess dormant therapeutic energy that becomes functional only after undergoing repeated purification and incineration. 
 From an Ayurvedic perspective, Indraneela is described as having Tikta–Kashaya tendencies with Sheeta Virya and specific Prabhava acting on the nervous and circulatory systems. Through Marana, the gem undergoes significant physicochemical transformation, producing micro-fine particles capable of assimilation at the Dhatu level. This process ensures safety while enhancing medicinal potency. 
 Method Of Preparation 
 1. Shodhana (Purification) 
 Neelam (Sapphire) is purified by subjecting it to steam treatment in Neeli swaras (juice of Indigofera tinctoria) using the Dolayantra method for 3 hours. 
 2. Marana (Incineration) 

लकुचद्रावसम्पिष्टैः शिलागन्धकतालकैः । वज्र विनान्यरत्नानि म्रियन्तेऽष्टपुटैः खलु’ ।। (Rasratna Samuchya 4/63)

 First, crush pure sapphire (Neelam) in an iron mortar to obtain a fine powder. Now, mix equal parts of purified haritala (orpiment), purified manashila (realgar), and purified gandhak (sulfur) with the sapphire powder in a mortar. Triturate the mixture with the juice of Artocarpus lakoocha and form small discs. Dry these discs, seal them in a crucible, and heat them in a furnace using the Gajaputa method. After eight such cycles of heating, the sapphire ash is obtained. The ash is white in color.
sections.properties_and_actions_of_neelam_bhasma:
श्वासकासहरं वृष्यं त्रिदोषघ्नं सुदीपनम् । विषमज्वरदुर्नामपापघ्नं नीलमीरितम्’ ।। (Rasratna Samuchya 4/53)


नीलं तु सुमृतं वृष्यं बल्यं दीपनमुत्तमम् । त्रिदोषशमनं वर्ण्य गुदजामयनाशनम् ।। त्वच्यं कुष्ठादिदोषघ्नं श्वासकासनिपूदनम् । कफपित्तानिलहरं विषमज्वरनाशनम्’ ।। (Ras Tarangni 23/101-102)


 Neelam Bhasma acts as Tridoshaghna, helping in the regulation and balance of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha Dosha. 
 It possesses Vrishya properties, supporting vitality and reproductive strength. 
 It functions as a Balya agent, enhancing physical strength and endurance. 
 It works as an Uttama Deepana, strongly stimulating digestive fire and metabolism. 
 It exhibits Varnavardhaka action, helping to improve complexion and skin radiance. 
 It acts as Arghanashaka, aiding in the management of chronic and difficult-to-treat disorders. 
 It is useful as a Kushtanashaka, supporting treatment of various skin diseases. 
 It shows Tvachya properties, promoting nourishment and health of the skin. 
 It is beneficial in Shvasa, helping relieve respiratory distress and breathing difficulty. 
 It is useful in Kasa, reducing cough and throat irritation. 
 It is effective in Vishama Jwara, particularly intermittent and chronic fever conditions. 
 It exhibits Papanashaka action, helping in eliminating toxins and harmful influences from the body. 

 Neelam Bhasma is considered stabilizing in nature, helping regulate abnormal physiological and neurological activity. 
 Clinical Use 

 Digestive Weakness (Agnimandya): Supports improvement of appetite and digestion by enhancing digestive fire. 
 Respiratory Disorders (Shvasa Kasa): Helpful in managing breathlessness, chest congestion, and chronic cough. 
 Skin Disorders (Kushtha): Used in chronic skin diseases to support purification and improve skin health. 
 Intermittent Fever (Vishama Jwara): Beneficial in irregular and recurrent fever patterns. 
 General Weakness (Daurbalya): Supports restoration of strength and endurance in debilitated individuals. 
 Reproductive Debility (Shukra Kshaya): Promotes vitality and supports reproductive strength due to its Vrishya action. 
 Complexion Disorders (Varnya Vikara): Helps improve skin tone and clarity through its Varnavardhaka property. 
 Chronic and Obstinate Diseases: Useful in long-standing disorders that are difficult to manage with routine therapy. 
 Toxic Conditions (Papa Dosha / Vishaja Avastha): Assists in detoxification and elimination of harmful influences. 
 Tridoshic Disorders: Helps in maintaining balance of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha in systemic diseases. 
 Convalescence: Supports recovery following prolonged illness by improving vitality and metabolic stability. 

 In clinical practice, it is often prescribed in micro-doses along with appropriate Anupana to direct its action toward specific systems.
sections.dosage:
Typical dosage: 15 mg to 60 mg per day 
 Anupana: Honey, ghee, milk, or physician-selected herbal preparations
sections.contraindications_and_precautions:
Not advised during pregnancy and lactation without expert supervision 
 Should not be used in high Pitta conditions without proper assessment 
 Avoid long-term unsupervised administration 
 Must be prepared strictly according to classical Rasashastra standards 

 Conclusion 
 Neelam Bhasma reflects the advanced pharmaceutical wisdom of Ayurvedic alchemy, where a powerful gemstone is transformed into a subtle therapeutic agent. When properly prepared and judiciously administered, it supports neurological stability, metabolic balance, and systemic strength. Its action is profound yet delicate, demanding precise dosage and expert supervision. Neelam Bhasma thus occupies a specialized place in Rasashastra, offering therapeutic benefit in select chronic and debilitated conditions while emphasizing the importance of classical processing and responsible clinical use.

 Properties And Actions Of Neelam Bhasma 
 
श्वासकासहरं वृष्यं त्रिदोषघ्नं सुदीपनम् । विषमज्वरदुर्नामपापघ्नं नीलमीरितम्’ ।। (Rasratna Samuchya 4/53)
 
 
नीलं तु सुमृतं वृष्यं बल्यं दीपनमुत्तमम् । त्रिदोषशमनं वर्ण्य गुदजामयनाशनम् ।। त्वच्यं कुष्ठादिदोषघ्नं श्वासकासनिपूदनम् । कफपित्तानिलहरं विषमज्वरनाशनम्’ ।। (Ras Tarangni 23/101-102)
 
 
 Neelam Bhasma acts as Tridoshaghna, helping in the regulation and balance of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha Dosha. 
 It possesses Vrishya properties, supporting vitality and reproductive strength. 
 It functions as a Balya agent, enhancing physical strength and endurance. 
 It works as an Uttama Deepana, strongly stimulating digestive fire and metabolism. 
 It exhibits Varnavardhaka action, helping to improve complexion and skin radiance. 
 It acts as Arghanashaka, aiding in the management of chronic and difficult-to-treat disorders. 
 It is useful as a Kushtanashaka, supporting treatment of various skin diseases. 
 It shows Tvachya properties, promoting nourishment and health of the skin. 
 It is beneficial in Shvasa, helping relieve respiratory distress and breathing difficulty. 
 It is useful in Kasa, reducing cough and throat irritation. 
 It is effective in Vishama Jwara, particularly intermittent and chronic fever conditions. 
 It exhibits Papanashaka action, helping in eliminating toxins and harmful influences from the body. 
 
 Neelam Bhasma is considered stabilizing in nature, helping regulate abnormal physiological and neurological activity. 
 Clinical Use 
 
 Digestive Weakness (Agnimandya): Supports improvement of appetite and digestion by enhancing digestive fire. 
 Respiratory Disorders (Shvasa Kasa): Helpful in managing breathlessness, chest congestion, and chronic cough. 
 Skin Disorders (Kushtha): Used in chronic skin diseases to support purification and improve skin health. 
 Intermittent Fever (Vishama Jwara): Beneficial in irregular and recurrent fever patterns. 
 General Weakness (Daurbalya): Supports restoration of strength and endurance in debilitated individuals. 
 Reproductive Debility (Shukra Kshaya): Promotes vitality and supports reproductive strength due to its Vrishya action. 
 Complexion Disorders (Varnya Vikara): Helps improve skin tone and clarity through its Varnavardhaka property. 
 Chronic and Obstinate Diseases: Useful in long-standing disorders that are difficult to manage with routine therapy. 
 Toxic Conditions (Papa Dosha / Vishaja Avastha): Assists in detoxification and elimination of harmful influences. 
 Tridoshic Disorders: Helps in maintaining balance of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha in systemic diseases. 
 Convalescence: Supports recovery following prolonged illness by improving vitality and metabolic stability. 
 
 In clinical practice, it is often prescribed in micro-doses along with appropriate Anupana to direct its action toward specific systems. 
 Dosage 
 
 Typical dosage: 15 mg to 60 mg per day 
 Anupana: Honey, ghee, milk, or physician-selected herbal preparations 
 
 Dosage must always be individualized due to its potency. 
 Contraindications And Precautions 
 
 Not advised during pregnancy and lactation without expert supervision 
 Should not be used in high Pitta conditions without proper assessment 
 Avoid long-term unsupervised administration 
 Must be prepared strictly according to classical Rasashastra standards 
 
 Conclusion 
 Neelam Bhasma reflects the advanced pharmaceutical wisdom of Ayurvedic alchemy, where a powerful gemstone is transformed into a subtle therapeutic agent. When properly prepared and judiciously administered, it supports neurological stability, metabolic balance, and systemic strength. Its action is profound yet delicate, demanding precise dosage and expert supervision. Neelam Bhasma thus occupies a specialized place in Rasashastra, offering therapeutic benefit in select chronic and debilitated conditions while emphasizing the importance of classical processing and responsible clinical use.

name: Palasha Kshara

sections.introduction: Palasha Kshara is an ayurvedic formulation. This is prepared from an herb palasha. Palasha is a famous ayurvedic herb, which is used since ancient times. This is famous for its leaves, which are used to make food plates. About kshara, it is an extract of the herb ashes, which are alkaline in nature. This kshara is given to the persons who suffer from worms, skin ailments or kidney stones.
sections.ingredients:
Whole Palasha plant 
 Lime powder 
 Conch powder 
 Shankha bhasma 
 Shukti choorna 

 Method of Preparation 

 Take the plant of palasha and burn in open air. 
 Take up to 3.072 kg ash and added up to 12 litre water. Boil this water and reduce one fourth level of water remained. 
 Then do filtration of this decoction for 21 times. Filtration is done with four folded cloth. 
 After filtration it is boiled till it becomes solid. 
 After its solidification, add conch powder up to 48 g, lime powder 24 g, shankha bhsama 192 g and shukti powder up to 96 g. 
 Take this mixture and heat this again until its all moisture got lost. 
 Now preserved this in heap of grains.
sections.dose: 250 mg to one gram per day with rock salt and trikuta churna, after food.
sections.indications:
Dysuria 
 Liver and spleen disorders 
 Malabsorption 
 Gastro-enteritis 
 Internal abscess 
 Urinary calculi
sections.contraindications:
Avoid self-medication. 
 Avoid in pregnancy and infants. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Panaviraladi Bhasma (Bhasmam)

sections.introduction: Panaviraladi Bhasma is an Ayurvedic medicine in the form of powder which is useful in treating the conditions of edema and ascites. According to Ayurvedic terms, it is Kshara type of preparation. Which is described by Ayurveda as a formulation that induces diuresis and decreases fluid accumulation in the body.
sections.ingredients:
It consists of Equal parts of:- 

 Panavirala ( Borassus flabellifer ) 
 Katalati ( Achyranthes aspera 
 Chulli (Hygrophila) ( Asteracantha longifolia ) Root 
 Rambha (Banana tree) ( Musa paradisiaca )
sections.dosage:
Consumption: 250 mg to 1 gram twice a day before or after food along with buttermilk or water, or as recommended by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 The powder is used by adding either with buttermilk, or with water. 
 It is also guided to consume it with hot or cold water or in water of cooked rice. 

 Method of Preparation 
 The drugs have to be burnt in an open earthen pot and ash should be obtained. 
 This ash is then added with water and filtered. The liquid is added with buttermilk and fermented.
sections.therapeutic_uses:
Its medicinal properties include Diuretic, Carminative, Digestive stimulant, liver protective, mild anodyne and mild anti-inflammatory effects 
 It is very useful Ayurvedic Medicine for the treatment of ascites, reducing the overall swelling. 
 An efficient remedy in Anemia. 
 It is also beneficial in providing relief in case of abdominal distension, liver and spleen disorders. 
 This is a good medicine in dropsy. 

 Contraindication 
 As this consists of variety of salts, therefore it may not be a perfect medicine for people having problem of hypertension. 
 Being alkaline in nature, it can result in excess loss of body fluid. 
 Having kshara as ingredient, this may influence the quality and quantity of sperm on long term use. Therefore people undergoing medical treatment for low sperm count should take precaution. 

 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Praval Bhasma

sections.overview: Praval Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Praval bhasma is a natural rich source of calcium and an Ayurvedic medicine prepared from Coral. It has been used traditionally in Indian Ayurvedic medicine as a supplement in treating various conditions of bone metabolic disorders associated mainly with calcium deficiency. It is also an Ayurvedic treatment for certain other diseases like asthma, cough, bleeding disorders etc. This medicine should only be taken strictly under medical supervision. 
 It maintain balances of Vata, Pitta and Kapha Doshas but especially Kapha and Vata Dosha.
sections.ingredients_of_praval_bhasma:
Purified coral pieces 
 Aloe vera juice extract/Shatavari ( Asparagus racemosus ) root juice extract or Jayanti juice extract or cow milk. 

 Method of Preparation 
 First of all grind purified coral pieces into fine powder which is further ground with aloe vera juice extract/Shatavari ( Asparagus racemosus ) root juice extract or Jayanti juice extract or cow milk. It is finally formed to a flat, disc shaped cakes and then it is dried and subjected to 800 – 900 degree Celsius for about 3 – 4 hours. This process is repeated for three times. Ultimately a white colored Bhasma (Coral calx) is obtained.
sections.therapeutic_uses:
Praval Bhasma has many uses like: 

 For eye disorders and phthisis 
 Chronic respiratory diseases 
 Bleeding disorders such as nasal bleeding, bleeding hemorrhoids, menorrhagia 
 Cough and cold 
 Excessive sweating, night sweating 
 Painful micturition and leucorrhoea 
 Toxic conditions 
 It is useful to improve digestive power, immunity, vision power, and skin complexion.
sections.dosage:
Consume about 250 mg of Bhasma either one or two times a day before or after food or as suggested by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 Traditionally it is administered along with butter, milk, ghee, sugar, candy or honey.
sections.contraindications_side_effects:
This medicine must be taken under strict medical direction. 
 Its self-medication can be unsafe. 
 Over-dosage may result in serious poisonous side effects. 
 It is better to avoid in case of pregnant and lactating mothers and even in children. 
 Have this medicine in precise dose and for limited period of time, as advised by doctor. 
 Store in a dry cool place. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Praval Pishti (Coral Calcium)

sections.overview:
Praval Pishti (Coral Calcium) 
 Reference: Ayurveda Sara Sangraha, Shodhana marana prakarana page: 119, AFI Vol. 1. 
 Praval Pishti is an Ayurvedic medicine which is prepared from Coral. Praval is the name given to coral in Hindi and in Ayurveda. However, coral calcium powder is not used directly in Ayurveda. Coral calcium powder is processed with edible rose water and ground to make a micro-fine powder. The coral calcium powder processed with rose water is known as Praval Pishti. It is used in Ayurvedic treatment of various health complications like cough, cold, Pitta related diseases etc. It should only be taken strictly under medical supervision.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Pravala – Purified Coral 
 Rose water – quantity sufficient. 

 How to Make? 
 Take purified Coral and it is pounded to powder form then it is thoroughly ground with rose water for 3 – 4 days, till it becomes as fine as collyrium and finally to obtain Pishti.
sections.dosage: 125 mg – 250 mg once or twice a day before or after food along with honey, butter or ghee or as directed by Ayurvedic doctor.
sections.indications:
Praval Pishti (Coral calcium) is helpful in following health conditions: 

 Bleeding disorders 
 Calcium deficiency 
 General debility 
 Headache 
 Burning sensation 
 Acidity 
 Ulcers 
 Ulcerative colitis 
 Jaundice 
 Hepatitis 
 Vomiting 
 Conjunctivitis 
 Fever 
 Depression 
 Anxiety with restlessness and worrying 
 Heart Palpitation 
 Tachycardia 
 Non-productive cough 
 Asthma with difficulty in coughing up sputum 
 Osteoarthritis 
 Osteoporosis 
 Low bone mineral density 
 Premature greying of hair 
 Hair fall 
 Sunburn 
 Post-Menopausal Osteoporosis Prevention 
 Painful periods (especially membranous dysmenorrhea) 
 Breast tenderness 
 Oligospermia (if person is also suffering with acidity and heat sensation)
sections.side_effects:

name: Raupya-Makshik Bhasma

sections.overview: Raupya-Makshik Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.reference_rasa_tarangini_21_19_20:
Mashika Bhasma is of two types: 

 Raupya Makshik Bhasma 
 Swarna Makshik Bhasma 

 Raupya Makshik Bhasma 
 Raupya Makshik Bhasma, an Ayurvedic medicine, formed of from an ore of Copper and Iron Pyrite. It has bitter, sweet principles. It can act as an Ayurvedic treatment of diabetes, piles, skin diseases etc. This medicine must be strictly taken only under medical supervision. It maintains the Balances of Kapha and Pitta Dosha. It consists of useful nutrients like iron and copper. And these nutrients are very essential components that keep the working of many biological functions in the body. Copper and iron both are essential for formation of Red blood cells (erythrocytes). Copper helps in the absorption of iron in the body and iron is necessary for the formation of hemoglobin.
sections.ingredients:
Purified Raupya Makshik 
 Lemon juice 

 Method of Preparation 
 This Bhasma is prepared using purified Raupya Makshik through various different methods. Here is one of the method explained below: 
 Boiling purified Raupya makshika with lemon juice which is further dried. Then it is again ground with lemon juice, formed into cakes. The further step is of heating them in a closed container in absence of air at a temperature of 500 – 600 degree Celsius. This process is repeated for 10 times to obtain its Bhasma (Calx).
sections.therapeutic_uses:
It has aphrodisiac and anti-aging properties. 
 Useful Ayurvedic treatment for diabetes. 
 Also useful in helminthiasis (Intestinal worms). 
 Eye diseases like burning sensation in the eyes. 
 Urinary tract disorders as burning micturition. 
 Hemorrhoids and bleeding piles. 
 Skin diseases like Itching. 
 Abdominal diseases and Anorexia. 
 Insomnia and Headache. 
 Inflammation and Poison. 
 Anemia and Jaundice. 
 Chronic low grade fever. 
 Heartburn. 
 Nausea and vomiting. 
 Leucorrhoea.
sections.dosage:
Take about 125 – 250 mg one or two times a day before or after having meals or as instructed by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 Contraindication/Side Effects 

 Self-medication of this Bhasma could result in risks to health. 
 Have this medicine in accurate dose and for limited period of time, as directed by doctor. 
 This Bhasma must be avoided in case of pregnancy, lactation and even in children. 
 Store in a dry and cool place. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Shankh (Shankha) Bhasma

sections.overview: Shankh (Shankha) Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Shankha Bhasma is an Ayurvedic preparation from Conch shell which is a powder of a substance obtained by calcination. It balances Vata and Pitta Dosha It is useful excellent Ayurvedic remedy for digestive system complaints like gastritis, abdominal pain, malabsorption syndrome etc. This Bhasma has properties to improve digestion, absorbs excess liquid content, improves appetite and cures gastritis, acidity, nausea etc. 
 Do you know about Shankha? 
 It is a soft body organism that lives inside dense, very hard and calcareous shell or conch. Shankha is also known as “Indian conch”. Two types of Shankha is available one is called Vama varta (opening of this shankha is on left side) and Dakshin varta (opening of this shankha is on right side). For medicinal preparation “Vama varta” shankha is used. 
 Different names of Shankha: 

 Sanskrit name: Shankha 
 English name: Conch shell 
 Hindi name: Shankh 
 Kannada name: Shankha 
 Gujarati name: Shankh 
 Malayalam name: Shankham
sections.ingredients:
Purified Conch shell 
 Aloe vera juice or lemon juice 

 Method of Preparation 
 Preparation of this Bhasma is by use of purified Conch shell. There are various different techniques for its preparation. Any method can be used. Here is one of the process. 
 First of all grinding purified shankha powder with aloe vera juice or lemon juice, and made into disc shaped cakes. This then dried and burnt in the absence of air, at a temperature of 800 – 900 degree Celsius and then it is allowed for self-cooling. This process is repeated twice to obtain bhasma. 
 Medicinal Properties
sections.therapeutic_uses:
Shankha Bhasma has ability to easily absorb and compensate the calcium required by the body. 
 It is coolant by nature and can improve skin complexion. 
 Useful remedy for gastritis, abdominal colic, vomiting, nausea, malabsorption syndrome, dyspepsia , acne, etc. 
 It is a natural source of calcium and vitamin C which is good for the development and maintenance of healthy bones, teeth and cell membranes. Therefore beneficial in growing children, adolescents and post-menopausal women who need more calcium. 
 This bhasma provides relief from the condition such as calcium deficiency without causing any side effect like Constipation and acid formation in stomach.
sections.health_benefits:
Anti-inflammatory: Beneficial in inflammatory conditions. 
 Antioxidant: Helps in detoxification of body.

sections.introduction:
Shringa Bhasma, an Ayurvedic medicine having its origin from animal and it is prepared from horn of Deer Here Shring means horn of Deer and is counted as tonic acting as a remedy for respiratory disorders. Shringa Bhasma appear as a white odorless powder, having same taste as that of chalk It comprises of calcium, carbonates, magnesium, sulphates, chlorides, potassium, tannins and proteins. 
 It can maintain balances of Vata and Pitta Doshas. It has properties Expectorant Mucolytic, Antitussive, Bacteriostatic, Antibacterial, Antimicrobial, Mild Anodyne and also Mild Antipyretic and is good for of heart burn, gastric pain, abdominal colic and asthma.
sections.ingredients:
Deer Horn 
 Latex of Arka ( Callotropis procera )
sections.doses:
Consume about 250 mg – 500 mg once or two times a day before or after having meals or as recommended by Ayurvedic doctor. 
 Traditionally it is being taken along with ghee or honey. 

 Method of Preparation 
 First of all horn of Deer is cut into small piece and is then burnt in open air. Then grinding it to get powder to which latex of Arka (Callotropis procera) is added. This is again ground well, formed into disc shaped cakes, dried, and burnt in the absence of air at a temperature of 800 – 900 degree Celsius. It is then kept for self-cooling. This method is repeated three times to finally get Bhasma.
sections.therapeutic_uses:
Shringa Bhasma chiefly acts as expectorant and mucolytic. 
 Its other medicinal use are like:- 

 Respiratory diseases – Asthma, difficult breathing Cough, Pleurisy/ Pleuritis (inflammation of the pleura, the lining surrounding the lungs) 
 Also provides strength the bones, joints, cartilages. 
 Cardiac colic 
 Hiccups 
 Abdominal distension and intestinal rumbling and gastritis. 
 Useful remedy in reducing anorexia 
 Intercostal neuralgia, 
 Heart burn etc.
sections.contraindications_side_effects:

 Practicing Self-medication with this bhasma might be a risk. 
 Have accurate dose this medicine and for restricted period of time, as directed by doctor. 
 Keep it out of approach and vision of children. 
 Store in a dry cool place

sections.overview:
Shukti Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage 
 (Reference: Ayurveda prakasha 2/327) 
 Shukti bhasma is an Ayurvedic preparation from Pearl Oyster. These pearl oysters are found in Indian Ocean. Shells of oyster are processed as per Ayurvedic texts to create calcinated shells. It is also known as the Mukta Shukti Bhasma. This Ayurvedic medicine is used in treatment of gastritis, abdominal colic and anorexia etc. This medicine should only be administrated strictly under medical supervision. 
 This Shukti bhasma is used as a natural source of calcium. It is also used as an ingredient in many Ayurvedic medicines which are used for improving bone strength. It also contains the calcium phosphate, calcium carbonate, magnesium oxide, aluminum oxide and organic matter.
sections.ingredients:
Purified Pearl Oyster 
 Method of preparation 

 Purified Pearl Oyster pieces are grinded and made into fine powder. 
 It is heated in absence of air at 800 – 900 º C for 2 – 3 hours. 
 This process is repeated for three times, to get white colored Shukti bhasma (Pearl oyster Calx).
sections.dosage: 125 – 250 mg once or twice in a day before or after food or as prescribed by your Ayurvedic doctor. It is traditionally administered along with butter, honey, milk and ghee.
sections.indications:
Use of this medicine is good in calcium deficiency like rickets and arthritis. 
 It is also used in the treatment of chronic fever and cough. 
 This is an excellent medicine to treat the peptic ulcer, vomiting, hyperacidity, dyspepsia, gastritis and abdominal colic. 
 It is used to treat the cardiac diseases. 
 It is useful in urinary calculi. 
 It is quite beneficial in the management of cardiac diseases like blockage in coronary artery. 
 It is used to treat the splenomegaly. 

 Contradictions 

 This medicine should only be taken strictly under medical supervision. 
 Self-medication with this medicine is dangerous. 
 Over-dosage may result in the severe side effects. 
 Take this medicine in precise dose and for limited period of time, as suggested by doctor. 
 Keep this medicine out of reach and sight of children. 
  Store in a dry cool place. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

sections.reference_ayurveda_prakasha_257_258:
Sphatika Bhasma is also known by the names like Tuvari, kankshi and Phataki etc. It is hemostatic, bitter, anti-inflammatory and antiseptic in nature. It acts as the blood purifier and used for treatment of various skin diseases like leucoderma and herpes. This Ayurvedic preparation is also beneficial in the treatment of bleeding disorders and hemorrhage. It is also helpful to treat the various other problems like abdominal pains, respiratory complications and a few gynecological disorders like menorrhagia. This medicine balances the vata and pitta dosha in body. 
 Ingredient 
 Alum (Sphatika) 
 Method of Manufacturing 
 Sphatika – Alum (Sphatika) is heated in a pan, in open air, till all the moisture is lost. At the end, white powder is collected.
sections.indications:

 It acts as the blood purifier.

 Lower back ache.

 Hematemesis (Blood vomiting).

 It is used to cure gynecological issues like leucorrhea and vaginal itching etc. 
 Used in the treatment of leucoderma and herpes etc. 
 Malarial fever, chronic fever and jaundice. 
 Eye diseases. 
 Constricts blood vessels and tissues.

 Take 125 – 250 mg, one or two times daily, before or after food, or as advised by Ayurvedic doctor.

sections.ingredients:
Swarna Makshik (Chalcopyrite or copper iron sulphide in English). 
 Method of Preparation 

 Purified Swarna makshika is boiled with lemon juice and then dried. 
 It is again ground with lemon juice and made into bars. 
 These bars are heated in a closed container in absence of air in 500 – 600 degree Celsius. 
 This process is repeated for 10 times to obtain its Bhasma (Calx).
sections.dosage: 125 – 250 mg once or twice a day before or after food or as directed by an Ayurvedic doctor.

 This medicine is also used to treat mouth ulcers.

name: Tamra Bhasma

sections.reference_ayurveda_prakasha_3_145_rasara: Tamra Bhasma is an Ayurvedic medicine, prepared from Copper. The main action of this Ayurvedic preparation is on the spleen, liver, stomach, intestines, skin and muscles. It stimulates the bile secretion from the liver and gallbladder. Hence, it helps to increase the peristaltic movements, eases digestion and stimulates appetite. Tamra bhasma is also used in the treatment of various other problems like skin diseases, obesity, piles and asthma etc. Tamra bhasma is very useful to cure food poisoning because it produces instant vomiting to extrude the poison from the body.
sections.ingredients:
Shuddha Tamra – Purified Copper 
 Method of Preparation 
 Purified Copper is added with purified Sulphur and crushed well. (Or Copper is pounded with aloe vera juice) thin cakes are prepared and heated in a closed container under 500 – 700 degree celcius for 24 hours, to obtain black colored bhasma (Copper Calx).
sections.dosage:
50 mg-125 mg once or twice a day before or after food or as suggested by an Ayurvedic doctor. 
 This medicine is traditionally administered along with ghee, honey milk or with sugar.
sections.indications:
Enlargement of liver and spleen. 
 Anemia. 
 This medicine is very useful to treat chronic respiratory conditions like bronchial asthma, cough, cold and tuberculosis. 
 Used to treat digestive health issues like hyperacidity and loss of appetite. 
 Piles. 
 It is used to treat high cholesterol. 
 Used in the treatment of cancer. 
 Food poisoning. 
 Ascitis. 
 Useful in the treatment of parasitic infections. 
 Used to cure various neurological disorders.
sections.side_effects:
This medicine should be taken only under strict medical supervision. 
 Self-medication with this medicine may prove to be dangerous. 
 Overdose may cause severe poisonous side effects. 
 Avoid this medicine during pregnant, lactating mothers and children. 
 Take this medicine in precise doses and for a limited period of time, as recommended by the doctor. 
 Keep out of reach and sight of children. 
 Store in a dry cool place. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Tankan Bhasma

sections.overview: Tankan Bhasma – Uses, Benefits, Indications, Side Effects and Dosage
sections.reference_rasa_tarangini_133_79_81:
What is tankan bhasma 
 Tankan Bhasma is a special Ayurvedic medicine prepared from Borax. This Ayurvedic calcined formulation is used to cure the various complications like bronchitis, abdominal pain, cough, breathing problems, wheezing, dandruff, bad breath, foul-smelling urine and dysmenorrhea. Tankan Bhasma is a very effective Ayurvedic treatment for the lack of menstruation in females. This Ayurvedic preparation helps to balance the vata and kapha doshas. 
 Tankan Bhasma Ingredients 
 Sodium borate 
 Method of Tankan Bhasma Preparation 
 Tankan Bhasma – Prepared from Sodium borate. The raw borax is first purified and then subjected to controlled heating to remove moisture. It is further heated until it transforms into a white, dry, amorphous powder, which is the final Bhasma form used for medicinal purposes. 
 Tankan Bhasma Dosage 
 125 mg to 250 mg of this Bhasma is taken daily along with honey and ghee. 
 Tankan Bhasma Uses and Benefits 

 Use of this medicine is quite effective to treat female health complications. It helps to induce menstruation in women suffering with amenorrhea or oligomenorrhea (Scanty menstrual flow). It helps to improve menstrual flow. 
 It is used to treat respiratory complications like cough, bronchitis, wheezing, asthma and chest congestion. 
 It is helpful to treat urinary infections. 
 It is good, quite good to improve the digestion power and also relieves the bloating. 
 It cures bad breath. 
 This medicine is used in the treatment of food poisoning and abdominal colic pain. 
 It is used to cure the skin sores. 
 It is helpful to treat viral infections of skin like hand foot and mouth disorder. 

 Tankan Bhasma Side Effects 

 Use of this increases Pitta and hence leads to the burning sensation in few people. So caution should be taken while administering this medicine in the case of gastritis and peptic ulcer patients. 
 Tankan Bhasma should be avoided during pregnancy. 
 Take this medicine during the lactation period only under medical supervision. 
 Long term usage of this medicine can cause oligospermia. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Trivang Bhasma

sections.overview: Trivang Bhasma – Uses, Benefits, Indications, Side Effects and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Trivang Bhasma is an Ayurvedic calcined formulation made from three elements Tin, lead and zinc. This formulation is very useful in curing diabetes, urinary disorders, premature ejaculation and generalized weakness. It shows its effects mainly on testes, ovaries, uterus, nerves and urinary bladder. The consumption of this formulation provides strength and important minerals and vitamins to the body. It should be used in a small dosage. 
 Trivang Bhasma Ingredients 

 Purified lead 
 Purified zinc 
 Purified tin 
 Sufficient amount of powdered Cannabis sativa and Papaver somniferum 

 Method of Trivang Bhasma Preparation 
 Mix the three purified elements and put them in an iron pan. Add the 2 powdered herbs slowly and gradually and mix rapidly till they become homogenous and in the form of a powder. Cover the pan with a lid and cook it for 12- 14 hours on high heat. When the mixture changes its color to a deep red, turn the flame off. Let it cool then strain it with a muslin cloth and triturate it with fresh Aloe Vera juice. After it dries off, heat it in a sealed container 7 times to obtain a yellow colored powder which is the final product. 
 Trivang Bhasma Dosage 
 125 mg twice a day after meals with butter or honey. 
 Trivang Bhasma Uses 

 Boosts immunity 
 Urinary disorders 
 Leucorrhea 
 Infertility 
 Underdeveloped female external and internal organs 
 Impotency in males 
 Anovulation 
 Night fall 
 Diabetes 
 Miscarriages 

 Trivang Bhasma Contraindications 

 It should be avoided during pregnancy and lactation. This formulation shouldn’t be given to kids. 
 Over dosage should be strictly avoided. 
 Self-medication is discouraged. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Vaikranta Bhasma

sections.introduction: Vaikranta Bhasma is prepared from Tourmaline which is used in treating Ascites, anemia, asthma, diabetes etc.
sections.ingredients:
Purified Vaikrant [Tourmaline] 
 Purified sulphur 
 Lemon juice for triturating 

 METHOD OF PREPARATION 
 Crush purified tourmaline into a fine powder and add equal amount of purified sulphur. Triturate with lemon juice and heat it at a high temperature of 800 degree Celsius in a sealed container. It has to be heated 8 times to obtain a soft, dull red colored product. If it’s not soft to touch it should be heated again.
sections.dosage:
60 mg with honey twice daily or as directed by your doctor. 
 This Bhasma can be mixed with 1/4th of suvarna Bhasma. Now add 60 mg each of powdered long pepper and Embelia ribes.
sections.indications:
Tuberculosis 
 Weakness in old age 
 Piles 
 Anemia 
 Respiratory disorders 
 Malabsorption syndrome 
 Mouth diseases 
 Chest ailments 
 Diabetes 
 Anti-aging properties 
 Strengthens and boosts immunity

 Take this medicine under stern doctor’s prescription.

name: Vajra (Diamond, Heerak) Bhasma

sections.overview: Vajra (Diamond, Heerak) Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction:
Vajra Bhasma is also known as Heerak Bhasma is a formulation of Diamonds. It is a carbon based medicine. There are other elements other than diamond which are present in a smaller quantity because of its processing in an iron container. This formulation acts as a rejuvenator, a nutritious tonic, aphrodisiac. It aids in strengthening the heart and the entire body. Heerak Bhasma is an excellent medicine to cure cardiac ailments by eradicating the hindrances in the coronary arteries, provides relief in Angina pectoris, eases the contraction of veins and blood clotting and enhances the blood circulation. 
 Also, it helps in keeping equilibrium of the three Doshas.
sections.ingredients:
Purified diamond 

 Method of Preparation 
 Grind equal quantities of purified diamond along with Ras sindoor and purified sulphur. Put it in a container and seal it properly and heat it at a high temperature of 800- 900 Celsius. Let it cool down and then repeat the same process for 14 times to get the final product.
sections.dosage:
It should be consumed in a very small amount, 5- 8 mg twice a day after meals. 
 It can be taken with butter, clarified butter, milk or honey.
sections.indications:
Diabetes 
 Respiratory ailments 
 Liver disorders 
 Anemia 
 Ascites 
 Obesity 
 Cancer 
 Arthritis 
 Inflammation 
 Eye diseases 
 Impotency 
 Tuberculosis 
 Cardiac disorders 
 Enhances libido
sections.contraindications:
Over dosage should be avoided and might cause severe gastritis. 
 It should be taken for a short duration. 
 Self-medication is discouraged and should be taken under medical supervision only. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

name: Vanga Bhasma

sections.overview: Vanga Bhasma – Benefits, Usage, Indications and Dosage
sections.introduction: Vanga Bhasma is calcined to form a powder. It is prepared from the metal Tin. Tin goes through all the steps of Bhasma preparation which makes it super fine as a result. It is nourishing and strengthening. This medicine is very effective in treating mental fatigue, worm infestation and sexual disorders also. This formulation should be properly prepared as raw Vanga Bhasma has severe side effects. It is extremely beneficial in treating male and female reproductive diseases, adrenal gland disorders.
sections.ingredients:
Purified tin metal 
 Aloe Vera juice 

 Method of Preparation 
 Take the pieces of purified tin and put them in an iron pan and let it melt. Add powdered Achyranthes aspera and Ficus religiosa and mix well. Now add Aloe Vera juice to this mixture and prepare round, flat discs. Put these discs in a tightly sealed container and heat them at a high temperature. Repeat this process seven times to get the final product.
sections.dosage:
125- 250 mg twice daily after meals. 
 It can be taken with Tinospora concoction, honey, turmeric, clarified butter. 
 Pungent products like chilies, tamarind etc. should be shunned.
sections.indications:
Urinary tract disorders 
 Halitosis 
 Anovulation 
 Amenorrhea 
 Leucorrhea 
 Dysmenorrhea 
 Polyuria 
 Menopause 
 Male reproductive system ailments 
 Worm infestation 
 Helps in the formation of RBCs 
 Pain reliever
sections.contraindications:
Over dosage can cause severe gastritis. 
 It should be prescribed by your doctor. Self-medication is strictly discouraged. 
 It should be avoided by pregnant women, lactating mothers and kids. 


 Note:- This is pure classical Ayurvedic medicine and should be strictly consumed only after prescription of an Ayurvedic doctor and to be taken under medical supervision only.

 According to Ayurveda acidity is known as Amlapitta which is one of the most common symptom (disease) seen and faced by people in the society. In acidity, pitta dosha is much more involved in comparison to vata kapha dosha. 
 Acidity comes under Gastro esophageal reflux disease (GERD). This problem or a disease happens when acid in the stomach regularly flows back into the tube connecting your mouth and stomach (oesophagus). People suffering from acidity experiences acidic reflux. 
 Acidity commonly results to heartburn. Hydrochloric acid is present in the stomach which helps in the efficient digestion of food and protect the growth of unwanted bacteria. So when there is an excessive production of this acid leads to the disturbance in the gastric glands of stomach. 
 CAUSES OF ACIDITY 

 Eating heavy meals close to bedtime 
 Highly spicy food 
 Life style 
 Consumption of beverages such as alcohol, coffee, tea, and carbonated drinks 
 Smoking 
 Anti-inflammatory medicine and some of the antibiotics 
 Being Pregnant 
 Stress and tension 

 COMPLICATIONS OF ACIDITY 
 1. Ulcers 
 Due to over secretion of gastric juices, there is the disruption in the lining of the upper part of small intestine. In some cases, ulcers can be the cause of cancer. 
 2. Dyspepsia and heart burns 
 Dyspepsia is the narrowing of the esophagus which creates the sensation of food being stuck in the throat. It occurs after taking meals and is brought by excess abdominal pressure. In acidity one has to face burning sensation in the chest, burping and sometimes leads to chest pain.

 Nausea 
 Burning sensation in the chest 
 Burping 
 Vomiting tendency 
 Chest pain

 Bloating 
 Severe pain in the stomach 
 Difficulty in breathing when acidity is at the acute stage 
 Due to hyper acidity there is erosion of gum and teeth 
 Bad breath

 Endoscopy is used to diagnose the problems in the esophagus. Small tube with a camera through the mouth is inserted in esophagus. 
 In Biopsy there is the removal of small piece from the lining of esophagus for diagnosis purpose. This procedure is done to identify any underlying cancer.

 FAQs 




 What is Acne? 
 Acne is one of a common skin problems. It usually occurs when the hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead cells of the skin. 
 Acne mostly appears on the face, chest, back, neck and shoulders as well. Effective treatments are generally available for more serious problem, but it can be persistent. While, the pimples and bumps heal slowly by its own. But it is seen, that when one begins to go away, then at the same time, other pimples crop up. 
 It is one of the most common problems among teenagers. Younger children are at higher risk of getting acne. 
 This skin problem may cause emotional stress and scar the skin as well. But it depends on its severity. So it is advisable to treat the condition as early as possible. Earlier treatment may lower the risk of getting any physical damage. 


 What are the Causes of Acne? 
 The common causes of this skin problem are listed below: 

 The production of oil on the skin. 
 When the cells of the skin become dead. 
 Clogged pores. 
 Bacteria are another main cause. 



 What are the Symptoms of Acne? 
 The symptoms of the acne depend on the severity of the condition and the common among them are listed below: 

 Whiteheads or the closed plugged pores. 
 Blackheads or open plugged pores. 
 Small and red colored tender bumps on the affected area. 
 Pimples with pus at their tips. 
 Large painful lumps that are present beneath the skin surface. 
 Presence of pus-filled lumps beneath the surface of the skin, also known as cystic lesions. 



 Diagnosis of Acne 
 In most of the cases, this skin problem is easily diagnosed by a dermatologist or other health care provider. However, a doctor may ask some questions regarding your general health to ensure a proper diagnosis. 
 He may ask the following questions: 

 About affected area or something about sensitive skin or eczema 
 Other history of diseases that may affect the ability of the medications to handle the skin problem. 
 Allergies to drugs. 
 Whether you are using steroids for body building. 
 About mood disorders or depression. 
 About usage of contraceptives and something about your current or past pregnancy as well as breast feeding. 
 In rare cases, acne may mimic other similar skin problems like rosacea. This information may also help a lot in diagnosing this skin problem. 



 Trigger factors for Acne 
 The following factors may worsen an existing acne problem: 
 Hormones 
 Hormones such as Androgens pose a higher risk of getting acne at the stage of puberty in young boys and girls. The hormone causes the sebaceous gland to make more sebum and is well responsible for its enlargement. 
 Hormonal changes during pregnancy is another risk factor of acne. The use of oral contraceptives may also affect the production of sebum. 
 Certain medications 
 Medicines containing corticosteroids, androgens or lithium in it, may also pose a risk factor for acne. 
 Diet 

 Diet also plays an important role in making the condition of acne worse. Foods such as dairy products and carbohydrate-rich foods like bread and chips are also responsible for acne. Chocolate is also known for making the condition of acne worse. 
 Stress

 Arthritis is a common joint problem that can affect one as well as multiple joints. Generally there are more than 100 different types of arthritis.
